17.title: Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?
17.body:
## Question

Which operating systems and editors does v0.1.0 promise to work on?

To decide:

- Whether Windows is supported, best-effort, or out of scope for v0.1.0, and whether WSL counts.
- The `engines.vscode` floor and the matching `@types/vscode` pin.
- Whether Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium are supported targets or merely not blocked.

## Context

- Both questions are listed in the seed's [Not yet specified](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#not-yet-specified). The two research tickets that block this one supply the facts.
- Anything cut here moves to the map's Out of scope.

lastComment.body:
## Answer

v0.1.0 promises **VS Code 1.105 or later on macOS and Linux**, with native Windows and the VS Code forks reachable but untested. The whole promise is one **Requirements** section in `packages/vscode/README.md`, which the Marketplace and Open VSX render, plus the `engines` field.

### Operating systems

| Platform | Tier | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (arm64, x64) | Supported | Tested by hand before a release. |
| Linux (arm64, x64), including dev containers and SSH remotes | Supported | CI runs here; the devcontainer is the development environment. |
| WSL remote window on a Windows host | Supported, as Linux | `extensionKind: workspace` puts the scout, `gh` and `claude` inside the distribution. **This is the documented route for Windows users.** |
| Native Windows (PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash) | Best-effort | The code avoids every trap the Windows research found, the README says "untested on Windows", Windows bugs are accepted but never block a release. Install Claude Code with the **native installer**, not npm. |

One universal `.vsix`: the extension bundles no native modules.

### Editors

- `"engines": { "vscode": "^1.105.0" }` and `"@types/vscode": "~1.105.0"` (exists on npm; the `@types/vscode` gaps start after 1.110). The floor is set by Node, not by any API: every API the Cockpit uses exists since 1.93, but 1.105 is the first version that both runs extensions on Node ≥ 22.18 (core's own engine) and that every fork has shipped. Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) on 1.126 is the ceiling the floor must stay under.
- The pin is a tilde because vsce 4 reads only the manifest string: a caret would pass packaging and still install 1.140 types.
- **Cursor, Devin Desktop and VSCodium are not blocked, not supported.** The `.vsix` is published to **Open VSX** (namespace `dbarjs`, decided in #19), the README says "built for VS Code; forks are expected to work", and fork bugs are accepted, not promised. The fork research could not verify terminal-in-editor-area, terminal icons or webview views inside any fork, and Cursor staff say the internals can sit on an older base than the declared version.

### Runtime requirements the README states

- **Claude Code ≥ 2.1.139**, the release that added exec-form hooks (`"args": [...]`, no shell), the newest feature the status plugin relies on. `SessionEnd` is 1.0.85, `PermissionRequest` 2.0.45, `StopFailure` 2.1.78, `async: true` predates 2.1.23. `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` (2.1.280) is not used: with the launch below, `--plugin-dir <path>` is never shell-quoted, so the variable would only raise the floor.
- **Node ≥ 22.18 on `PATH`** in the session's environment, because the hooks run `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/report.mjs` and Claude Code itself ships no Node. On Windows that means a real `node.exe`. Handing the session the extension host's Node instead is a possible later refinement, not a v0.1.0 question.
- `gh` authenticated, for the GitHub tracker (already implied by #3).

### Decisions this forces on the launch

- **A session runs `claude` as the terminal's own process**: `createTerminal({ shellPath: 'claude', shellArgs: [...] })`, never a command typed into a shell with `sendText`. VS Code resolves the binary on `PATH` and node-pty quotes each argument, so the ticket title and the `/wayfinder …` prompt never pass through PowerShell, cmd or Git Bash (which would otherwise rewrite the slash-command as a path). Consequences accepted: the terminal closes when `claude` exits, which is the "ended" signal #6 chose; there is no shell for follow-up commands in that terminal; shell integration is unavailable. Feeds #21.
- **The extension resolves `claude` on `PATH` itself** for the scout and the launch, and on Windows prefers `claude.exe`; an npm `.cmd` shim can't be spawned by `child_process` without a shell, so it's best-effort only.
- **No gating on editor or OS.** The extension activates everywhere the floor allows, with no warning on forks or Windows. On activation it writes `vscode.env.appName`, `appHost`, the VS Code version, `process.platform` and the resolved `claude` path to the Cockpit's output channel, so bug reports from a fork or Windows carry what the research could not verify.

### Not an ADR

None of this is hard to reverse: the floor is a manifest number, the tiers are README text, and the `shellPath` launch is a few lines. The reasoning lives here; the `createTerminal` call gets a code comment when it's built.

### Out of scope, after v0.1.0

- The twelve-item real-Windows test from [`docs/research/windows-behavior.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/windows-behavior/docs/research/windows-behavior.md).
- Verifying terminals, icons and webview views inside each fork.

Sources: #11 and #12, and the Claude Code changelog read on 2026-10-02 (latest release 2.1.288).
lastComment.author: dbarjs

18.title: How is the extension tested?
18.body:
## Question

What does the test setup for v0.1.0 look like, and what does CI run?

To decide:

- What is covered by unit tests through `vp test`, and where the seams are (core has no `vscode` imports).
- Whether integration tests launch VS Code in CI, or whether that waits until after v0.1.0.
- How the webview and the session status plugin are tested, if at all.

## Context

- The seed lists extension testing in [Not yet specified](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#not-yet-specified). The research ticket that blocks this one supplies the options.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

**Every tier is in: the harness is a first-class deliverable of v0.1.0.** Eduardo's steer on 2026-10-02 was "the harness is very important, add test for everything", and he accepted every point below as recommended. The research that fed this ticket is [How can a VS Code extension be integration-tested under Vite+?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/13); the runners decision is recorded as [ADR 0004](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-extension-host-tests-run-on-mocha-beside-vitest.md).

### Decided

1. **Four tiers.**

   | Tier | Runner | Entry point | Covers |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | Unit | Vitest (`@effect/vitest` for Effect code) | `vp test` | `@hero-synergy/core`, the extension's pure logic, the session status plugin |
   | Component | Vitest + happy-dom + `@vue/test-utils` | `vp test` | The Cockpit's Vue app outside VS Code, `acquireVsCodeApi()` stubbed |
   | Extension host | Mocha through `@vscode/test-cli` + `@vscode/test-electron` | `vp run --filter hero-synergy test:integration` | Activation, the view resolving, terminals, the real `vscode` API |
   | End-to-end | Vitest `e2e` project launching VS Code through `playwright._electron` | `vp test --project e2e` | The whole path, including the Cockpit inside its webview |

   Playwright is a library here, not a runner: two runners total (Vitest, Mocha), never three. `vp test` with no `--project` excludes `e2e`, so the fast loop stays fast. `retry: 1` on the `e2e` project only; zero retries everywhere else.

2. **The seam in the extension package.** `vscode` is imported only in adapter modules under `packages/vscode/src/vscode/`. Everything else is pure TypeScript or an Effect service whose live `Layer` imports `vscode` and whose test `Layer` is in-memory (terminals, the webview, the events-file watcher, workspace folders). Host tests cover the adapters; the bulk is unit-tested. This is a working-agreement rule in the map's Notes.

3. **`gh` and `claude -p` in core.** One process-runner Effect service with a live layer and a replay layer. Real `gh api graphql` and `claude -p --json-schema` outputs are recorded once (this repo's own maps as the subject), checked in under `packages/core/test/fixtures/`, and replayed; they also pin the exact GraphQL shape the one-query decision depends on. Plus **one live `gh` job** in CI against this repo's own maps with `GITHUB_TOKEN` (6 rate-limit points per run), **non-blocking for merge**, to catch GitHub changing the sub-issue or dependency API shape. `claude -p` stays fixture-only.

4. **The session status plugin.** Both sides: a unit test spawns `node claude-plugin/report.mjs` with `HERO_SYNERGY_TICKET` and `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS` set and a hook payload on stdin, then asserts the appended status event; the extension's reader is tested on recorded event files. Payloads and files come from the status-hooks prototype's recorded runs, so the corrected six-row table from [Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/6) is pinned by tests, including out-of-order `SessionEnd` and `/clear` starting a new session id. Neither needs Claude Code installed.

5. **Faking `claude` and `gh` for host and end-to-end tests.** Both mechanisms: a user-facing setting for the `claude` location (nvm and Homebrew users need it anyway) that tests point at a stub, and stub executables in `test/fixtures/bin/` on `PATH` for the one test that proves the default lookup works. The stub `claude` records its argv and writes status events on a script (started, working, waiting for you, ended), so live status is driven end-to-end. The fixture workspace uses the **local markdown tracker**, so the map needs no `gh` at all; the stub `gh` covers the GitHub path with the same recorded fixtures as core.

6. **VS Code builds.** Host and end-to-end tests run on **both** the floor (`1.105.0`, the promise made in [Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/17)) and the newest stable, as an array in `.vscode-test.mjs`.

7. **Coverage.** Report now (`vp test --coverage`, the number visible in CI); a failing threshold comes in its own ticket after the first implementation lands, because picking a number now is picking it blind. Coverage applies to the Vitest tiers only.

8. **CI runners and jobs.** Linux for every tier, **macOS for host and end-to-end** (the terminal and the `claude` spawn are the OS-specific surface; the repo is public, so macOS minutes are free). Three parallel jobs: `check` (build, lint, types, unit, component), `vscode` (host and end-to-end on Linux under `xvfb-run -a` and on macOS, the VS Code download cached by OS and version), `live` (the `gh` job). `check` and `vscode` are required for merge; `live` is not.

9. **House rules.** The "use `vp` for everything" rule now reads: every test runs through a `vp` command, `vp test` for Vitest and `vp run --filter hero-synergy test:integration` for the extension host; never call `vitest`, `mocha` or `vscode-test` directly. The adapter rule from point 2 joins it. ADR 0004 records the two runners and the stack additions: `@vscode/test-cli`, `@vscode/test-electron`, `@types/mocha`, `playwright`, `happy-dom`, `@vue/test-utils`.

### Ruled out for v0.1.0

A Windows CI runner (native Windows is best-effort and the real-Windows test is already out of scope); Insiders builds; a live `claude -p` job (no credentials in CI, and the interpret step is still open); Vitest Browser Mode (end-to-end already covers real rendering, and its provider must be pinned to Vite+'s exact Vitest); Playwright Test, `vitest-environment-vscode`, `wdio-vscode-service` and ExTester as runners.

### Defaults for the spec

Not decisions; `/to-spec` may change them freely.

- Host tests in `packages/vscode/test/integration/**/*.test.ts`, bundled to CommonJS by a second `pack` entry into `out-test/` (gitignored, outside `files`, so neither cleaned by `vp pack` nor shipped in the VSIX), with their own tsconfig so `@types/mocha` globals don't leak into Vitest files. `.vscode-test.mjs` with `mocha: { ui: 'bdd' }`, `node:assert/strict`, `launchArgs: ['--disable-extensions']`, and a `workspaceFolder` pointing at the fixture workspace.
- End-to-end tests in `packages/vscode/test/e2e/`, the VS Code download shared with the host tests through `@vscode/test-electron`'s `.vscode-test/` cache (gitignored and ignored by lint and format).
- The fixture workspace in `packages/vscode/test/fixtures/workspace/`: a `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` naming the local markdown tracker and a `.scratch/<effort>/map.md` with a few tickets.
- `.vscode/launch.json` with an `extensionHost` configuration whose `testConfiguration` points at `.vscode-test.mjs`, so the Extension Test Runner extension and the debugger work locally.

### Not verified

Nothing here has been run; the research was reading only. Whether `vp pack` with an array `pack` block produces `.cjs` files that `vscode-test` loads, whether a Vitest project can launch Electron under `vp test`, and whether ESM test files load in the host are proved by the task ticket [Do the two test runners coexist under Vite+?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/25) before `/to-spec` depends on them.

19.title: Which publisher ID and npm names?
19.body:
## Question

Under which names is hero-synergy published?

To decide:

- The Marketplace publisher ID: `hero-synergy` (the brand) or `dbarjs`. It fixes the extension ID, `<publisher>.hero-synergy`, which is painful to change later.
- Whether to claim the unscoped `hero-synergy` npm name so `npx hero-synergy` works. The extension's workspace package already uses that name, so one of them would need another.
- The Open VSX namespace.

## Context

- See [Not yet specified](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#not-yet-specified) in the seed. The research ticket that blocks this one says which names are free.
- The extension ID is hard to reverse, so this decision probably deserves an ADR.

lastComment.body:
## Answer

Decided with Eduardo on 2026-10-02.

| Name | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Marketplace publisher ID | `dbarjs`. Eduardo created the publisher during this session, so the ID is secured. |
| Extension ID | `dbarjs.hero-synergy` |
| Open VSX namespace | `dbarjs`, because both registries read the same `publisher` field. It can be claimed on its own, since it matches Eduardo's GitHub ID. |
| Extension `name` | `hero-synergy`. The bare name belongs to the extension. |
| Unscoped npm `hero-synergy` | Not claimed. `npx @hero-synergy/cli` already runs the `hero-synergy` bin. |
| Scoped npm names | `@hero-synergy/core` and `@hero-synergy/cli` stand, for whichever of them ships. The organization is Eduardo's. |

Why `dbarjs` and not the brand: it mirrors the repository (`dbarjs/hero-synergy`), it says plainly that a person is behind an unofficial companion, and its Open VSX ownership claim doesn't wait on the Marketplace. The full trade-off, with the rejected options, is in [ADR 0001](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-publish-the-extension-as-dbarjs-hero-synergy.md).

## Changes

- `docs/adr/0001-publish-the-extension-as-dbarjs-hero-synergy.md` records the decision.
- `packages/vscode/package.json` now has `"publisher": "dbarjs"`; the scaffold had hard-coded `hero-synergy`.

## Against the seed

- Appendix A.2's `"publisher": "hero-synergy"` is superseded.
- The Open VSX setup step `npx ovsx create-namespace hero-synergy` becomes `dbarjs`, and the ordering constraint the name research found (Marketplace publisher first) no longer applies.

## Accepted risks

- Someone else may publish an unscoped `hero-synergy` package on npm.
- The extension stays tied to a personal publisher if the project ever moves to an organization.

## Not decided here

The publisher's display name: it can be changed at any time.

20.title: Which registries must be live for v0.1.0 to count as published?
20.body:
## Question

Where must v0.1.0 be installable from on release day?

To decide:

- Which of these are required and which can follow later: the VS Code Marketplace, Open VSX, and a GitHub release with the `.vsix` attached.
- How the seed's release pipeline changes now that the extension is the only published artifact: the npm publish step, the Changesets group and the per-package release notes.

## Context

- See [Releases](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#releases) in the seed: each registry is switched on with a repository variable, and every GitHub release carries the `.vsix` regardless.
- npm is not a candidate: [What ships in v0.1.0 besides the extension?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/4) decided that v0.1.0 publishes nothing to npm, with `@hero-synergy/core` private and the CLI cut.
- Doing the one-time registry setup is out of scope for this map; this ticket only decides which registries the spec must cover.

lastComment.body:
## Answer

Decided with Eduardo on 2026-10-02. v0.1.0 is published when it is installable from **all three** surfaces: the VS Code Marketplace, Open VSX and a GitHub release carrying the `.vsix`. The GitHub release is the one step that can never be skipped; the two registries are targets the release never waits for.

| Surface | Required for v0.1.0 | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub release `v0.1.0` with the `.vsix` attached | Yes, always | Created on every release run once the `.vsix` is built, even if a registry step failed (`if: !cancelled()`). It is the fallback install route. |
| VS Code Marketplace (`dbarjs.hero-synergy`) | Yes | Published through the `marketplace` environment with Entra ID, `vsce publish --packagePath --azure-credential --skip-duplicate`. |
| Open VSX (namespace `dbarjs`) | Yes, with a safety valve | The only route #17 promised the forks. The namespace claim is human-reviewed and the first version must be published by hand with a token before trusted publishing can be registered, so if Open VSX is not switched on when the Release PR is ready, the release ships anyway and v0.1.0 reaches Open VSX through the backfill workflow. |
| npm | No | Ruled out in #4. |

### Pipeline

The spine of the seed's `release.yml` (A.3) was built around npm and goes:

- **No `changesets/action` pack or publish jobs, and no `select-mode`.** The workflow decides on its own: if any `.changeset/*.md` other than `README.md` exists on `main`, run `changesets/action/version@v2` (the **Release hero-synergy** PR); otherwise, if no `v<version>` tag exists for the version in `packages/vscode/package.json`, build, `vsce package`, publish to each registry whose `PUBLISH_*` variable is `true`, then `gh release create v<version>`. Nothing else runs. Reason: `select-mode` says `publish` only while a private package has no `<name>@<version>` git tag, so without Changesets' own tags it would fire on every push to `main` forever.
- **One tag per release, `v<version>`, created by `gh release create`.** Changesets' `hero-synergy@x.y.z` and `@hero-synergy/core@x.y.z` tags are never created. The version is read from `packages/vscode/package.json`, not core.
- **Registries first, release last, release always.** Install links in the notes come from the `PUBLISH_*` variables, not from publish success; every registry step is idempotent (`--skip-duplicate`), so a failed step is rerun, never a reason to withhold the release.
- **A backfill workflow** (`workflow_dispatch`, input: tag) downloads the `.vsix` from that GitHub release and publishes it to every registry that is switched on, reusing the `publish:*` scripts and the `marketplace` environment. It covers Open VSX arriving after a release, a failed registry step, and any registry switched on later.
- **No approval gate** on the `marketplace` environment. Merging the Release PR is the approval; the environment exists to scope the Entra federated credential and the Open VSX trusted publisher.
- **Open VSX's first publish is by hand**, once, with a personal token (the seed's setup step), then trusted publishing is registered, `PUBLISH_OPEN_VSX=true` is set, and the backfill workflow publishes whatever shipped in between. No `OVSX_PAT` secret in CI.

### Changesets and release notes

- The fixed group stays (`@hero-synergy/core` and `hero-synergy` share one version, as the seed decided), but **every changeset names `hero-synergy`**, the package users install. A scout fix lives in core and is a Hero Synergy change in the notes. Changesets still writes `packages/core/CHANGELOG.md` ("No changes in this release.") and `Updated dependencies` lines into the extension's changelog; the first is never linked, the second is stripped by the notes script.
- `scripts/release-notes.ts` stays as a small script (`pnpm release:notes` previews it) and shrinks to one section: title `hero-synergy v<version>`, the extension's changelog entry, an install line with the Marketplace and Open VSX links (each only if its variable is on) and the attached `.vsix`, and the compare link. The `npx @hero-synergy/cli` line goes.

### Marketplace listing

The listing is release work even though the polished README is out of scope (#22). v0.1.0 ships with `categories: ["Other"]` (check whether a better category exists at build time), keywords `claude code`, `wayfinder`, `mattpocock`, `skills`, `agent`, `bugs` and `homepage` pointing at the repo, and a **simple placeholder icon** in the AI Hero spot-illustration spirit, as a build item in the spec, not a map ticket. The real logo arrives with the polished README. vsce 4 does not refuse `"private": true`, treats a missing `repository` or LICENSE as a warning in CI, and does nothing about a missing icon; the Marketplace just shows a grey placeholder.

## Why

- **All three, because each does a different job.** The Marketplace is where VS Code users look, Open VSX is the only route to the forks, and the `.vsix` on the release is what works when neither registry does. None of them costs a release day.
- **The release never waits for a registry** because the `.vsix` is the fallback: a Marketplace hiccup or a slow Open VSX claim leaving users with nothing would defeat the point of attaching it.
- **Own mode detection** because the alternative is three tags per release (`changeset tag` to empty Changesets' publish plan) or a workflow that reruns on every merge. Two shell lines are more legible than an action whose private-package semantics had to be read from source.

## Facts checked (2026-10-02, primary sources)

- `changesets/action/select-mode@v2` returns `publish` only for a non-empty `changeset publish-plan`; private packages enter the plan only as `tag-only` entries for versions without a `<name>@<version>` tag. `changeset pack` with no publishable packages logs "No packages to pack." and uploads an empty artifact.
- A fixed-group member with no changeset of its own is bumped and gets a CHANGELOG entry ("No changes in this release." or `Updated dependencies`).
- Open VSX trusted publishing: "the first version has to be published the ordinary way, with an access token." `ovsx publish --trusted-publishing` and `--skip-duplicate` exist in ovsx 1.2.0.
- `@vscode/vsce` 4.0.0: `publish --packagePath --azure-credential --skip-duplicate` exist; `private: true` is not checked; missing icon is silent.

## Against the seed

- The `[P]` "each registry is switched on with a repository variable" stands; "every GitHub release carries the `.vsix` regardless" is strengthened to "the release always runs".
- A.3 `release.yml`: the `select-mode`, `pack` and `publish` jobs go; the `extension` job no longer gates on `published-packages`; `github-release` no longer requires `needs.extension.result != 'failure'`; the tag is read from `packages/vscode`, not `packages/core`. A new `workflow_dispatch` backfill workflow is added.
- A.6 `release-notes.ts`: one section instead of three, no `npx` install line.
- One-time setup: the npm steps no longer apply (already noted in #4); the Open VSX steps stand with namespace `dbarjs` (#19), and their ordering (hand-publish, register trusted publisher, set the variable) is now a stated constraint rather than an aside.

## Not decided here

- The one-time registry setup itself (Entra identity, Open VSX claim and first publish): out of scope for this map.
- The real icon and the polished listing text: with the README, after the release (#22).
- Whether a coverage gate or any other check blocks the Release PR: the Release PR runs CI like any PR; nothing release-specific.

No glossary change and no ADR: every choice here is a workflow edit or a repository variable away from being reversed.

21.title: How does the Cockpit handle a session's lifecycle?
21.body:
## Question

A ticket has at most one live session, and a session lives in a VS Code terminal that can close, be resumed, or sit at a dialog no hook reports. What does the Cockpit do at each point?

To decide:

- **Resume.** When a ticket's terminal closes, what the Cockpit offers: `claude --resume "<ticket title>"` (which returns to the worktree by itself), a fresh launch, or both; and how the Cockpit tells "ended on purpose" from "terminal died".
- **One live session per ticket.** How the Cockpit holds to it when a ticket is claimed on the tracker but no terminal is open here, or a terminal is open but the tracker shows the ticket unclaimed. Status belongs to the ticket and its terminal, not to a session id, which changes on `/clear`.
- **AFK tickets.** Whether research and AFK task tickets run without a terminal in v0.1.0 (`claude --bg` with `claude attach <id>` later), or always in a terminal. Headless runs never see the worktree exit prompt and leave the worktree in place.
- **Local tracker launch.** The command without `-w`, with file paths in place of URLs.
- **Dialogs no hook reports.** Workspace trust at launch, and the keep-or-remove worktree prompt at `/exit` (accepted as a gap in [How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/5)): what the Cockpit shows while the session sits there.

## Context

- Graduated from the map's fog by [How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/5) and bound by [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md): the Cockpit launches and watches, never runs git or writes to the tracker.
- The status table and the "terminal closing is the truth for ended" rule come from [Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/6).
- See [Sessions](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#sessions) in the seed.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

**A ticket's session is none, starting, live or ended; liveness comes from the Cockpit's terminal and from Claude Code's own session registry; Resume is `--resume <session id>` with the id learned from the status events; every ticket runs in a terminal and `--bg` is cut; performance means VS Code stays responsive and the battery untouched.** Eduardo agreed to all eighteen points on 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-03.

### Decided

1. **Session, redefined.** A Session is one live `claude` process for a ticket or action, in a VS Code terminal, whoever started it. The conversation claude persists is not a Session: it is what Resume takes as an argument. A ticket's session state is **none**, **starting** (a terminal exists, no `SessionStart` yet), **live** (status from the table in [Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/6)) or **ended** (no process, last session id known). A ticket claimed on the tracker with no session and no known id shows as **claimed elsewhere**; its only actions are opening the issue and a fresh launch, which wayfinder accepts for a named ticket.
2. **Liveness has two sources.** The Cockpit's own terminal is its handle when it has one. Claude Code's live-session registry (`claude agents --json`: pid, cwd, session id, `-n` name, `busy|idle|waiting`) decides liveness for everything else: hand-started sessions, sessions in another window, and a process that exited non-zero while VS Code keeps the pane open with an exit alert, where `onDidCloseTerminal` never fires. The files under `~/.claude/sessions/` are never parsed: a watcher on that directory is the trigger, the documented command is the reader, debounced one second or more.
3. **The name is the key.** Session names are `#<number> <title>`; a session matches a ticket by the leading `#<number>` within the repo. It holds on both trackers, survives `/clear` (the id changes, the name doesn't) and matches hand-started sessions that follow the convention, which the README states. Claude renames a second live session with the same name to `<name>-<two words>`, so the prefix still matches; the Cockpit shows both under the ticket with a warning and kills nothing. The worktree path is corroboration in the focus pane, never the key.
4. **One live session per ticket.** While a ticket is starting or live its only action is "focus terminal" (none when the live session isn't one of the Cockpit's terminals). The Cockpit never launches a second.
5. **Ended is one state.** Its detail is text, in order of trust: the `SessionEnd` reason (`prompt_input_exit` → "exited", `logout`, `other`); else the terminal's `exitStatus` (`User` → "terminal closed", `Shutdown` → "window closed", `Process` with a non-zero code → "exited with code N"); else "process gone" when only the registry noticed. `clear` and `resume` reasons never end a ticket: the next `SessionStart` in the same terminal carries the new id. No separate crashed state, and the actions don't branch on the detail.
6. **Resume is by id.** The id is the `session_id` of the ticket's last status event; nothing is passed at launch (`--session-id` is not used), so `/clear` tracking comes for free. The command runs in a fresh terminal from the workspace root with `HERO_SYNERGY_*` set again: `claude --resume <uuid> -n "#21 <title>" --plugin-dir <ext>/claude-plugin`. Claude returns to the worktree by itself; `--plugin-dir` is not restored by claude, so the Cockpit passes it again. With no known id the action is **Resume by name**, labelled so: `claude --resume "#21 <title>"`, resolved by claude (exact match resumes, an ambiguous one opens its picker).
7. **Ended actions**: Resume first, Launch fresh second, both with their command shown, no confirmation. Launch fresh is the plain Work ticket command; `-w <slug>` reopens an existing worktree.
8. **Reload and close.** On activation the Cockpit adopts any terminal whose name starts with `#<number>` as that ticket's terminal (claude sets the terminal title to the `-n` name; VS Code keeps the processes alive across a reload but hands back no env or args), and the registry confirms it is live. A ticket with no live match whose last event isn't `SessionEnd` becomes ended with "window closed". Cockpit terminals are neither `isTransient` nor `hideFromUser`.
9. **Live with no events** (hand-started, or the plugin failed to load): shown as "live · <registry word>", unmapped. Mapping `busy/idle/waiting` onto the status table belongs to [When the scout and the status hooks disagree, which does the Cockpit believe?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/28).
10. **No `--bg` in v0.1.0.** Every ticket, AFK or HITL, runs in a terminal; an AFK ticket is a terminal you don't have to watch. The Cockpit never starts one on its own (principle 3).
11. **Local tracker launch**: `claude -n "#NN <title>" --plugin-dir <ext>/claude-plugin "/wayfinder .scratch/<effort>/map.md .scratch/<effort>/issues/NN-<slug>.md"`, without `-w`, cwd the workspace root, paths relative to it, `NN` from the file prefix. The ticket shows the note from [How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/5) that sessions share the checkout.
12. **Dialogs no hook reports.** Starting shows its age and, after 15 s without `SessionStart`, a hint: "no status yet, the session may be waiting at a prompt, open the terminal". The keep-or-remove prompt at `/exit` stays under the last event, "waiting for you", with its age. No terminal scraping. The Cockpit never edits `hasTrustDialogAccepted` in claude's config.
13. **Starting counts as live** for point 4.
14. **The events file** is read incrementally by byte offset (one full read at activation) and compacted by the Cockpit above a size cap, keeping the last event per ticket. It lives in extension storage and persists across restarts, because it is a ticket's only memory of its last session id. The exact path is a spec detail.
15. **Performance bar**: VS Code's perceived responsiveness and the battery, not latency numbers. Nothing lifecycle-related on the UI path; activation renders stored state and spawns nothing until a trigger fires; every read and spawn is async in the extension host; no polling timers (every refresh has a cause: a terminal event, a status event, a registry change, window focus, the view shown); spawns debounced one second or more; the only timer is the one 15 s timeout per launch. Soft targets for the spec: a status change or an ending visible within about a second.
16. **Hidden Cockpit**: the terminal and status-event listeners stay on (they are pushed and keep the ended record right for Resume); the registry watcher stops and nothing is spawned; one refresh when the view is shown.
17. **AFK tickets launch exactly like HITL ones**; the only difference is the type icon from [How do maps render in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/7).
18. **Ticket, terminal, not session id**: all state is keyed on the ticket and its terminal, as [Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/6) asked.

### Facts that shaped it

- `claude agents --json` lists every live session (interactive and background) without a TTY: `pid, cwd, kind, startedAt, sessionId, name, status`. Measured here at 100 to 200 ms. Backed by `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`, undocumented, with stale files for dead pids left behind. The docs say to read session state through the command, not the files.
- `--resume <uuid>` works from any cwd and keeps the id; `--resume <name>` resolves within the repo and its worktrees, exact match resumes, ambiguous opens the picker. A resumed worktree session returns to its worktree. `--plugin-dir`, `--mcp-config`, `--settings` and `--add-dir` are not restored on resume. `SessionStart` fires with `resume`; `--fork-session` gets `fork` and a new id. ([sessions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md), [worktrees](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md))
- A live interactive session started with a `-n` name another live session uses is renamed `<name>-<two words>` (2.1.232+).
- A **named** `-w` session always prompts keep-or-remove on exit, clean or not; unnamed clean ones are removed silently; no setting suppresses it. On keep, claude prints `claude --worktree <name> --resume`. A killed process leaves the worktree in place.
- Workspace trust is keyed on the repository root, so a worktree never re-triggers the dialog; `-w` in an untrusted repo exits with an error. The only non-interactive acceptance is editing `projects.<root>.hasTrustDialogAccepted` in claude's config (here `~/.claude/.claude.json`). Hooks from settings files are held back until trust is accepted. ([permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md))
- `--bg`: cannot be combined with `-p`; `-w` with `--bg` is undocumented; hooks in a background session are undocumented; a background session that edits files commits, pushes its own branch and opens a draft PR on finish, the opposite of the push-to-`main` routine; `claude rm` deletes its worktree. ([agent view](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view.md))
- `SessionEnd` reasons: `clear`, `resume`, `logout`, `prompt_input_exit`, `other`; 1.5 s default budget. Nothing in the hooks doc covers SIGHUP or `kill -9`. ([hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md))
- VS Code: `TerminalExitStatus { code, reason: Unknown | Shutdown | Process | User | Extension }`; the trash icon gives `User` with no code. A window reload keeps terminal processes (`terminal.integrated.enablePersistentSessions`, unless `isTransient`) and rebuilds `Terminal` objects with the name but without `env`, `shellPath` or `shellArgs`; a window close kills them with `Shutdown`. No API signals that a running process waits on input. (`vscode.d.ts`, `terminalService.ts`)
- `claude` as the terminal's own process (decided in [Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/17)) means a non-zero exit leaves the pane open with an exit alert and no close event.

### Handed to #28

Three facts for [When the scout and the status hooks disagree, which does the Cockpit believe?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/28): the ticket states above, the registry as a liveness source with its own `busy|idle|waiting` word, and the name match. The registry's documented `waitingFor` values (`permission prompt`, `input needed`, `dialog open`) are confirmed for background sessions only; if they fire for interactive ones, they close the dialog and Esc gaps without scraping.

### Out of scope

`claude --bg` with `claude attach` for AFK tickets, for v0.1.0.

### Recorded

The **Session** term in [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md) and a relationship line, pushed to `main` together with the stranded [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md) commit from #5. No ADR: nothing here is hard to reverse.

22.title: The front door: READMEs, Marketplace listing and repository cards
22.body:
## Destination

Every place where someone first meets Hero Synergy is finished and live: the repository page on GitHub (the README with the trailer playing, the About box with its website and topics), the card a shared link unfolds into, the pin on Eduardo's profile, and the VS Code Marketplace page and Extensions view (the listing README, description, category and keywords) through a published release. Each one says what Hero Synergy is in one line, shows the real Cockpit, and takes a reader from install to their first ticket session.

## Notes

- **This map carries execution**, as [#64 next, the terminal pre-alpha of the Cockpit](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/64) does. Research and grilling settle the facts and the words. The prototype drafts the READMEs on a `prototype/<name>` branch for Eduardo to react to. Tasks do the work and end on `main`, in a release or in the repository's settings.
- **Origin.** Converted on 2026-10-09 from Eduardo's wish of 2026-10-02, which the conversion comment below keeps: a beautiful, sophisticated README for the extension and for the repository, with a logo and screenshots of the Cockpit. Since then v0.1.0 and v0.1.1 have shipped to the Marketplace with plain READMEs, the logo has become the Wayfinder Seal, and a 30-second trailer has been made. The scope grew from two READMEs to every first impression.
- **Settled inputs.** The logo, its files, colors and rules are in [`docs/brand.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/brand.md). The vocabulary is in [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md). The READMEs describe the product as shipped, never what is planned. The art reference is still the one in Eduardo's comment of 2026-10-02 below.
- **The trailer.** `hero-synergy-30s.mp4` is 30 seconds of 1920 × 1080 at 60 fps with stereo sound, 24.5 MB, at `/tmp/hero-synergy-30s.mp4` in the devcontainer. Its source is not in the repository. Its beats are "One giant map.", "Too many terminals.", "Which one needs you?", the Seal, "See the frontier.", "One click. One named session.", "Live status for every session." and "Close one. Unblock the rest.". It ends on "A hero with this many skills needs synergy." Three things in it differ from the product:
  - Its Cockpit is a stylized board of Decided, Frontier and Blocked columns. The shipped Cockpit is the Tree, the Focus pane and the Detail.
  - Its outro reads "VS Code extension + CLI", and no CLI ships.
  - The command it types, `claude -n "Define the snapshot schema" -w define-snapshot-schema "/wayfinder #1 #12"`, names the session without its number. The shipped Work ticket runs `claude -n "#<number> <title>" -w <number> …`, and the Cockpit matches a session to its ticket by that leading number. [#115 How do the best developer-tool READMEs and extension listings open?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/115) found this one.
- **Honesty.** Screenshots come from the running extension, never from a mockup shown as the UI. Every claim holds for the release it ships in. Both READMEs keep the line that Hero Synergy is unofficial and not affiliated with or endorsed by Matt Pocock or Anthropic.
- **Where things land.** The listing README is `packages/vscode/README.md`. The Marketplace, the Extensions view and, later, Open VSX all show it, and it reaches the Marketplace only through a release. README, manifest and media changes go through a PR with a changeset, merged once `check`, `vscode (linux)` and `vscode (macos)` are green. Glossary and ADR edits follow the routine in `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Skills.** Grilling tickets use `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling`. Prototypes use `/prototype`. Research tickets use `/research` and save findings as `docs/research/<name>.md` on a `research/<name>` branch.
- **Issue numbers.** Every ticket and map is shown as `#number title`.
- **Driver.** Eduardo (`dbarjs`). A claim is an assignment to him.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket: the gist, then the link -->
- [How do the best developer-tool READMEs and extension listings open?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/115) — lead with the wayfinder map and its frontier, since GitLens Pro and three neighbours already sell live Claude Code sessions; one reused line that works in its first 40 characters; the trailer only on GitHub, captioned as stylized beside real screenshots, with its CLI outro and unnumbered session command fixed; listing images absolute, tag-pinned and badge-free
- [What do the VS Code Marketplace page and the Extensions view accept?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/114) — vsce ignores `repository.directory`, so listing README links must be absolute `https://` URLs pinned to the release; the Marketplace strips `<picture>`, `srcset`, `<kbd>` and a video's `muted` (an autoplay video plays with sound for visitors from search), while GIF, animated WebP and APNG play everywhere; descriptions show about 37 characters in VS Code's list and 78 on search tiles; `AI` is a valid category; keywords cap at 30; README media under `media/` ships in the VSIX; verification can't start before 2027-04-09
- [What do the GitHub repository page, its link preview and a profile pin accept?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/113) — only an uploaded `user-attachments` video alone on its line plays in a README (muted, no autoplay, capped at 10 MB on a free plan against the 24.5 MB trailer), `<video>` and `srcset` lists are stripped, the description shows whole up to 140 characters in search and 200 on a pin, the social card is a PNG or JPG under 1 MB at 1280 × 640 that only the browser can set, like the pins and home-page sections, and `hero-synergy` is already pinned first
- [Capture the real Cockpit in screenshots and a loop](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/116) — `vp run capture` takes every shot and a 9-second ▶-to-waiting loop (GIF, WebP, MP4, all under 300 KB) from the installed VSIX on a demo local map; the macOS set on `prototype/screenshots` is the one to keep; the terminal is empty and a local map shows no `-w`
- [What does Hero Synergy say about itself?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/117) — written for someone already on `/wayfinder`; one line everywhere, "See your wayfinder frontier and start each ticket as a named Claude Code session, with live status."; one shared opening paragraph that says unofficial and links Matt Pocock's skills and Claude Code; today's disclaimer kept; the trailer's three beats as the repository README's why; the tagline only as a sign-off and on the social card; category `AI`, `preview` while 0.x, 14 keywords, 8 topics, the About website pointing at the listing
- [Cut the trailer for the web](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/118) — `front-door-media/make.sh` on `prototype/front-door-media` remakes everything: a 9.4 MB 1080p60 README video with sound at `/tmp/hero-synergy-readme.mp4`, out of git and still carrying the trailer's three differences; a title-card poster; Seal, title and outro social cards at 1280 × 640 under 1 MB, the outro cut above its "+ CLI" footer; 4:1 and 3:1 title banners at device scale 2, where the JPGs are the ones to use
- [Prototype the two READMEs and the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/119) — drafts on `prototype/readme`: the repository README opens on the 3:1 banner, version and licence badges, then the trailer, the real window and the problem, with the trailer's four beats as headings over real shots and a Mermaid "How it works"; the listing opens on the Tree with live statuses, which reads at listing width where the whole window doesn't, and runs from install to the first ticket session; the trailer is cut to 15.5 s, which drops all three differences so it needs no caption; the social card is `card-outro.png`; media live in `docs/media/`, outside the VSIX
- [When does the capture run again, and how do new shots reach the READMEs?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/128) — Capture also runs on PRs that touch the Cockpit's UI, never in the release; the shots it outdates are refreshed in that same PR by hand with `vp run refresh-media` (the macOS artifact into `docs/media/`), with no bot PR; the capture makes `badge-icon.png` too; stale shots are noticed in the job summary, never failed, except by a test that every referenced file exists; the 1440 × 676 macOS window is kept
- [Upload the trailer, fill in the About box, set the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/120) — the 15.5 s cut is uploaded as `user-attachments/assets/e1d5cc19-…` for the README to embed; the About box shows the one line, the listing as its website and the 8 topics; `card-outro.png` is the live social preview; Releases is the only home-page section
- [Does the repository page need community files?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/146) — three, all in `.github/` and shipped in the release PR: a bug report form labelled `needs-triage` (blank issues stay allowed), a four-line `CONTRIBUTING.md` that links the README's Developing section, and a `SECURITY.md` that points at private vulnerability reporting, turned on first; no PR template or code of conduct; the README doesn't link them; `"qna": false` drops the Marketplace's Q & A tab
- [Land the front door and release it](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/121) — shipped as [v0.1.3](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/releases/tag/v0.1.3) through [#152](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/152) and the Release PR. The trailer plays on the repository page; the Marketplace serves the new listing byte for byte, under `AI`, as preview, with no Q & A. Listing images are pinned to `v0.1.3`, and a test keeps them on a tag. The card and the pin are live, and Community Standards ticks the form and both files. The REST community profile still reports `issue_template: null` for a YAML form
- [#149 Re-take the README shots when the Cockpit changes](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/149) — merged in [#157](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/157). Capture now runs on PRs that change the Cockpit's UI, shoots `badge-icon.png` itself, and summarises the six kept files. `vp run refresh-media` copies them from the branch's latest `capture-macos` artifact into `docs/media/`, and a unit test fails when a README references a missing `docs/media/` file

## Not yet specified

Nothing left. The last patch, whether the v0.1.0 release notes get the Marketplace link, was settled on 2026-11-16: they do, so [v0.1.0](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/releases/tag/v0.1.0)'s install line now reads like v0.1.1 to v0.1.3. Open VSX, out of scope here, is tracked in [#186 Publish to Open VSX](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/186).

## Out of scope

- Publishing to Open VSX. The registry setup carries on separately, and the listing README serves Open VSX unchanged.
- Product work: changing the Cockpit for a screenshot or to match the trailer, or a first-run walkthrough inside VS Code. That belongs to its own map.
- New brand work. The logo, its colors and its rules are fixed in `docs/brand.md`.
- Verifying the publisher `dbarjs` on the Marketplace. It cannot start before 2027-04-09, and it needs a domain registered for at least six months, as [#114 What do the VS Code Marketplace page and the Extensions view accept?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/114) found.
- A website, docs site or landing page beyond the repository page.
- Announcing Hero Synergy: posts, threads, newsletters, or asking to be listed anywhere. This map ends when the front door is ready to be found.

## Destination reached

All 12 tickets are closed, and the last patch in Not yet specified is settled: [v0.1.0](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/releases/tag/v0.1.0)'s release notes got the Marketplace link today, like v0.1.1 to v0.1.3.

Checked live on 2026-11-16: the README plays the trailer; the About box has the one line, the listing as its website and the 8 topics; `card-outro.png` is the social preview; `hero-synergy` is pinned first on the profile; the Marketplace serves the v0.1.3 listing.

Open VSX stays out of scope here and is now tracked in [#186 Publish to Open VSX](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/186).

23.title: Where does the Cockpit live: sidebar, editor tab, or both?
23.body:
## Question

Does the Cockpit open as a sidebar view, as an editor tab, or both, and if both, which one is the default?

## Context

- [How do maps render in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/7) decided a tree of maps with a focus pane, built once for two widths: the pane beside the tree at editor-tab width, inline under the clicked row at sidebar width. The prototype on [`prototype/map-rendering`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/tree/prototype/map-rendering/packages/vscode/webview/src/prototype) shows both (`?variant=M4&width=sidebar` and `&width=panel`).
- A sidebar view is always one click away and sits next to the terminal panel; an editor tab gives the two-pane layout room but competes with files.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

**Both: a side view (the Tree) and an editor tab (the Detail), one Vue bundle, one selection.** Eduardo decided it on 2026-10-03 in a grilling session. It revises point 4 of [How do maps render in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/7): the two widths stay one component, but the sidebar variant shrinks and the editor variant drops the tree.

### Decided

1. **The Tree** is a webview view in its own Activity Bar container, `Hero Synergy`. The user can drag it to the secondary side bar or the Panel; it is not contributed to the secondary side bar by default, because that contribution point is finalized only in VS Code 1.106 and the floor is `^1.105.0`. It shows the tree of maps from #7 with a compact **Focus pane** under the selected row: type and HITL/AFK, state and claim, the live session's status and time since its last status event, the **Work ticket** action with its exact command, the title linking to the issue, and an **↗ Open** button. A closed ticket gets the same pane plus the first line of its decision gist. The ⚑ Map row's pane shows the destination line and the counts. The Tree draws its own empty state (`viewsWelcome` applies to tree views only).
2. **The Detail** is one webview panel, detail only (no tree), titled `#n title` and reused: it follows the Tree's selection. It opens from ↗, a double-click, Enter, or `Hero Synergy: Open Cockpit Detail` (which shows the current selection, or the first map in order when nothing is selected). For a ticket: the header, the two-column neighbourhood "Waits on → Clears the way for", the issue body rendered as Markdown, and the resolution comment when closed; no comment thread. For a map: destination, decisions so far, fog and out of scope. The ≋ Fog and ✓ Decisions rows open the map's Detail scrolled to that section. Webview panels always open pinned, so no preview-tab behaviour.
3. **One selection, mirrored both ways.** The extension host holds it; clicking a neighbour or a listed ticket in the Detail selects it in the Tree and unfolds its map.
4. **Badge**: the number of sessions that need you, nothing else. It renders on whichever container hosts the Tree. What counts as "needs you" is [How does the Cockpit handle a session's lifecycle?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/21)'s to define.
5. **Activation**: `workspaceContains:docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` and `onView:<tree view id>`, so the badge and the scout run before the Tree is first opened.
6. **State**: `retainContextWhenHidden` on both webviews; expanded maps and the selection persist in `workspaceState`; a `WebviewPanelSerializer` restores the Detail after a reload on the same selection.
7. **Session terminals** open in the Panel by default, with a setting `heroSynergy.sessions.terminalLocation: panel | editor`. That is the API's whole range: a terminal cannot be created in a side bar.
8. **Names**, in the glossary (commit [`6042232`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/commit/6042232)): **Cockpit** widened to the whole UI; **Tree**, **Detail** and **Focus pane** added; _avoid_ "sidebar" and "panel" as terms since VS Code lets the Tree live in either.

No ADR: two webview hosts sharing one bundle and one selection is reversible and unsurprising, and the trade-off is recorded here.

### What this changes elsewhere

- [What does the snapshot hold for a map and a ticket?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/26): the snapshot must carry issue bodies and, for closed tickets, the resolution comment.
- [How does the Cockpit handle a session's lifecycle?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/21): defines the "needs you" states the badge counts; inherits the terminal-location setting.
- [How are actions placed and named in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/24): **Work ticket** appears in the Focus pane and in the Detail; **↗ Open** and the palette command are not Actions (no skill behind them).
- For the spec: the scaffold installed `@types/vscode@1.100.0`, while [Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/17) decided `~1.105.0`.

### Facts verified during the session

Against `@types/vscode` and the VS Code source at tags 1.105.0 and 1.106.0: `secondarySidebar` view containers are proposed in 1.105 (`contribSecondarySidebar`) and finalized in 1.106; `WebviewView.badge` exists and follows the view's container; `retainContextWhenHidden`, `visible`, `onDidChangeVisibility` and `show()` exist on webview views; `TerminalLocation` is `Panel | Editor` only; `createWebviewPanel` always opens a pinned editor and `WebviewPanelSerializer` restores it; `<viewId>.focus` is registered for every contributed view; `viewsWelcome` is tree-views only.

25.title: Do the two test runners coexist under Vite+?
25.body:
## Question

Do the two test runners decided in [How is the extension tested?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/18) coexist under Vite+: a second `pack` entry bundling Mocha tests to CommonJS that `vscode-test` loads, and a Vitest `e2e` project launching VS Code through `playwright._electron`, both started by `vp` commands?

This is a task ticket (AFK), like the `@effect/vitest` spike. On a throwaway `task/test-runners` branch, not for `main`:

- Add `@vscode/test-cli`, `@vscode/test-electron`, `@types/mocha` and `playwright` to `packages/vscode`.
- Write one host test (the extension activates) and one end-to-end test (the window opens with the extension loaded).
- Run `vp run --filter hero-synergy test:integration` under `xvfb-run -a` on the floor (`1.105.0`) and stable, and `vp test --project e2e`.
- Confirm `vp test` alone does not launch VS Code, and that `vp pack` leaves `out-test/` alone.

Record: whether `vp pack` with an array `pack` block produces `.cjs` test files that `vscode-test` loads; whether ESM test files load in the host; the Node version inside the host on each build; timings; any override or peer-dependency warning; anything in the research's sketch that turned out wrong.

## Context

- Decided in [How is the extension tested?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/18) and [ADR 0004](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-extension-host-tests-run-on-mocha-beside-vitest.md).
- The research, [How can a VS Code extension be integration-tested under Vite+?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/13), was reading only; its config sketches are in [`docs/research/extension-integration-testing.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/extension-integration-testing/docs/research/extension-integration-testing.md).
- The seed's "use `vp` for everything" rule now covers both runners; see the map's Notes.

lastComment.body:
## Answer

**Yes.** Both runners coexist under Vite+ 1.0.0, each behind a `vp` command, and `vp test` alone never launches VS Code. One `pack` call emits the extension and the Mocha tests, `vscode-test` loads the CommonJS bundle on the floor and on stable, and a Vitest `e2e` project drives VS Code through `playwright._electron`. Everything the research sketched held except four details, listed under **Wrong in the sketch**.

### What was done

On the throwaway branch [`task/test-runners`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/tree/task/test-runners) (commit [5de11d4](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/commit/5de11d4), not for `main`), in this arm64 Linux devcontainer on Node 26.10 and pnpm 12.8.1:

- `packages/vscode`: `@vscode/test-cli` 0.0.15, `@vscode/test-electron` 3.1.0, `@types/mocha` 10.0.10 and `playwright` 1.63.0 as devDependencies; `engines.vscode` and `@types/vscode` moved to the decided `^1.105.0` floor; `activationEvents: ["onStartupFinished"]` so the e2e test can see the extension running.
- [`packages/vscode/vite.config.ts`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/task/test-runners/packages/vscode/vite.config.ts): `pack` as an array — `src/extension.ts` to `dist/` and `test/integration/**/*.test.ts` to `out-test/`, both CommonJS with `vscode` and `mocha` external, plus a spike-only ESM entry to `out-test-esm/`.
- [root `vite.config.ts`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/task/test-runners/vite.config.ts): Vitest `projects` — `unit` (everything, minus the Mocha and e2e folders and the build outputs) and `e2e` (`root: packages/vscode`, `retry: 1`, 120 s test timeout, no file parallelism).
- [`.vscode-test.mjs`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/task/test-runners/packages/vscode/.vscode-test.mjs): labels `floor` (`1.105.0`) and `stable`, `bdd`, 20 s timeout, `--disable-extensions`, a short `--user-data-dir`, the fixture workspace.
- [`test/integration/extension.test.ts`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/task/test-runners/packages/vscode/test/integration/extension.test.ts): the extension activates; logs the host's VS Code, Electron and Node versions. [`test/e2e/window.test.ts`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/task/test-runners/packages/vscode/test/e2e/window.test.ts): downloads VS Code into the shared cache, launches it with Playwright, opens *Developer: Show Running Extensions* and finds `dbarjs.hero-synergy`.
- Script: `"test:integration": "vp pack && vscode-test"`.

### Result

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `xvfb-run -a vp run --filter hero-synergy test:integration` | **floor 1.105.0: 2 passing; stable 1.140.0: 2 passing.** 2 min 14 s the first time (downloads: 150 MB for 1.105.0, 323 MB for 1.140.0, linux-arm64), 18.6 s on the first cached run, **6.3 s warm** for both builds including the pack |
| `xvfb-run -a vp test --project e2e` | **1 passed, 6.35 s warm**; VS Code resolved from cache in 0.4 to 0.7 s, window up in 0.9 to 1.3 s |
| `vp test` (no flags) | 1 file, 120 ms, `unit` only — no VS Code |
| `vp test --project unit` | same |
| `vp pack` | `dist/extension.cjs` 0.45 kB and `out-test/extension.test.cjs` 1.86 kB in 18 ms |
| `vp check`, `vp run -r build`, `vp run --filter hero-synergy typecheck` | pass; `vp check` type-checks the two test folders (14 files) with no `@types/mocha` leak |
| ESM test files (`out-test-esm/*.test.mjs`) | **stable 1.140.0: 2 passing. Floor 1.105.0: the extension host goes unresponsive** (`UNRESPONSIVE extension host: starting to profile NOW`) and never exits; killed after 10 minutes |
| `vsce ls --no-dependencies` | `LICENSE`, `package.json`, `dist/extension.cjs` — `out-test/` stays out of the VSIX through `files` |
| `pnpm install` | no peer or override warning; one `vitest` (5.0.1) and one `mocha` (11.8.0, from `@vscode/test-cli`); the only new deprecation notice is `glob@10.5.0` under Mocha |

Node inside the host, measured: **1.105.0 → Electron 37.6.0, Node 22.19.0; 1.140.0 → Electron 43.7.3, Node 24.21.0.**

### Facts later tickets can rely on

1. **The array `pack` block works and each entry cleans its own `outDir`.** Stray files in `dist/`, `dist/webview/` and `out-test/` were all removed by one `vp pack` ("Cleaning 6 files"). So `vp pack` also empties `dist/webview`: the `build` script's order `vp pack && vp build` matters, and `test:integration` leaves `dist/webview` empty until the next `vp build`. `out-test/` is owned and rewritten by the second entry, never touched by the first, never shipped.
2. **Mocha files must be kept out of the `unit` project explicitly.** Vitest's default include is `**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)` from the root, which also matches the *compiled* `out-test*/**/*.test.cjs|mjs`; a Mocha file under Vitest fails on `describe` being undefined. The exclude list that works: `packages/vscode/test/integration/**`, `packages/vscode/test/e2e/**`, `**/out-test*/**`, `**/.vscode-test/**`, plus `node_modules` and `dist`.
3. **`e2e` is opt-in by construction.** Vitest 5 has no "excluded unless named" project, so the root config lists `e2e` only when `process.argv` carries `-p`/`--project` (Vite+ loads the config in the same process, so the flag is visible). `vp test` → `unit`; `vp test --project e2e` → `e2e`; `vp test --project unit` → `unit`.
4. **Run `vp test` from the repo root.** From `packages/vscode` Vitest 5 reads that package's `vite.config.ts` (rooted at `webview`), finds no tests and exits 1.
5. **Target Node 22 for the host bundles and stay CommonJS.** The floor's Node is 22.19 (the research's 20.19 was for 1.100). ESM test files are a hang on the floor, not an error, so a CI job would run to its timeout.
6. **Pass a short `--user-data-dir`.** The CLI's default is `.vscode-test/user-data` under the package; Electron's IPC socket lives there and Unix caps socket paths at 107 characters. In this worktree both builds failed to start (`ENOENT`/`EINVAL` on `1.14-main.sock`) until `launchArgs` carried `--user-data-dir=<os.tmpdir()>/hero-synergy-vscode-test`, which the CLI honours. A `claude -w` worktree under `.claude/worktrees/<name>` lands near 100 characters, so this belongs in the config, not in CI only. The e2e test gives Playwright its own `--user-data-dir` and `--extensions-dir` in a `mkdtemp`.
7. **One download cache.** `vscode-test` caches in `packages/vscode/.vscode-test/` (next to its config). The e2e test must pass `cachePath` explicitly, because Vitest's cwd is the repo root; with `path.join(extensionDir, '.vscode-test')` both tiers share the same `vscode-linux-arm64-1.140.0`. Both directories are gitignored, and `vp check` skips gitignored paths (the un-ignored `out-test-esm` was flagged until ignored).
8. **Per-folder tsconfigs are enough.** `test/integration/tsconfig.json` with `types: ["mocha", "node", "vscode"]` and `test/e2e/tsconfig.json` with `types: ["node"]`, each `include: ["*.ts"]`; `vp check` picks them up and passes.
9. **`.vscode-test.mjs` takes an array with labels**; `vscode-test` runs every label by default and `--label floor` selects one. Glob entries work for `pack` (`test/integration/**/*.test.ts` → `out-test/extension.test.cjs`).
10. **Playwright specifics.** `_electron.launch` with the `@vscode/test-electron` executable and `--extensionDevelopmentPath`, `--disable-extensions`, `--disable-workspace-trust`, `--disable-updates`, `--skip-welcome`, `--skip-release-notes`, `--no-sandbox`, `--disable-gpu-sandbox` and the workspace path. `--disable-extensions` keeps the development extension. Running Extensions lists it by **ID** (`dbarjs.hero-synergy`), not display name. The first key press after `.monaco-workbench` appears is lost before the workbench takes focus, so the test presses F1 until `.quick-input-widget` is visible; `retry: 1` did not rescue the naive version. `playwright` installs without browsers and `_electron` needs none (whether `playwright-core` alone suffices was not tried).
11. **Dependency hygiene.** `pnpm add pkg@x.y.z` writes exact pins; the spec should use ranges. No override needed anywhere.
12. **This devcontainer** needed `sudo apt-get install xauth libgtk-3-0t64` before `xvfb-run` would start VS Code (`xvfb-run: error: xauth command not found`); GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` image has both.

### Wrong in the sketch

- The floor's Node is 22, not 20 (the floor moved to 1.105.0 after the research).
- The default user-data dir breaks in a deep worktree; the sketch had no `--user-data-dir`.
- The e2e test cannot rely on the cwd for `cachePath`.
- "`out-test/` is left alone by `vp pack`" is half true: the extension's entry never touches it, but the tests' own entry cleans and rewrites it on every pack — which is what we want.

### What this unblocks

`/to-spec` can take the two-runner layout as proven, with the four corrections above and the `--project` gating written in. [ADR 0004](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-extension-host-tests-run-on-mocha-beside-vitest.md) now carries the measured Node versions, the ESM hang, the opt-in `e2e` project and the short user-data dir. No new ticket or fog comes out of this.
