26.title: What does the snapshot hold for a map and a ticket?
26.body:
## Question

Which fields does the snapshot carry for each map and each ticket, and which of them are facts the tracker reports (state, parent, blockers, assignees) rather than something the scout read out of a body?

It has to fit both trackers: on GitHub a ticket is an issue with a URL and a claim is a person; on the local markdown tracker a ticket is a file path and a claim is a `Status: claimed` line that names nobody. It also has to carry drift warnings per map and per ticket, since the scout reads with code and shows anything it cannot read as drift.

## Context

- Decided in [Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/16): the scout is code only. The prototype's code reading on `prototype/scout` (`packages/core/scout-prototype/scout.mjs`, functions `parseMap`, `parseTicket`, `reconcile`) is a first draft of the fields.
- The drift catalogue: [Which wayfinder conventions exist in the wild?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/10).
- Effect Schema models the snapshot ([ADR 0002](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-effect-schema-models-all-boundary-data.md)); the webview imports its types only.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

**The snapshot is tracker-only and nested per map. It holds three kinds of value: facts the tracker reports, sections code reads from bodies, and coded drift warnings. It holds nothing derived and nothing about sessions.** Decided with Eduardo on 2026-10-06 in two grilling rounds; every recommendation stood.

### Shape

```ts
Snapshot {
  tracker: { kind: 'github', owner, repo } | { kind: 'local' }
  repoRoot: string
  collectedAt: string                 // ISO
  maps: WayfinderMap[]                // tracker order; display order is derived
  unmapped: Ticket[]                  // tickets with no map, each with a `no-map` warning
  warnings: Warning[]
}

WayfinderMap {
  number, title, ref                  // fact
  body: string                        // fact: raw Markdown, rendered by the Detail
  tickets: Ticket[]                   // fact: map order (sub-issue order / file number)
  destination: string | null          // read
  notes: string | null                // read
  decisions: { number: number | null, title: string, link: string, gist: string }[]   // read
  notYetSpecified: { text: string, tickets: number[] }[]   // read, addressed by index
  outOfScope: { text: string, tickets: number[] }[]        // read
  warnings: Warning[]
}

Ticket {
  number, title, ref                  // fact
  state: 'open' | 'closed'            // fact: issue state / `Status: resolved`
  type: 'research' | 'prototype' | 'grilling' | 'task' | null   // fact: label / `Type:` line
  claim: { by: string[] } | null      // fact: assignees / `Status: claimed` (empty `by`)
  blockedBy: Blocker[]                // fact: native dependencies / `Blocked by:` line
  body: string                        // fact: raw Markdown
  resolution: { body: string, author: string | null, at: string | null } | null   // read: last comment / `## Answer`
  outcome: 'decided' | 'out-of-scope' | 'unrecorded' | null   // read against the map; null while open
  gist: string | null                 // read: the map's Decisions-so-far line for this ticket, verbatim
  warnings: Warning[]
}

Ref     = { tracker: 'github', url: string } | { tracker: 'local', path: string }   // path is repo-relative
Blocker = { number: number, title: string, state: 'open' | 'closed', ref: Ref }
Warning = { code: WarningCode, detail?: string }
```

### Decided

1. **Identity** is a shared `number` and `title` on both trackers (the "issue numbers everywhere" rule) plus a tagged `ref` that says how to open and launch it: a URL on GitHub, a repo-relative path on a local tracker. A local ticket's `number` is its `NN` file prefix.
2. **Nested, not flat.** Tickets live under their map in map order. A ticket with no map (no native parent, no task-list entry, no `Part of` line) goes to `unmapped` with a `no-map` warning. Nothing is dropped.
3. **Facts versus reads.** Facts: number, title, ref, state, type, claim, parent and order, blockers, body. Reads: the map's five sections, the ticket's resolution, outcome and gist. The scout never guesses a read; what it cannot parse is `null` plus a warning.
4. **Provenance is a warning, not a field.** The prototype's `mapVia` and per-blocker `via` go. A value that arrived through a text fallback (`Part of #n`, a task list, `Blocked by:`) stands as a plain value with a drift warning, since v0.1.0 does not promise the fallbacks ([Which trackers and workspace shapes does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/3)).
5. **Bodies are stored raw** for both maps and tickets, because the Detail renders them as Markdown ([Where does the Cockpit live: sidebar, editor tab, or both?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/23)). Maps also carry all five sections parsed: destination and fog feed the Tree, decisions and out of scope feed the outcome, notes is cheap. Tickets carry no `question` or `summary` field; a missing `## Question` is still a warning.
6. **Resolution** is the last comment (the `## Answer` section locally), with `author` and `at` null where the tracker has none. A closed ticket with no comment gets `closed-no-resolution`.
7. **Gist** is the map's own Decisions-so-far line for the ticket, verbatim, with no computed fallback: that line was written by a human for exactly this purpose.
8. **Outcome** classifies a closed ticket by the map: listed under Decisions so far is `decided`, linked from Out of scope is `out-of-scope`, neither is `unrecorded` with a warning. GitHub's `stateReason` is ignored; the map's sections are the convention.
9. **Claim** is `{ by: string[] } | null`. Any assignee counts, matching the frontier query; `by` is empty on a local tracker, which names nobody.
10. **Blockers** are references with `number`, `title`, `state` and `ref`, so a blocker outside the map still renders in "Waits on" and still gates. `blocking` ("Clears the way for") is derived by inversion, never stored, so the two directions cannot disagree.
11. **Nothing derived.** Frontier, `next`, open-blocker counts, decided/total, the Finished fold and map ordering are pure functions exported by `@hero-synergy/core` and applied in the extension host. The snapshot is cached ([What is the scout's budget: refresh cadence, caching and rate limits?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/27)), and derived values in a cache are stale or redundant.
12. **Warnings are coded**: a closed literal union of codes with an optional free-text `detail` (which label, which line), at three levels (snapshot, map, ticket), one fixture per code. Core ships no UI copy; the Cockpit maps codes to messages. An unreadable item (a free-form map) stays in the snapshot with nulls and a warning, as [ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md) asks.
13. **Timestamps**: `collectedAt` on the snapshot. Per-item `updatedAt` and local content hashes are the scout's cache keys, owned by #27, so the snapshot type does not move when the caching strategy does.
14. **The boundary**: tracker-only. Sessions, status events, worktrees and actions are joined in by the Cockpit ([How does the Cockpit handle a session's lifecycle?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/21), [When the scout and the status hooks disagree, which does the Cockpit believe?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/28)). The "can't show maps" cases from #3 are a scout error type, not a snapshot field.
15. **HITL or AFK** is derived from `type` in the Cockpit; a task ticket shows as "task". No field, because the scout would have to guess it.
16. **Local titles** come from the file's first H1, else from the slug or the effort directory humanized, with a warning on the fallback.
17. **Names in core**: `WayfinderMap` (since `Map` shadows the global), `Ticket`, `Snapshot`, `Ref`, `Claim`, `Blocker`, `Warning`, in `packages/core/src/snapshot/`. Types exported, schema objects not ([ADR 0002](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-effect-schema-models-all-boundary-data.md)).

### Warning codes, v0.1.0

| Level | Code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| snapshot | `unknown-wayfinder-labels` | the repo has `wayfinder:` labels the scout does not know |
| map | `map-body-legacy` | M2, M3 or M4 headings (detail says which) |
| map | `map-body-partial` | some of the five sections, not all |
| map | `map-body-free-form` | no recognizable section |
| map | `map-no-destination` | no Destination section |
| map | `decision-line-unparsed` | a Decisions-so-far bullet is not `[title](link) — gist` |
| map | `decision-links-open-ticket` | Decisions so far links a ticket that is still open |
| map | `children-as-task-list` | children listed as a task list in the body |
| map | `map-title-from-directory` | local: no H1, title from the effort directory |
| ticket | `parent-as-part-of-line` | parent given by `Part of #n` |
| ticket | `blockers-as-text-line` | blockers given by `Blocked by:` |
| ticket | `blockers-as-slugs` | `Blocked by:` holds slugs, not numbers |
| ticket | `type-as-line` | type given by a `Type:` line on GitHub |
| ticket | `type-missing` | no type label or line |
| ticket | `type-several` | more than one type label |
| ticket | `claim-legacy-label` | `wayfinder:claimed` label |
| ticket | `unknown-wayfinder-labels` | a `wayfinder:` label the scout does not know |
| ticket | `no-question-heading` | no `## Question` |
| ticket | `closed-no-resolution` | closed with no comment or `## Answer` |
| ticket | `closed-unrecorded` | closed, in neither Decisions so far nor Out of scope |
| ticket | `no-map` | no parent found; the ticket is in `unmapped` |
| ticket | `blocker-outside-map` | a blocker that is not a ticket of the same map |
| ticket | `ticket-title-from-slug` | local: no H1, title from the file slug |
| ticket | `unknown-status` | local: a `Status:` value other than `claimed` or `resolved` |

### Not in the snapshot

Derived values; sessions, status events, worktrees and actions; per-item `updatedAt`; scout failures; provenance; raw labels; the map's body form (a warning instead); a map `state` (closed maps are never collected); a ticket `question` or `summary`; HITL/AFK.

### Local tracker

`.scratch/<effort>/map.md` is the map, `issues/NN-<slug>.md` the tickets, in number order. `state` is `Status: resolved`, `claim` is `Status: claimed`, `type` the `Type:` line, `blockedBy` the `Blocked by: NN` line, `resolution` the `## Answer` section. The effort slug a local launch command needs ([How does the Cockpit handle a session's lifecycle?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/21), point 11) is derived from the `ref` path.

### Recorded

The **Snapshot** and **Drift** terms in [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md). No ADR: core is a private package in v0.1.0, so every field here is cheap to change.

### New ticket

[How does the Cockpit show drift?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/29): nothing yet decides how the Tree and the Detail display a warning. Blocked by this ticket.
lastComment.author: dbarjs

27.title: What is the scout's budget: refresh cadence, caching and rate limits?
27.body:
## Question

How often does the scout refresh, what does it cache and under which key, and what does the Cockpit do when GitHub rate-limits it or `gh` fails?

Known inputs: one GraphQL query returns a whole map page for 6 rate-limit points in about 2 s, out of 5,000 points an hour; `updatedAt` does not move when a parent or blocker is added, so relationships must be collected fresh every time ([Can one GraphQL query collect everything the scout needs?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/9)); Eduardo's repos hold up to 45 maps, most of them finished. With no model call there is no bundle size limit and no `--safe-mode` fallback to plan for.

## Context

- The scout is code only, decided in [Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/16).
- Refresh triggers named in the seed: activation, window focus, `.scratch` changes, a session stopping, a timer while the Cockpit is visible, the refresh button.

lastComment.body: Constraint from [When the scout and the status hooks disagree, which does the Cockpit believe?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/28), agreed with Eduardo on 2026-10-06: two session events are scout refresh triggers, because each is the moment a tracker fact is expected to change: a ticket session's **`SessionStart`** (the claim follows within seconds) and a ticket session **ending** (a resolution, or an abandoned claim). The existing triggers (activation, window focus, `.scratch` changes, view shown, the refresh button) stand. #28 names the triggers; this ticket decides their debounce and what a refresh costs. The Cockpit also shows the snapshot's age ("tracker read <age>") on the repo row; the refresh policy behind it is this ticket's.

28.title: When the scout and the status hooks disagree, which does the Cockpit believe?
28.body:
## Question

A session has claimed a ticket but the tracker does not show the assignee yet, or a ticket is closed on the tracker while its session still reports work: which side does the Cockpit believe, and for how long?

Status belongs to the ticket and its terminal, not to a session id, which changes on `/clear`.

## Context

- The scout is code only and refreshes on the budget decided in [What is the scout's budget: refresh cadence, caching and rate limits?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/27).
- The status hooks: [Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/6). The session lifecycle: [How does the Cockpit handle a session's lifecycle?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/21).

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

**Neither side overrides the other: each source owns its facts. The tracker alone says claimed, open or closed, blocked; the session side alone says none, starting, live or ended and the status word. An off-path combination is a named situation with a note, never a silent override, and it lasts until the next scout refresh, which the session's own start and end trigger. For a live session the status word comes from Claude Code's registry (`claude agents --json`), not from the hooks; the plugin shrinks to three hooks.** Eduardo agreed to all sixteen points on 2026-10-06 in two grilling rounds.

### Decided

1. **Own your facts.** The tracker owns claim, state and blockers; the Cockpit's terminal, the registry and the status events own liveness and status. A row shows both. Nothing ever shows a claim or a closure the tracker has not recorded, and the snapshot stays tracker-only ([What does the snapshot hold for a map and a ticket?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/26)).
2. **Live here, unclaimed on the tracker.** A ticket with a session starting or live here leaves the frontier at once (liveness is a certain local fact; [How does the Cockpit handle a session's lifecycle?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/21) already forbids a second launch). It shows "live · claim not on tracker yet" until the first snapshot collected *after* `SessionStart` shows the claim; if that snapshot still shows no assignee, the note becomes the warning "not claimed on the tracker". No timer: the switch is "a refresh happened after the session started".
3. **Closed on the tracker, session still live** is the normal tail of every ticket (map update, glossary push, keep-or-remove prompt). Closed is closed: the row moves to the map's decisions fold, keeps its live indicator, status and "focus terminal", and counts for the badge when it needs you. The focus pane calls the situation **wrapping up**. No warning, no timer.
4. **Session events that trigger a scout refresh:** a ticket session's `SessionStart` (the claim follows within seconds) and a ticket session ending (a resolution or an abandoned claim), beside the existing triggers. [What is the scout's budget: refresh cadence, caching and rate limits?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/27) decides their debounce and cost; the list is posted there.
5. **Claimed by someone else, session live here:** the tracker's claimant and the live session are shown together with the warning "claimed by <login> on the tracker, session live here". Actions stay the session's. The Cockpit never arbitrates claims; v0.1.0 has no multi-dev model.
6. **A live session whose `#number` matches no collected ticket** (map closed, label removed, issue deleted or transferred) is kept: one **Sessions without a ticket in view** row at the repo level, next to the health-warnings row from [How are actions placed and named in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/24), listing each as `#number <name>` with its status, counting for the badge, focus terminal as its only action. Its ended record stays so Resume works if the ticket returns. Different from #24's ticketless terminals, which never had a number.
7. **The tracker's age is shown:** "tracker read <age>" from `collectedAt` on the repo row with the refresh button, repeated in the focus pane of any row in situation 2, 3 or 5. The refresh policy behind it is #27's.
8. **Local tracker:** the same rules; the situations resolve within milliseconds because `.scratch` changes trigger a refresh.
9. **Registry word → status table:** `busy` → working; `idle` → waiting for you; `waiting` with `permission prompt` → needs approval; `input needed` → waiting for you; `dialog open` → waiting for you (a dialog you opened yourself shows for the second it is open; the Cockpit cannot tell them apart); `sandbox request`, `worker request` and any unknown `waitingFor` → needs approval.
10. **Registry first.** While the registry lists the session, its word is the status. The plugin's `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse` and `PostToolUseFailure` events stop being status inputs. Events supply what the registry cannot say: `SessionStart` for starting → live and the session id, **failed** from `StopFailure`, and the ended reason from `SessionEnd`. The Cockpit also records `sessionId` from the registry while live, since the entry vanishes about a second after exit. "Fresher wins" was rejected: the registry word carries no timestamp through the supported `--json` interface.
11. **The plugin shrinks** to `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd` and `StopFailure`. This reverses point 2 of [Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/6), whose reason for hooking tool calls ("the only way to say working again after an approval") no longer holds: the registry turns `busy` 67 ms after an approval. No `node` process per tool call.
12. **Failed sticks:** a `StopFailure` event overrides the registry's `idle` until the registry next turns `busy`. The one case where an event outranks the registry.
13. **No registry entry, terminal alive** (the trust dialog, the hidden Cockpit's watcher stopped, a `claude` too old for `agents --json`): Cockpit terminal + no `SessionStart` + no entry is **starting**, with the 15 s hint worded "no status yet, the session may be waiting at the trust dialog, open the terminal"; last event live + no entry shows that event's status with its age.
14. **The Esc gap is closed:** the registry turns `idle` 75 ms after Esc, shown as "waiting for you". #6's accepted gap is withdrawn.
15. **Needs you**, for the badge from [Where does the Cockpit live: sidebar, editor tab, or both?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/23): waiting for you, needs approval, failed. Working, starting, ended and none do not count. Wrapping-up sessions and sessions without a ticket in view count by the same rule.
16. **Recorded in the glossary:** a **Registry** term, the **Status event** term narrowed to what the registry cannot say, and two relationship lines (registry first; each source owns its facts). No ADR: the plugin can grow back in an afternoon.

### Facts that shaped it

Measured on Claude Code 2.1.289, interactive session in a pty, 2026-10-06:

- `claude agents --json` lists interactive sessions with `pid, cwd, kind, startedAt, sessionId, name, status, waitingFor`. `status` took `idle`, `busy` and `waiting`; `waitingFor` took `permission prompt` (a Bash approval), `input needed` (AskUserQuestion) and `dialog open` (`/model` on an idle session), spelled as the [agent view docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view.md) list them. `sandbox request` and `worker request` were not exercised. The docs call the command "the supported way to read session state from outside Claude Code".
- Latency: Enter → `busy` ~30 ms; approval → `busy` 67 ms; answer → `busy` 46 ms; **Esc → `idle` 75 ms**; the permission and question states were written before the TUI had rendered them. Every change is one atomic rewrite of `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`; `updatedAt == statusUpdatedAt` on each.
- **No entry exists while the trust dialog is open**; registration happens once trust is accepted. After `/exit` the entry is gone within about a second, from `--json --all` too (`--all` retains background sessions only).
- `--json` omits `statusUpdatedAt`, `version`, `messagingSocketPath` and the other raw fields; the raw file shape was identical between 2.1.287 and 2.1.289 but is undocumented, and #21 already ruled out parsing it.
- `ls -la` needs no approval in default mode (read-only commands are auto-allowed); a filesystem write was needed to produce `permission prompt`.

### New ticket

[Which Claude Code version does the Cockpit need?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/30) (research): the README floor is ≥ 2.1.139, and the status model now leans on `claude agents --json`, `status`, `waitingFor`, `-n` names and `--resume <name>`; the changelog decides the floor.

### Handed on

- #27: the two session-caused refresh triggers (comment posted).
- #6: points 11 and 14 noted on its thread.

29.title: How does the Cockpit show drift?
29.body:
## Question

Where and how do the Tree and the Detail display a drift warning: an icon on the map or ticket row, a line in the Focus pane, a section in the Detail, or all three? Which codes are loud and which are quiet, and does a snapshot-level warning (unknown `wayfinder:` labels in the repo) get a place of its own?

Every warning is a code from the closed catalogue, with an optional free-text detail; the Cockpit maps codes to messages, core ships no UI copy. An unreadable item, such as a free-form map, is in the snapshot with nulls and a warning and must still render with a link to its issue.

## Context

- The snapshot's shape and the warning catalogue: [What does the snapshot hold for a map and a ticket?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/26).
- The scout is code only and shows what it cannot read as drift: [Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/16).
- The Tree, the Focus pane and the Detail: [How do maps render in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/7), [Where does the Cockpit live: sidebar, editor tab, or both?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/23).

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

**Two levels, shown only where the user already looks.** A loud warning marks the Tree row with ⚠. A quiet one only appears in the Focus pane, as a count, and in the Detail's Drift section. Decided with Eduardo on 2026-10-06 in two grilling rounds; every recommendation stood.

### Decided

1. **Two levels, one rule.** A warning is **loud** when what the Cockpit shows may be wrong or missing, and **quiet** when an old or fallback form was read correctly. Each code has one fixed level, set in a table in the Cockpit next to its message. Core ships neither severity nor copy.
2. **Levels for the v0.1.0 catalogue** ([What does the snapshot hold for a map and a ticket?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/26)):
   - **Loud:** `map-body-free-form`, `map-body-partial`, `map-no-destination`, `decision-line-unparsed`, `decision-links-open-ticket`, `type-missing`, `type-several`, `blockers-as-slugs` (always loud), `no-map`, `closed-unrecorded`, `closed-no-resolution`, `unknown-status`.
   - **Quiet:** `map-body-legacy`, `children-as-task-list`, `parent-as-part-of-line`, `blockers-as-text-line`, `type-as-line`, `claim-legacy-label`, `no-question-heading`, `blocker-outside-map`, `map-title-from-directory`, `ticket-title-from-slug`, `unknown-wayfinder-labels` (both levels).
3. **Ticket row.** A loud warning puts ⚠ after the title (the `warning` codicon in `editorWarning.foreground`), and hovering it lists the loud messages. A quiet warning leaves the row unmarked. Inside the Unmapped node, `no-map` doesn't mark the row.
4. **Map row.** It shows ⚠ when the map or any of its tickets, open or closed, has a loud warning. The tooltip gives counts ("map body is free-form · 2 tickets with drift"). The Finished fold node doesn't add up its maps' warnings, and drift never changes how maps are ordered.
5. **Focus pane.** Each loud warning gets one line. All quiet warnings together get one muted line, "n old forms". The ⚑ Map row's pane adds "k tickets with drift". Clicking any of these lines opens the Detail at its Drift section. With no warnings, nothing about drift appears.
6. **Detail.** A **Drift** section at the end, for maps and tickets. Each entry gives the message, the `detail` text and a one-line hint on the current convention. A map's section also lists its tickets' warnings grouped under `#n title`, closed tickets included, since that's the only place a `closed-unrecorded` ticket shows up. When anything there is loud, the header gets a ⚠ chip that scrolls to the section. The section is hidden when there's no drift.
7. **Unreadable map** (free-form or partial). The Detail renders the sections that were read, then the line "This map's body isn't in the current form; shown as written", then the raw body as Markdown. The Tree row still unfolds into its tickets; the Fog and Decisions nodes are left out when their section is null.
8. **Unmapped tickets** go in a synthetic, folded **⚠ Unmapped** node above the Finished fold, shown only when not empty. They behave like any ticket: Focus pane, Detail, and ▶ when unclaimed and unblocked.
9. **Repo-level warnings** (`unknown-wayfinder-labels`) appear as a quiet entry in the pinned health row from [How are actions placed and named in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/24). A **Dismiss** is saved in `workspaceState` for that exact `detail` (the label list), so the entry only returns when the set of labels changes.
10. **Messages** state what was found plus a one-line hint on the current convention. No warning has an Action: the Cockpit never writes to the tracker ([ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md)), and a "fix with Claude" Action would be outside the five capabilities.
11. **No pushing for attention.** Drift doesn't count toward the badge, doesn't affect ordering, and never raises a VS Code notification.

### Recorded

**Warning** (with loud and quiet) is added to [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md) in `6234c97`. No ADR: this is all presentation and easy to change.

### What this changes elsewhere

- [How do maps render in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/7): the Tree gains the Unmapped node.
- [How are actions placed and named in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/24): the pinned health row also holds repo-level drift, with a Dismiss per entry.
- The message and hint text for each code is spec work, one entry per code, tested against #26's fixture for that code.
lastComment.author: dbarjs

30.title: Which Claude Code version does the Cockpit need?
30.body:
## Question

What is the lowest Claude Code version in which everything the Cockpit relies on works, and does the README floor (≥ 2.1.139, from [Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/17)) need raising?

Pin from the Claude Code changelog (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) and the docs the version each of these landed in, plus any later change that altered their shape:

- `claude agents --json`, and its `status` (`busy|idle|waiting`) and `waitingFor` fields for **interactive** sessions
- `-n <name>` session names, `--resume <name>`, and the rename of a second live session to `<name>-<two words>` (docs say 2.1.232+)
- default display names for unnamed sessions (docs say 2.1.196+)
- `-w <slug>` worktrees and `claude --worktree <name> --resume`
- `--plugin-dir`
- the hooks the plugin keeps: `SessionStart` (with `source`), `SessionEnd` (with `reason`), `StopFailure`
- `SessionStart` hooks being held back until workspace trust is accepted

Report the floor, which feature sets it, and the measured version (2.1.289) as the tested ceiling. Findings go to `docs/research/claude-code-version-floor.md` on a `research/claude-code-version-floor` branch.

## Context

- Graduated from [When the scout and the status hooks disagree, which does the Cockpit believe?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/28), which made the registry the primary status source for a live session.
- The README states the floor as a requirement, not a gate ([Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/17)).

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

**Floor: Claude Code ≥ 2.1.212.** The README's ≥ 2.1.139 from [Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/17) has to go up. Tested ceiling: 2.1.289.

**What sets it:** the registry status the Cockpit relies on, per [When the scout and the status hooks disagree, which does the Cockpit believe?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/28).
- **2.1.145**: `claude agents --json` lists interactive sessions with `status` (2.1.144 rejects `--json`).
- **2.1.162**: `waitingFor` appears. Without it the Cockpit can't tell an approval from a question.
- **2.1.212**: sessions waiting on an MCP input, sandbox or managed-settings prompt report `waiting` instead of `busy`. Below this, such a session shows "working" and never reaches the "needs you" badge.

**Everything else is older than 2.1.212:**

| Feature | Version |
|---|---|
| `-n`/`--name` | 2.1.76 |
| `--resume <name>` | 2.0.64 |
| `-w`/`--worktree` | 2.1.49 (reusing a clean name resets it since 2.1.208) |
| `--plugin-dir` | before 2.1.74 |
| `SessionStart` | 1.0.62 |
| `SessionEnd` | 1.0.85 |
| `StopFailure` | 2.1.78 |
| exec-form hooks | 2.1.139 |
| trust-gated hooks | trust-requiring by 2.1.3 |

**These don't affect the floor:**
- **Default names (2.1.196) and unique `<name>-<word>-<word>` renames (2.1.232):** irrelevant, because the Cockpit always passes `-n "#<n> <title>"` and matches on the prefix.
- **Sessions listed twice in `--json`:** before 2.1.246, a session sent to the background can appear twice, which shows up as a false duplicate warning. Accepted.
- **The `claude agents` trust prompt (2.1.225):** it doesn't affect `--json`.

**Unverified:**
- The behaviour of old versions was read from their bundled code and checked with a made-up registry entry. No real sessions were run on them.
- `-n` together with `--resume` was not checked below 2.1.289.
- The changelog doesn't say when the `source`/`reason` fields arrived.

Findings: [`docs/research/claude-code-version-floor.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/claude-code-version-floor/docs/research/claude-code-version-floor.md) on `research/claude-code-version-floor`.
lastComment.author: dbarjs

31.title: Which mattpocock-skills version does the Cockpit read?
31.body:
## Question

Which mattpocock-skills versions does the Cockpit read, and what did 1.3.0 change that the Cockpit depends on?

The map was charted, and every decision so far was made, against mattpocock-skills **1.2.3** (installed 2026-08-12, commit `84fdeff`). 1.3.0 has since been released. Diff 1.2.3 against 1.3.0, primary sources only (the plugin's repo, release notes and the `SKILL.md` files themselves), for everything the Cockpit reads or spawns:

- the `/wayfinder` map body: the five sections, their headings and the Decisions-so-far line shape
- ticket types and their `wayfinder:*` labels, the `wayfinder:map` label, HITL/AFK
- claims (assignee), blocking (native dependencies or the `Blocked by` fallback), sub-issues, the frontier rule
- the tracker docs' "Wayfinding operations" sections, for GitHub and local markdown
- skill names and namespacing (`/<plugin>:<name>`), and any skill added, renamed or removed that an Action spawns (`/to-spec`, `/research`, `/grilling`, `/prototype`, `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`, ...)
- `SKILL.md` frontmatter used for action discovery

For each change, say which decision it touches: the snapshot ([What does the snapshot hold for a map and a ticket?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/26)), drift ([How does the Cockpit show drift?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/29)), actions ([How are actions placed and named in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/24)), legacy forms ([Which wayfinder conventions exist in the wild?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/10)). Recommend whether the README states a minimum skills version, the way it states one for Claude Code. Findings go to `docs/research/mattpocock-skills-version.md` on a `research/mattpocock-skills-version` branch.

## Context

- Raised while working [Which Claude Code version does the Cockpit need?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/30), which covers Claude Code only.
- Conventions upstream already span three generations ([Which wayfinder conventions exist in the wild?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/10)), so the format does move between releases.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Findings: [`docs/research/mattpocock-skills-version.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/mattpocock-skills-version/docs/research/mattpocock-skills-version.md) on `research/mattpocock-skills-version` (commit `cba760e`). Primary sources only: a clone of `mattpocock/skills` (tags `v1.2.3`, `v1.3.0`, `v1.3.1`, `main` at 2026-10-06), its release notes, the installed 1.2.3 copy, and the `anthropics/claude-plugins-official` manifest history.

**The Cockpit reads maps written by any release that ships `/wayfinder` (1.1.0 onward).** Between 1.2.3 and 1.3.0, exactly one thing the scout parses changed: the Decisions-so-far line went from `- [title](link) — gist` to `- [title](link): gist` (PR #905, 2026-08-19). Every heading, `## Question`, both label families, HITL/AFK, assignee-as-claim, native blocking and the `Blocked by:` fallback, sub-issues, the frontier rule and all three tracker templates' "Wayfinding operations" are the same text; the templates still say "Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body", so the mismatch found in [Which wayfinder conventions exist in the wild?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/10) survives into 1.3.1. 1.3.1 changes nothing the Cockpit reads or spawns.

**Per decision:**

- Snapshot ([#26](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/26)) and drift ([#29](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/29)): a map charted on 1.2.3 and worked on 1.3.0 holds **both line forms in one list**, since each session appends its own line. So the `gist` reader accepts either separator **per line, with no warning**; an em-dash line is not legacy on a map still being written in both forms. Split at the first separator after the link's closing `)`, since gists contain colons. `decision-line-unparsed` (loud) stays for lines that match neither.
- Actions ([#24](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/24)): no skill an Action names (`wayfinder`, `to-spec`, `setup-matt-pocock-skills`, `to-tickets`, `implement`) was added, renamed or removed; all five exist in every manifest from 1.1.0 to 1.3.1. The manifest adds `implement-spec`, `pr`, `retro` and drops `resolving-merge-conflicts`, so the user-invoked set is now 16, not 14. `pr` is the first skill with a nested `metadata:` map in its frontmatter and six `description` values are now YAML-quoted (with `\"` escapes in `code-review`): the frontmatter reader must be a real YAML parser that ignores unknown keys, and QuickPick `detail` is read from the file, never hard-coded. 1.3.0's wayfinder tells the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` rather than running it, which confirms the Cockpit's Setup Action as the one automated route.
- Legacy forms ([#10](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/10)): D2 (the colon line) is released now.

**The version string does not identify the content.** The official marketplace pins `main` commits, not tags: four different contents have shipped as `"version": "1.2.3"`, two of which already write the colon line, and on 2026-10-07 the marketplace still serves `c55ee46` (pinned 2026-09-22), whose wayfinder text is byte-identical to 1.3.0's but reports 1.2.3. `claude plugin list --json` gives only the version; the commit is `gitCommitSha` in `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`.

**README: no numeric floor for mattpocock-skills.** Nothing the Cockpit reads is version-gated, the number is unenforceable (see above), and a missing `wayfinder` skill is already a health row. Requirements text: "mattpocock-skills with the `wayfinder` skill (any release from 1.1.0; built and tested against 1.2.3 and 1.3.1), installed as a plugin or with skills.sh." Claude Code ≥ 2.1.212 stays the only hard version requirement. Note that no README file exists in the repo yet; the Claude Code floor lives in [#30](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/30)'s resolution until [#22](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/22) writes one.

**One change lands on this repo, not on the Cockpit:** 1.3.0 renames the domain doc from `CONTEXT.md` to `GLOSSARY.md`, and `domain-modeling` looks only for the new name. The scout never reads it, so no decision moves, but when the installed plugin is upgraded past `c55ee46` the repo needs one commit: `git mv CONTEXT.md GLOSSARY.md` plus the pointers in `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/agents/domain.md` and ADR 0003. Until then sessions run the installed 1.2.3, which reads `CONTEXT.md`.

**Not verified:** the marketplace pin before 2026-09-16; `claude plugin update` and skills.sh were not run; how Claude Code's `/` menu renders `pr`'s `metadata`; no real map with both line forms was observed (inferred from the append-one-line rule).
lastComment.author: dbarjs

32.title: Write the upstream register: every Claude Code, skills and VS Code contract the Cockpit relies on
32.body:
## Question

What, exactly, does the Cockpit rely on from each upstream (Claude Code, mattpocock-skills, VS Code, `gh`, Node), and which versions has each been checked against, all written down in one place?

This is a task ticket (AFK): write the register, then record what was done. It unblocks [How does an upstream review run when Eduardo comes back?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/33) and [Does CI watch the upstreams for breaks between visits?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/34), which both work from it.

## Why

Eduardo comes back to hero-synergy regularly to improve it (recorded 2026-10-07). Each time, Claude Code, the skills and VS Code may have moved: breaking changes to adapt to, new features to use. Each return should start from one page, not from a fresh research hunt.

## Work

Write `docs/upstream.md`, the **upstream register**. It has one section per upstream. Each section opens with the **floor**, the **tested ceiling** and the **date and version last checked**, followed by one row per contract:

| Contract | Since | Source | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claude agents --json` `waitingFor` | 2.1.162 | changelog line or doc page | decision that relies on it |

Contracts are flags, JSON fields, hook events and payload fields, map body headings, labels, `SKILL.md` frontmatter keys, command namespacing, VS Code APIs and the GraphQL fields the scout queries. "Used by" links the decision ticket for now. Once the code exists, the build points it at the module.

The file lands on `main` through the `CLAUDE.md` routine, like glossary and ADR edits. `docs/seed.md` stays frozen; where it lists a contract, the register supersedes it.

33.title: How does an upstream review run when Eduardo comes back?
33.body:
## Question

When Eduardo comes back to hero-synergy, how does he find out what changed upstream since the last check (what breaks and what's newly possible), and how does that turn into tickets?

## Context

- Eduardo returns regularly to improve hero-synergy, not just once (recorded 2026-10-07). Upstream moves in between: Claude Code ships almost daily, mattpocock-skills has no compatibility promise, and VS Code and the workspace's own dependencies (vite-plus, Effect, TypeScript, Vue) release on their own schedules.
- [Write the upstream register](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/32) gives the last-checked version and the contracts for each upstream.

## Starting proposal to grill

A project skill, `.claude/skills/upstream-review/SKILL.md`, invoked by the user (`disable-model-invocation: true`), built on `/research` and written with `/writing-for-agents`. A run:

1. Reads the register for each upstream's last-checked version.
2. Reads only primary sources for everything since: the Claude Code `CHANGELOG.md` and CLI/hooks docs, mattpocock/skills releases and the diff of every `SKILL.md` and tracker doc the register cites, the VS Code release notes (extension API sections), `gh` releases, and `pnpm outdated` for the workspace.
3. Sorts every change into **breaks** (a register row changes), **opportunity** (a new feature the Cockpit could use, or one that lets an Out of scope item come back, e.g. `--bg` sessions or the CLI) and **irrelevant** (one line each).
4. Writes `docs/research/upstream-review-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` on a `research/` branch, files one issue per break and per opportunity worth doing, breaks first, and moves "last checked" only for the rows it verified.

Points to settle: whether it's a skill at all or a checklist in the register; whether opportunities become plain issues or a new wayfinder map; whether the workspace's own dependencies belong in the same run. As a user-invoked skill in this repo, the Cockpit would list it as an Action ([How are actions placed and named in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/24)).

lastComment.body: Resolved above: a by-hand `/upstream-review` project skill with a Review log in the register, written in #36 after the map; glossary and register updated at 5ecb4c7.

34.title: Does CI watch the upstreams for breaks between visits?
34.body:
## Question

Does CI watch Claude Code, mattpocock-skills and VS Code for breaking changes between Eduardo's visits, so the breakage is already ticketed when he comes back? If it does, what does it check, and what does it do when something fails?

## Context

- Claude Code updates itself on users' machines, and the skills have no compatibility promise. A break can land between two visits (recorded 2026-10-07).
- [How is the extension tested?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/18) split CI into `check`, `vscode` and `live`, with `gh` and `claude` replayed from recorded fixtures behind one process-runner service, plus one non-blocking live `gh` job. It ruled out Insiders builds and a live `claude -p` job for v0.1.0.
- [How does an upstream review run when Eduardo comes back?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/33) covers new features when he's here. This ticket is only about catching breaks while he's away.
- [Write the upstream register](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/32) lists the contracts a failure would point to.

## Starting proposal to grill

A scheduled, non-blocking workflow (weekly, plus `workflow_dispatch`), beside `live`:

1. Install the latest Claude Code (native installer), check out mattpocock/skills at its latest release and at `main`, and use the latest VS Code stable.
2. Re-capture what doesn't need secrets: `claude --version`, `--help` output for the register's flags, `SKILL.md` frontmatter, the `/wayfinder` map headings and labels, and the tracker docs' "Wayfinding operations". Whether `claude agents --json` and hook payloads can be captured without a login is open.
3. Decode everything with core's Effect Schemas and the scout's parsers, and run the extension-host suite on the latest VS Code.
4. On a failure, open one issue per upstream, or comment on the existing one ("Upstream drift: <upstream> <version>"). It names the failing contract and its register row, and attaches the captured output as a fixture to be.

Building it happens after this map, with the rest of the build.

lastComment.body: Resolved above: a daily canary workflow files one upstream break per upstream; glossary updated at a64332d.

35.title: Does the Cockpit warn when Claude Code or the skills are too old or change shape?
35.body:
## Question

When the user's Claude Code is below the floor, or when Claude Code or the skills change a shape the Cockpit reads, should the Cockpit say so, and how loudly?

## Context

- [Which Claude Code version does the Cockpit need?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/30) set the floor at ≥ 2.1.212, with 2.1.289 as the tested ceiling.
- [Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/17) decided **no gating**: the README states the floor as a requirement, not a gate, and at activation the extension logs the resolved `claude` path and editor details to its output channel.
- [How are actions placed and named in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/24): health warnings are one pinned Tree row. [How does the Cockpit show drift?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/29): repo-level drift joins that row and has a Dismiss button.
- Without a warning, a renamed `claude agents --json` field silently turns every session into "unknown". The user blames hero-synergy, not the upgrade.

## Starting proposal to grill

- At activation, read `claude --version` and the skills version. Below the floor, show **loud** repo-level drift with the floor and the version found. Still never gate.
- When registry output, a hook payload or `SKILL.md` frontmatter fails to decode, show loud drift that names the upstream and its version: "Claude Code 2.3.0 changed `claude agents --json`; session status may be wrong."
- **Never** warn just for being above the tested ceiling. Claude Code ships almost daily, so that warning would always be on.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

**Yes, the Cockpit says so, and it never gates. A too-old Claude Code, a registry or hook payload that no longer decodes and a skill file that will not parse are *health* warnings about the machine, shown in the same pinned row and at the same two levels as drift.** Decided with Eduardo on 2026-10-07 in two grilling rounds; every recommendation stood.

### Decided

1. **Warning has two kinds.** *Drift* is about the tracker (a map or ticket off the current conventions), *health* is about the machine (Claude Code, the skills, the registry). The loud/quiet rule from [How does the Cockpit show drift?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/29) applies to both: loud when what the Cockpit shows may be wrong or missing. Calling a version floor "drift" would have made the Scout's definition wrong, so the term was widened instead.
2. **Shape and home.** Core exports a second closed union `HealthCode` with the same `{ code, detail? }` shape as drift, so the webview imports one `Warning` type and tells the kind from the code. The extension host produces health warnings; the scout produces drift; the snapshot stays tracker-only ([What does the snapshot hold for a map and a ticket?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/26), point 14). The Cockpit holds the level-and-copy table, core ships no copy.
3. **The floor is checked** with one `claude --version` spawn at activation, on the refresh button, and on any refresh where the resolved `claude` path differs from the last one. Compare the leading `x.y.z` numerically and ignore any suffix. Nothing is checked on the skills side: [Which mattpocock-skills version does the Cockpit read?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/31) showed the number is unenforceable.
4. **Below 2.1.212 is loud** ("Claude Code 2.1.200 found; hero-synergy needs 2.1.212 or later"), because below it a session waiting on an MCP or sandbox prompt shows as working forever ([Which Claude Code version does the Cockpit need?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/30)). **Above the tested ceiling says nothing**: Claude Code ships almost daily, so that entry would always be on. **No gating** stands from [Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/17).
5. **A registry that fails to decode** (not an array; an entry without `sessionId`, `name` or `status`; a `status` other than `busy`/`idle`/`waiting`) gives one loud entry naming the upstream and version, "Claude Code 2.3.0 changed `claude agents --json`; session status may be wrong", and every affected session shows the honest word **status unknown**: no badge count, focus terminal and the ended record kept. Falling back to the last status event was rejected: since [When the scout and the status hooks disagree, which does the Cockpit believe?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/28) shrank the plugin, that event would say "live" forever, the silent wrong display this ticket exists to prevent. An unknown `waitingFor` stays a status mapping (#28, point 9), not a warning.
6. **A hook payload that changes shape.** The plugin writes what it got; the Cockpit decodes leniently. `SessionStart` without `session_id` is loud ("Resume may have to use the session name") while the session still goes starting → live on the event's arrival; `SessionEnd` without `reason` is quiet.
7. **A skill file that will not parse.** The Action is greyed with the reason (per [How are actions placed and named in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/24)) plus a health entry naming the plugin and its reported version: loud for `wayfinder` and `to-spec` (a context Action is gone), quiet for any other skill, loud for an unreadable `plugin.json`. The version is the one `claude plugin list --json` reports; `installed_plugins.json` is never read.
8. **A newer wayfinder's map shape** gets no new code: the scout cannot tell "newer" from "wrong", and guessing is forbidden (#26, point 3). Instead the hint on `map-body-partial`, `unknown-wayfinder-labels` and `decision-line-unparsed` gains one sentence: "a newer mattpocock-skills may write this; check for a hero-synergy update".
9. **No Action on a warning** (#29, point 10). The floor's hint names `claude update` "or upgrade through your package manager", since the install method varies.
10. **Dismiss** lives in `globalState` for health, keyed on `(code, detail)` (the version found; the `(what changed, version)` pair), because the machine's condition is the same in every repo. Drift stays in `workspaceState`.
11. **The pinned row** follows the ticket-row rule: ⚠ when any entry is loud, unmarked when all are quiet, labelled "Health · 2 warnings" / "Health · 1 note"; hover lists the loud messages, the Focus pane lists every entry with hint and Dismiss, the row is absent when empty. No badge, no notification, no effect on ordering.
12. **Every health entry is logged once** to the output channel with what the Cockpit saw: the `--version` line, the first 2 KB of the output or payload that failed, the parse error. The Tree entry stays one line plus a hint.
13. **Fixtures:** one recorded fixture per health code, replayed through the process-runner stub from [How is the extension tested?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/18), plus a recorded `claude agents --json` from 2.1.212 and from the current ceiling so the floor's shape is pinned. No live job against the floor build: #18 ruled live `claude` jobs out, and `agents --json` with no live session returns `[]`.

### Health catalogue, v0.1.0

| Level | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| loud | `claude-not-found` | no `claude` resolved on `PATH`; every Action greyed with the reason |
| loud | `claude-below-floor` | `claude --version` parses and is < 2.1.212 |
| quiet | `claude-version-unreadable` | no leading `x.y.z`; the floor check is skipped |
| loud | `registry-unreadable` | `claude agents --json` is not an array of entries |
| loud | `registry-entry-unreadable` | an entry lacks `sessionId`, `name` or `status` |
| loud | `registry-status-unknown` | `status` is not `busy`/`idle`/`waiting` |
| loud | `hook-payload-unreadable` | `SessionStart` without `session_id` |
| quiet | `hook-reason-missing` | `SessionEnd` without `reason` |
| loud | `plugin-manifest-unreadable` | a plugin's `plugin.json` or its `skills` array can't be read |
| loud / quiet | `skill-unreadable` | a `SKILL.md` frontmatter can't be parsed: loud for `wayfinder` and `to-spec` |
| loud | `skill-missing` | #24's "no `wayfinder`, Work ticket unavailable" |
| quiet | `skill-installed-twice` | #24's "installed twice" |
| quiet | `plugin-disabled` | #24's "plugin disabled" |

Two wording rules for the spec: every machine message names the upstream and the version it saw; every hint names the one thing to do. Draft copy per code is in the grilling above; final copy is spec work tested per code, as #29 did.

### Recorded

**Warning** rewritten with its two kinds, plus one relationship line ("the scout reports drift; the extension host reports health; a warning never gates"), in [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md) at `14a7088`. No ADR: every item is a table entry, a string or a `globalState` key.

### What this changes elsewhere

- #17: `claude-not-found` names what happens when `claude` is not on `PATH`, which that ticket left open.
- #24: the pinned health row gains the levels, the ⚠ rule and a Dismiss per entry.
- #29: the hint text on three drift codes gains the "newer skills" sentence.
- #30: when the floor is next bumped, record that version's `claude agents --json` as the fixture of point 13.

No new ticket and no new fog: this closes the last open question about upstream versions.

36.title: Write the upstream-review skill
36.body:
Write `.claude/skills/upstream-review/SKILL.md`: the user-invoked project skill decided in [How does an upstream review run when Eduardo comes back?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/33). Its resolution comment is the spec. The glossary ([`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md)) defines upstream review, upstream break, opportunity and the canary; the register ([`docs/upstream.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/upstream.md)) holds the dates, the "Not relied on" watch-lists and the Review log shape.

## What the skill does, from the resolution

1. Frontmatter: `name: upstream-review`, `disable-model-invocation: true`, a one-line human-facing description, `argument-hint` for an optional list of upstreams (`claude-code`, `skills`, `vscode`, `gh`, `node`; default all five).
2. Step zero, for the human: update Claude Code, the plugin, VS Code, `gh` and Node by hand. The run never updates the machine; it records what it finds installed.
3. Fan out one research subagent per upstream. Each starts from the canary's last step summary ([Does CI watch the upstreams for breaks between visits?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/34)) for the versions already passed, reads its primary sources since the section's last-checked version (resolution point 9 names them per upstream), captures the cheap outputs on this machine (`claude --version`, `claude agents --json`, `claude plugin list --json`, the `--help` of the register's flags, every installed `SKILL.md`), and returns every change sorted into upstream break, opportunity or irrelevant, with its source. Once the build exists, the captures are decoded with core's schemas and the scout's readers, and VS Code's ceiling comes from the newest green host run, local or canary.
4. The main session edits the register: last-checked dates, tested ceilings for what ran, Since cells recording a shape change, Unverified marks it closed, "Ahead of the ceiling" notes. Never the floor, the "Not relied on" lists, a decision's outcome, code or the machine: those become upstream break issues.
5. Files one `needs-triage` issue per upstream break, then per opportunity, titled `Upstream break: <upstream> <version>: <what>` or `Upstream opportunity: <upstream> <version>: <what>`, with the register rows, the primary-source link, the proposed response and the bin, after searching open and closed issues for that upstream and version (the canary's own issues are titled `Upstream break: <upstream> <version>`); comments on an existing one instead of filing twice. Never charts a map.
6. Writes the Review log entry (Read, Ran, Found per upstream, issues linked, irrelevant changes counted) and pushes one commit to `main` through the `CLAUDE.md` routine.

## How to write it

With `/writing-for-agents`: steps in order, each ending on a completion criterion; the per-upstream source table as in-file reference; nothing restated that the register already says, point at it instead.

## Done when

- The file is on `main` and `claude` lists `/upstream-review` in this repo.
- `vp check` passes.
- Every numbered point above has a step or a reference line in the skill.

37.title: Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit
37.body:
Produced by `/to-spec` from the finished map [#1 hero-synergy v0.1.0, fully decided](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/1). Every decision below has a ticket on that map; the ticket holds the reasoning and the measurements, this spec holds what to build. Vocabulary is the glossary ([`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md)); the five ADRs in `docs/adr/` and the upstream register ([`docs/upstream.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/upstream.md)) bind this spec. Where this spec and a ticket disagree, the ticket wins and this spec has a bug.

## Problem Statement

Driving a big `/wayfinder` map by hand is a chore that grows with the map. To take the next ticket I have to query the tracker for the frontier (open, unblocked, unclaimed), open a terminal, type the right `/wayfinder <map> <ticket>` line with the right command name for how the skills are installed and the right `claude` flags (a session name, a worktree, the status plugin), and then remember which of my open terminals is waiting for my answer, which needs an approval, and which failed. My repos hold many maps at once, most of them finished (one project: 45 maps, about 85% done), so "where does this effort stand" is spread over dozens of issues, and maps charted by older skill versions use older conventions. Nothing shows me the whole picture, and nothing tells me when a session needs me.

## Solution

Hero Synergy, an unofficial VS Code extension (`dbarjs.hero-synergy`): the Cockpit. It reads every open wayfinder map in the window's repo from its tracker (GitHub through `gh`, or local markdown) with code alone, and shows them as one Tree, each map unfolding into its tickets with the frontier, blockers, claims, fog and decisions, a compact Focus pane under the selected row and a Detail editor tab with the full issue. One click launches a frontier ticket as a named `claude` session in a VS Code terminal, with the exact command shown first, and the Cockpit follows the session's status (working, waiting for you, needs approval, failed, ended) from Claude Code's own registry and a tiny status plugin, with a badge for the sessions that need me. Matt's user-invoked skills appear as context-aware Actions. The Cockpit refreshes on causes, never on a timer; it reports drift in maps and health on the machine as warnings and never gates; it never writes to the tracker and never runs git. It ships from CI to the Marketplace, Open VSX and a GitHub release.

## User Stories

**Maps and tickets**

1. As a developer, I want to install Hero Synergy from the Marketplace or Open VSX and open a repo that uses Matt's skills, so that my maps appear with no configuration.
2. As a developer, I want every open map in the repo listed in one Tree like the file explorer, so that I see the whole picture of many efforts at once.
3. As a developer, I want each map row to show its number, title, how many sessions need me, how many tickets are takeable (or that nothing is) and decided-of-total, so that I can judge a map without opening it.
4. As a developer, I want maps ordered by urgency (a session needs me, then something takeable, then stuck), so that the map that needs attention is at the top.
5. As a developer, I want finished maps that are still open folded into one node at the bottom and closed maps hidden, so that 38 finished maps don't bury the active ones.
6. As a developer, I want a map to unfold into a ⚑ Map item, its open tickets and folded Fog and Decisions nodes, so that I can read an effort top-down.
7. As a developer, I want a map's tickets ordered as claimed (with session status), then the frontier with the first ticket marked `next`, then blocked tickets with `waits on #n #m` inline, so that I always know what to take next and why the rest waits.
8. As a developer, I want every ticket and map shown as `#number title` with the number in a muted monospace run before the name, so that I can refer to it by name and still find it on the tracker.
9. As a developer, I want a ticket's type (research, prototype, grilling, task) and whether it is HITL or AFK visible, so that I know what kind of session I am about to start.
10. As a developer, I want a Focus pane under the selected row with state, claim, session status, the Work ticket command, the title linking to the issue and an ↗ Open button, so that I can act without leaving the Tree.
11. As a developer, I want a Detail editor tab that follows my Tree selection and shows the issue body as Markdown, the two-column neighbourhood (Waits on → Clears the way for) and, for a closed ticket, its resolution comment, so that I can read a ticket in full without a browser.
12. As a developer, I want the Detail of a map to show its destination, decisions so far, fog and out of scope, and the Fog and Decisions Tree rows to open it scrolled to that section, so that the map body is one click away.
13. As a developer, I want clicking a neighbour in the Detail to select it in the Tree and unfold its map, so that the two surfaces always show the same selection.
14. As a developer, I want my expanded maps and selection restored after a window reload, so that the Cockpit opens where I left it.
15. As a developer, I want the Tree in its own Activity Bar container that I can drag to the secondary side bar or the Panel, so that the Cockpit sits where my layout wants it.
16. As a developer, I want a ticket whose blocker lives outside its map still shown with that blocker in "Waits on" and still gated, so that the frontier never lies.
