## Implementation Decisions

### Packages, stack and boundaries

- Two workspace packages: `@hero-synergy/core` (private, bundled into the extension, never published) and `hero-synergy` (the extension). The scaffold's CLI package (`@hero-synergy/cli`) stays in the workspace as a private placeholder with no code, the seat for the private `next` CLI a parallel map will develop; it and core get `private: true` with their publish configuration dropped, so nothing goes to npm (revised 2026-10-07 in #39; the original decision removed it). The Changesets fixed group stays, and every changeset names `hero-synergy`. (#4, [ADR 0001](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-publish-the-extension-as-dbarjs-hero-synergy.md))
- Core holds the snapshot types, the tracker readers and the scout's collect and reconcile logic, the drift catalogue, the derived functions (frontier, ordering, neighbourhood), the registry and status-event decoders, the health codes, skill discovery and the launch-command builder. Core never imports `vscode`. Pure functions where possible; Effect services at the edges (process runner, file system, file watching, clock). (#26, #18)
- Effect 4 for workflows; Effect Schema for every boundary: the snapshot, configuration, webview messages, status events, registry entries, plugin list output, `SKILL.md` frontmatter and hook payloads. Boundary data is plain JSON with no transforms (timestamps stay ISO strings). Core exports types and parsing functions, never schema objects; the webview imports types only and does not validate; the host validates every message arriving from the webview. zod is not used. (#15, [ADR 0002](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-effect-schema-models-all-boundary-data.md))
- The extension imports `vscode` only in adapter modules in one directory; everything else is pure TypeScript or an Effect service whose live layer uses `vscode` and whose test layer is in-memory (terminals, webviews, the events-file watcher, workspace folders, storage). (#18, [ADR 0004](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-extension-host-tests-run-on-mocha-beside-vitest.md))
- `gh`, `claude` and read-only `git` run behind one process-runner Effect service with a live layer and a replay layer that serves recorded fixtures. (#18)
- No model call anywhere; the Agent SDK is not installed. ([ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md))
- Toolchain as scaffolded: TypeScript 7 at the root, TypeScript 6 with vue-tsc inside the extension for SFC checks, Vite+ for build, check, test and pack, Vue 3.5 for the webview, UnJS utilities before other dependencies. Two new runtime dependencies are expected and each gets the short ADR the working agreement asks for: a real YAML parser for frontmatter (nested maps and quoted values exist upstream) and a Markdown renderer for the Detail. (#2, #31)

### The snapshot

Tracker-only, nested per map, three kinds of value: facts the tracker reports, sections code reads from bodies, and coded drift warnings. Nothing derived, nothing about sessions. This shape was settled in #26 and is the contract between the scout and the Cockpit:

```ts
Snapshot { tracker: { kind: 'github', owner, repo } | { kind: 'local' }; repoRoot; collectedAt (ISO)
           maps: WayfinderMap[] (tracker order); unmapped: Ticket[]; warnings: Warning[] }
WayfinderMap { number, title, ref, body (raw Markdown), tickets: Ticket[] (map order)
               destination | null, notes | null,
               decisions: { number | null, title, link, gist }[],
               notYetSpecified: { text, tickets: number[] }[], outOfScope: { text, tickets: number[] }[],
               warnings }
Ticket { number, title, ref, state: 'open' | 'closed', type: research | prototype | grilling | task | null,
         claim: { by: string[] } | null, blockedBy: Blocker[], body (raw Markdown),
         resolution: { body, author | null, at | null } | null,
         outcome: 'decided' | 'out-of-scope' | 'unrecorded' | null, gist: string | null, warnings }
Ref = { tracker: 'github', url } | { tracker: 'local', path (repo-relative) }
Blocker = { number, title, state, ref }      Warning = { code, detail? }
```

- Identity is `number` plus `title` on both trackers, with a tagged `ref` saying how to open and launch it. A local ticket's number is its `NN` file prefix. A local map has no number on its tracker; this spec (not the map) gives it its 1-based position in directory order so the shared identity holds.
- Facts are never guessed; what cannot be read is `null` plus a warning. Provenance is a warning, not a field: a value that arrived through a text fallback stands as a plain value with a drift warning.
- `resolution` is the last comment on GitHub and the `## Answer` section locally. `gist` is the map's own Decisions-so-far line for the ticket, verbatim, no computed fallback. `outcome` classifies a closed ticket by the map: in Decisions so far → `decided`, linked from Out of scope → `out-of-scope`, neither → `unrecorded` with a warning; GitHub's `stateReason` is ignored.
- `blocking` ("Clears the way for") is derived by inversion, never stored. Frontier, `next`, open-blocker counts, decided-of-total, finished, map ordering and the neighbourhood are pure functions in core applied by the extension host; HITL/AFK is derived from `type` (research is AFK, prototype and grilling are HITL, task shows as "task").
- Names in core: `WayfinderMap` (since `Map` shadows the global), `Ticket`, `Snapshot`, `Ref`, `Claim`, `Blocker`, `Warning`, plus the closed unions `WarningCode` (drift) and `HealthCode`, both `{ code, detail? }` so the webview imports one `Warning` type and tells the kind from the code. (#35)

### Collecting from GitHub

- Only GitHub on github.com, through `gh api graphql`, no preview headers. Non-github.com remotes are tried and their error shown. The repo is `owner/name` from the git remote. (#3, #9)
- Map-first: one cheap list of the open `wayfinder:map` issues (label names passed explicitly, since the API matches a label list as an OR and ignores unknown names) together with `repository.labels(query: "wayfinder:")` for the unknown-labels check, then aliased `issue(number: N)` blocks for each open map with its `subIssues` (capped at 100 per parent, within one page), and for each sub-issue its labels, assignees, state, body, the last comment, `parent`, and `blockedBy` nodes with each blocker's `number`, `title`, `state` and URL. A closed blocker stays in the nodes with `state: CLOSED`; the scout gates on each blocker's `state`, never on the summary counts. Every request also selects `rateLimit { remaining resetAt }`, which costs nothing. (#27, #32)
- At most 5 maps per request, requests sent one after another, never in parallel; `gh` is killed after 20 s. Closed maps are never collected. Tickets that are not native sub-issues of an open map are never collected; a map body that lists children as a task list earns the map a drift warning instead. `unmapped` is therefore empty on GitHub by construction; it holds, on a local tracker, the issue files of an effort with no readable map. (#27 point 7)
- Relationships are read fresh on every collect, because `updatedAt` does not move when a parent or blocker is added. No per-item caching, no REST change probes. (#9, #27 points 4 and 9)
- The scout parses raw stdout whatever the exit code, because `gh` skips `--jq` on GraphQL errors and exits 1 for nearly everything; headers come from `gh api -i`. A `NOT_FOUND` on one map's block drops that map (closed or deleted between the list and the fetch); any other error fails the whole collect. (#27 point 10)
- Recorded `gh` outputs for this repo's own maps are the fixtures that pin the exact query shape. (#18)

### Reading a local tracker

- `.scratch/<effort>/map.md` is the map and `.scratch/<effort>/issues/NN-<slug>.md` the tickets, in number order; every effort directory is a map (no open or closed state exists; a user hides a map by removing its directory). `state` comes from `Status: resolved`, `claim` from `Status: claimed` (with an empty `by`), `type` from the `Type:` line, `blockedBy` from the `Blocked by: NN, NN` line, `resolution` from the `## Answer` section, titles from the first H1 with a warning when they fall back to the slug or the directory name. The effort slug a launch needs comes from the `ref` path. (#26, #3)

### Reading bodies: the conventions the scout knows

- The current map body has five H2 sections: Destination, Notes, Decisions so far, Not yet specified, Out of scope. Legacy heading sets from the conventions research (the Notes / Decisions so far / Fog body, the Deferred form, the single-file form) are recognised by their headings and read with a quiet `map-body-legacy` warning whose detail names the form. Some sections present but not all is `map-body-partial`; none recognisable is `map-body-free-form`; both keep the map in the snapshot with nulls. (#10, #26)
- A Decisions-so-far line is `- [title](link) — gist` or `- [title](link): gist`; both separators are accepted per line with no warning, split at the first separator after the link's closing parenthesis, because gists contain colons and one map can hold both forms. A line matching neither is `decision-line-unparsed`. A decision that links a still-open ticket is `decision-links-open-ticket`. (#31)
- Out of scope and Not yet specified entries keep their text and the ticket numbers they link. A ticket body without a `## Question` heading is a warning, not an error. Type comes from the `wayfinder:<type>` label (a `Type:` line on GitHub is `type-as-line`; none is `type-missing`; several is `type-several`); any assignee is the claim; the `wayfinder:claimed` label is `claim-legacy-label`; a `Blocked by:` line is `blockers-as-text-line`, or `blockers-as-slugs` when it holds slugs; a `Part of #n` line is `parent-as-part-of-line`.
- The drift catalogue, each code with one fixed level set in the Cockpit (core ships neither severity nor copy): (#26, #29)

| Level | Loud | Quiet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| snapshot | | `unknown-wayfinder-labels` |
| map | `map-body-free-form`, `map-body-partial`, `map-no-destination`, `decision-line-unparsed`, `decision-links-open-ticket` | `map-body-legacy`, `children-as-task-list`, `map-title-from-directory` |
| ticket | `type-missing`, `type-several`, `blockers-as-slugs`, `no-map`, `closed-unrecorded`, `closed-no-resolution`, `unknown-status` | `parent-as-part-of-line`, `blockers-as-text-line`, `type-as-line`, `claim-legacy-label`, `no-question-heading`, `blocker-outside-map`, `ticket-title-from-slug`, `unknown-wayfinder-labels` |

- Every message states what was found plus a one-line hint on the current convention; the hints on `map-body-partial`, `unknown-wayfinder-labels` and `decision-line-unparsed` add "a newer mattpocock-skills may write this; check for a hero-synergy update". No warning carries an Action. (#29, #35 point 8)

### Finding the repo and its tracker

- One repo per window, named in the Tree. In a multi-root workspace: the first folder, in workspace order, whose repo root has a tracker doc; else the first folder inside a git repo, which gets the setup message. A folder inside a repo (a package opened alone) works: the root comes from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, the tracker is read there and sessions start there. A folder holding several repos shows "no repo was found". (#3)
- The tracker doc decides, by its heading, with no model: `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` first, then the link in the `## Agent skills` block of `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`. `# Issue tracker: GitHub` and `# Issue tracker: Local Markdown` are supported; any other heading is an unsupported tracker. One tracker per repo: if the doc says GitHub, `.scratch` maps are not read, and the reverse. (#3, #10)
- When maps cannot be shown, the Tree shows one plain message and no maps; Actions that need no tracker stay. The cases are a scout error type, not snapshot fields: no tracker doc (leads with Setup); GitLab or "Other" doc (names the tracker, says it isn't supported yet); GitHub doc with a remote not on github.com (tries, shows the error); `gh` missing or not logged in (shows `gh auth login`); no repo found. (#3)

### The scout's budget: when it runs, what it keeps

- No timer. A refresh starts when the view becomes visible (activation with the view open included), the window gains focus, a ticket session's `SessionStart` arrives, a ticket session ends, the registry reports a session gone, a file under `.scratch/**` changes (local tracker, debounced 1 s), or the refresh button is pressed. Not triggers: tool-call events, activation while the view is hidden. (#27, #28 point 4)
- One collect at a time and at most one queued behind it. Automatic triggers need 60 s since the last successful collect; the button ignores the gap and attaches to a running collect instead of starting another. The local tracker has no gap and no pause.
- Cache: one entry per repo, the last successful snapshot stamped with its collect time, in extension storage, keyed by tracker kind + repo identity (`owner/name` or the repo root path) + the snapshot's schema version. Activation renders it right away. Nothing is cached per issue.
- Budget protection: when `remaining` drops below 1,000 points, automatic triggers pause until `resetAt` and the Tree shows "paused until HH:MM"; the button still works. On `remaining: 0` automatic triggers stop until the reset header and the button shows "rate-limited until HH:MM" without calling. On a secondary limit (403 or `retry-after`) automatic triggers pause for `retry-after` or 60 s, doubling on each repeat and resetting after a success. Not logged in (exit 4) or 401 shows the `gh auth login` fix. Network failure, timeout or 5xx is shown as such and the next trigger tries again. Nothing retries on its own.
- Staleness: the repo row carries the refresh button and "tracker read <age>" from `collectedAt`; it is emphasised with the reason when the last collect failed or the snapshot is older than 5 minutes. While a collect runs the view shows VS Code's progress bar; rows get no spinners. (#27 point 6, #28 point 7)

### Sessions

- A Session is one live `claude` process in a VS Code terminal for one ticket or action, named `#<number> <title>`, whoever started it. A ticket's session state is **none**, **starting** (a terminal exists, no `SessionStart` yet), **live** or **ended** (no process, last session id known); a tracker claim with no session and no known id is **claimed elsewhere**. All state is keyed on the ticket and its terminal, never a session id. Starting counts as live for the one-live-session rule. (#21)
- The launch runs `claude` as the terminal's own process (`shellPath` is the resolved binary, `shellArgs` the argv), never typed into a shell: `claude -n "#<number> <title>" -w <number> --plugin-dir <extension>/claude-plugin "<wayfinder command> <map ref> <ticket ref>"`, cwd the repo root, env `HERO_SYNERGY_TICKET` (the ticket number) and `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS` (the events file), the terminal named like the session, an icon per ticket type, location from the setting. On a local tracker there is no `-w`, and the map and ticket are repo-relative paths. The worktree is `.claude/worktrees/<number>` on branch `worktree-<number>`, created by Claude Code; the Cockpit never creates, merges or removes one. (#17, #24 point 11, [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md))
- The extension resolves `claude` on `PATH` itself (preferring `claude.exe` on Windows; an npm `.cmd` shim is best-effort only), overridable by the setting for its location. Resolution is logged at activation.
- Liveness has two sources: the Cockpit's own terminal when it has one, and Claude Code's registry (`claude agents --json`) for everything else: hand-started sessions, sessions in another window, and a process that exited non-zero while VS Code keeps the pane open. The files under `~/.claude/sessions/` are never parsed: a watcher on that directory is the trigger, the command is the reader, debounced one second or more, stopped while the Cockpit is hidden. A session matches a ticket by the leading `#<number>` of its name within the repo; the worktree path is corroboration, never the key. A second live session with the same prefix (Claude Code renames it `<name>-<two words>`) is shown under the ticket with a warning; the Cockpit kills nothing. (#21 points 2 and 3)
- Status, registry first: while the registry lists the session its word is the status: `busy` → working; `idle` → waiting for you; `waiting` with `permission prompt` → needs approval, `input needed` → waiting for you, `dialog open` → waiting for you, `sandbox request`, `worker request` or any unknown value → needs approval. Status events supply what the registry cannot: `SessionStart` turns starting into live and carries the session id, `StopFailure` is **failed** and sticks until the registry next turns `busy`, `SessionEnd` carries the ended reason. The Cockpit also records the session id from the registry while live, since the entry vanishes about a second after exit. (#28 points 9 to 12)
- Ended is one state whose detail is text, in order of trust: the `SessionEnd` reason (`prompt_input_exit` → "exited", `logout`, `other`), else the terminal's exit status (`User` → "terminal closed", `Shutdown` → "window closed", `Process` with a non-zero code → "exited with code N"), else "process gone". `clear` and `resume` reasons never end a ticket; the next `SessionStart` in the same terminal carries the new id. The terminal closing is the truth for ended on every platform. (#21 point 5, #6)
- Resume is by id: `claude --resume <session id> -n "#<number> <title>" --plugin-dir <extension>/claude-plugin` in a fresh terminal from the repo root with the env set again (`--session-id` is never passed at launch; Claude Code returns to the worktree by itself but does not restore `--plugin-dir`). With no known id the Action is **Resume by name**: `claude --resume "#<number> <title>"`. Launch fresh is the plain Work ticket command and reopens an existing worktree. No confirmation on either. (#21 points 6 and 7)
- Reload and close: on activation the Cockpit adopts any terminal whose name starts with `#<number>` as that ticket's terminal and lets the registry confirm it is live; a ticket with no live match whose last event is not `SessionEnd` becomes ended with "window closed". Cockpit terminals are neither transient nor hidden. (#21 point 8)
- No registry entry while a terminal is alive (the trust dialog, the hidden Cockpit's watcher stopped, a `claude` too old): Cockpit terminal + no `SessionStart` + no entry is starting, and after 15 s shows "no status yet, the session may be waiting at the trust dialog, open the terminal"; a last event of live with no entry shows that event's status with its age. The keep-or-remove prompt at exit stays under the last status with its age. No terminal scraping; the Cockpit never edits Claude Code's trust configuration. (#28 point 13, #21 point 12)
- The events file: one per repo identity under the extension's global storage, so it persists across restarts and is a ticket's memory of its last session id; read incrementally by byte offset after one full read at activation; compacted by the Cockpit above a size cap keeping the last event per ticket; the reader treats `SessionEnd` as final for its session id regardless of line order; the file is created before it is watched, and a slow poll backs the watcher where events can be dropped. (#21 point 14, #11)
- Situations where the tracker and the session side disagree are named, never overridden, and last until the next refresh: a session starting or live here on an unclaimed ticket leaves the frontier at once and shows "live · claim not on tracker yet" until the first snapshot collected after `SessionStart` shows the claim, then the warning "not claimed on the tracker" if it still doesn't; a ticket closed with a live session moves to the decisions fold as **wrapping up**, keeps its status, focus terminal and badge count; a ticket claimed by someone else with a session live here shows "claimed by <login> on the tracker, session live here"; a live session whose `#number` matches no collected ticket goes to one **Sessions without a ticket in view** row at the repo level, counting for the badge, with focus terminal as its only action and its ended record kept. (#28 points 2, 3, 5 and 6)
- Needs you, for the badge: waiting for you, needs approval, failed. Working, starting, ended and none do not count. (#28 point 15)
- Worktree state per ticket, read-only through `git worktree list` and `git log main..<branch>`: exists, has uncommitted files, has commits not on `main`. (#5 point 6)
- Performance bar: VS Code's perceived responsiveness and the battery. Nothing lifecycle-related on the UI path; activation renders stored state and spawns nothing until a trigger fires; every read and spawn is async; no polling timers; spawns debounced one second or more; the only timer is the 15 s per launch. Hidden Cockpit: the terminal and status-event listeners stay on, the registry watcher stops, nothing is spawned, one refresh when shown. Soft target: a status change or an ending visible within about a second. AFK tickets launch exactly like HITL ones; `--bg` is not used. (#21 points 10, 15 to 17)

### The status plugin

- A Claude Code plugin shipped inside the extension (`claude-plugin/` in the VSIX) and loaded with `--plugin-dir`, no install step. Three hooks: `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `StopFailure`, each the exec-form handler `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/report.mjs` with `async: true`. The report appends one JSON line to the file in `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS` with the ticket from `HERO_SYNERGY_TICKET`, the hook name, the session id, the detail the payload carries (`source` for start, `reason` for end, `error` for failure), its write time, and the payload fields it got, so the Cockpit can decode leniently; with no `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS` it exits 0. (#6, #28 point 11, #35 point 6)
- The seed's appendix A.7 is the base; its six hooks shrink to three and its `report.mjs` gains the raw fields.

### Actions

- An Action is anything the Cockpit offers that spawns a process in a terminal, always shown with the exact command. ↗ Open, focus terminal and the palette commands are buttons. (#24)
- Skill discovery, on every refresh: for each skill the Cockpit needs, look in the project's `.claude/skills/<name>`, then `~/.claude/skills/<name>`, then an enabled plugin that lists it (`claude plugin list --json` for the install path, that plugin's `plugin.json` `skills` array, each `SKILL.md` frontmatter through the YAML parser, unknown keys ignored). The first two give `/<name>`, the plugin gives `/<plugin>:<name>`; found in both, the unnamespaced copy wins with the quiet health note "installed twice"; a disabled plugin counts as not installed. `disable-model-invocation: true` marks a user-invoked skill. The inventory is not snapshot data.
- Contexts and their Actions:

| Context | Actions |
| --- | --- |
| Frontier ticket | **Work ticket** |
| Claimed elsewhere | **Launch fresh** |
| Blocked ticket | none |
| Starting or live session | none (focus terminal is a button) |
| Ended | **Resume**, then **Launch fresh** / **Resume by name** |
| ⚑ Map, unfinished | none (the `next` row carries ▶) |
| ⚑ Map, finished (open, every ticket closed) | **To spec**: `<to-spec command> <map url or path>` |
| Repo (Tree title bar) | **Chart a map**, **Run skill…** |

- The row's ▶ runs the context's first Action, its tooltip showing that command; second Actions live only in the Focus pane and the Detail; live and blocked rows show no ▶. Work ticket appears in the Focus pane and the Detail.
- **Run skill…** is a native QuickPick from the Tree title bar and the Command Palette (`Hero Synergy: Run skill…`), listing every discovered user-invoked skill: label the command (`/mattpocock-skills:grill-me`), description `plugin 1.2.3` / `project` / `personal`, detail the frontmatter description read from the file; the title states `Runs claude "<skill>" in a new terminal`. `/to-tickets` and `/implement` live only here.
- Empty states: no user-invoked skill found → both install commands (`claude plugins install mattpocock-skills`, `npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills`) each with ▶ and the "pick one, never both" line; skills found but no tracker doc → **Setup** (`<setup-matt-pocock-skills command>`), reached through the `onView` activation; tracker doc but no open map → **Chart a map**. **Chart a map** is `claude -n "Chart a map" "<wayfinder command>"` with no input; the session asks for the loose idea.
- The command is one string built once from argv, rendered shell-quoted in a code block with a copy button, the full plugin path included, nothing elided; environment variables appear as a second muted `env:` line.
- Ticketless terminals (Chart a map, Run skill…, Setup, installs) are plain terminals: no plugin, no env, no status, no badge.
- An Action whose skill is not found is greyed with the reason, never hidden.

### Warnings: drift and health in the Cockpit

- One rule for both kinds: loud when what the Cockpit shows may be wrong or missing, quiet when something old or odd was still read correctly. The level-and-copy table lives in the Cockpit. (#29, #35)
- Ticket row: a loud warning puts ⚠ after the title (the `warning` codicon in the editor-warning colour), hover lists the loud messages; quiet leaves the row unmarked. Map row: ⚠ when the map or any of its tickets, open or closed, has a loud warning, with counts in the tooltip; the Finished fold does not add up warnings; drift never changes ordering.
- Focus pane: one line per loud warning, one muted line for all quiet ones ("n old forms"); the ⚑ Map row's pane adds "k tickets with drift"; clicking opens the Detail at its Drift section. Nothing about drift appears when there is none.
- Detail: a **Drift** section at the end for maps and tickets, each entry with message, detail and hint; a map's section groups its tickets' warnings under `#n title`, closed tickets included; a ⚠ chip in the header scrolls to it when anything is loud; hidden when empty. An unreadable map renders the sections that were read, then "This map's body isn't in the current form; shown as written", then the raw body; its Tree row still unfolds into tickets, with Fog and Decisions nodes left out when null.
- Unmapped tickets go in a synthetic folded **⚠ Unmapped** node above the Finished fold, shown only when not empty, behaving like any ticket.
- Repo-level entries (`unknown-wayfinder-labels`, every health code) live in one pinned row at the top of the Tree: ⚠ when any entry is loud, labelled "Health · n warnings" / "Health · 1 note", hover listing the loud messages, the Focus pane listing every entry with its hint and a Dismiss, the row absent when empty. Drift dismissals go in `workspaceState` keyed on the exact detail; health dismissals in `globalState` keyed on `(code, detail)`. No badge, no ordering effect, no notification, no Action on any warning.
- Health is produced by the extension host, never the scout. The floor is checked with one `claude --version` at activation, on the refresh button and when the resolved path changes, comparing the leading `x.y.z` numerically; below 2.1.212 is loud with the hint naming `claude update` "or upgrade through your package manager"; above the tested ceiling says nothing. A registry that fails to decode gives one loud entry naming the upstream and version, and every affected session shows **status unknown** (no badge count, focus terminal and ended record kept). Every health entry is logged once to the output channel with what was seen (the version line, the first 2 KB of the failing output, the parse error). The catalogue:

| Level | Code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| loud | `claude-not-found` | no `claude` resolved; every Action greyed with the reason |
| loud | `claude-below-floor` | `claude --version` parses and is below 2.1.212 |
| quiet | `claude-version-unreadable` | no leading `x.y.z`; the floor check is skipped |
| loud | `registry-unreadable` | `claude agents --json` is not an array of entries |
| loud | `registry-entry-unreadable` | an entry lacks `sessionId`, `name` or `status` |
| loud | `registry-status-unknown` | `status` is not `busy`, `idle` or `waiting` |
| loud | `hook-payload-unreadable` | `SessionStart` without `session_id` (the session still goes live) |
| quiet | `hook-reason-missing` | `SessionEnd` without `reason` |
| loud | `plugin-manifest-unreadable` | a plugin's manifest or its `skills` array can't be read |
| loud / quiet | `skill-unreadable` | a `SKILL.md` frontmatter can't be parsed: loud for `wayfinder` and `to-spec` |
| loud | `skill-missing` | no `wayfinder`: Work ticket unavailable |
| quiet | `skill-installed-twice` | a skill found as a local copy and in a plugin |
| quiet | `plugin-disabled` | the plugin that holds a needed skill is disabled |

Every machine message names the upstream and the version it saw; every hint names the one thing to do.

### The Cockpit's surfaces

- **The Tree** is a webview view in its own Activity Bar container, "Hero Synergy", draggable to the secondary side bar or the Panel but not contributed there by default (that contribution point is finalised only in 1.106). It draws its own empty states. Its badge is the number of sessions that need you, nothing else. (#23)
- **The Detail** is one webview panel, detail only, titled `#n title`, reused and following the Tree's selection; it opens from ↗, a double-click, Enter, or `Hero Synergy: Open Cockpit Detail` (the current selection, or the first map in order). Webview panels always open pinned. The Fog and Decisions rows open the map's Detail scrolled to that section.
- One selection, held by the extension host and mirrored both ways. `retainContextWhenHidden` on both webviews; expanded maps and the selection persist in `workspaceState`; a panel serializer restores the Detail after a reload on the same selection.
- One Vue bundle serves both hosts; the two widths are one component. At Tree width the Focus pane sits inline under the clicked row, a second click or ✕ closes it; the Detail shows the full header, neighbourhood, body and resolution. No graph and no layout library: the neighbourhood draws only a ticket's immediate neighbours. Tickets and maps always render as `#number title`; codicons for the ⚑ ≋ ✓ ⚠ marks and type icons. (#7)
- Host → webview messages carry the view model the host derives (maps in display order with their derived counts, frontier and `next`, each ticket's session state and status, warnings with level and copy, the Actions with their command strings, the repo row's age and pause state, health entries, selection and expansion). Webview → host messages are select, expand or collapse, run an Action, open the issue, focus a terminal, dismiss a warning, copy a command, open the Detail at a section. The host validates inbound messages with Effect Schema; the webview validates nothing.
- Activation events: `workspaceContains:docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` and `onView:<tree view id>`, nothing else. On activation the host renders stored state, adopts terminals by name, checks the floor, logs `appName`, `appHost`, the VS Code version, `process.platform` and the resolved `claude` path to the output channel, and spawns nothing more until a trigger fires. No gating on editor, OS or version anywhere. (#17, #23)
- Settings: `heroSynergy.sessions.terminalLocation` (`panel` | `editor`, default `panel`) and `heroSynergy.claude.path` (the `claude` location; empty means resolve on `PATH`). Commands: `Hero Synergy: Open Cockpit Detail`, `Hero Synergy: Run skill…`, `Hero Synergy: Refresh` (also the Tree title-bar button). No other configuration.

### Manifest, listing and README

- `publisher: dbarjs`, `name: hero-synergy`, `displayName: Hero Synergy`, `engines.vscode: ^1.105.0`, `@types/vscode ~1.105.0` (tilde, since vsce reads the manifest string only), `extensionKind: ["workspace"]`, one universal `.vsix` with no native modules. The scaffold's `^1.100.0` / `~1.100.0` moves to the floor. (#17, #19)
- Listing: `categories: ["Other"]` (check for a better category at build time), keywords `claude code`, `wayfinder`, `mattpocock`, `skills`, `agent`, `bugs` and `homepage` pointing at the repo, a simple placeholder icon in the AI Hero spot-illustration spirit (the real logo comes with the polished README), `files` limited to the built extension, the webview assets, the plugin, the changelog, the licence, the README and the icon. (#20)
- A plain README in the extension package, rendered by both registries, with one **Requirements** section: VS Code 1.105 or later; macOS and Linux supported (dev containers and SSH remotes included), WSL remote as the documented Windows route, native Windows untested and best-effort with the native Claude Code installer; Claude Code ≥ 2.1.212; mattpocock-skills with the `wayfinder` skill ("any release from 1.1.0; built and tested against 1.2.3 and 1.3.1"), installed as a plugin or with skills.sh, never both; Node ≥ 22.18 on `PATH` in the session's environment; `gh` authenticated for a GitHub tracker. It also states the session-naming convention for hand-started sessions, the recommended push-back routine for worktree sessions, and "built for VS Code; forks are expected to work". A short root README points at it. (#17, #30, #31, #5)

### CI, release and the canary

- CI has three parallel jobs: `check` (build, `vp check`, `vp test` with coverage reported, the vue-tsc typecheck), `vscode` (the host and end-to-end tiers on Linux under `xvfb-run -a` and on macOS, the VS Code downloads cached by OS and version, host tests on both the floor and the newest stable), and `live` (the one `gh` job against this repo's own maps with the workflow token). `check` and `vscode` are required for merge; `live` is not. (#18)
- The release workflow runs on pushes to `main` and detects its mode itself: if any changeset file exists, run the Changesets version action to open or update the **Release hero-synergy** PR; otherwise, if no `v<version>` tag exists for the version in the extension's manifest, build, `vsce package`, publish to each registry whose `PUBLISH_*` repository variable is `true` (Marketplace through the `marketplace` environment with Entra ID login and `--azure-credential --skip-duplicate`; Open VSX with `--trusted-publishing --skip-duplicate`), then always create the GitHub release `v<version>` with the `.vsix` attached, even if a registry step failed. No `select-mode`, pack or publish jobs from Changesets, no Changesets tags, no approval gate on the environment. (#20)
- A backfill workflow (`workflow_dispatch`, input: tag) downloads that release's `.vsix` and publishes it to every registry switched on, reusing the same scripts and environment.
- Release notes come from a small script: title `hero-synergy v<version>`, the extension's changelog entry, an install line with the Marketplace and Open VSX links (each only if its variable is on) and the attached `.vsix`, and the compare link; `Updated dependencies` lines stripped; core's changelog never linked. Changelog files stay excluded from formatting.
- The canary is a separate daily workflow (off-the-hour minute, plus `workflow_dispatch`) with one job per upstream: `claude` (native installer, latest, no login: `--version` through the Cockpit's parser, `--help` containing every launch flag in the register, `agents --json` decoding with the registry schema, `plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official` then `plugin list --json` decoding), `skills` (latest tag, `main`, and the marketplace install: every `SKILL.md` frontmatter decodes, the wayfinder skill and the GitHub tracker template still carry the headings, labels and operations the scout reads), `vscode` (host and end-to-end on `stable`, Linux and macOS), `gh` (the live job on the schedule), `node` (`vp test` on the latest Node). A break is only what the Cockpit would choke on: a schema that fails to decode, a suite that fails, a flag missing from `--help`; new fields and skills never break. On a break: one open issue per upstream titled `Upstream break: <upstream> <version>`, labelled `canary` and `ready-for-human`, assigned to Eduardo, with the failing contracts and register rows, last green → first red from the previous step summary, the error, ≤ 2 KB of output inline and the full capture as an artifact; later runs comment only when the failing set or version changes; a return to green comments and leaves the issue open. On green: nothing on `main`, a step summary of the versions seen. Each run re-enables itself against GitHub's 60-day idle disable (unverified; fall back to a dated commit per run if it doesn't reset the clock). The register gains a "Watched by the canary" list per upstream when the canary is built. (#34)

### Repository housekeeping that ships with the build

- Keep the CLI package as a private placeholder, mark core private, move the VS Code floor in the manifest, gitignore the test output and download directories, add the launch configuration for the Extension Test Runner, keep `docs/seed.md` frozen. The glossary rename to `GLOSSARY.md` is **not** done now: it is the first upstream break an upstream review will file once the installed plugin passes commit `c55ee46`. The `/upstream-review` skill is its own issue outside this spec. (#31, #33, #36)
- Every user-facing change ships a changeset naming `hero-synergy`, written for the person updating; refactors, tests and CI need none.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test exercises external behaviour through a seam and asserts what a user or a neighbouring module would observe: the snapshot a recorded tracker produces, the frontier a snapshot yields, the status a sequence of registry outputs and events yields, the command string a ticket yields, what the Tree renders for a view model. Tests never assert on private state, call order or file layout. Every test runs through a `vp` command: `vp test` for Vitest and `vp run --filter hero-synergy test:integration` for the extension host; never `vitest`, `mocha` or `vscode-test` directly. (#18, [ADR 0004](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-extension-host-tests-run-on-mocha-beside-vitest.md))
- The seams, from highest to lowest, all already decided:
  1. **End-to-end through VS Code**: a Vitest `e2e` project launches VS Code through Playwright's Electron support against a fixture workspace on the local markdown tracker (no `gh` needed), with a stub `claude` on `PATH` or in the setting that records its argv and writes status events on a script (started, working, waiting for you, ended), so live status is driven end-to-end. Opt-in by `--project e2e`, `retry: 1`, never launched by plain `vp test`.
  2. **The extension host**: Mocha through `@vscode/test-cli` on the floor (1.105.0) and the newest stable, covering activation, the view resolving, terminals and the real `vscode` API; only the adapter modules need it.
  3. **The process runner**: core's replay layer serving recorded `gh api graphql`, `claude agents --json`, `claude --version`, `claude plugin list --json` and `git` outputs from checked-in fixtures; a stub `gh` for host tests reuses the same recordings.
  4. **Pure functions and in-memory Effect layers**: readers, derived functions, the status reducer, the command builder, skill discovery over an in-memory file system, the scout's trigger and budget logic over a test clock.
  5. **The Cockpit app**: Vitest with happy-dom and Vue Test Utils, `acquireVsCodeApi()` stubbed, fed view models.
- Modules tested: every core module (readers for each body form and each drift code, one fixture per warning code; the collect against recorded fixtures pinning the query shape; the frontier, ordering and neighbourhood functions; the registry, plugin-list, frontmatter, hook-payload and status-event decoders, one recorded fixture per health code plus `claude agents --json` recorded from 2.1.212 and from the current ceiling); the extension's pure logic (the session state machine, including out-of-order `SessionEnd`, `/clear` starting a new id, failed sticking, every named situation, needs-you, adoption on reload; the refresh policy with its floor, coalescing, pauses and backoff; Action contexts and empty states; command strings with their shell quoting; warning levels and copy per code); the status plugin from both sides (spawn the report with the env and a hook payload on stdin and assert the appended event; read recorded event files from the prototype's runs); the adapters in the host tier; the Cockpit components (Tree rows and ordering, Focus pane, Detail sections, drift marks, two widths); the whole path end-to-end.
- Prior art: the proven two-runner layout on the `task/test-runners` branch (#25: the array `pack` block, the `--project` gating, the short `--user-data-dir`, the shared VS Code download cache, CommonJS Node-22 host bundles, the per-folder tsconfigs), the Effect test conventions on `task/effect-vitest` (#14: Effect tests import from `@effect/vitest`, plain tests from `vite-plus/test`, with the "one Vitest instance" check), the status-hooks prototype's recorded runs (#6) and the scout prototype's fixtures in every legacy form (#16).
- Coverage is reported now in CI and gated later in its own ticket once the first implementation exists. Zero retries everywhere except the `e2e` project. Never trim coverage for CI cost.

## Out of Scope

- Building and running the one-time registry setup (the Entra identity, the Open VSX namespace claim and first hand-publish) and the v0.1.0 release run itself.
- A model call anywhere in the scout, and the Agent SDK fallback ([ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md)).
- Background sessions (`claude --bg` with `claude attach`) for AFK tickets.
- A polished README, the real logo and the polished listing text (#22, after the release).
- GitLab; "Other" trackers and the agentic collect step; any promise for GitHub Enterprise Server, the text fallbacks or cross-repo relationships; grouping maps per folder or a repo picker in a multi-root workspace; a folder holding several repos; closed maps.
- Any CLI command (the package stays as an empty private placeholder); core as a public npm package; anything on npm; Nitro, a browser Cockpit and a docs site.
- The twelve-item real-Windows test and verifying terminals, icons and webview views inside Cursor, Devin Desktop and VSCodium; a Windows CI runner; Insiders builds; a live `claude -p` job; Vitest Browser Mode; Playwright Test, `vitest-environment-vscode`, `wdio-vscode-service` and ExTester as runners; the coverage threshold.
- Tracking sessions that belong to no ticket (Chart a map, Run skill…, Setup and installs stay plain terminals).
- Writing to the tracker from the Cockpit; the Cockpit running git (creating, merging or removing worktrees); chaining user-invoked skills automatically; telemetry; a hosted service; a TUI; Claude Code's agent view; the official Claude Code VS Code extension; sandboxes; agents other than Claude Code.
- Workspace dependency bumps (vite-plus, Effect, TypeScript, Vue), the `/upstream-review` skill (#36) and the `GLOSSARY.md` rename.
- A full dependency graph or a layout library; a "fix with Claude" Action on a warning; VS Code notifications for drift or health; a multi-developer claim model.

## Further Notes

- The map's Notes carry the working agreements that bind every implementation session: work in a `claude -w` worktree, never the shared checkout; `pnpm exec vp` since the devcontainer has no global `vp`; `vp check --fix` before pushing; glossary and ADR edits reach `main` by the routine in `CLAUDE.md`; issue numbers ride in front of names everywhere; design every view and budget for many maps per repo.
- Reference material with measurements: the research branches `research/scout-graphql-query`, `research/wayfinder-conventions`, `research/windows-behavior`, `research/fork-vscode-versions`, `research/extension-integration-testing`, `research/claude-code-version-floor`, `research/mattpocock-skills-version` and `research/name-availability`; the prototypes `prototype/status-hooks` (recorded hook runs), `prototype/map-rendering` (the seven variants and the M4 shape the Tree follows) and `prototype/scout` (code-only readers for every legacy form, the fixtures to port); the spikes `task/test-runners` and `task/effect-vitest`.
- The upstream register lists every contract with the version it appeared in and the decision that relies on it; once code exists, each row should point at the module instead of the decision. The Windows traps the code must avoid are in the Windows research: no shell between the Cockpit and `claude`, a real `node.exe` for the plugin's hooks, a byte-offset reader with a slow poll for the events file, `claude.exe` before any shim.
- Facts proven by the spikes that the build should not re-derive: ESM test files hang the 1.105.0 extension host, so host bundles stay CommonJS targeting Node 22; the default user-data directory overflows the Unix socket path limit inside a worktree; `vp pack` cleans each entry's output directory, so pack before build; run `vp test` from the repo root; `pnpm add` writes exact pins, use ranges; run `vp check --fix` after adding a dependency.
- Open items the build must prove, each with a fallback already decided: `subIssues` order after a reprioritisation (the frontier's "first in map order" depends on it); the canary's keepalive resetting the 60-day clock; `claude` with no credentials printing `--version`, `--help`, `agents --json` and `plugin list --json` on a runner; `claude plugin install` working non-interactively there.
- Soft targets, not gates: a status change or a session ending visible within about a second; a collect of a repo with seven open maps around 35 rate-limit points.

38.title: Write a throwaway next script that launches the first takeable ticket of this spec
38.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Personal tooling for the v0.1.0 build, not part of the Cockpit: a pre-alpha of the Cockpit's own loop (the frontier of a map, then the launch of its first takeable ticket) that Eduardo runs by hand while the tickets of this spec are implemented. The boundary of [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md) applies by analogy: the script reads and launches, never writes.

## What to build

One file under the repo's `scripts` directory, plain Node with no dependencies, outside the workspace packages and never packed or published. It lives on `main` because it must run from the checkout that launches the sessions; it is not a wayfinder prototype ticket, so there is no `prototype/` branch and no `/prototype` skill involved. The CLI package stays removed, as the spec says.

`node scripts/next.mjs --list` prints this spec's frontier: the open sub-issues of #37 with no open blocker and no assignee, in sub-issue order, each as `#number title` with its open blockers inline, the first one marked `next`. It also skips any ticket whose `#number` session is live in Claude Code's registry (`claude agents --json`), which is the Cockpit's own rule, so two terminals never take one ticket.

`node scripts/next.mjs` prints the exact command and then launches it in the foreground from the repo root: `claude -n "#<number> <title>" -w <number> "<skill line>"`. The skill line is one constant at the top of the file, defaulting to the wayfinder form with the spec and ticket URLs as full references, so the session never resolves `#n` against the wrong list; the implement form is the alternative, one line to swap. `node scripts/next.mjs <number>` launches that ticket.

It never assigns, comments or closes: the session claims, as the skill prescribes. No tests: it is throwaway, built for this one spec, and it is deleted or kept at Eduardo's choice once Work ticket (#54) lands in the Cockpit. Where the Cockpit later implements the same query and launch (#45, #47, #54), the script is a reference to compare against, never a dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `node scripts/next.mjs --list` prints the frontier of #37 in sub-issue order as `#number title` with open blockers inline and `next` on the first, without writing to the tracker.
- [x] `node scripts/next.mjs` prints the command, then launches the first takeable ticket as a session named `#<number> <title>` in its own worktree.
- [x] A ticket with a live `#number` session in the registry is skipped.
- [x] `node scripts/next.mjs <number>` launches that ticket.
- [x] No changeset: nothing ships.

## Blocked by

- None — can start immediately.

lastComment.body:
Follow-up: terminals started by `node scripts/next.mjs` kept the tab title `node`, and `/rename` inside the session changed nothing, while sessions started with `cc` by hand were titled correctly.

**Cause.** Claude Code writes the session name into the terminal title itself, but only takes effect when `claude` is the shell's foreground job. Spawned directly from node with inherited stdio, the foreground process stayed `node`, so VS Code never showed Claude's title.

**Fix.** The launch now runs through an interactive zsh and the `cc` alias: `zsh -ic 'cc "$@"' cc -n "#<number> <title>" -w <number> "<skill line>"`. The alias expands, the `claude` wrapper function sees `-n` and passes the arguments through untouched, and the tab shows `#<number> <title>` with Claude's status glyph. The launcher word (`cc`) and the shell (`zsh`) are constants at the top of the script, and the printed command is now exactly the line to type by hand.

Verified through a stub `claude` that the alias expands and the five arguments arrive intact with the exit code propagated. The tab title itself needs a real VS Code terminal to confirm.

## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec sections: "Packages, stack and boundaries", "Repository housekeeping that ships with the build", "Testing Decisions" (seams 3 and 4). ADRs 0001 and 0002. Prior art: the `task/effect-vitest` branch (the Effect test conventions).

## What to build

The workspace the rest of the build stands on. The CLI package leaves the workspace; core is private with its publish configuration dropped, so nothing goes to npm; the Changesets fixed group stays with the CLI entry gone. The extension manifest moves to the VS Code floor: engines 1.105 and the matching types range with a tilde. Effect 4 comes in as core's runtime dependency with `@effect/vitest` for tests, carrying the spike's conventions over: Effect tests import from `@effect/vitest`, plain tests from `vite-plus/test`, and the "one Vitest instance" check stays as a test.

Core gets its first two Effect services, the edges every later ticket uses. A process runner spawns `gh`, `claude` and read-only `git` with a timeout and returns stdout, stderr and the exit code whatever the exit code, with a live layer and a replay layer that serves recorded fixtures checked into the repo. A file-system service has a live layer and an in-memory layer. Both are deep modules: a small interface, the replay keyed so a test names the fixture it expects.

Core never imports `vscode`; the extension keeps importing `vscode` only in its one adapter directory, as the scaffold does today. The seed document stays frozen.

- [ ] `vp install`, `vp run -r build`, `vp check` and `vp test` pass from the repo root with the CLI package gone and core private.
- [ ] The extension manifest's engines field and VS Code types are on the 1.105 floor.
- [ ] Effect tests run through `@effect/vitest` and plain tests through `vite-plus/test`; one test proves both share the one Vitest instance.
- [ ] The process runner's replay layer serves a recorded fixture for a named command and arguments, and a test asserts what a caller observes; the live layer kills a process after its timeout and still returns what was captured.
- [ ] The file-system service has an in-memory layer a test can seed, and a live layer.
- [ ] New dependencies are pinned as ranges and `vp check --fix` was run after adding them.
- [ ] No changeset: nothing user-facing changes.

## Blocked by

- None — can start immediately.

40.title: Ship the status plugin: three hooks that append status events
40.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec sections: "The status plugin", "Sessions" (the events file), "Testing Decisions" (the plugin tested from both sides). Prior art: the `prototype/status-hooks` branch (its plugin and recorded runs) and the seed's appendix A.7.

## What to build

A Claude Code plugin shipped inside the extension package and loaded by the launch with `--plugin-dir`, with no install step. It has three hooks, SessionStart, SessionEnd and StopFailure, each the exec-form handler running the report script with Node, asynchronous. The seed's six hooks shrink to these three.

The report appends one JSON line to the file named by `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS`: the ticket from `HERO_SYNERGY_TICKET`, the hook name, the session id, the detail the payload carries (`source` for a start, `reason` for an end, `error` for a failure), the write time as an ISO string, and the raw payload fields it received, so the Cockpit can decode leniently. With no `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS` in the environment it exits 0 and writes nothing. It never throws: an empty or malformed stdin still appends a line carrying whatever it got.

The plugin is plain JavaScript with no dependencies and no build step, listed in the extension's packaged files.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Spawning the report with the two env variables and a SessionStart, SessionEnd or StopFailure payload on stdin appends exactly one line with the fields above; a test asserts the line for each hook.
- [x] With `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS` unset the report exits 0 and the file is untouched.
- [x] An empty or malformed stdin exits 0 and appends a line that carries the raw fields it got.
- [x] The prototype's recorded event files are ported as fixtures and a test reads them to pin the line shape the Cockpit will decode.
- [x] The hooks manifest declares exactly the three hooks with `async: true`; `claude --plugin-dir` accepts the directory, checked by hand once and recorded in the close-out comment.
- [x] A changeset naming `hero-synergy`, written for the person updating.

## Blocked by

- None — can start immediately.

lastComment.body:
## Close-out

Shipped on `main` in 58d31e0 (rebased from the `worktree-40` branch).

**What landed**

- `packages/vscode/claude-plugin/`: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (`hero-synergy-status`), `hooks/hooks.json` with exactly `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd` and `StopFailure`, each the exec-form handler `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/report.mjs` with `async: true`, and `report.mjs`, plain JavaScript with only `node:fs` imported, no build step. The directory was already in the extension's `files`.
- **The line** `report.mjs` appends to `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS`, in this key order: `ticket` (from `HERO_SYNERGY_TICKET`, `null` when unset), `hook`, `session`, `detail` (`source` for a start, `reason` for an end, `error` for a failure), `at` (write time, ISO string), `payload` (the whole stdin object). When stdin is not a JSON object, `payload` is `null` and an extra `stdin` field carries the text as it came (capped at 64 KB). Decoded fields that are missing or of the wrong type are `null`; the payload keeps them as they were. With no `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS` it exits 0 and writes nothing. It never throws: an append failure goes to stderr and the exit code stays 0.
- `packages/vscode/test/status-plugin/report.test.ts`, 37 tests through `vp test`: the report spawned as a hook with each of the three payloads; the unset-variable case (file untouched, nothing on stdout or stderr); empty, malformed, non-object and wrong-typed stdin; three hooks in a row; no ticket; a missing directory. The hooks manifest is read and pinned (three hooks, exec-form, async). The recorded runs are replayed through the real report and must reproduce the checked-in lines.
- `packages/vscode/test/fixtures/status-events/`: the prototype's nine runs from [Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably? (#6)](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/6), ported as `<run>.payloads.jsonl` (the probe's records for the three hooked events, the whole payload Claude Code sent) and `<run>.events.jsonl` (what the report writes for them, `at` stamped with the recorded fire time). A README gives the provenance (Claude Code 2.1.287) and the run table. The `UserPromptSubmit`, `Notification` and `Stop` records are not ported; those hooks were dropped in #28.
- `.changeset/status-plugin-three-hooks.md`, `hero-synergy: minor`.

**Checked by hand once**, as the acceptance criteria ask: on Claude Code 2.1.292 in the devcontainer, `claude --plugin-dir packages/vscode/claude-plugin --model haiku -p "Reply with the single word: pong"` with `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS` and `HERO_SYNERGY_TICKET=40` set accepted the directory, answered, and the file held two lines:

```
{"ticket":"40","hook":"SessionStart","session":"0dcf11b3-…","detail":"startup","at":"2026-10-07T15:23:49.192Z","payload":{…,"hook_event_name":"SessionStart","source":"startup"}}
{"ticket":"40","hook":"SessionEnd","session":"0dcf11b3-…","detail":"other","at":"2026-10-07T15:23:51.610Z","payload":{…,"hook_event_name":"SessionEnd","reason":"other"}}
```

`claude plugin details <path>` does not take a directory (it wants an installed plugin name), so the real session is the check.

42.title: Model the snapshot and read map and ticket bodies with the drift catalogue
42.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec sections: "The snapshot", "Reading bodies: the conventions the scout knows", "Testing Decisions" (one fixture per warning code). [ADR 0002](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-effect-schema-models-all-boundary-data.md) and [ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md). Prior art: the `prototype/scout` branch (code-only readers for every legacy form, and the legacy fixture to port); the `research/wayfinder-conventions` branch.

## What to build

Core's model of what the scout produces, and the readers that fill it from Markdown bodies. The snapshot shape settled in #26 is the contract between the scout and the Cockpit (a type shape, so inlined from the spec):

```ts
Snapshot { tracker: { kind: 'github', owner, repo } | { kind: 'local' }; repoRoot; collectedAt (ISO)
           maps: WayfinderMap[] (tracker order); unmapped: Ticket[]; warnings: Warning[] }
WayfinderMap { number, title, ref, body (raw Markdown), tickets: Ticket[] (map order)
               destination | null, notes | null,
               decisions: { number | null, title, link, gist }[],
               notYetSpecified: { text, tickets: number[] }[], outOfScope: { text, tickets: number[] }[],
               warnings }
Ticket { number, title, ref, state: 'open' | 'closed', type: research | prototype | grilling | task | null,
         claim: { by: string[] } | null, blockedBy: Blocker[], body (raw Markdown),
         resolution: { body, author | null, at | null } | null,
         outcome: 'decided' | 'out-of-scope' | 'unrecorded' | null, gist: string | null, warnings }
Ref = { tracker: 'github', url } | { tracker: 'local', path (repo-relative) }
Blocker = { number, title, state, ref }      Warning = { code, detail? }
```

Modeled with Effect Schema; core exports the types and parse functions, never schema objects; boundary data is plain JSON with no transforms, timestamps staying ISO strings. The names are `WayfinderMap`, `Ticket`, `Snapshot`, `Ref`, `Claim`, `Blocker`, `Warning`, plus the closed unions `WarningCode` (drift) and `HealthCode`, both `{ code, detail? }` so the webview imports one `Warning` type and tells the kind from the code.

The readers. The current map body has five H2 sections: Destination, Notes, Decisions so far, Not yet specified, Out of scope. The legacy heading sets from the conventions research (the Notes / Decisions so far / Fog body, the Deferred form, the single-file form) are recognised by their headings and read with a quiet `map-body-legacy` warning naming the form; some sections present but not all is `map-body-partial`; none recognisable is `map-body-free-form`; both keep the map with nulls. A Decisions-so-far line is `- [title](link) — gist` or `- [title](link): gist`, both accepted with no warning, split at the first separator after the link's closing parenthesis; a line matching neither is `decision-line-unparsed`; a decision linking a still-open ticket is `decision-links-open-ticket`. Out of scope and Not yet specified entries keep their text and the ticket numbers they link. `outcome` classifies a closed ticket by the map alone (in Decisions so far is decided, linked from Out of scope is out-of-scope, neither is unrecorded with `closed-unrecorded`); the tracker's state reason is ignored. `gist` is the map's own line for the ticket, verbatim, no computed fallback. Ticket conventions: type from the `wayfinder:<type>` label, with `type-as-line`, `type-missing` and `type-several`; any assignee is the claim and `wayfinder:claimed` is `claim-legacy-label`; `blockers-as-text-line` and `blockers-as-slugs`; `parent-as-part-of-line`; `no-question-heading`; `closed-no-resolution`; `blocker-outside-map`; `no-map`; `unknown-status`; `ticket-title-from-slug`; `map-title-from-directory`; `map-no-destination`; `children-as-task-list`; `unknown-wayfinder-labels`.

Facts are never guessed: what cannot be read is null plus a warning. Provenance is a warning, not a field. Core ships the codes only; severity and copy live in the Cockpit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parsing a JSON snapshot round-trips: the decoded and encoded shapes are the same and timestamps stay strings.
- [ ] One fixture per drift code in the catalogue, and a test per code asserting the warning it yields and the nulls beside it.
- [ ] This repo's own map body, recorded from the tracker, reads with every field exact: its decisions with gists, its out-of-scope lines with ticket numbers, its destination.
- [ ] The legacy fixture from the scout prototype yields the same warnings the prototype reported, one per drift point.
- [ ] No changeset.

44.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec sections: "Finding the repo and its tracker", "Reading a local tracker", user story 18. [ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md). Decided in #3 and #26.

## What to build

The scout's entry for a window, in core over the file-system service and the process runner. Given the workspace folders in order, it finds the one repo the Cockpit shows: the first folder whose repo root has a tracker doc; else the first folder inside a git repo, which gets the setup message. A folder inside a repo (a package opened alone) resolves its root through `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, and the tracker is read there. A folder holding several repos is "no repo was found". The tracker doc decides by its heading alone, with no model: the agent tracker doc first, then the link in the Agent skills block of the repo's CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md. `# Issue tracker: GitHub` and `# Issue tracker: Local Markdown` are supported; any other heading is an unsupported tracker, named in the error. One tracker per repo: a GitHub doc means `.scratch` maps are not read, and the reverse. The cases where maps cannot be shown are a typed scout error, not snapshot fields: no tracker doc, unsupported tracker, GitHub doc with a remote not on github.com, `gh` missing or not logged in, no repo found.

The local reader: every directory under `.scratch` is a map, its `map.md` the body and its `issues/NN-<slug>.md` files the tickets in number order; no open or closed state exists, a user hides a map by removing its directory. `state` comes from `Status: resolved`, `claim` from `Status: claimed` with an empty `by`, `type` from the `Type:` line, `blockedBy` from the `Blocked by: NN, NN` line, `resolution` from the `## Answer` section, titles from the first H1 with `ticket-title-from-slug` or `map-title-from-directory` when they fall back. A local map's number is its 1-based position in directory order; a ticket's number is its file prefix; refs carry repo-relative paths, from which a launch takes the effort slug. The issue files of an effort with no readable map go to `unmapped`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fixture `.scratch` tree with two efforts, seeded in the in-memory file system, yields a snapshot with both maps numbered by position, their tickets in number order, states, claims, blockers and answers.
- [ ] Each tracker-finding case above yields the typed error or the repo root a test asserts, over a seeded file system and the replay runner for `git`.
- [ ] A workspace of two folders where only the second has a tracker doc picks the second; a folder two levels inside a repo resolves the root and reads the tracker doc there.
- [ ] An effort directory with issue files and no map puts those tickets in `unmapped` with `no-map`.
- [ ] No changeset.

## Blocked by

- #42 Model the snapshot and read map and ticket bodies with the drift catalogue

Resolved: on `main` through [PR #75, Find the repo and its tracker, and read a local tracker into a snapshot](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/75). Core gains `packages/core/src/scout/`, built in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/44` and rebased onto the merge of #43 before the PR. `vp check`, `vp test` (170 tests), `vp run build` and the extension typecheck pass from the repo root; no changeset.

**Done**

- `scout/find-repo.ts`: `findRepo(folders)`, the scout's entry for a window. The first folder, in workspace order, whose repo root has a tracker doc; else the first folder inside a git repo, which gets `NoTrackerDoc`; else `NoRepoFound`. The root comes from `git -C <folder> rev-parse --show-toplevel`, so a package opened alone reads the tracker at its repo root. A folder holding several repos is no repo. The result is a `RepoTracker`: the root, the `Tracker` for the snapshot and the doc's repo-relative path.
- `scout/tracker-doc.ts`: the doc decides by its first H1 alone. `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` first, then the `.md` the `## Agent skills` block of `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` links or backticks (the `### Issue tracker` subsection when there is one). `# Issue tracker: GitHub` and `# Issue tracker: Local Markdown`, case and spacing aside, are supported; any other heading is `UnsupportedTracker` naming it, and a doc with no H1 names `null`.
- `scout/errors.ts`: `ScoutError` = `NoRepoFound | NoTrackerDoc | UnsupportedTracker | NoRemote`, Effect tagged errors, never snapshot fields.
- `scout/local.ts`: `readLocalTracker(repoRoot)` and `collectLocal(repoRoot)`. Every directory under `.scratch` is a map numbered by its 1-based position in directory order; `map.md` is the body and `issues/NN-<slug>.md` the tickets in number order; a stray file under `.scratch` is nothing. Refs carry repo-relative paths (`.scratch/<effort>/map.md`, `.scratch/<effort>/issues/NN-slug.md`). State, claim, type, blockers, resolution and the fallback titles come from `readSnapshot` as #42 built it. An effort with issue files and no map yields no map, and its tickets go to `unmapped` with `no-map`. A repo with no `.scratch` has no maps and no error. `collectedAt` comes from Effect's `Clock`.
- Fixtures: `packages/core/fixtures/local-tracker/`, a repo on the local tracker with three efforts (two maps, one `/to-spec` effort without a map) and a stray file, seeded into the in-memory file system by `seed.ts`. `.gitignore` re-includes `.scratch` under a fixtures directory; core's tsconfig includes `fixtures/**/*.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] The fixture `.scratch` tree yields both maps numbered 1 and 2 by position, tickets in number order, `closed` from `Status: resolved`, `claim: { by: [] }` from `Status: claimed`, blockers resolved from `Blocked by: 01, 02` with each blocker's state, the `## Answer` as the resolution, `decided` and `out-of-scope` outcomes from the map's own lines (`local.test.ts`).
- [x] Every tracker-finding case yields its typed error or the repo root, over a seeded file system and the replay runner for `git` (`find-repo.test.ts`, 22 cases).
- [x] Two folders where only the second has a tracker doc picks the second; a folder two levels inside a repo resolves the root and reads the doc there; a folder outside any repo ahead of one with a doc is skipped; the first repo without a doc gets the setup message.
- [x] The map-less effort's tickets land in `unmapped` with `no-map`.
- [x] No changeset.

**Two readings I settled, and why**

- **A GitHub doc with a remote off github.com is not an error here.** This ticket's text lists it among the typed errors, but the spec's "Finding the repo" section says "tries, shows the error" and #45 says "a non-github.com remote is tried and its error returned", and the snapshot's `Tracker` has no host field to carry one. So `findRepo` takes `owner/name` from the remote `gh` would pick (upstream, then github, then origin, else the first listed), on any host, and the collect's `gh api graphql` shows what github.com answers. Only a repo with no remote, or a remote URL that names no owner and repository, is `NoRemote`.
- **`gh` missing or not logged in is not raised here.** Nothing in the finder runs `gh`; #45's collect does, and it adds those cases to `ScoutError` in the shape its typed failures take (exit 4, 401, rate limits, network, timeout).

**Facts later tickets lean on**

- Local ticket numbers are file prefixes, unique within an effort and not across the tracker: `billing-rewrite/issues/01-…` and `cockpit-colors/issues/01-…` are both ticket 1. The local reader feeds one `Collected` per effort to `readSnapshot` for that reason. Anything keying tickets by number across maps on a local tracker (a `needsYou` set in `SessionFacts`, a cache, a selection) has to key by `ref.path` or by map and number together; #43's derived functions already scope every lookup to one map.
- A local map's number is its position among all effort directories, map or not, so adding or removing a directory renumbers the maps after it. The `ref.path` is the stable identity; the number is for display beside the name.
- `readLocalTracker` needs `FileSystem` only; `findRepo` needs `FileSystem` and `ProcessRunner`, and runs `git -C <folder> rev-parse --show-toplevel` once per folder until a doc is found, plus `git -C <root> remote -v` once for a GitHub doc. The replay layer keys on the exact arguments, so a test records one line per folder.
- `RepoTracker.trackerDoc` is the doc's repo-relative path, for the Tree's setup and unsupported messages to link.
- The e2e fixture workspace (`packages/vscode/test/fixtures/workspace`) still has no `.scratch`; the core fixture under `packages/core/fixtures/local-tracker/.scratch` is the tree to copy or seed when the Tree ticket needs maps to render.

45.title: Collect a GitHub tracker's open maps through gh api graphql
45.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec sections: "Collecting from GitHub", "Finding the repo and its tracker" (the GitHub cases), "Testing Decisions" (seam 3, the replay runner). Decided in #9, #27 and #32. Prior art: the `research/scout-graphql-query` branch and the query on `prototype/scout`.

## What to build

The scout's GitHub collect, through the process runner only. Only github.com, through `gh api graphql`, no preview headers; the repo is `owner/name` from the git remote; a non-github.com remote is tried and its error returned. Map-first: one cheap list of the open `wayfinder:map` issues with the label names passed explicitly (the API matches a label list as an OR and ignores unknown names), together with the repository's `wayfinder:` labels for the unknown-labels check; then aliased `issue(number:)` blocks for each open map with its sub-issues (capped at 100 per parent, within one page), and for each sub-issue its labels, assignees, state, body, the last comment, `parent`, and `blockedBy` nodes with each blocker's number, title, state and URL. A closed blocker stays in the nodes with its state; the scout gates on each blocker's state, never on the summary counts. Every request also selects `rateLimit { remaining resetAt }`, and the figures ride on the result for the budget.

At most 5 maps per request, requests one after another, never in parallel; `gh` is killed after 20 s. Closed maps are never collected. Tickets that are not native sub-issues of an open map are never collected; a map body listing children as a task list earns `children-as-task-list` instead, so `unmapped` is empty on GitHub by construction. Relationships are read fresh on every collect; no per-item caching, no change probes. Raw stdout is parsed whatever the exit code, since `gh` skips `--jq` on GraphQL errors and exits 1 for nearly everything; headers come from `gh api -i`. A NOT_FOUND on one map's block drops that map; any other error fails the whole collect with a typed reason the refresh policy will act on: not logged in (exit 4 or 401), rate-limited, secondary limit (403 or `retry-after`, carrying the value), network, timeout, 5xx.

Recorded `gh` outputs for this repo's own maps are the fixtures, and they pin the exact query shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Against the recorded fixtures, the collect yields the snapshot of this repo's maps with every ticket typed, claimed, blocked and classified as the tracker shows.
- [ ] A fixture where one map returns NOT_FOUND yields the other maps and no error; a fixture with another GraphQL error yields the typed failure.
- [ ] Fixtures for exit 4, a 401, a 403 with retry-after, a 5xx and a timeout each yield their typed reason, and the rate-limit figures ride on a successful result.
- [ ] Seven open maps are collected in two requests of five and two, in order, and each request body matches the recorded query text exactly.
- [ ] A closed blocker in the nodes does not gate; a task-list child is not collected and the map carries `children-as-task-list`.
- [ ] No changeset.

## Blocked by

- #42 Model the snapshot and read map and ticket bodies with the drift catalogue

53.title: Refresh on causes, cache the last snapshot and protect the gh budget
53.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec section: "The scout's budget: when it runs, what it keeps", user stories 49 to 54. Decided in #27 and #28.

## What to build

The refresh policy as pure extension logic over a clock, wired to the host's triggers. Triggers: the view becoming visible (activation with the view open included), the window gaining focus, a file under `.scratch` changing on a local tracker (debounced one second), and the Refresh button; the session triggers join in the disagreements ticket. Not triggers: tool-call events, activation while the view is hidden. Never a timer. One collect at a time and at most one queued behind it; automatic triggers need 60 s since the last successful collect; the button ignores the gap and attaches to a running collect instead of starting another; the local tracker has no gap and no pause.

The cache: one entry per repo in extension storage, the last successful snapshot stamped with its collect time, keyed by tracker kind, repo identity (`owner/name` or the repo root path) and the snapshot's schema version, rendered immediately at activation and swapped when a fresh one lands; nothing cached per issue. VS Code's progress bar while a collect runs, no row spinners.

Budget protection: when `remaining` drops below 1,000 points, automatic triggers pause until `resetAt` and the repo row shows "paused until HH:MM", the button still works; at 0 remaining automatic triggers stop until the reset and the button shows "rate-limited until HH:MM" without calling; a secondary limit pauses for `retry-after` or 60 s, doubling on each repeat and resetting after a success; not logged in shows the `gh auth login` fix; network failure, timeout or 5xx is shown as such and the next trigger tries again. Nothing retries on its own. The repo row's age is emphasised with the reason when the last collect failed or the snapshot is older than 5 minutes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Over a test clock, an automatic trigger 30 s after a success does not collect and one at 61 s does; two triggers during a collect coalesce into one queued collect; the button during a collect attaches rather than starting another; the local tracker has no gap.
- [ ] A result with 999 remaining pauses automatic triggers until `resetAt` and the row text says so; 0 remaining stops them and the button says rate-limited without calling; a secondary limit backs off 60, 120 and 240 s and resets after a success.
- [ ] Activation renders the cached snapshot before any process spawns (host tier); a cache under an older schema version or another repo identity is ignored.
- [ ] A `.scratch` change triggers one collect after the debounce on a local tracker and nothing on a GitHub tracker.
- [ ] The age is emphasised after a failed collect and after 5 minutes.
- [ ] A changeset naming `hero-synergy`, written for the person updating.

## Blocked by

- #50 Show a GitHub tracker's maps in the Tree, with the tracker's error states and the live CI job
