55.title: Release from CI: the Release PR, the registries, the GitHub release and the backfill
55.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec sections: "CI, release and the canary" (the release workflow, the backfill, the release notes), "Repository housekeeping that ships with the build" (changesets), user stories 69 to 71. Decided in #20 and #4. Prior art: the seed's appendices A.3 and A.6. Out of scope: the one-time registry setup and the v0.1.0 release run itself.

## What to build

The release workflow runs on pushes to `main` and detects its mode itself. If any changeset file exists, it runs the Changesets version action to open or update the **Release hero-synergy** PR. Otherwise, if no `v<version>` tag exists for the version in the extension's manifest, it builds, runs `vsce package`, publishes to each registry whose `PUBLISH_*` repository variable is `true` (the Marketplace through the `marketplace` environment with Entra ID login and `--azure-credential --skip-duplicate`; Open VSX with `--trusted-publishing --skip-duplicate`), then always creates the GitHub release `v<version>` with the VSIX attached, even when a registry step failed. No select-mode, pack or publish jobs from Changesets, no Changesets tags, no approval gate on the environment.

A backfill workflow on `workflow_dispatch` with a tag input downloads that release's VSIX and publishes it to every registry switched on, reusing the same scripts and environment. Release notes come from a small script: title `hero-synergy v<version>`, the extension's changelog entry, an install line with the Marketplace and Open VSX links each only if its variable is on and the attached VSIX, and the compare link; `Updated dependencies` lines stripped; core's changelog never linked. Changelog files stay excluded from formatting. The Changesets config keeps the fixed group, every changeset naming `hero-synergy`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The release-notes script has tests: a changelog entry with an `Updated dependencies` line yields notes without it; each registry link appears only when its variable is on; the compare link spans the previous tag.
- [ ] A push to `main` with a changeset present opens or updates the Release PR, observed once with the run linked in the close-out comment.
- [ ] The publish mode passes workflow linting and a review against the spec: it is not run, since the first run is the v0.1.0 release itself.
- [ ] The backfill workflow, dispatched with an existing tag and every registry variable off, downloads the VSIX and reaches the publish steps as skipped.
- [ ] A failing registry step does not stop the GitHub release step.
- [ ] No changeset.

## Blocked by

- #51 Finish the manifest, the listing and the README, and package the VSIX

prs.title: Release from CI: the Release PR, the registries, the GitHub release and the backfill

**Blocked on a setting.** The push to `main` ran the Release workflow in version mode ([run](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/actions/runs/37688479453)). The mode detection picked `version`, and `changeset version` ran. Creating the PR then failed: `GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests`. To fix it, turn on **Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests**, then re-run that run. The **Release hero-synergy** PR should open. Don't merge it: that is the v0.1.0 release run.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] Release-notes script has tests: `Updated dependencies` stripped, each registry link only when its variable is on, compare link spans the previous tag (`scripts/release-notes.test.ts`, 17 tests).

56.title: Build the canary that files upstream breaks
56.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec section: "CI, release and the canary" (the canary), user story 72. The glossary's Canary and Upstream break; the upstream register. Decided in #34. The open items the build must prove: the keepalive resetting the 60-day clock; `claude` with no credentials printing its outputs on a runner; `claude plugin install` working non-interactively there.

## What to build

A separate daily workflow at an off-the-hour minute plus `workflow_dispatch`, one job per upstream. `claude`: the native installer, latest, no login; `--version` through the Cockpit's parser, `--help` containing every launch flag in the register, `agents --json` decoding with the registry schema, `plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official` then `plugin list --json` decoding. `skills`: the latest tag, `main`, and the marketplace install; every `SKILL.md` frontmatter decodes, and the wayfinder skill and the GitHub tracker template still carry the headings, labels and operations the scout reads. `vscode`: the host and end-to-end tiers on stable, Linux and macOS. `gh`: the live job on the schedule. `node`: `vp test` on the latest Node.

A break is only what the Cockpit would choke on: a schema that fails to decode, a suite that fails, a flag missing from `--help`; new fields and new skills never break. On a break: one open issue per upstream titled `Upstream break: <upstream> <version>`, labelled `canary` and `ready-for-human`, assigned to Eduardo, with the failing contracts and register rows, last green and first red from the previous step summary, the error, up to 2 KB of output inline and the full capture as an artifact; later runs comment only when the failing set or the version changes; a return to green comments and leaves the issue open. On green: nothing on `main`, a step summary of the versions seen. Each run re-enables itself against GitHub's 60-day idle disable, falling back to a dated commit per run if that does not reset the clock. The register gains a "Watched by the canary" list per upstream, and each open item's outcome is recorded there.

57.title: Drive a ticket's session state from status events
57.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec sections: "Sessions" (the state, the events file, ended, no registry entry while a terminal is alive), "The status plugin", user stories 24, 30, 31 and 32. Decided in #21, #28 and #6. Prior art: the recorded runs on `prototype/status-hooks`; the events-file findings in `research/windows-behavior` (a byte-offset reader with a slow poll).

## What to build

The events file and the session state machine. One events file per repo identity under the extension's global storage, so it persists across restarts and is a ticket's memory of its last session id; created before it is watched; read fully once at activation and then incrementally by byte offset; a slow poll backs the watcher where events can be dropped; compacted by the Cockpit above a size cap, keeping the last event per ticket.

The reducer is a pure function tested with sequences. `SessionStart` turns starting into live and carries the session id. `StopFailure` is failed and sticks until the registry next reports busy. `SessionEnd` carries the ended reason (`prompt_input_exit` is "exited", then `logout` and `other`) and is final for its session id whatever the line order; `clear` and `resume` reasons never end a ticket, and the next `SessionStart` in the same terminal carries the new id. Ended is one state whose detail is text, in order of trust: the `SessionEnd` reason, else the terminal's exit status, else "process gone"; the terminal closing is the truth for ended on every platform. A Cockpit terminal with no `SessionStart` after 15 s shows "no status yet, the session may be waiting at the trust dialog, open the terminal", the only timer in the Cockpit. Each ticket row and its Focus pane show the state and status word with the time since the last status event. The container badge counts the sessions that need me, failed for now. With the Cockpit hidden the terminal and status-event listeners stay on; a soft target of about a second from event to Tree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The reducer passes a table of sequences: start then end; end before start; failure then busy; clear then a new start; resume; two tickets interleaved; the 15 s hint; each yielding the state, status, id and detail the spec names.
- [ ] The events-file reader over the in-memory file system reads incrementally, survives a compaction, and treats a late `SessionEnd` as final.
- [ ] In the end-to-end tier, the stub `claude` writes SessionStart then SessionEnd on a script and the Tree shows live, then ended with "exited", within about a second each.
- [ ] The badge shows 1 for a failed session and 0 for working, starting and ended.
- [ ] A changeset naming `hero-synergy`, written for the person updating.

59.title: Show drift in the Tree, the Focus pane and the Detail
59.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec sections: "Reading bodies: the conventions the scout knows" (the drift catalogue table), "Warnings: drift and health in the Cockpit", user stories 55 to 58. Decided in #29 and #35.

## What to build

The level-and-copy table for every drift code lives in the Cockpit, never in core: loud when what the Cockpit shows may be wrong or missing, quiet when something old or odd was still read correctly. Every message states what was found plus a one-line hint on the current convention; the hints on `map-body-partial`, `unknown-wayfinder-labels` and `decision-line-unparsed` add "a newer mattpocock-skills may write this; check for a hero-synergy update". No warning carries an Action.

| Level | Loud | Quiet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| snapshot | | `unknown-wayfinder-labels` |
| map | `map-body-free-form`, `map-body-partial`, `map-no-destination`, `decision-line-unparsed`, `decision-links-open-ticket` | `map-body-legacy`, `children-as-task-list`, `map-title-from-directory` |
| ticket | `type-missing`, `type-several`, `blockers-as-slugs`, `no-map`, `closed-unrecorded`, `closed-no-resolution`, `unknown-status` | `parent-as-part-of-line`, `blockers-as-text-line`, `type-as-line`, `claim-legacy-label`, `no-question-heading`, `blocker-outside-map`, `ticket-title-from-slug`, `unknown-wayfinder-labels` |

A loud warning puts ⚠ after a ticket's title (the warning codicon in the editor-warning colour) with the loud messages on hover; quiet leaves the row unmarked. A map row shows ⚠ when the map or any of its tickets, open or closed, has a loud warning, with counts in the tooltip; the Finished fold adds nothing up; drift never changes ordering. The Focus pane shows one line per loud warning and one muted line for all quiet ones ("n old forms"); the ⚑ Map row's pane adds "k tickets with drift"; clicking opens the Detail at its Drift section; nothing appears when there is no drift. The Detail ends with a Drift section, hidden when empty, each entry with message, detail and hint, a map's section grouping its tickets' warnings under `#n title` with closed tickets included, and a ⚠ chip in the header scrolling to it when anything is loud. An unreadable map renders the sections that were read, then "This map's body isn't in the current form; shown as written", then the raw body; its Tree row still unfolds into tickets, with the Fog and Decisions nodes left out when null. Unmapped tickets go in a synthetic folded ⚠ Unmapped node above the Finished fold, shown only when not empty. Drift dismissals go in workspace state keyed on the exact detail. No badge, no ordering effect, no notification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every drift code has a level, a message and a hint, and a test asserts the table covers the whole `WarningCode` union.
- [ ] The Cockpit tests render ⚠ on a loud ticket and its map and nothing on a quiet one, the pane lines, the Drift section grouped per ticket, the free-form map as written with its folds left out, and the Unmapped node.
- [ ] A dismissed entry stays hidden after a reload and reappears when its detail changes (host tier).
- [ ] In the end-to-end tier, the fixture's legacy map shows ⚠ and its Detail ends with the Drift section.
- [ ] A changeset naming `hero-synergy`, written for the person updating.

## Blocked by

- #52 Open the Detail for a map or a ticket

60.title: Read live status from the registry
60.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec sections: "Sessions" (liveness, status registry first, needs you, the performance bar), user stories 24, 25, 26 and 32. The registry contract in the upstream register. Decided in #21 and #28.

## What to build

Claude Code's registry as the second source of liveness, for everything the Cockpit's own terminal cannot see: hand-started sessions, sessions in another window, and a process that exited non-zero while VS Code keeps the pane open. The files under Claude Code's sessions directory are never parsed: a watcher on that directory is the trigger and `claude agents --json` through the process runner is the reader, debounced one second or more, stopped while the Cockpit is hidden with one refresh when shown.

While the registry lists a session its word is the status: `busy` is working; `idle` is waiting for you; `waiting` with `permission prompt` is needs approval, with `input needed` or `dialog open` is waiting for you, with `sandbox request`, `worker request` or any unknown value is needs approval. The Cockpit records the session id from the registry while live, since the entry vanishes about a second after exit. A session matches a ticket by the leading `#<number>` of its name within the repo, whoever started it; the worktree path is corroboration, never the key. A second live session with the same prefix (Claude Code renames it `<name>-<two words>`) is shown under the ticket with a warning; the Cockpit kills nothing. A last event of live with no registry entry shows that event's status with its age; the keep-or-remove prompt at exit stays under the last status with its age. The badge now counts waiting for you, needs approval and failed. No terminal scraping; the Cockpit never edits Claude Code's trust configuration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given recorded registry outputs and event sequences, the reducer yields the status words above, registry first, with a test per waiting detail and one for an unknown value.
- [ ] A registry entry named `#12 …` with no Cockpit terminal makes ticket 12 live with its status and records its id; two entries with that prefix show the duplicate warning.
- [ ] The watcher stops while the view is hidden and spawns nothing; showing the view refreshes once (host tier with the in-memory layers).
- [ ] In the end-to-end tier, the stub `claude` serves `agents --json` on a script of busy, idle and waiting, and the Tree shows working, waiting for you and needs approval, the badge counting the last two.
- [ ] A changeset naming `hero-synergy`, written for the person updating.

## Blocked by

- #57 Drive a ticket's session state from status events

[ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md). Decided in #21 and #5.

## What to build

An ended ticket offers **Resume**, by session id, in a fresh terminal from the repo root with the plugin reattached and the env set again (Claude Code returns to the worktree by itself but does not restore `--plugin-dir`), and **Launch fresh**, the plain Work ticket command, which reopens an existing worktree. 62.title: Name the disagreements between the tracker and the session side
62.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec sections: "Sessions" (situations where the tracker and the session side disagree), "The scout's budget" (the session triggers), user stories 35 to 38. Decided in #28.

## What to build

The tracker alone says claimed, open, closed and blocked; the session side alone says alive and what status; neither overrides the other, and each named situation lasts until the next refresh. A session starting or live here on an unclaimed ticket leaves the frontier at once and shows "live · claim not on tracker yet" until the first snapshot collected after `SessionStart` shows the claim, then the warning "not claimed on the tracker" if it still doesn't. A ticket closed on the tracker with a live session moves to the map's decisions fold as **wrapping up**, keeping its status, focus terminal and badge count. A ticket claimed by someone else with a session live here shows "claimed by <login> on the tracker, session live here". A live session whose `#number` matches no collected ticket goes to one **Sessions without a ticket in view** row at the repo level, counting for the badge, with focus terminal as its only action and its ended record kept.

The refresh policy gains its session triggers: a ticket session's `SessionStart`, a ticket session ending, and the registry reporting a session gone, each subject to the 60 s gap like any automatic trigger.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each situation renders its text in the Cockpit tests from a view model, and the live-but-unclaimed ticket is off the frontier so the ▶ moves to the next one.
- [ ] Over the test clock, `SessionStart` triggers a collect; the snapshot after it carrying the claim clears the "not yet" text, and one without it shows the warning.
- [ ] A ticket closed on the tracker with a live session sits in the decisions fold as wrapping up and still counts for the badge when waiting.
- [ ] A live registry session `#999` with no ticket in the snapshot appears in the repo-level row, counts for the badge when waiting, and keeps its ended record after it ends.
- [ ] A changeset naming `hero-synergy`, written for the person updating.

63.title: Report health in a pinned row and log the environment to the output channel
63.body:
## Parent

#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit. Spec sections: "Warnings: drift and health in the Cockpit" (health, the catalogue), "The Cockpit's surfaces" (activation logging), user stories 59 to 62, 66 and 68. Decided in #35, #30 and #17.

## What to build

Health is produced by the extension host, never the scout. The floor is checked with one `claude --version` at activation, on the Refresh button and when the resolved path changes, comparing the leading `x.y.z` numerically: below 2.1.212 is loud with the hint naming `claude update` "or upgrade through your package manager"; above the tested ceiling says nothing. A registry that fails to decode gives one loud entry naming the upstream and the version it saw, and every affected session shows **status unknown**, with no badge count, focus terminal and the ended record kept. The plugin and skill codes come from discovery.

| Level | Code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| loud | `claude-not-found` | no `claude` resolved; every Action greyed with the reason |
| loud | `claude-below-floor` | the version parses and is below 2.1.212 |
| quiet | `claude-version-unreadable` | no leading `x.y.z`; the floor check is skipped |
| loud | `registry-unreadable` | `claude agents --json` is not an array of entries |
| loud | `registry-entry-unreadable` | an entry lacks `sessionId`, `name` or `status` |
| loud | `registry-status-unknown` | `status` is not `busy`, `idle` or `waiting` |
| loud | `hook-payload-unreadable` | `SessionStart` without `session_id` (the session still goes live) |
| quiet | `hook-reason-missing` | `SessionEnd` without `reason` |
| loud | `plugin-manifest-unreadable` | a plugin's manifest or its `skills` array can't be read |
| loud / quiet | `skill-unreadable` | a `SKILL.md` frontmatter can't be parsed: loud for `wayfinder` and `to-spec` |
| loud | `skill-missing` | no `wayfinder`: Work ticket unavailable |
| quiet | `skill-installed-twice` | a skill found as a local copy and in a plugin |
| quiet | `plugin-disabled` | the plugin that holds a needed skill is disabled |

Repo-level entries (every health code and `unknown-wayfinder-labels`) live in one pinned row at the top of the Tree: ⚠ when any entry is loud, labelled "Health · n warnings" or "Health · 1 note", hover listing the loud messages, the Focus pane listing every entry with its hint and a Dismiss, the row absent when empty. Health dismissals go in global state keyed on code and detail. Every machine message names the upstream and the version it saw; every hint names the one thing to do. The output channel logs at activation the app name, app host, VS Code version, platform and the resolved `claude` path, and each health entry once with what was seen: the version line, the first 2 KB of the failing output, the parse error. No badge, no ordering effect, no notification, no Action on any warning.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every health code has a level, a message and a hint; a test asserts the table covers the whole `HealthCode` union.
- [ ] Over the replay runner, a version fixture of 2.1.211 yields the loud floor entry and 2.1.212 none; an unparsable registry yields its entry and the affected sessions show status unknown with no badge count and focus terminal kept.
- [ ] The Cockpit tests render the pinned row's label, hover and pane for a loud set and a quiet set, and nothing when empty.
- [ ] A dismissed health entry stays dismissed in another workspace (global state) and returns when its detail changes.
- [ ] The host tier asserts the activation log lines and that an entry is logged once across two refreshes.
- [ ] A changeset naming `hero-synergy`, written for the person updating.

## Blocked by

- #58 Offer the skill Actions: To spec, Chart a map, Run skill, Setup and the installs
- #59 Show drift in the Tree, the Focus pane and the Detail
- #60 Read live status from the registry

64.title: next, the terminal pre-alpha of the Cockpit
64.body:
## Destination

By the release of v0.1.0, `scripts/next.mjs` lists, launches, resumes and watches the tickets of spec #37 and of this map from the terminal, with the same warnings the Cockpit shows. Everything it shares with the Cockpit comes from `@hero-synergy/core`. It then becomes the prior art the official CLI map starts from; nothing in it ships.

## Notes

- This map carries execution. Every ticket is a `wayfinder:task` resolved when its change is on `main`: no grilling, no research, nothing left to decide. The route follows the spec's own order: each ticket reuses what one spec ticket delivers and is blocked by it.
- `next` stays one plain-Node file in `scripts/` with no `package.json` and no npm dependencies of its own. It imports core's built `dist/` by relative path, so `pnpm install` and `pnpm exec vp run build` are its prerequisites, as the worktree routine in `CLAUDE.md` already requires. It never becomes a workspace package here.
- It reads and launches, never writes to the tracker, never runs git except read-only ([ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md)).
- No tests. Anything with logic moves into core, which is tested. A ticket may move a pure function from the extension into core when `next` needs it; it never adds to core behaviour the Cockpit does not use.
- Tickets are chained in map order, so one session at a time edits the one file. Each is also blocked by the spec ticket whose delivery it reuses, so this map's frontier trails the spec's.
- Sessions start with `node scripts/next.mjs <number>` from the `main` checkout: wayfinder form, map and ticket as URLs. A session claims the ticket first, does the work in its worktree, runs `pnpm exec vp check --fix`, commits, `git pull --rebase origin main`, `git push origin HEAD:main`, posts the resolution comment, closes the ticket and appends its line to Decisions so far.
- Personal tooling for the v0.1.0 build. Read spec #37 and `CONTEXT.md` before each ticket. Reading a spec's sub-issues is the one thing `next` does that the Cockpit never will; it stays in the script.

## Decisions so far

- [Read this map beside the spec, and say in the header that next lives until v0.1.0 ships](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/65) — `next` reads spec #37 then map #64 from a constant list in one request; `--list` shows both, no argument launches the first takeable across both, the launch line carries the ticket's own parent; the header says it lives until v0.1.0 ships.
- [Read with core: the scout's collect, the frontier derivation and the registry decoder replace the script's own](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/66) — the map side runs through core's collect, snapshot, frontier and registry decoder via a new `collectGitHubPromise`; the spec keeps its own query; `--list` is unchanged.
- [Launch with core's command string: the Work ticket command the Cockpit runs, skill form chosen by a flag](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/67) — the launch is core's `workTicket` (name, worktree, `--plugin-dir`, `HERO_SYNERGY_*` env); `--implement` swaps only the skill line; core's skill discovery warns, never gates; core gained `discoverSkillsPromise`.
- [Show each ticket's session state from the registry and the status events](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/68) — the session reducer and registry grouping moved into core, with `sessionsOf` and `sessionText`; `--list` shows the Focus pane's state word per ticket from one read of the events file and the registry, and an ended session is takeable again.
- [Resume an ended session and show its worktree](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/69) — `next resume <number>` runs the Cockpit's Resume for an ended session, by id or by name via core's new `resumeEnded` (the Cockpit now calls it too), and refuses any other ticket, offering `next <number>` as the relaunch when nothing is running; `--list` shows each ticket's worktree (path, branch, what is not on `main`) through core's `worktreeText` and `readWorktreesPromise`.
- [Print the warnings: drift, health and the disagreements between the tracker and the session side](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/70) — `--list` prints Health at the top, drift under its map or ticket row (loud warnings one per line, the old forms as one muted count per map) and the disagreements under their ticket, with the Cockpit's codes and words and no gating; the drift table, the health table, `disagreementOf` and `sessionTitleOf` moved into core and the Cockpit now calls them too.

## Not yet specified

Nothing left. Both patches were absorbed by the tickets above, with no ticket of their own (checked 2026-11-16):

- A blocker outside the map: `next` reads its maps through core's collect, snapshot and frontier rules (483e716), so it agrees with the Tree on what is takeable, an outside blocker included.
- The plugin dir and status events of a session started outside VS Code: `next` launches with core's Work ticket command (efc4b2a), passing the status plugin with `--plugin-dir` and the events file `.scratch/hero-synergy-events.jsonl`.

## Out of scope

- A workspace package, a published CLI and any command beyond list, launch and resume: the official CLI map after v0.1.0, which starts from `next` as prior art the way the prototype branches fed the spec.
- A local tracker: `next` reads this repo's GitHub tracker only.
- Refresh, caching and the gh budget: each run is one call, on demand.
- Reading spec issues in the Cockpit: the spec keeps the Tree to maps; `next`'s spec reading stays its own.

Make `next` the second consumer of `@hero-synergy/core`: its own GraphQL for maps, its frontier rules and its hand-parsed registry go, and core's take their place.

If core's entry points are Effect programs, `next` runs them through whatever core already exposes for the extension host; moving a small Promise-returning wrapper into core is in bounds, inventing one that only `next` uses is not.
- This map is read through core's GitHub collect (#45) and its snapshot (#42); the frontier, the order and the counts come from core's derivation (#43), so `next` and the Tree agree on what is takeable, including a blocker that sits outside the map.
- Spec #37 is not a map and core never reads one, so the spec's sub-issues keep the script's own query. Only the map side moves.
- `claude agents --json` is decoded with core's registry decoder (#46); the "live session" note keeps its meaning, a session named `#<number> …` that is not done.

The image rules: HTTPS only, SVG only from trusted badge providers, and whether GIF, animated WebP and APNG pass. Which HTML survives on the Marketplace and in the Extensions view (`align`, `<picture>`, `<details>`, `<video>`, tables), and how the Extensions view themes and sizes images.
- **Package size.** What images under `media/` add to the VSIX through `files` in `package.json`, and whether README media should live outside the package.
- **Verified publisher.** What the verified badge takes for publisher `dbarjs`, and what the page shows without it.

115.title: How do the best developer-tool READMEs and extension listings open?
115.body:
## Question

What do the READMEs and Marketplace pages that developers admire put on their first screen, and in what order does the rest follow?

To find out, from about a dozen examples read at the source, each one linked:

- **Examples.** Widely installed VS Code extensions (GitLens, Error Lens, Pretty TypeScript Errors, the Total TypeScript extension, Claude Code's own extension), agent tools (Claude Code, Cline, Continue, Aider), and TypeScript projects known for their READMEs (Effect, Vite, tRPC, Zod, and `mattpocock/skills` itself). Swap any of them for a better one and say why.
- **The first screen.** The logo or hero image. The one-line pitch, its length and its verbs. The demo (GIF, video, screenshot or none). Badges. The call to action.
- **The rest.** The order of problem, features, quick start, requirements, configuration, how it works, credits and contributing, and how long each section runs.
- **Companions.** How a tool built on someone else's project credits it and says it is unofficial without sounding apologetic.
- **What fails.** Badge walls, stale GIFs, marketing words, walls of settings.

End with what to take for each surface: the repository README, the listing README and the one-line About. Findings go to `docs/research/readme-patterns.md` on a `research/readme-patterns` branch.

## Context

- Today's READMEs are [`README.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/README.md) and [`packages/vscode/README.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/packages/vscode/README.md).
- [#117 What does Hero Synergy say about itself?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/117) and [#119 Prototype the two READMEs and the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/119) wait on this.

## Resolution

Findings: [`docs/research/readme-patterns.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/readme-patterns/docs/research/readme-patterns.md) on the branch `research/readme-patterns`, commit `18b8606`. 19 examples were read at the source: each README raw from GitHub, and each listing through the Marketplace gallery API together with the README it actually serves. The rendering rules were read in the source of vsce 4.0.0 and of VS Code.

**Name, one line, proof.** Tools you watch at work put a real image on the first screen: a before-and-after pair (Pretty TypeScript Errors), a GIF captioned with what to notice (tRPC), a screenshot and then an uploaded video (claude-squad). Taglines run 4 to 10 words and definitions 15 to 22; the clearest Marketplace descriptions are 8 or 9 words. Matt's own README shows no image at all and argues in the first person ("real engineering - not vibe coding"), with a time-boxed install that ends in "Bam - you're ready to go."

**Sessions with live status are no longer what sets Hero Synergy apart.** GitLens Pro (53 million installs) now shows Claude Code "Agent sessions" with "live state: working, idle, or needs input", and turns an issue into a worktree and a session. claude-squad, Vibe Kanban and opcode all run many sessions in worktrees. Only the wayfinder map and its frontier are Hero Synergy's own.

**The two READMEs render under different rules.** GitHub plays an uploaded video inline, at most 10 MB per upload on a free plan; the 24.5 MB trailer encodes to 2.9 MB at 720p and 30 fps. The listing takes only https PNG or GIF. vsce rewrites relative paths from the repository root, ignoring `packages/vscode`, and links any whitespace-preceded `#<digits>` to this repository's issues, even inside code. VS Code's details page drops `<picture>`.

**The one-line About is empty.** A shared link unfolds into a card with no line, only the avatar and "0 Stars". The Extensions view shows roughly the first 40 characters of the description. Draw.io Integration reuses one sentence as its README line, its About and its description.

**Unofficial, without apology.** Draw.io Integration opens "This unofficial extension integrates Draw.io ... into VS Code."; opcode puts "not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Anthropic" in a note on its first screen. Two Claude Code companions credit Anthropic without any disclaimer, and three named after Claude have since been renamed.

**The trailer makes claims the product does not.** Beyond the stylized board and the "+ CLI" outro, the command it types names the session without its `#<number>`. The shipped Work ticket runs `claude -n "#<number> <title>" -w <number> …`, and the listing README says the Cockpit matches sessions by that leading number.

What [#117 What does Hero Synergy say about itself?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/117) should take:

- Lead the line with the map and the frontier; sessions second, status third.
- One sentence, reused for the About and the manifest description: 8 to 17 words, at most about 110 characters, with the job done in the first 40. Verb first, glossary nouns, upstreams by their own names, none of the marketing words listed in the doc.
- Keep "unofficial" as an adjective in the first sentence and keep today's not-affiliated line. Keep upstream marks out of the name and the art.
- Weigh the AI category against Other, at most 30 keywords in the searcher's words, the Marketplace listing as the About's website, and topics. Candidate lines are in the doc, labelled as candidates.

What [#119 Prototype the two READMEs and the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/119) should take:

- A section order for each README, three first-screen variants for the repository README (trailer first, product first, problem first) and two for the listing (screenshot first, loop first).
- The trailer only on GitHub, re-encoded under 10 MB, captioned as stylized, with a real screenshot on the same screen. Its beats become headings over real screenshots. On the listing, a text link or a title-card poster.
- Fix, rather than caption, the two claim-level differences (the CLI outro and the typed command); caption the board.
- Listing images as absolute https PNG or GIF URLs pinned to the release tag, or relative paths with `--baseImagesUrl` in the `package` script. Add `--no-gitHubIssueLinking` to `package`. No logo, badges or self-links on the listing, and short settings.

**Not verified:** how the Marketplace website renders `<video>`, `<picture>` and inline styles, since nothing was published; whether VS Code's details page actually plays a video, which its sanitizer and content policy allow but which was not rendered; the 40-character estimate; Eduardo's GitHub plan, which sets the video limit at 10 MB or 100 MB; whether GitHub truncates a long description on the default card; why the Claude-named companions were renamed, which no page read explains (and none of this is legal advice); and whether the release workflow pushes the version tag before it packages.

116.title: Capture the real Cockpit in screenshots and a loop
116.body:
## Question

What does the shipped Cockpit look like at its best? Take the screenshots and the loop that the READMEs choose from, with a run that can take them again.

- **Data.** A demo workspace whose map reads like real work: a local tracker with one map that holds a destination, three or four decisions so far, a frontier of three or four tickets of different types, two blocked tickets and some fog. Sessions on frontier tickets in each status the Tree shows (working, waiting for you, needs approval), and one ended. No Health warnings unless a shot is about them.
- **Shots.**
  - The Tree with the map unfolded and its frontier.
  - A frontier ticket's Focus pane with Work ticket and its exact command.
  - A ticket session's terminal, named `#<number> <title>`, beside the Tree.
  - The Activity Bar badge.
  - The Detail of the map.
  - The Detail of a ticket with its neighbourhood.

  Dark Modern first, plus one light-theme shot of the Tree.
- **Loop.** One short recording of the real flow: ▶ on a frontier ticket, its terminal opening as `#<number> <title>`, and the row going from starting to working to waiting for you. Make it a loop that plays by itself, in the formats [#113 What do the GitHub repository page, its link preview and a profile pin accept?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/113) and [#114 What do the VS Code Marketplace page and the Extensions view accept?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/114) allow, small enough for the Marketplace page to load fast.
- **How.** Through the e2e tier's Playwright-on-Electron harness and its stub `claude`, as a script run with `vp run`, never by hand. Shoot at device scale 2, cropped to the window or to the part a shot is about. Linux under xvfb works in the devcontainer. The macOS CI runner may render fonts better, so try both and keep the better.
- **Where.** The script lands on `main` through a PR, with tests for any logic it adds. The images and the loop go on a `prototype/screenshots` branch, linked from the resolution with a contact sheet.

Resolved when the shots and the loop are on the branch and one command takes them again.

## Context

- The views and their words are in [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md). The e2e tier is `packages/vscode/test/e2e/`, decided in [#18 How is the extension tested?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/18).
- AFK: the session drives it alone.
- [#119 Prototype the two READMEs and the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/119) waits on these shots.

## Resolution

The shots and the loop are on [`prototype/screenshots`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/tree/prototype/screenshots), and its [contact sheet](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/prototype/screenshots/README.md) shows the macOS and Linux sets side by side. One command takes them again: `vp run capture` in `packages/vscode`. It landed on `main` in [#122 Capture the real Cockpit in screenshots and a loop](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/122).

### What the run does

- It packs the VSIX and installs it into a fresh VS Code stable, so the window is a user's window. The title bar has no "[Extension Development Host]", and no other extension is installed.
- It opens a demo repo on the local tracker (`test/capture/demo.mts`). The map is #1 Docs search, with four decisions, two fog items and one out-of-scope line. Of its open tickets, #5 grilling, #6 prototype and #7 task are claimed. #8 research and #9 prototype are on the frontier. #10 and #11 are blocked.
- The sessions are served through the e2e tier's stub `claude` and the registry. #5 is working, #6 needs approval, #7 is waiting for you and #9 has ended (exited). They start apart, so the ages read about 1m, 40s and 20s. The Activity Bar badge shows 2. There are no Health warnings.
- The shots are taken at device scale 2, each cropped to its part:
  - `tree-dark.png` and `tree-light.png`;
  - `badge.png`;
  - `focus-pane.png`: Work ticket and its exact command on #8;
  - `focus-pane-session.png`: #7 waiting for you;
  - `detail-map.png`;
  - `detail-ticket.png`: #10, waiting on #5 and clearing the way for #11;
  - `window-map.png`: the Tree beside the Detail of the map;
  - `terminal.png`: the `#8 Typo tolerance` terminal beside the Tree and its Detail.
- The loop: ▶ on #8 opens the terminal named `#8 Typo tolerance`, and the row goes from starting to live, then to "not claimed on the tracker". The session then claims the ticket, as `/wayfinder` does, and the row goes to working, then to waiting for you. It is about 9 s long and is written three ways:
  - `launch.gif`, about 260 to 280 KB, for the Marketplace, the Extensions view and GitHub;
  - `launch.webp`, 90 to 190 KB;
  - `launch.mp4` (H.264, faststart), about 230 KB, for a GitHub `user-attachments` upload.

  All three are far under the 10 MB limit that [#113 What do the GitHub repository page, its link preview and a profile pin accept?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/113) found.
- Linux without a display re-runs itself under `xvfb-run`. The new **Capture** workflow runs on Linux and macOS, on demand and on PRs that touch the capture run, and uploads `capture-linux` and `capture-macos` artifacts. A run takes about 3 minutes per OS.
- The logic has 22 unit tests in `test/capture/*.test.mts`. They cover the crops, frame trimming, the ffconcat list, the ffmpeg arguments, the WebP encoder pick, the contact sheet, and the demo map and its registry.

### Keep macOS

The macOS set is better: SF Pro is crisper, the status words are bold, and the title bar is plain. Two caveats come with it:

- The runner's screen makes its window 1440 × 676 rather than 900 tall.
- Homebrew's ffmpeg has no WebP encoder, so `macos/launch.webp` was encoded afterwards from `macos/launch.mp4` with the run's settings.

The Linux set is the full-height alternative.

### For [#119 Prototype the two READMEs and the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/119)

- The terminal in the shots is empty, because the stub `claude` prints nothing.
- On a local tracker, the Work ticket command has no `-w <number>` and says "No worktree on a local tracker: this session shares the checkout". A GitHub map would show the worktree form that [#115 How do the best developer-tool READMEs and extension listings open?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/115) quoted.
- The Detail of a local ticket renders its file as written: a second title, then `Type:` and `Blocked by:` as a paragraph.
- After the claim, the Focus pane's Claim is empty, because a local `Status: claimed` names no one.
- If the READMEs need the GitHub look, the demo can move to a stubbed GitHub tracker. That is a change to `demo.mts` and the stub, not a new harness.

### A side effect to undo, or keep

On its first attempt, the run's `code --install-extension` call was forwarded through the devcontainer's VS Code IPC hook. It installed this branch's 0.1.2 VSIX into the devcontainer's own VS Code server, replacing the 0.1.0 VSIX installed there earlier on 2026-10-09. The run now strips `VSCODE_IPC_HOOK_CLI` before calling the CLI. The extension that shipped as 0.1.2 is the same code, so this is harmless, but it was not asked for.

117.title: What does Hero Synergy say about itself?
117.body:
## Question

Which words does every surface share? That means the one line, the tagline, the opening paragraph, the first terms a newcomer meets, and the words people search with.

Decide with `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling`:

- **The reader.** Who the first line is written for: someone already working with `mattpocock/skills` and `/wayfinder`, someone on Claude Code without the skills, or someone browsing the Marketplace for AI tools. What each must understand by the end of the first screen.
- **The one line.** One sentence for the GitHub About, the pin and the Marketplace `description`, within the limits that [#113 What do the GitHub repository page, its link preview and a profile pin accept?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/113) and [#114 What do the VS Code Marketplace page and the Extensions view accept?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/114) found. Today the manifest says "Unofficial cockpit for mattpocock/skills: wayfinder maps, frontier tickets and named Claude Code sessions in VS Code terminals." The trailer says "A VS Code cockpit for mattpocock/skills".
- **The tagline.** Whether the trailer's "A hero with this many skills needs synergy." leads, and where it appears.
- **The problem.** Whether the trailer's three beats, "One giant map. Too many terminals. Which one needs you?", become the READMEs' why, or other words do.
- **Terms.** Which glossary words reach the first screen (Cockpit, map, ticket, frontier, session), and how each one is introduced to someone who has never run `/wayfinder`.
- **Credit.** How `mattpocock/skills` and Claude Code are named and linked, and the final wording of the unofficial line, within the naming rules that [#114 What do the VS Code Marketplace page and the Extensions view accept?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/114) found.
- **Discovery.** The GitHub topics, the Marketplace keywords and category, and whether the listing carries the Preview flag while the version is 0.x.

The resolution states every string in its final form, ready to paste.

## Context

- The trailer's beats and words are in the map's Notes. [#115 How do the best developer-tool READMEs and extension listings open?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/115) gathers how other projects word theirs.
- HITL: decided with Eduardo.
- [#119 Prototype the two READMEs and the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/119) and [#120 Upload the trailer, fill in the About box, set the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/120) wait on these words.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Decided with Eduardo on 2026-10-09 in two grilling rounds. Every string below is final and ready to paste.

### The reader

The first screen is written for someone already using `mattpocock/skills` and `/wayfinder`, with maps on the tracker and too many terminals open: only they can use the extension the day they find it, and only the map and its frontier set Hero Synergy apart from GitLens Pro, claude-squad, Vibe Kanban and opcode. By the end of the first screen:

- that reader knows it is their wayfinder maps in VS Code, a session per frontier ticket, and live status;
- a Claude Code user without the skills knows it needs Matt Pocock's skills, and has the link to install them;
- a Marketplace browser can tell from the description that it is for wayfinder maps.

No "what is an agent" prose.

### The one line

The GitHub About, the pin and the manifest `description`, word for word:

```text
See your wayfinder frontier and start each ticket as a named Claude Code session, with live status.
```

99 characters, 17 words. The Extensions list shows "See your wayfinder frontier and start…" (37); a Marketplace search tile shows "See your wayfinder frontier and start each ticket as a named Claude Code sessi…" (78); GitHub search and the pin show it whole. It carries neither "unofficial" nor `mattpocock/skills`: each would spend the first 37 characters, and the README's first sentence carries both.

### The opening paragraph

The first paragraph of both `README.md` and `packages/vscode/README.md`:

```markdown
Hero Synergy is an unofficial Visual Studio Code cockpit for the wayfinder maps of [Matt Pocock's skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills). It shows each map's frontier, the tickets you can take right now, and starts any of them with one click as a [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs) session named after the ticket. Every session's status stays in view, so you can see which one needs you.
```

Worktrees are left out because they hold only on a GitHub tracker; they belong in "How it works".

### The unofficial line

Today's wording, unchanged, in both READMEs, directly under the opening paragraph:

```markdown
Hero Synergy is a personal project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Matt Pocock or Anthropic.
```

### Credit

- In prose, link each upstream once, at first mention: `[Matt Pocock's skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills)` and `[Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs)`. In plain-text fields, write `mattpocock/skills` and "Claude Code".
- Each README's first sentence says "Visual Studio Code"; "VS Code" after that and in the plain-text fields.
- No trademark sentence, no "Powered by" badge, no Claude or Anthropic marks or colours, and no mention of Microsoft: "Hero Synergy" uses none of the three brands.
- The Credits section at the end of the repository README:

```markdown
Hero Synergy relies on the wayfinder conventions of [Matt Pocock's skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) (MIT) and launches your own [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs) CLI. It ships neither.
```

### The problem

The repository README only, after the trailer and its screenshot. The listing goes from the opening paragraph straight to its screenshot.

```markdown
**One giant map. Too many terminals. Which one needs you?**

A wayfinder map holds more work than one agent session can, so you work its tickets in many sessions at once, often across several maps. Soon there are more terminals than you can watch, and the one waiting for you is somewhere among them.
```

The bold line is the trailer's slogan, kept verbatim; the prose under it is literal, since a repo usually has many maps.

### The tagline

```text
A hero with this many skills needs synergy.
```

It never leads and is never the description or the About. It appears as:

- the repository README's sign-off, the last line before Credits;
- the trailer's outro;
- the social card, under the Seal and the name. A thumbnail carries eight words, not a 99-character line, and the link preview's text already shows the About line.

It stays off the listing README, which stays literal.

### Terms on the first screen

- Only **map, frontier, ticket, session**. Map gets the skills link, and "wayfinder" carries the rest; frontier is glossed at first use as "the tickets you can take right now"; ticket and session are plain English.
- **Cockpit** is a lowercase common noun in the first sentence, and capitalised from "What you see" on.
- **Tree, Focus pane, Detail, Needs you and claim** stay below the first screen.
- The glossary's _Avoid_ words (dashboard, board, backlog; agent or job for a session) never appear in prose. "Agent session" in the problem paragraph is Matt's phrase for a Claude Code session in general.

### Discovery

The manifest, `packages/vscode/package.json`:

```json
"displayName": "Hero Synergy",
"description": "See your wayfinder frontier and start each ticket as a named Claude Code session, with live status.",
"categories": ["AI"],
"keywords": [
  "agent",
  "agent skills",
  "ai",
  "claude",
  "claude code",
  "github issues",
  "issue tracker",
  "matt pocock",
  "mattpocock",
  "sessions",
  "skills",
  "terminal",
  "wayfinder",
  "worktree"
],
"preview": true,
```

- `AI` alone, so the breadcrumb reads "AI"; `Chat` doesn't fit, since there is no chat.
- `preview: true` while the version is 0.x; it is removed at 1.0.0. It shows only in the Marketplace and VS Code headers, never in search.
- No competitors' names and no `anthropic`, which could read as affiliation.

The GitHub About box:

```sh
gh repo edit dbarjs/hero-synergy \
  --description "See your wayfinder frontier and start each ticket as a named Claude Code session, with live status." \
  --homepage "https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=dbarjs.hero-synergy" \
  --add-topic vscode-extension,claude-code,mattpocock,agent-skills,wayfinder,github-issues,git-worktree,terminal
```

The website points at the Marketplace listing, as Draw.io Integration, Error Lens and Pretty TypeScript Errors do, since there is no other site. The pin shows the description; nothing else to set.

### Where it lands

- [#119 Prototype the two READMEs and the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/119) drafts with the opening paragraph, the unofficial line, the problem, the tagline, the credits and the terms rules.
- [#120 Upload the trailer, fill in the About box, set the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/120) runs the `gh repo edit` line.
- [#121 Land the front door and release it](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/121) puts the manifest block in its PR, `preview` included.

123.title: Launch AFK sessions with permissions bypassed in isolated environments
123.body:
## Destination

A spec, handed to `/to-spec` and filed as `ready-for-agent` build issues, for letting the Cockpit launch AFK sessions with permissions bypassed: two machine-scoped settings, off by default, the isolated-environment detection that can gate them, and exactly which Actions carry the flag.

## Notes

- Planning map: tickets resolve decisions, nothing is built here. Grilling tickets invoke `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling`; read `CONTEXT.md`, [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md) and `docs/upstream.md` first.
- Every `claude` command is built in `packages/core/src/claude/actions.ts`; the flag joins the argv, so the Focus pane's command shows it (an Action always shows its exact command).
- Settled while charting:
  - **Shape**: `heroSynergy.sessions.skipPermissions` = `off` (default) | `afkSessions` | `allSessions`, and `heroSynergy.sessions.skipPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated`, boolean, default `true`. Final names: `heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissions` = `off` | `afkTickets` | `allSessions` and `heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated` (see the Actions ticket below).
  - **AFK sessions**: ticket sessions that are not HITL — research, task, and any ticket labelled `ready-for-agent`. Prototype and grilling keep their prompts; plain Actions get the flag only under `allSessions`.
  - **Flag**: bypass only, sent as `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` unless research says otherwise.
  - **Scope**: both settings are `"scope": "machine"`, like `heroSynergy.claude.path`, so a cloned repo's workspace settings can never turn bypass on.
  - **Detection**: a pure function in core over facts the host collects at activation (`vscode.env.remoteName`, env vars, marker files). Remote-SSH and WSL are not isolated. It never gates anything but whether the flag is added; a quiet health warning says when the setting is on and no isolation was found.
  - **Hands off**: the Cockpit never accepts Claude Code's bypass warning for you, never writes `~/.claude`, never sets `IS_SANDBOX`.

## Decisions so far

- [Signals of an isolated environment in the extension host](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/125) — `vscode.env.remoteName` (`dev-container`, `attached-container`, `k8s-container`, `apple-container`, `codespaces`) is unspoofable by a repo; `/.dockerenv` and `/run/.containerenv` come second; env vars are only labels (a shell profile reaches the host); a container is not a sandbox, so bypass stays the user's call.
- [Claude Code's bypass-permissions contract](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/124) — the two flags are equivalent since before the floor; `--resume` (by id or name) drops bypass, so resumes must pass it again; root refuses bypass unless the undocumented `IS_SANDBOX=1`; `disableBypassPermissionsMode` silently downgrades; the one-time interactive dialog leaves no registry entry, so the session shows "starting" until accepted.
- [The isolated-environment detection rule](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/126) — isolated when `remoteName` is allowlisted, else `/.dockerenv`, else `/run/.containerenv`, first match wins; `/run/.toolboxenv` (toolbx, distrobox) vetoes the markers; env vars never count; facts read once at activation into a pure `isolationOf`; glossary term **Isolated environment** added.
- [Which Actions carry the bypass flag, and the settings' final names](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/127) — the ticket decides, not the Action: on an AFK ticket (`ready-for-agent`, or research/task without `ready-for-human`; untyped is HITL) every ticket Action bypasses under `afkTickets`, resumes included; plain Actions only under `allSessions`; installs and the scout never; `Ticket` gains `labels`, label strings come from `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`; settings renamed to `bypassPermissions` (`off` | `afkTickets` | `allSessions`) and `bypassPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated`; glossary terms **AFK ticket** and **Bypassed session** added.
- [The health warnings bypass adds](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/129) — two codes from a pure core `bypassHealth`: `bypass-not-isolated` (quiet, detail says what detection saw) and `bypass-refused-as-root` (loud, uid 0 with no `IS_SANDBOX`/`CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP`; the flag is still added); the bypass dialog gets no code, only a starting hint that names it; `disableBypassPermissionsMode` isn't detected.

## Not yet specified

Nothing left. The spec, [Launch AFK sessions with permissions bypassed in isolated environments](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/155), settled the last patch (the README section and the `docs/upstream.md` rows) in its Docs section.

## Out of scope

- The `next` CLI: it reads no VS Code settings.
- A general permission-mode passthrough (`acceptEdits`, `auto`, …): this map is bypass only.
- A per-ticket bypass toggle in the Focus pane.
- Setting up the sandbox or container itself.

Its build is [#179](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/179), which covers the whole spec in one PR (core, the Cockpit, the README, `docs/upstream.md` and a changeset), so the spec isn't split into tickets. The PR waits for Eduardo's merge.

124.title: Claude Code's bypass-permissions contract
124.body:
## Question

What exactly is Claude Code's bypass-permissions contract, on the floor and the tested ceiling in `docs/upstream.md`?

- Are `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` equivalent, and since which version?
- Is there a one-time confirmation dialog on first bypass use, where is its acceptance stored, and does `-w` or a fresh worktree re-trigger it?
- Does bypass refuse to start as root without `IS_SANDBOX=1` (or another variable), and what does it print?
- Does `--resume <id>` or `--resume <name>` keep the permission mode, or must the flag be passed again?
- What do `disableBypassPermissionsMode` (managed or user settings) and auto mode's classifier do to a session launched with the flag — refused, downgraded, silently ignored?
- How does a bypassed session appear in `claude agents --json` (does `waitingFor` ever report a dialog)?

Cite primary sources (changelog, docs, `--help`) and run the real binary in this devcontainer where it is safe.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Findings: [`docs/research/claude-code-bypass-contract.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/bypass-contract/docs/research/claude-code-bypass-contract.md) on `research/bypass-contract`. Measured on 2.1.212 (the floor), 2.1.289 (the ceiling) and 2.1.292, always with a scratch `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and never `~/.claude`. The devcontainer runs as uid 1000, not root; the root cases ran through `sudo`.

- **Are the two flags equivalent?** Yes. The docs say "The `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag is equivalent", and both give `permissionMode: bypassPermissions` on 2.1.212, 2.1.289 and 2.1.292. Both are older than the floor: the skip flag is in changelog 1.0.7, and `--permission-mode` is undated, first mentioned in 2.1.132. Keep `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`.
- **Is there a one-time dialog?** Yes, in interactive sessions only. It comes after the trust dialog, and "No, exit" is preselected. Accepting writes `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt: true` to user settings (`~/.claude/settings.json`). The key can also come from local, `--settings` or managed settings, but not from project settings. Accepted in user settings, a `-w` or fresh worktree doesn't bring it back (read from code; not run with `-w`). `-p` never shows it.
- **Does root refuse?** Yes. It prints `--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons` and exits 1, even for `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`. In code, the check is skipped when `IS_SANDBOX=1` or `CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP` is set; the docs only say "a recognized sandbox". Measured on all three versions.
- **Does `--resume` keep bypass?** No. Resuming by `<id>` or `<name>` starts in the default mode (auto on 2.1.292); the docs say so, and I measured it. The flag must be passed again, so `resumeById` and `resumeByName` in `actions.ts` need it as well as `workTicket`.
- **What do `disableBypassPermissionsMode` and auto mode do?** `disableBypassPermissionsMode` downgrades the session; it doesn't refuse it. The session starts in the built-in default (auto on 2.1.289/2.1.292, `default` on 2.1.212). Interactively the footer shows "Bypass permissions mode was disabled by settings"; `-p` prints nothing. Since 2.1.257, project settings can't set `defaultMode: bypassPermissions`. Auto mode's classifier never runs in a bypassed session, because the flag wins over the auto default. Ask/deny rules, `AskUserQuestion` and critical-path `rm` still stop a bypassed session; the `rm` prompt denies after two minutes since 2.1.281.
- **How does it look in `claude agents --json`?** It shows no permission mode. While the bypass dialog is open there is no registry entry at all (`[]`), so `waitingFor` never reports it. The Cockpit sees "starting" until someone accepts. Once running, the session can still be `waiting` for a `permission prompt` (critical `rm`, ask rules) or `input needed`.

Gaps: `-w` with the dialog wasn't run, and the scratch config had no login, so no real tool call ran in bypass. `IS_SANDBOX` and `CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP` are undocumented. The docs say "rejects" for `disableBypassPermissionsMode`, but the binaries downgrade.

125.title: Signals of an isolated environment in the extension host
125.body:
## Question

Which signals tell a VS Code extension host that it runs in an isolated environment — a devcontainer, GitHub Codespaces, a plain Docker/Podman container, Gitpod or similar — and how trustworthy is each?

- Every `vscode.env.remoteName` value (`dev-container`, `attached-container`, `codespaces`, `wsl`, `ssh-remote`, `tunnel`, …) and what each means for isolation.
- Environment variables: `REMOTE_CONTAINERS`, `REMOTE_CONTAINERS_IPC`, `VSCODE_REMOTE_CONTAINERS_SESSION`, `CODESPACES`, `GITPOD_WORKSPACE_ID`, `container`, `DEVCONTAINER`, … — who sets them, and whether they reach the extension host process.
- Marker files: `/.dockerenv`, `/run/.containerenv`, cgroup hints.
- For each: can a repository or a user's shell profile spoof it, and what does it look like in this devcontainer (record the real values)?

Cite primary sources (VS Code and dev-containers docs, `microsoft/vscode-remote-release`, Codespaces docs).

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Findings: [`docs/research/isolation-signals.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/isolation-signals/docs/research/isolation-signals.md) on branch `research/isolation-signals`.

**Answer.** `vscode.env.remoteName` is the strongest signal: it is the authority prefix chosen by the resolver extension, and only allowlisted extensions can register resolvers. Marker files (`/.dockerenv`, `/run/.containerenv`) come second: the container engine creates them and a repo can't. Environment variables are hints only, because VS Code and Dev Containers copy the user's login-shell environment into the extension host, so a profile can add any of them. A repo can't spoof any signal on a non-isolated machine through `.vscode/settings.json` or `devcontainer.json`. The one path is `.envrc` via direnv, and only when the user runs `code .` from that shell, since the CLI's env becomes the window's `userEnv`.

Suggested rule for the core function: isolated when `remoteName ∈ {dev-container, attached-container, k8s-container, apple-container, codespaces}`, or `/.dockerenv` or `/run/.containerenv` exists. Env vars only label what was found. Caveat: "container" is not "sandbox". A repo's `devcontainer.json` controls mounts, `--privileged` and the Docker socket, so the setting stays the user's call.

| Signal | Meaning | Reaches the host | Spoofable by a repo | Value here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `remoteName` `dev-container` / `attached-container` / `k8s-container` / `apple-container` | Dev Containers window in a container (resolver names from the 0.470.0 VSIX) | Yes (API, all hosts) | No | `dev-container` (inferred) |

126.title: The isolated-environment detection rule
126.body:
## Question

What is the isolated-environment detection rule? From the signals research found: which count as isolated, which order they are checked in, what the result names (the signal that matched, shown to the user), whether `skipPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated` can be fooled by a repo, and how detection is tested (a pure core function over collected facts). Add the glossary term for an isolated environment to `CONTEXT.md`.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Grilled with Eduardo; every recommendation accepted.

**What counts.** A window is in an isolated environment when either holds, checked in this order, first match wins:

1. `vscode.env.remoteName` ∈ {`dev-container`, `attached-container`, `k8s-container`, `apple-container`, `codespaces`};
2. `/.dockerenv` exists;
3. `/run/.containerenv` exists.

Environment variables never count and are not used as labels: a shell profile or `.envrc` can set any of them.

**Toolbx/distrobox veto.** If `/run/.toolboxenv` exists, the marker-file tier (2 and 3) doesn't count. Toolbx creates it ([docs](https://containertoolbx.org/doc/)); distrobox's init `touch`es it too. Both share `$HOME`, the SSH agent and D-Bus by design. The veto doesn't overrule `remoteName`.

**Remote names.** `ssh-remote`, `wsl`, `tunnel` and no remote don't count by name, but don't veto either: the markers still decide. That's how an SSH session into a Gitpod/Ona container is caught.

**Result shape** (core):

```ts
type IsolationSignal =
  | { kind: 'remote'; remoteName: 'dev-container' | 'attached-container' | 'k8s-container' | 'apple-container' | 'codespaces' }
  | { kind: 'marker'; path: '/.dockerenv' | '/run/.containerenv' }
type Isolation =
  | { isolated: true; signal: IsolationSignal }
  | { isolated: false; vetoedBy: '/run/.toolboxenv' | null; remoteName: string | null }
```

On a match, the result is the matched signal and nothing else. On no match, it carries the `remoteName` seen and any veto, so the not-isolated health warning can say what it saw ("Remote-SSH, no container marker", "toolbx container — shares your home").

**Facts.** Collected once at activation by the host: `remoteName` plus three `exists` checks through core's `FileSystem`. Neither changes while a window is open. On Windows the checks come back false, so there's no special case.

**Can a repo fool it?** It can't fool the detection. A repo can't set `remoteName` or create files at `/`. `.envrc` only reaches env vars, which don't count. Both settings are machine-scoped. A repo's `devcontainer.json` *can* mount the Docker socket or `$HOME`. That's accepted on purpose: isolated means "in a container", not "sandboxed". The glossary and the README say so, and nothing inspects the container's config.

**Testing.** `isolationOf(facts)` is a pure core function. It gets a table test over every `remoteName` (all five allowlisted names, plus `ssh-remote`, `wsl`, `tunnel` and `undefined`) crossed with every combination of the three files. The host's fact collector is tested against an in-memory `FileSystem` layer. The resolver names become `docs/upstream.md` contract rows. A canary check for them is out of scope for this map.

**Glossary.** **Isolated environment** added to `CONTEXT.md` (fb5d677 on `main`).

127.title: Which Actions carry the bypass flag, and the settings' final names
127.body:
## Question

Which Actions carry the bypass flag, and what are the settings finally called? Given the bypass contract research found: Work ticket, Launch fresh, Resume by id and Resume by name, and the plain Actions (Chart a map, To spec, Run skill…, Setup) under each mode; how "AFK session" is read from the snapshot (mode and the `ready-for-agent` label); the final setting names, enum values and descriptions; and the glossary term for a bypassed session in `CONTEXT.md`.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Grilled and agreed. Glossary: **AFK ticket** and **Bypassed session** added to `CONTEXT.md` on `main` (90eeb0c), with a relationship line.

- **AFK ticket**: labelled `ready-for-agent`, or typed research or task and not labelled `ready-for-human`. A ticket with no type label is HITL. A task ticket that hands you a checklist still counts: bypass only removes prompts, and the snapshot can't tell the two kinds apart.
- **Snapshot**: `Ticket` gains `labels: ReadonlyArray<string>`, a plain fact from the tracker (a local tracker's body labels line, else empty). A pure core function `isAfkTicket(ticket, triage)` decides, so the snapshot stays free of session logic.
- **Label strings**: read the `ready-for-agent` and `ready-for-human` rows of `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` (right-hand column); fall back to the default names when the file is missing or unreadable. This is a new contract row in `docs/upstream.md`. A wrong name only means fewer sessions bypass, which is the safe direction.
- **Which Actions carry the flag** (the isolation gate applies on top of every row):

  | Action | `off` | `afkTickets` | `allSessions` |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Work ticket, Launch fresh | – | AFK tickets | every ticket |
  | Resume (by id), Resume by name | – | AFK tickets | every ticket |
  | Chart a map, To spec, Run skill…, Setup | – | – | ✓ |
  | Install plugin, Install with npx, the scout's background `claude` | – | – | – |

  The ticket decides, not the Action. Resumes repeat the flag because `--resume` drops it, and Resume by name gets it too, even for a session you started by hand.
- **Settings** (both `"scope": "machine"`):
  - `heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissions`: `off` (default) | `afkTickets` | `allSessions`.
    - Value descriptions: "Never bypass permissions." / "Bypass for AFK tickets: research and task tickets, and any ticket labelled `ready-for-agent`." / "Bypass for every Claude Code session the Cockpit launches."
    - Main description: "Start sessions with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, so they run without permission prompts. Claude Code asks you once, in the first bypassed session, to accept bypass mode. Only your user settings are read, so a repository cannot turn this on."
  - `heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated`: boolean, default `true`.
    - Description: "Bypass permissions only in an isolated environment: a Dev Containers or Codespaces window, or a Docker or Podman container. Elsewhere sessions keep their prompts and the Cockpit shows a warning. Only your user settings are read."
- **Shown command = spawned command**: the flag is decided when the Actions are planned, never at spawn time. They are planned again whenever either setting changes (`onDidChangeConfiguration`), so the copied command and the spawned argv are always the same.

128.title: When does the capture run again, and how do new shots reach the READMEs?
128.body:
## Question

When does the capture run again, and how do its new images reach the READMEs?

[#116 Capture the real Cockpit in screenshots and a loop](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/116) left one command, `vp run capture`, and a **Capture** workflow. The workflow runs on demand and on PRs that touch the capture run, on Linux and macOS, and takes about 3 minutes per OS. Its images are artifacts and never a commit. Decide:

- **The trigger.** By hand before a release, on every PR that touches the Cockpit's UI (`webview/src`, `src`), as a step of the release workflow, or a mix.
- **The path to the READMEs.** Who moves a new image into the place the READMEs read it from: `packages/vscode/media/` in the VSIX, or an absolute tag-pinned URL as [#114 What do the VS Code Marketplace page and the Extensions view accept?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/114) found. Whether that is a hand-made PR or a bot PR.
- **Stale shots.** Whether a shot that no longer matches the Cockpit should fail anything, or only be noticed.
- **The macOS screen.** Whether the runner's 1440 × 676 window is good enough for the shots the READMEs keep.

## Context

- Grilling: `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling`.
- It waits on [#119 Prototype the two READMEs and the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/119), which chooses the shots and where the READMEs read them from.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Decided with Eduardo on 2026-10-09.

### Where the shots are read from

As [#119 Prototype the two READMEs and the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/119) decided, every README image lives in `docs/media/`, outside the VSIX. The repository README reads them from `main`. The listing reads `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/<tag>/docs/media/<file>`, so the Marketplace shows whatever `docs/media/` held at the release tag. Nothing goes in `packages/vscode/media/`.

### The trigger

The **Capture** workflow also runs on every PR that touches `packages/vscode/src/**` or `packages/vscode/webview/src/**`. It still runs on demand and on PRs that touch `packages/vscode/test/capture/**` or the workflow itself. It is not added to the release workflow: by the time that workflow runs, the tag is fixed and its `docs/media/` can't change. A run takes about 3 minutes per OS, and that cost is not a reason to cut it.

### The path to the READMEs

Updated shots ship in the same PR as the UI change that made them stale, so they are reviewed together. A new command copies them by hand: `vp run refresh-media` in `packages/vscode`. It downloads the branch's latest `capture-macos` artifact with `gh run download` and copies the kept files into `docs/media/`. There is no bot PR, because a PR opened with `GITHUB_TOKEN` doesn't trigger CI.

### The capture makes every kept shot

The crop that made `badge-icon.png` by hand on `prototype/readme` (commit `0cac0b3`) moves into `capture.mts`. One run then remakes every captured file the READMEs use: `window-map.png`, `focus-pane.png`, `focus-pane-session.png`, `detail-ticket.png`, `badge-icon.png` and `launch.gif`. The banner and the social card aren't captures and stay hand-made.

### Stale shots

A stale shot is noticed, not failed. Pixel diffs would flake, because session ages and the loop's timing change on every run. On a UI PR, the Capture job summary lists the kept files and the `refresh-media` command. One unit test does fail: every `docs/media/` file that either README references must exist, and every file `refresh-media` copies must be one the capture produces.

### The macOS screen

The runner's 1440 × 676 window is good enough. Every kept shot except `window-map.png` is a crop, and Eduardo approved `window-map.png` at that size in #119's dark render. We stay on the macOS runner and don't try to force a taller screen.

### Next

The work is a new AFK task, **Re-take the README shots when the Cockpit changes**. It is blocked by [#121 Land the front door and release it](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/121), which puts the images in `docs/media/` on `main`.

129.title: The health warnings bypass adds
129.body:
## Question

Which health warnings does bypass add, each with its code, level (quiet or loud), detail and words? The candidates:

- The setting is on and `skipPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated` holds it back. The detection rule's not-isolated result carries the `remoteName` seen and any `/run/.toolboxenv` veto, so the words can say what was seen ("Remote-SSH, no container marker", "toolbx container — shares your home"). See [The isolated-environment detection rule](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/126).
- A bypassed session sits in "starting" because Claude Code's one-time bypass dialog leaves no registry entry.
- Bypass is set but Claude Code runs as root (it refuses without `IS_SANDBOX=1`, which the Cockpit never sets), or `disableBypassPermissionsMode` silently downgrades it. See [Claude Code's bypass-permissions contract](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/124).

Decide which are detectable from what the host already reads, which earn a warning at all, and their codes in core's health table. A warning never gates.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Grilled with Eduardo; every recommendation accepted. Bypass adds two health codes and one starting hint. Neither code gates anything.

- **`bypass-not-isolated`** (quiet). Raised when `bypassPermissions` ≠ `off`, `bypassPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated` is `true`, and `isolationOf` says not isolated. It doesn't depend on whether any AFK ticket is open.
  - **Detail**: `<where>, <why>`.
    - `<where>` maps `remoteName`: `ssh-remote` → "Remote-SSH", `wsl` → "WSL", `tunnel` → "Remote Tunnel", none → "local window", anything else → the raw name.
    - `<why>` is "no container marker", or "a toolbx or distrobox container" when `/run/.toolboxenv` vetoed it.
  - **Message**: "Bypass permissions is on, but this window is not an isolated environment (<detail>), so sessions keep their permission prompts."
  - **Hint**: "Reopen the folder in a Dev Container, or turn off heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated."
  - The detail is part of the dismissal key, so a dismissal holds only for that environment.
- **`bypass-refused-as-root`** (loud). Raised when all three hold:
  1. The flag would actually be added (the setting is on and the isolation gate passes).
  2. `process.getuid?.() === 0`. This is never true on Windows.
  3. The host's env has neither `IS_SANDBOX=1` nor `CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP`. Reading these only silences the warning, never gates.

  The flag is still added, and the shown command stays the spawned command.
  - **Message**: "Claude Code refuses bypass permissions as root, so bypassed sessions exit as soon as they start."
  - **Hint**: "Run the window as a non-root user (a devcontainer's `remoteUser`), or set heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissions to off." The hint never names `IS_SANDBOX`.
- **Stuck at the bypass dialog: no health code.** It's about one session, not the machine. For a session whose planned command carried the flag, the 15 s starting hint (`NO_STATUS_HINT`) becomes "no status yet, the session may be waiting at the trust or bypass-permissions dialog, open the terminal". Otherwise it stays as it is.
- **`disableBypassPermissionsMode`: not detected, no code.** Detecting it would take managed settings in per-OS paths plus MDM, registry and server-managed settings the host can't see, as well as user, project and local settings. That's too many contracts for a partial answer, and Claude Code's footer already says "Bypass permissions mode was disabled by settings". It belongs in the README and the upstream register.
- **Where the logic lives**: a pure core function `bypassHealth({ bypassPermissions, onlyWhenIsolated, isolation, root, sandboxEnv }): Raised[]`. It gets a table test over setting × gate × isolation × root × env. The host collects `root` and `sandboxEnv` at activation, beside the isolation facts, and calls the function again on `onDidChangeConfiguration`. Both codes join `healthCodes` and `HEALTH_TABLE`. There's no "bypass is active" note, because the Focus pane's command already shows the flag.
- **Glossary**: no change.
