130.title: State reading for local trackers, tested against a real five-month tracker
130.body:
## Destination

A spec, handed to `/to-spec` and filed as `ready-for-agent` build issues, for how the scout reads every ticket's and map's state from local markdown in every form a real five-month tracker holds, with the sanitized fixtures it is tested against already on `main`.

## Notes

- Planning map with one execution exception: it builds the fixtures, a sanitized mirror of the real tracker with its truth file and a pattern fixture for every catalogued form. Everything else is decided here and built after `/to-spec`. Grilling tickets invoke `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling`; read `CONTEXT.md`, [ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md), the mattpocock-skills local tracker row of `docs/upstream.md`, upstream's history in [`wayfinder-conventions.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/wayfinder-conventions/docs/research/wayfinder-conventions.md) ([#10](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/10)) and the findings of [State forms on a real local tracker](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/131) first.
- Every reading rule is code, per ADR 0005: what code cannot read is drift, never interpreted.
- Words: "state" is open or closed, and "Status line" the literal `Status:` line; "status" alone is a session's registry status. The careful reading of a file, recorded in the truth file, is what the scout must agree with.
- Settled while charting:
  - **Scope**: the local tracker (`.scratch/`) only, and every Markdown file in it: maps, tickets, and issue files with no map. State in the broad sense (open, closed or claimed, the triage role, blocked, finished) and the lines it is read from: `Status:`, `Assignee:`, `Blocked by:` and `Blocks:`, `Map:` and `Parent:`, `Label:`, `Labels:` and `Type:`, the map file's name and its own `Status:` line, and wherever the resolution lives.
  - **Fixtures**: both kinds. The mirror keeps every effort and file of the real tracker with its text replaced, plus a truth file holding the careful reading of every ticket and map: the end-to-end benchmark at real scale. The pattern fixtures are invented, one per catalogued form, each with its careful reading, for one unit test per rule. The truth comes from the survey; [The truth for the files a careful reader can't call](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/134) settles the files it could not call.
  - **Sanitization**: an allowlist. Kept: header keys, state words and section headings (in either of the tracker's two languages), `wayfinder:` labels, triage roles, AFK/HITL, Markdown structure and separators, line styles, ticket numbers and the links between files with their targets renamed, and dates in their formats and order, shifted by one fixed offset. Replaced: titles, slugs, effort names, prose, code, paths, URLs, people, the real project's ticket keys and numbers in prose; long prose collapses to short placeholder lines. The raw corpus is never committed, pasted into an issue, a PR, a commit message or a research note, and the source project is never described beyond "a private five-month production tracker". Every artifact derived from the corpus passes the leak check before it leaves the machine, against a reviewed-words list that names each kept word; the mirror's first push also waits for Eduardo's OK.
  - **Private material**: the corpus at `/tmp/example-scratches`, and the survey records with the leak-check and counting scripts at `/tmp/example-scratches-survey`, on Eduardo's devcontainer only, never copied into the repo, a worktree or an issue. `/tmp` empties when the container is rebuilt: if that happens before [A sanitized mirror of the real tracker, with its truth](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/132) closes, Eduardo copies the corpus back and that ticket reruns the survey.

## Decisions so far

<!-- the index — one line per closed ticket: enough to judge relevance, then zoom the link for the detail the ticket holds -->

- [State forms on a real local tracker](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/131) — 342 files of a five-month tracker: every map is `MAP.md`; the Status line's first word agrees with a careful reader on 241 of 257 tickets; type, claim, blockers and map sit on GitHub-shaped header lines; 17 of 227 resolutions are under `## Answer`.
- [Where a local ticket's type and blockers come from](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/137) — header lines before the first H2, bold keys too; type from `Type:`/`Label:`/`Labels:`, never the H1; a `HITL` note only ever takes a ticket out of AFK; a blocker is the reference at the start of each `Blocked by:`/`Blocks:` item, never a note; the directory decides membership, a disagreeing `Map:` line is loud.
- [Where a local ticket's resolution lives](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/138) — one resolution: `## Answer`, else the last `Resolution` heading or bold label (either language), else, on a closed ticket only, the last entry under `## Comments`; byline from the label's ISO date and a dated item's `(<person>)`; the two fallbacks raise quiet drift, none at all stays loud.
- [A pattern fixture for every catalogued form](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/133) — 164 invented files in `packages/core/fixtures/local-forms`, one per form plus the several-candidate resolutions, each with its careful reading in `truth.json`; 9 readings stay unsettled until [The truth for the files a careful reader can't call](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/134) closes; `localForms()` feeds one table test.
- [The truth for the files a careful reader can't call](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/134) — the truth is what a file's own lines declare; boxes, comments, headings and a map's prose never change it, and are listed as disagreements; no "in progress": `ready-for-human` is an open ticket's role, one OPEN half keeps a ticket open, a map with `route walked` or no Status line is open (finished when its tickets are all closed).
- [Semicolons between blocker items](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/145) — a `;` outside brackets ends a blocker item only before a reference (link, `NN-<slug>.md`, `NN`/`#NN`), else it is annotation; `,` always splits; no new drift code.
- [A local map's own state](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/136) — `map.md` in any casing, two side by side loud; only a Status line led by `DONE` or `destination reached` closes a map (35/35 on the mirror), any other unknown lead quiet; a closed local map is hidden with its tickets, like GitHub; `Label:`, `Charted:` and gist state words ignored.
- [A sanitized mirror of the real tracker, with its truth](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/132) — `packages/core/fixtures/scratch-mirror`: 49 efforts, 342 files with their text replaced, and `truth.json` in the local-forms shape (states from the survey and #134, the rest read from the mirror under #137, #138 and #145; no "in progress"); sanitizer, truth builder and leak check committed in `tools/` so it rebuilds byte for byte.
- [How the scout reads a local ticket's Status line and claim](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/135) — the Status value's first word, any case or bold: `closed`/`done`/`resolved`/`wontfix` close, `open` and the triage roles are open, `claimed` claims; after `open` one more word (role or `claimed`) is read; an open ticket is claimed by a name on `Assignee:`, a closed one never; an unknown first word reads open with loud `unknown-status`; no new drift codes; a triage role never changes the frontier.
- [Which issue files are a map's tickets](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/139) — a ticket needs its effort's map and no `Parent:` naming a PRD; every other issue file is an **unmapped issue**: in the Unmapped fold grouped by effort (keys carry the effort), hidden once closed, never on a frontier, no `no-map` or `type-missing`; effort-29's map finishes, 17 open issues in 7 groups on the mirror.

## Not yet specified

Nothing left. The spec, [Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/163), settled the last three patches (the drift words and how a triage role and a long Status line show; the canary and the upstream register; the refresh cost) and is split into eleven `ready-for-agent` build tickets.

## Out of scope

- The GitHub tracker: its state comes from the API.
- Rewriting a tracker into the current conventions: drift is reported, never corrected.
- A model reading a free-form line ([ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md)).
- How the Detail renders bodies ([ADR 0007](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0007-markdown-it-renders-tracker-bodies-in-the-detail.md)) and the `next` CLI's presentation.
- The content of PRDs, handoffs, research notes and asset notes: the scout only has to know they are not tickets.
- Fixtures from other real trackers: a fresh effort.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Findings: [`docs/research/local-tracker-state-forms.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/local-tracker-state-forms/docs/research/local-tracker-state-forms.md) on `research/local-tracker-state-forms`. A script checked that each file was recorded once, then counted. The note holds shapes and counts only, and it passed the leak check against the corpus.

- **The scout reads almost none of it today.** All 35 maps are named `MAP.md`, so on a case-sensitive file system it finds no map. Even with the maps found, only 2 of the 227 closed tickets read as closed. `unknown-status` fires on 255 tickets, 18 get a type, 17 get a resolution, and most `Blocked by:` values turn into slugs or into numbers that aren't blockers.

  - The other 16: `ready-for-human` (13), two claims written in a dash clause, and one line holding two states.
- **Maps carry their own state.** 31 of 35 have a narrative `Status:` line, led by `DONE`, `destination reached`, `in progress`, `charted`, `REOPENED` or `route walked`.
- **Type, claim, membership and blockers sit on GitHub-shaped header lines**: `Label:` or `Labels: wayfinder:<type> (AFK|HITL …)`, `Assignee:`, `Map:` and `Blocked by:`. None is in the local template, and upstream never shipped any of them ([#10](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/10)).

Gaps:
- This is one tracker.
- The careful reading is a model's; [#134](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/134) settles the files it could not call.
- The source repo's tracker doc wasn't copied.

134.title: The truth for the files a careful reader can't call
134.body:
## Question

What is the true state of each file the survey could not call? Go through them with Eduardo one group at a time, from the survey records at `/tmp/example-scratches-survey`. Paths and lines stay in the terminal; the resolution comment names shapes and counts only.

- The 13 tickets whose Status line is `ready-for-human`: the survey read 8 as closed ("built, waiting on a human step"), 4 as open and 1 as in progress.
- The ticket whose Status line holds a DONE half and an OPEN half.
- The 2 maps whose Status line starts with `route walked`, and the 4 maps with no Status line.
- The map whose prose closes a range of tickets that their own files never close.

Write the settled readings into the truth of whichever fixtures already exist ([A sanitized mirror of the real tracker, with its truth](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/132) and [A pattern fixture for every catalogued form](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/133)), and record them as shapes on this ticket for the ones that don't exist yet.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Settled with Eduardo on 2026-10-09, in two grilling rounds. Shapes and counts only; the per-file readings live beside the private survey records, never in the repo.

### What the truth records

- **The truth is what a file's own lines declare.** A ticket's state comes from its own header lines, read with judgment about what their words mean. Ticked boxes, comments, the map's prose and headings never change a state. Where they contradict it, the truth lists a **disagreement** on that file, which the rules may raise as drift. The alternative, the state "actually true" across the effort, was rejected: the scout could only match it by reading prose or checkboxes, which [ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md) rules out.
- **No "in progress".** A ticket's truth is open, claimed or closed, with its triage role and its open blockers. A map's truth is open or closed, and finished or stuck is derived from its tickets, never stored. A ticket with a person or session on its `Assignee:` line is claimed. Every survey `in-progress` is re-read under these words when the mirror's truth is built.

### The readings (21 files: 15 tickets, 6 maps)

- **`Status: ready-for-human`, bare or annotated (13 tickets):** all open, triage role `ready-for-human`, unclaimed. Blockers are read from their own files: 6 are unblocked and 7 are blocked by other open tickets of the same group. 8 of them carry two disagreements: every acceptance box is ticked, and their map's prose calls them closed.
- **`Status: <prose> half DONE <date> (…); <prose> OPEN (HITL — …)` (1 ticket):** open, since one open half keeps the ticket open. Claimed through its `Assignee:` line. Disagreement: the Status line holds two states. Whether code reads the line or raises drift on it is for [How the scout reads a local ticket's Status line and claim](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/135).
- **`Status: **route walked …**` (2 maps):** both open. `route walked` is not a closing word: it describes a finished map. One has every ticket closed, so it's finished; the other has one HITL ticket on its frontier. Only `DONE` and `destination reached` close a map.
- **No Status line (4 maps):** all open. Headings and prose (`## Destination reached`, `Frontier: **empty**`, "stays open") never close a map. Two are finished, two have open tickets.
- **The map whose prose closes a range of tickets (`tickets <NN>–<NN> (all closed …)`):** 9 of those tickets' own files say open: 8 `ready-for-human` and 1 `ready-for-agent`. The truth keeps them open and lists the disagreement on the map and on each ticket. Whether that map reads as finished depends on [Which issue files are a map's tickets](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/139) deciding whether `**Parent:** [<title>](../PRD.md)` issues are its tickets, and its truth follows that answer.

### Where the readings go

Neither fixture exists yet. [A sanitized mirror of the real tracker, with its truth](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/132) takes the per-file readings from the private records and adds a `disagreements` field to its truth. [A pattern fixture for every catalogued form](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/133) gets one fixture per shape above: a bare `ready-for-human`, a two-state Status line, `route walked` with every ticket closed, `route walked` with one open ticket, a map with no Status line, and a map whose prose closes tickets its files keep open.

No glossary change: "disagreement" is a fixture word, and drift already names what the user sees. "Triage role" belongs to #135.

135.title: How the scout reads a local ticket's Status line and claim
135.body:
## Question

How does the scout read a local ticket's state and claim from its Status line, against the forms in the findings of [State forms on a real local tracker](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/131) and the truth [The truth for the files a careful reader can't call](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/134) settled?

- **Vocabulary**: which leading keywords mean closed (`closed`, `done` or `DONE`, `resolved`, `wontfix`), open (`open`) and claimed (`claimed`), and what the triage roles (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`) mean on a ticket of a map.
- **Annotation**: what follows the keyword (a date, a parenthesis, a dash clause) is ignored, kept as detail, or read for a second keyword (`open — claimed <date>`); casing, and a bold key or value.
- **Claim**: the template's `Status: claimed`, a claim in the dash clause, and `Assignee:`, whose `claimed <date>` outlives the ticket.
- **Never read**: a Status line after the first H2 or quoted in code, and what the scout says of a line holding two states.
- **Drift**: which codes the new forms raise and at which level (quiet when read correctly, loud when the Cockpit may be wrong), and whether `unknown-status` keeps its meaning.

Update the glossary's Claim, and add the terms the answer needs (a triage role).

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Settled with Eduardo on 2026-10-09 in one grilling round. Every rule agrees with the careful readings in `packages/core/fixtures/local-forms/truth.json`. Header lines are read only before the first H2 ([#137](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/137)), so a `` `Status: closed` `` quoted under `## Question` is never read. A map's own Status line belongs to [A local map's own state](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/136).

- **Vocabulary.** The scout reads the first word of the Status value, ignoring case and any `**` around the key or value.
  - **Closed:** `closed`, `done`, `resolved`, `wontfix`.
  - **Open:** `open`, `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`.
  - **Claimed:** `claimed`, the template's word; the ticket is open and claimed.
  - **No Status line:** open.
- **Triage role.** One of `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human` or `wontfix`, read from the Status line or a `Labels:` line. It is shown with the ticket and never changes the frontier: open, unblocked and unclaimed is takeable, whatever the role. `wontfix` both closes the ticket and is its role. Gating the frontier on a role was rejected, since neither the wayfinder skill nor GitHub's labels do.
- **Annotation.** The scout reads one more word, and only after `open`: the first word after a dash (`—`, `–`, ` - `) or an opening parenthesis.
  - A role there sets the role: `open (ready-for-human — …)`, `open — needs-triage (blocked)`.
  - `claimed` there claims the ticket: `open — claimed <date>`.
  - Nothing else is read, so no word in a closed line's annotation can reopen a ticket.
  - The whole value is kept verbatim as the Status annotation, for display.
- **Claim.** An open ticket is claimed by a `claimed` Status line, by `open — claimed …`, or by an `Assignee:` line that names someone.
  - **Who holds it:** the Assignee's name, the text before any parenthesis or dash (`agent (wren) — claimed …` gives `agent`). With no name, nobody is named (`by: []`).
  - **Lines that name nobody:** `—`, an empty value, `(unclaimed)` and `— (unclaimed)`.
  - **A closed ticket** keeps its Assignee as history but is never claimed. The `claimed <date>` left on 59 closed tickets is ignored.
- **Never read as state.** The scout never searches prose for state words ([ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md)). A Status line whose first word isn't in the vocabulary, such as the line with a DONE half and an OPEN half:
  - reads as open, so the ticket stays visible instead of vanishing;
  - can still be claimed through `Assignee:`;
  - raises `unknown-status`.

  That gives the truth's reading of the two-state line (claimed) without parsing it. When a ticket has two Status header lines, the first is read and the second raises `unknown-status`.
- **Drift.** No new codes. A vocabulary word, an annotation, a claim after the dash, an `Assignee:` claim and a closed ticket's leftover `claimed <date>` raise nothing: they are read correctly, and a quiet warning on 255 of 257 real tickets would bury real drift. `unknown-status` keeps its meaning (a Status line the scout can't read) and stays loud. Only its hint changes, to list the vocabulary. Its wording stays in the map's Not yet specified section.

Glossary: **Claim** updated and **Triage role** added in [#156](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/156).
lastComment.author: dbarjs

136.title: A local map's own state
136.body:
## Question

Does a local map have a state of its own, and how does the scout read it?

- **The map file**: `map.md` as the template says, `MAP.md` as all 35 maps of the real tracker are named, or any casing; and what the scout says on a case-sensitive file system when only `MAP.md` exists.
- **The map's own `Status:` line** (31 of 35 maps): which leading keywords mean closed (`DONE`, `destination reached`, and `route walked` as [The truth for the files a careful reader can't call](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/134) settled it) and which mean open (`in progress`, `charted`, `REOPENED`); a narrative of up to 4,670 characters; and the maps with no Status line.
- **A closed local map in the Cockpit**: hidden like a closed GitHub map, or shown as a finished map; and what the map says when its Status line and its tickets disagree.
- **The other lines**: `Label: wayfinder:map`, `Charted:`, and state words at the start of a decision's gist (`— CLOSED <date> …`): read, ignored, or drift.

Add the glossary term for a closed local map if the answer needs one.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Settled with Eduardo on 2026-10-09, in one grilling round. Shapes and counts only.

### Facts it rests on

- Today the scout opens only `.scratch/<effort>/map.md`, exact and lowercase (`packages/core/src/scout/local.ts:75`), and treats every local map as open. On a case-sensitive file system none of the real tracker's 35 maps (all `MAP.md`) would be found, and every one of their tickets would read as loud `no-map`.
- 31 of 35 maps carry a Status line (up to 4,616 characters, median 432). Leading words: `DONE` 14, `in progress` 5, `charted` 4, `route walked` 2, `destination reached` 1, `REOPENED` 1, prose or numbers first 4.
- The rule below agrees with the mirror's truth on all 35 maps: 15 closed, 20 open. Every closed map has all its tickets closed; two open maps are finished.

### Decisions

1. **The map file**: `map.md` in any casing, directly in the effort directory. A non-template casing (`MAP.md`) raises no drift. When more than one casing exists side by side, raise loud `map-file-ambiguous` and read `map.md` if present, else the first name in byte order. An effort with no map file keeps reporting its tickets as `no-map`; one with no map and no tickets is silently ignored (PRD and note folders).
2. **What closes a map**: only the map's own `Status:` header line (before the first H2, plain or bold key). Strip leading `**`, compare the first word(s) case-insensitively: `DONE` or `destination reached` closes it; anything else, and no Status line, is open. The rest of the line is annotation the scout never parses, so a later `DONE` (`07 DONE <date>`, `<prose> **DONE <date>**`) never closes a map. This is the rule from [The truth for the files a careful reader can't call](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/134), now as code.
3. **Drift on the Status line**: none for `DONE`, `destination reached`, `in progress`, `charted`, `REOPENED`, `route walked`. Any other lead raises quiet `map-status-unknown` (read as open, which the careful reader agrees with in every real case). A missing Status line raises nothing, since upstream's template has none; having a Status line at all isn't drift.
4. **A closed local map in the Cockpit**: hidden, like a closed GitHub map. The scout leaves it and all its tickets out of the snapshot, so they don't show up as unmapped. An open map with every ticket closed stays a finished map, folded in the Tree. A closed map with an open ticket raises no drift: it's hidden as GitHub hides one, and the real tracker has none.
5. **Other lines**: `Label:`/`Labels: wayfinder:map`, `Charted:`, `Redrawn:`, and a state word at the start of a decision's gist (`— CLOSED <date> …`) are ignored, with no drift. The directory and the file name make a map ([Where a local ticket's type and blockers come from](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/137)), dates don't affect state, and a decision gist is free text, the closed ticket's own file holds its state.
6. **Glossary**: no new term. **Map** now says the local file is `map.md` in any casing and that a local map is closed when its Status line starts with `DONE` or `destination reached`; a closed map is hidden.

### For the spec

- Two new drift codes for `drift-table.ts`: `map-file-ambiguous` (loud) and `map-status-unknown` (quiet).
- The pattern fixtures already hold every Status form (`map-done-*`, `map-destination-reached`, `map-route-walked`, `map-numbers-first`, `map-prose-first`, `map-reopened`, `map-no-status`, `map-lower-case`); the build adds one for two casings side by side, which needs a case-sensitive file system in the test's in-memory one.

137.title: Where a local ticket's type and blockers come from
137.body:
## Question

Where does the scout read a local ticket's type, blockers and map from, beyond the template's `Type:` and `Blocked by: NN, NN` lines? The forms and their counts are in the findings of [State forms on a real local tracker](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/131).

- **Type**: `Type: <type>`, `Type: wayfinder:<type> (AFK)`, `Label:` and `Labels: wayfinder:<type> (…)` with their annotations and extra triage labels, and the H1 prefix (`# Task: …`); which one wins when two disagree, and whether AFK or HITL is read.
- **Blockers**: links, bare file names, numbers with prose, none markers (`—`, `(none — frontier)`), state notes on closed blockers (`(closed <date>)`, `**UNBLOCKED**`), and `Blocks:`, the inverse edge. A blocker is never a number made of digits from prose or a link title.
- **Membership**: `Map: [<title>](../MAP.md)`, `Map: ../MAP.md` and `**Parent:** [<title>](../PRD.md)`, against the directory the file sits in.
- **Drift**: bold keys (`**Blocked by:**`), and the code and level each form raises.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Grilled with Eduardo on 2026-10-09; every recommendation was taken. Forms and counts come from [State forms on a real local tracker](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/131). Glossary: **Header line** and **Blocker** added, **Ticket** and **AFK ticket** amended ([#142](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/142)).

### Header lines

- The scout reads only `Key: value` lines before the first H2. Keys are case-insensitive, and the first line of each key wins. A line after the first H2 or inside code is never read.
- A bold key (`**Blocked by:**`) is read like a plain one and raises one quiet code shared by every key, `header-key-bold`, with the key as detail. [How the scout reads a local ticket's Status line and claim](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/135) inherits this for `**Status:**`.

### Type

- **Sources**: `Type:`, `Label:` and `Labels:`. The H1 prefix (`# Task: …`) is never a type, and the title stays verbatim.
- **Value**: an optional `wayfinder:` prefix, then the first word. The parenthesis after it is never searched for types or numbers. `Labels:` is split on commas, and every `wayfinder:<type>` in it counts.
- **Conflict**: when the sources name different types, the scout raises `type-several` (loud) and reads no type.
- **Drift**: a plain `Type: <type>` raises nothing. A `Label:`/`Labels:` line or a `wayfinder:` prefix raises the new quiet code `type-as-label`. An unknown `wayfinder:` word raises `unknown-wayfinder-labels`.
- **Triage role on `Labels:`** (`ready-for-agent`, …): read as the ticket's triage role, with the meaning #135 gives one on the Status line. #135 decides what happens when the two disagree. Other labels are ignored.

### AFK or HITL

The scout reads only a leading `AFK` or `HITL` inside the type value's parenthesis, and the annotation can only take a ticket out of AFK, never put one in:

- `HITL` on a task or research ticket makes it HITL: it isn't an AFK ticket and is never bypassed.
- `AFK` on a research or task ticket agrees with the type.
- `AFK` on a prototype or grilling ticket leaves it HITL and raises the new loud code `mode-conflicts-type`.

### Blockers

- **Items**: the scout splits the `Blocked by:` value on commas outside brackets and parentheses. Each item names at most one blocker, taken from its start:
  1. a Markdown link to a ticket file gives the target file's number, and the link title is never read;
  2. a bare `NN-<slug>.md` gives its number;
  3. a leading `NN` or `#NN` gives that number.
- **Annotation**: whatever follows the reference (`(closed <date>)`, `**UNBLOCKED**`, `resolved <date>; …`, `— <prose>`) is never read. A blocker's state always comes from its own file.
- **Targets**: they resolve against the ticket's directory. A target outside the effort, or a number with no file, raises `blocker-outside-map` and doesn't gate, as today.
- **None markers**: an empty value, or one that starts with `—`, `-`, `none`, `nothing`, `(none` or `(nothing`, means no blockers and raises nothing.
- **Unreadable items**: a lone slug-shaped item keeps `blockers-as-slugs` (loud). Any other item with no reference at its start raises the new loud code `blocker-unread`, with the item as detail.
- **Drift**: the template form `NN, NN` and the none markers raise nothing. Every other form that is read raises the new quiet code `blockers-not-template`, with the raw value as detail.
- **`Blocks:`** is read with the same item grammar. `A — Blocks: B` adds A to B's blockers, and both directions are merged, so a one-sided edge still gates. It raises the new quiet code `blocks-line`.

### Membership

- The directory decides membership, as today. `Map:` and `Parent:` are read only as a link target or path, resolved against the file's directory, and the link title is never read.
- A target that is the effort's own map file raises nothing. The comparison is case-insensitive, against whichever file the scout reads as the map.
- A target that is another effort's map, or a missing file, raises the new loud code `map-line-disagrees`, and the directory still wins.
- A target that is a PRD or any other non-map file is left to [Which issue files are a map's tickets](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/139).

### New drift codes

The words for these stay in the map's Not yet specified.

| code | level |
|---|---|
| `header-key-bold` | quiet |
| `type-as-label` | quiet |
| `blockers-not-template` | quiet |
| `blocks-line` | quiet |
| `mode-conflicts-type` | loud |
| `blocker-unread` | loud |
| `map-line-disagrees` | loud |

138.title: Where a local ticket's resolution lives
138.body:
## Question

Where does the scout find a closed local ticket's resolution, which the Detail shows and `closed-no-resolution` checks?

The template's `## Answer` holds it for 17 of 227 closed tickets in the real tracker. The rest put it under `### Resolution (<date> …)` inside `## Comments` (108), in a `## Resolution (<date> …)` H2 (38), in a bold `**Resolution …**` paragraph (31), in a dated list item under `## Comments` (20) or in other text under `## Comments` (11); 21 tickets title the heading in the tracker's second language. Which of these count and in which order, what the Detail shows when a ticket has several, and what drift each raises.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

A closed local ticket has exactly one resolution, read by code in this order. Grilled with Eduardo on 2026-10-09 and accepted wholesale.

1. **Which labels count.** `## Answer`, or a heading at any level or a bold label leading a paragraph whose first word is `Resolution` or its second-language word (accented and unaccented), case-insensitive, outside code fences. A bold `**Resolved**` or `**Done**` and `## Decision` don't count. The word list is code.
2. **No label: the last comment, closed tickets only.** The last entry under the last `## Comments` heading is the resolution: the last dated item, the last `###` subsection, or the trailing text. This mirrors GitHub, where it's the last comment. A ticket that isn't closed never gets a resolution this way.
3. **Several candidates.** `## Answer` comes first, then the **last** Resolution label (a reopened ticket's second closing wins), then the last comment. The Detail shows that one only. The rest stay in the body.
4. **How far each one runs.** A heading runs to the next heading of the same or a higher level. A bold label runs from its line to the next heading. A dated item is the item plus its continuation lines. The label line itself is not in the body.
5. **Byline.** `at` is the first ISO date in the label or dated item. `author` is the `(<person>)` right after a dated item's date. Otherwise both are null. Nothing comes from prose.
6. **Drift.**
   - `## Answer` raises nothing.
   - A Resolution label raises a new **quiet** `resolution-outside-answer`, whose detail names the form.
   - The last-comment fallback raises a new **quiet** `resolution-from-last-comment`.
   - `closed-no-resolution` stays **loud**, and its hint mentions the Resolution heading.
   - The wording stays in the map's fog about `drift-table.ts`.
7. **Glossary.** **Resolution** is a closed ticket's one answer; "answer" names only the local section. See [Name a ticket's resolution in the glossary](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/143).

**What it covers on the real tracker** (count-only probe of its closed tickets, by the first word of the Status line):
- A label: 105 `### Resolution` under `## Comments`, 34 `## Resolution`, 31 bold labels and 10 `## Answer` alone.
- The last comment: 22 tickets with dated items only.
- `closed-no-resolution`: 3.
- Several candidates:
  - 7 `## Answer` plus dated items, which `## Answer` wins.
  - 6 a bold `Resolved`/`Done` beside a Resolution heading, which the heading wins.
  - 1 `## Resolution` plus dated items.
  - 2 with two `### Resolution` headings, of which the last wins.
- On tickets that aren't closed: 9 carry dated items and 1 carries a `### Resolution`. The fallback ignores all of them.

For the fixtures: [A pattern fixture for every catalogued form](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/133) needs one fixture per form, plus one for each kind of several-candidate ticket above. The truth file of [A sanitized mirror of the real tracker, with its truth](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/132) records which form each closed ticket's resolution comes from.

139.title: Which issue files are a map's tickets
139.body:
## Question

Which issue files does the scout count as a map's tickets, and what does it show for the rest?

- The 13 effort directories with no map, whose 1 to 3 issue files carry triage roles or `done`, and the effort whose `PRD.md` lists its 10 `/to-tickets` issues as done.
- The 12 `/to-tickets` issues filed in a wayfinder effort's `issues/` beside its tickets, with `**Parent:** [<title>](../PRD.md)` and no `wayfinder:` type.
- Whether each lands in `unmapped`, on the map or nowhere; how its triage role shows (read as [How the scout reads a local ticket's Status line and claim](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/135) decided); whether a closed one disappears; and what drift each raises.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Grilled and agreed on 2026-10-09.

1. **Membership.** An issue file is a map's ticket only when its effort has a map **and** it has no `Parent:` line naming a file other than that map. Every other issue file is an **unmapped issue**: every file of an effort with no map, and every PRD-parented `/to-tickets` file beside a map. A map's tickets, frontier and finished state count tickets only. On the mirror, effort-29's 21 wayfinder tickets are all closed, so its map is finished and moves to Finished; its 12 PRD issues leave the map.
2. **Where they show.** All unmapped issues go in the one Unmapped fold above Finished, **grouped by effort** in directory order and in number order inside a group. A group is labelled with its map's title when the effort has one, else with the directory name. A row's key includes the effort. Today `unmappedKey(number)` collides across efforts, because local ticket numbers repeat (12 of the mirror's 24 mapless files are `#1`).
3. **Closed.** A closed unmapped issue is hidden, and an effort with no open unmapped issue shows no group, like a closed map with its tickets. Each file's state comes from its own Status line ([How the scout reads a local ticket's Status line and claim](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/135)); a `PRD.md` ticking its issues off is a note and changes nothing. Mirror: 17 open issues in 7 groups (effort-29 holds 9 of them; 6 mapless efforts hold 8); effort-46 and the 7 all-closed mapless efforts disappear.
4. **Drift.** An unmapped issue raises neither `no-map` nor `type-missing`: an issue with no map and no type is a normal local form, not drift. Every other ticket-line rule still applies (`unknown-status`, blockers under #137 and #145). No new drift codes; `no-map` stays in the table but never fires on a local tracker, and GitHub's `unmapped` stays empty because only sub-issues are collected.
5. **Role and frontier.** The triage role is read as #135 decided and kept on the issue. An unmapped issue is never on a frontier and never "next", whatever its role, including `ready-for-agent`. How the row, Focus pane and Detail show the role stays in the map's fog item on drift words and triage-role presentation.
6. **Glossary.** **Unmapped issue** added to `CONTEXT.md` (de6dd12 on `main`).

**Fixtures:** no change needed. The mirror's `truth.json` already records each file's effort `map` and its PRD `parent`, so membership derives from it as "`map` set and `parent` null". The spec should add one local-forms pattern for a PRD-parented file beside a map if `/to-spec` finds none.

145.title: Semicolons between blocker items
145.body:
## Question

Does a `;` separate `Blocked by:` items the way a `,` does?

[Where a local ticket's type and blockers come from](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/137) splits the value on commas outside brackets and parentheses, and it never reads the annotation after an item's reference. The real tracker also separates linked blockers with semicolons: `[<title>](<NN>-<slug>.md) (closed <date> — <prose>); [<title>](<NN>-<slug>.md) (closed <date> — <prose>)`, on 2 tickets, one of them open. Read by the #137 rule, that open ticket loses its second blocker.

A careful reader sees two blockers. The pattern fixture `.scratch/blockers/issues/13-swap-step-13.md` in [`packages/core/fixtures/local-forms`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/tree/main/packages/core/fixtures/local-forms) records `blockedBy: [1, 2]`. Also decide whether a `;` that follows a reference and starts prose, as in `<NN> resolved <date>; frontier — <prose>`, ends the item or belongs to the annotation. Under either rule that prose names no blocker.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Grilled with Eduardo on 2026-10-09; every recommendation was taken. The counts come from the private corpus, shapes only.

### What the tracker holds

229 files carry a `Blocked by:` or `Blocks:` line, and 28 of those lines hold a `;`. Almost all of those semicolons sit inside parentheses or a none marker, so the rule of [Where a local ticket's type and blockers come from](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/137) already ignores them. Five sit outside parentheses:

- 2 separate linked blockers: `[<title>](<NN>-<slug>.md) (closed <date>); [<title>](<NN>-<slug>.md) (closed <date> — <prose>)`.
- 3 start prose that names no ticket: `[<title>](…) — <prose>; <prose>`, `[…](…), … — <prose>; **<prose>**` and `<NN> (<prose>); <prose> (…)`.

### The rule

- **`;`**: outside brackets and parentheses, a `;` ends an item only when the text after it starts with a reference: a Markdown link, a bare `NN-<slug>.md`, or a leading `NN` or `#NN`. Otherwise the `;` and everything after it belong to the item's annotation, which is never read.
- **`,`**: unchanged. It is the template's separator and always splits; prose after a comma still raises `blocker-unread` (loud). The one real case reads like a dependency that isn't a ticket, so loud is honest.
- **Drift**: no new code. A value read through `;` raises the quiet `blockers-not-template` with the raw value, like every other non-template form.
- **`Blocks:`** shares the item grammar, so the same rule applies.
- **Accepted risk**: prose after a `;` that happens to start with a number reads as a blocker, the same risk a comma already carries.

### Fixtures and glossary

The truth in [`packages/core/fixtures/local-forms`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/tree/main/packages/core/fixtures/local-forms) already agrees: `blockers/issues/13-swap-step-13.md` reads `blockedBy: [1, 2]`, and `blockers/issues/21-swap-step-21.md` (`<NN> resolved <date>; frontier — <prose>`) reads `blockedBy: [1]` with no `blocker-unread`. The glossary's **Blocker** entry already covers this, so `CONTEXT.md` is unchanged.

146.title: Does the repository page need community files?
146.body:
## Question

Does the repository page need community files, and which: a contributing guide, a security policy, issue templates, a pull request template, a code of conduct? For each one it does need, what does it say, and does it stay short enough to point at the repository README's Developing section rather than repeat it?

GitHub shows these files in the repository's sidebar and community profile, and offers the templates when someone opens an issue. The repository README drafted in [#119 Prototype the two READMEs and the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/119) now has a Developing section with the build, check and test commands, and a Credits section.

## Context

- Hero Synergy is a personal project; issues are also the wayfinder tracker the project itself runs on (`docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`, the `wayfinder:*` and triage labels), so an issue template must not break how `/wayfinder` and the triage labels read issues.
- Whatever this decides ships in the PR of [#121 Land the front door and release it](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/121), or goes out of scope.
- HITL: grilling with Eduardo, using `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling`.

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Grilled with Eduardo in two rounds, both accepted as recommended. The repository page gets **three community files** and the listing loses its Q & A tab. All of it ships in [#121 Land the front door and release it](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/121)'s PR.

### Facts it rests on

- The community profile was at 28%: `README.md` and `LICENSE` only.
- Nobody but Eduardo and `github-actions[bot]` has opened an issue or PR. Discussions is off and private vulnerability reporting was off.
- The listing's "Report issue" (`bugs.url`) already sends Marketplace visitors to Issues. `qna` was unset, so the Marketplace ran its own Q & A tab.
- Issue templates only shape GitHub's web "New issue" form. `/wayfinder`, triage and the canary create issues through `gh issue create --body`, which goes through the API and ignores templates, so no template can break the tracker.
- `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` already says outside PRs are not a way to ask for changes.
- GitHub shows CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY and LICENSE as tabs beside the README, wherever those files live.

### Decisions

| File | Decision | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Issue template | **One bug report form**, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml`, labelled `needs-triage`. No `config.yml`, so blank issues stay allowed for ideas and questions. | The likeliest stranger arrives from "Report issue", and a bug without its three versions is the costliest to triage. |
| PR template | **None.** | Outside PRs aren't a way to ask for changes, and agents write their own PR bodies. |
| Contributing guide | **`.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`**, four facts. It links the README's Developing section and doesn't repeat it. | GitHub links it on the new-issue and new-PR pages, which is when those facts are needed. |
| Security policy | **`.github/SECURITY.md`**, plus private vulnerability reporting turned on. | The extension starts terminal commands from ticket titles, so command injection is a real class of bug. |
| Code of conduct | **None.** Revisit if the project gains contributors or a place where people talk. | One person and no community space: nobody else to enforce it. The profile percentage is not a goal. |
| Marketplace Q & A | **`"qna": false`** in `packages/vscode/package.json`. | One route for strangers, "Report issue", to Issues, instead of a tab nobody reads. |

- The repository README does **not** link them: GitHub's tabs already do, and its Developing section stays as drafted in [#119 Prototype the two READMEs and the social card](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/119).
- No glossary or ADR change: no product term moved, and every choice is cheap to reverse.

### The files as agreed

`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml`

```yaml
name: Bug report
description: Something in Hero Synergy doesn't work as it should.
labels: [needs-triage]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: For a security problem, don't open an issue. Report it privately as the security policy says.
  - type: input
    id: version
    attributes: { label: Hero Synergy version, description: "In the Extensions view." }
    validations: { required: true }
  - type: input
    id: vscode
    attributes: { label: VS Code version, description: "Help → About." }
    validations: { required: true }
  - type: input
    id: claude
    attributes: { label: Claude Code version, description: "`claude --version`" }
    validations: { required: true }
  - type: dropdown
    id: os
    attributes:
      label: Where VS Code runs
      options: [macOS, Linux, Dev container or SSH remote, Windows (WSL), Windows (native)]
    validations: { required: true }
  - type: dropdown
    id: tracker
    attributes:
      label: Tracker
      options: [GitHub, Local markdown, Other]
  - type: textarea
    id: what
    attributes: { label: What happened, description: "And what you expected instead. Screenshots welcome." }
    validations: { required: true }
```

`.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`

```markdown
# Contributing

Thanks for your interest in Hero Synergy.

- **Open an issue first.** Describe the bug or the idea before writing code. A pull request without an issue may be closed.
- **This repository plans its own work in its Issues**, with [Matt Pocock's wayfinder skill](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills). That's why you'll see `wayfinder:*` and triage labels such as `needs-triage` and `ready-for-agent`.
- **To build, check and test**, follow [Developing](../README.md#developing) in the README.
- **A change people will notice in the extension needs a changeset**: run `pnpm changeset` and write it for the person updating.

For a security problem, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
```

`.github/SECURITY.md`

```markdown
# Security policy

Hero Synergy starts terminal commands from ticket titles and numbers it reads from your tracker, so a way to make it run something you didn't ask for is a security bug.

**Report it privately**: on this repository's Security tab, choose "Report a vulnerability". Please don't open a public issue.

Only the latest release on the Marketplace gets fixes.
```

### How it ships

In #121's single PR: the three files and `"qna": false`. Before that PR merges, turn on private vulnerability reporting:

```sh
gh api --method PUT repos/dbarjs/hero-synergy/private-vulnerability-reporting
```

Eduardo runs it if the session may not. #121's live checks gain two: the community profile lists the contributing guide, security policy and issue template, and the listing shows no Q & A tab.

149.title: Re-take the README shots when the Cockpit changes
149.body:
## Question

Make the README shots easy to re-take whenever the Cockpit changes, as [#128 When does the capture run again, and how do new shots reach the READMEs?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/128) decided. This is one PR to `main`:

- **Trigger.** Add `packages/vscode/src/**` and `packages/vscode/webview/src/**` to the `pull_request` paths in `.github/workflows/capture.yml`.
- **`badge-icon.png` comes from the capture.** Move the crop to the icon and its badge (done by hand on `prototype/readme`, commit `0cac0b3`) into `packages/vscode/test/capture/capture.mts`, with a unit test.
- **`vp run refresh-media`** in `packages/vscode`. It downloads the current branch's latest `capture-macos` artifact with `gh run download` and copies the kept files into `docs/media/`: `window-map.png`, `focus-pane.png`, `focus-pane-session.png`, `detail-ticket.png`, `badge-icon.png` and `launch.gif`. Its logic is unit-tested.
- **Job summary.** When a PR runs Capture, the job summary lists the kept files and the `refresh-media` command.
- **The one failing check.** A unit test fails when a `docs/media/` file referenced by `README.md` or `packages/vscode/README.md` (by relative path or by the tag-pinned raw URL) doesn't exist, or when a file that `refresh-media` copies isn't one the capture produces.
- Run `refresh-media` once, end to end, against a real Capture run. Show the result in the PR, including any shots that changed.

Merge once `check`, `vscode (linux)`, `vscode (macos)` and `capture` are green.

## Context

- Blocked by [#121 Land the front door and release it](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/121), which puts the READMEs and `docs/media/` on `main`.
- AFK.

prs.title: Re-take the README shots when the Cockpit changes

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Done in [#157 Re-take the README shots when the Cockpit changes](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/157), merged to `main` as ea61c43 once `check`, `vscode (linux)`, `vscode (macos)` and `capture` were green.

- **Trigger.** `capture.yml` also runs on PRs that touch `packages/vscode/src/**` or `packages/vscode/webview/src/**`.
- **`badge-icon.png` comes from the capture.** It is a square as wide as the Activity Bar, centred on the Cockpit's icon (`iconSquare` in `test/capture/media.mts`, unit-tested). It shows what the hand crop from `0cac0b3` showed.
- **`vp run refresh-media`** (in `packages/vscode`; the logic is in `test/capture/refresh.mts`, tested with a fake `gh`):
  - It takes the branch's newest finished Capture run, downloads `capture-macos` and copies the six kept files into `docs/media/`.
  - It reports each file as new, updated or unchanged.
  - If the run lacks a kept file, it copies nothing.
  - `--run <id>` and `--branch <name>` override the run and the branch.
- **Job summary.** On a PR, the macOS capture job lists the kept files with their sizes and the command.
- **The one failing check.** `refresh.test.mts` fails when a `docs/media/` file referenced by either README (by relative path or tag-pinned raw URL) doesn't exist, or when a kept file isn't in `CAPTURED`. `shoot()` only accepts a `CAPTURED` name, and the capture itself fails if it made no kept file.
- **End to end.** The run against #157's own Capture run is shown in [this PR comment](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/157#issuecomment-6088235464).
  - `badge-icon.png` is now the capture's own shot.
  - The other three changed files differ only in the sessions' elapsed times.

One thing to know: the macOS capture flaked once ("Timed out waiting for #8 Typo tolerance to start") and passed on rerun. Since Capture now runs on every Cockpit UI PR, this flake will show up more often.

155.title: Launch AFK sessions with permissions bypassed in isolated environments
155.body:
From the map [#123 Launch AFK sessions with permissions bypassed in isolated environments](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/123). Every decision below was settled there: [#124](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/124) (Claude Code's bypass contract), [#125](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/125) (isolation signals), [#126](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/126) (detection rule), [#127](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/127) (which Actions bypass, setting names) and [#129](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/129) (health warnings). Glossary terms used: **AFK ticket**, **Bypassed session**, **Isolated environment**, **Action** (`CONTEXT.md`).

## Problem Statement

When I work a ticket from the Cockpit, the session stops at every permission prompt, even on an AFK ticket (research, task, or anything labelled `ready-for-agent`) that the agent is meant to work alone. I run these sessions in a devcontainer so they *can* run unattended. But the Cockpit always launches plain `claude`, so I have to sit beside each AFK session and approve tool calls, or relaunch it by hand with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`. When I resume an ended session the flag is gone again, because `--resume` drops it.

I also can't safely turn bypass on everywhere. A cloned repository must never be able to switch it on for me. On my laptop, over Remote-SSH or in a toolbx container that shares my home, I want sessions to keep their prompts even if I left the setting on. When bypass can't work (as root, Claude Code refuses it outright), I want to be told why.

## Solution

Two machine-scoped settings, off by default:

- `heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissions`: `off` | `afkTickets` | `allSessions`.
- `heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated`: boolean, default `true`.

When they allow it, the Cockpit adds `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` to the Actions it plans. Under `afkTickets` that is every ticket Action (Work ticket, Launch fresh, Resume, Resume by name) on an AFK ticket. Under `allSessions` it is every ticket Action plus the plain Actions (Chart a map, To spec, Run skill…, Setup). The flag is part of the argv, so the Focus pane shows it and Copy command copies it.

By default the flag is added only in an isolated environment: a Dev Containers or Codespaces window, or a Docker/Podman container that isn't toolbx or distrobox. Elsewhere sessions keep their prompts, and a quiet health warning says what the Cockpit saw. A loud health warning says so when the window runs as root, where Claude Code would refuse the flag. A session that sits in "starting" with the flag gets a hint that it may be waiting at Claude Code's one-time bypass dialog. The Cockpit never accepts that dialog for you, never writes `~/.claude` and never sets `IS_SANDBOX`.

## User Stories

1. As a Cockpit user, I want bypass to be off until I turn it on, so that installing or updating Hero Synergy never changes how my sessions run.
2. As a Cockpit user, I want a `heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissions` setting with `off`, `afkTickets` and `allSessions`, so that I choose how far bypass reaches.
3. As a Cockpit user, I want each value to have a description in the Settings UI, so that I know what `afkTickets` covers without reading docs.
4. As a Cockpit user, I want both bypass settings to be machine-scoped, so that a cloned repository's `.vscode/settings.json` can never turn bypass on or loosen the isolation gate.
5. As a Cockpit user, I want the setting's description to say Claude Code asks once, in the first bypassed session, to accept bypass mode, so that the dialog doesn't surprise me.
6. As a Cockpit user with `afkTickets`, I want Work ticket on a research ticket to start with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, so that research runs without prompts.
7. As a Cockpit user with `afkTickets`, I want Work ticket on a task ticket to bypass, so that task tickets run alone.
8. As a Cockpit user with `afkTickets`, I want any ticket labelled `ready-for-agent` to bypass whatever its type, so that the triage label decides as it does for agents elsewhere.
9. As a Cockpit user with `afkTickets`, I want a research or task ticket labelled `ready-for-human` to keep its prompts, so that a ticket marked for me is never run unattended.
10. As a Cockpit user with `afkTickets`, I want prototype and grilling tickets to keep their prompts, so that HITL sessions stay interactive.
11. As a Cockpit user with `afkTickets`, I want a ticket with no type label to keep its prompts, so that an unknown ticket is treated as HITL.
12. As a Cockpit user, I want Launch fresh on an AFK ticket to bypass like Work ticket, so that relaunching doesn't quietly drop the mode.
13. As a Cockpit user, I want Resume (by id) on an AFK ticket to pass the flag again, so that a resumed AFK session keeps running without prompts even though `--resume` drops the mode.
14. As a Cockpit user, I want Resume by name on an AFK ticket to pass the flag too, even for a session I started by hand, so that the ticket decides, not how the session began.
15. As a Cockpit user with `afkTickets`, I want Chart a map, To spec, Run skill… and Setup to keep their prompts, so that plain Actions where I'm present stay interactive.
16. As a Cockpit user with `allSessions`, I want every ticket Action on every ticket to bypass, HITL included, so that I can run everything without prompts in a throwaway environment.
17. As a Cockpit user with `allSessions`, I want Chart a map, To spec, Run skill… and Setup to bypass, so that `allSessions` means every Claude Code session the Cockpit launches.
18. As a Cockpit user, I want Install plugin, Install with npx and the scout's background `claude` never to carry the flag, so that installs and reads are never bypassed.
19. As a Cockpit user, I want the Focus pane's command to show `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` when it will be passed, so that I see exactly what will run.
20. As a Cockpit user, I want Copy command to copy the same argv the Cockpit would spawn, flag included, so that running it by hand behaves the same.
21. As a Cockpit user, I want the planned commands to update as soon as I change either setting, so that what I see never lags behind what would be spawned.
22. As a Cockpit user, I want a changed setting to apply to the next launch only, so that sessions already running are left alone.
23. As a Cockpit user, I want `bypassPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated` on by default, so that turning bypass on doesn't bypass on my laptop.
24. As a Cockpit user in a Dev Containers window (`dev-container`, `attached-container`, `k8s-container`, `apple-container`), I want the window to count as isolated, so that bypass applies there.
25. As a Cockpit user in a Codespace, I want the window to count as isolated, so that bypass applies there.
26. As a Cockpit user whose extension host runs in a plain Docker container (`/.dockerenv`), I want it to count as isolated, so that I don't need Dev Containers for bypass.
27. As a Cockpit user in a Podman container (`/run/.containerenv`), I want it to count as isolated, so that Podman works like Docker.
28. As a Cockpit user over Remote-SSH into a Gitpod/Ona container, I want the container marker to count, so that a remote container is recognised by its marker even though `ssh-remote` alone doesn't count.
29. As a Cockpit user in toolbx or distrobox, I want the window not to count as isolated even though a container marker exists, so that a container sharing my home, SSH agent and D-Bus doesn't unlock bypass.
30. As a Cockpit user in a local window, over WSL, Remote-SSH to a plain host or a Remote Tunnel, I want the window not to count as isolated, so that ordinary machines keep their prompts.
31. As a Cockpit user, I want environment variables never to count toward isolation, so that a shell profile or an `.envrc` can't fake a container.
32. As a Cockpit user who turned bypass on outside an isolated environment, I want a quiet `bypass-not-isolated` health warning that says where I am and why it didn't count ("Remote-SSH, no container marker", "local window, a toolbx or distrobox container"), so that I know why sessions still prompt.
33. As a Cockpit user, I want that warning's hint to say "reopen the folder in a Dev Container, or turn off heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated", so that I know the one thing to do.
34. As a Cockpit user who dismissed `bypass-not-isolated` in one environment, I want it back when I open the same folder somewhere else that isn't isolated, so that a dismissal holds only for the environment I dismissed it in.
35. As a Cockpit user who turned off `bypassPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated`, I want the flag added anywhere and no not-isolated warning, so that the gate is fully my call.
36. As a Cockpit user, I want no bypass warning at all while the setting is `off`, so that the Health row stays quiet when I haven't opted in.
37. As a Cockpit user whose window runs as root, I want a loud `bypass-refused-as-root` warning when the flag would be added, so that I know bypassed sessions will exit as soon as they start.
38. As a Cockpit user running as root with `IS_SANDBOX=1` or `CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP` already in my environment, I want no root warning, so that a sandbox I set up myself isn't flagged.
39. As a Cockpit user, I want the root warning's hint to suggest a non-root `remoteUser` or turning the setting off, and never to name `IS_SANDBOX`, so that the Cockpit doesn't teach me to get around Claude Code's guard.
40. As a Cockpit user running as root, I want the flag still added and the shown command still the spawned command, so that the warning informs and never gates.
41. As a Cockpit user, I want a bypassed session that shows no status after 15 s to say it may be waiting at the trust or bypass-permissions dialog, so that I open the terminal and accept it myself.
42. As a Cockpit user, I want a session launched without the flag to keep today's trust-dialog hint, so that the hint names only the dialog that can apply.
43. As a Cockpit user, I want the Cockpit never to accept Claude Code's bypass dialog, write `~/.claude` or set `IS_SANDBOX`, so that every consent to bypass is mine, given in Claude Code.
44. As a Cockpit user on a repo whose `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` renames `ready-for-agent` or `ready-for-human`, I want the Cockpit to use the repo's label strings, so that AFK detection matches the repo's own vocabulary.
45. As a Cockpit user on a repo with no or an unreadable `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`, I want the default label names used silently, so that a missing file costs nothing (a wrong name only means fewer sessions bypass).
46. As a Cockpit user on a local tracker, I want a ticket's labels read from its body when it carries them, and none otherwise, so that local tickets still classify by type.
47. As a Cockpit user, I want the extension README to list both settings and explain bypass, the isolation gate and what isolated does and doesn't mean, so that I can turn it on knowingly.
48. As a Cockpit user, I want the README to say that `disableBypassPermissionsMode` silently downgrades a bypassed session and the Cockpit doesn't detect it, so that a session that prompts anyway isn't a mystery.
49. As a Cockpit user, I want the README to say that an isolated environment is "in a container", not "sandboxed", because a repo's `devcontainer.json` can mount my home or the Docker socket, so that I judge the container myself.
50. As a maintainer, I want `docs/upstream.md` to record the bypass flag, the resume behaviour, the root refusal and its undocumented escapes, the dialog's missing registry entry, the `disableBypassPermissionsMode` downgrade, the resolver names, the marker files and the triage-labels table, so that an upstream change is caught by the register.
51. As a maintainer, I want the isolation, AFK and health rules to be pure core functions with table tests, so that every combination is tested without a VS Code host.
52. As a user of the `next` CLI, I want its commands unchanged, so that bypass stays a Cockpit-only feature.

## Implementation Decisions

**Settings (manifest).** Two new entries in the VS Code extension's contributed configuration, both `"scope": "machine"` like `heroSynergy.claude.path`:

- `heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissions`: string enum `off` (default) | `afkTickets` | `allSessions`.
  - Value descriptions: "Never bypass permissions." / "Bypass for AFK tickets: research and task tickets, and any ticket labelled `ready-for-agent`." / "Bypass for every Claude Code session the Cockpit launches."
  - Main description: "Start sessions with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, so they run without permission prompts. Claude Code asks you once, in the first bypassed session, to accept bypass mode. Only your user settings are read, so a repository cannot turn this on."
- `heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated`: boolean, default `true`. Description: "Bypass permissions only in an isolated environment: a Dev Containers or Codespaces window, or a Docker or Podman container. Elsewhere sessions keep their prompts and the Cockpit shows a warning. Only your user settings are read."

**Flag.** Always `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, never `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. The two are equivalent on the floor (2.1.212) and the ceiling.

**Core: isolation detection** (new module beside the other pure core rules). A pure `isolationOf(facts)` over facts the host collects once at activation: `remoteName: string | null` and whether `/.dockerenv`, `/run/.containerenv` and `/run/.toolboxenv` exist. First match wins:

1. `remoteName` ∈ {`dev-container`, `attached-container`, `k8s-container`, `apple-container`, `codespaces`};
2. `/.dockerenv` exists;
3. `/run/.containerenv` exists.

If `/run/.toolboxenv` exists, tiers 2 and 3 don't count. The veto never overrules tier 1. `ssh-remote`, `wsl`, `tunnel` and no remote neither count nor veto. Environment variables are never read for isolation. Result shape (from #126):

```ts
type IsolationSignal =
  | { kind: 'remote'; remoteName: 'dev-container' | 'attached-container' | 'k8s-container' | 'apple-container' | 'codespaces' }
  | { kind: 'marker'; path: '/.dockerenv' | '/run/.containerenv' }
type Isolation =
  | { isolated: true; signal: IsolationSignal }
  | { isolated: false; vetoedBy: '/run/.toolboxenv' | null; remoteName: string | null }
```

A core fact collector checks the three paths through core's `FileSystem` service. On Windows the checks come back false, with no special case.

**Core: AFK ticket rule.**

- The snapshot's `Ticket` gains `labels: ReadonlyArray<string>`, a plain fact from the tracker. On GitHub it comes from the labels the map query already fetches. On a local tracker it comes from the ticket body's labels line when present, else empty.
- A pure `isAfkTicket(ticket, triage)` decides: AFK when labelled the repo's `ready-for-agent` string, or when typed research or task and not labelled the repo's `ready-for-human` string. A ticket with no type is HITL. The snapshot itself carries no session logic.
- A core reader parses the `ready-for-agent` and `ready-for-human` rows of `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` (right-hand column). It falls back to the default names, silently, when the file is missing, unreadable or lacks a row.

**Core: the bypass decision.** One pure function decides whether a given Action carries the flag, from the mode, the gate, the isolation result, the Action's kind (ticket Action, plain Action, install) and, for a ticket Action, whether its ticket is AFK. The table (the isolation gate applies on top of every row):

| Action | `off` | `afkTickets` | `allSessions` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Work ticket, Launch fresh | – | AFK tickets | every ticket |
| Resume (by id), Resume by name | – | AFK tickets | every ticket |
| Chart a map, To spec, Run skill…, Setup | – | – | ✓ |
| Install plugin, Install with npx, the scout's background `claude` | – | – | – |

**Core: Action builders.** `workTicket`, `launchFresh`, `resumeById`, `resumeByName`, `resumeEnded`, `toSpec`, `chartMap`, `runSkill` and `setup` take an optional bypass input, default off. When it's on they add `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` to the argv, so `command` (the shell-quoted render) carries it. The install builders take no such input. `next` passes nothing and is unchanged.

**Core: health.**

- Two codes join `healthCodes` and `HEALTH_TABLE`: `bypass-not-isolated` (quiet) and `bypass-refused-as-root` (loud).
- A pure `bypassHealth({ bypassPermissions, onlyWhenIsolated, isolation, root, sandboxEnv }): Raised[]` raises them. `bypass-not-isolated` is raised when mode ≠ `off`, the gate is on and `isolation.isolated` is false, whether or not any AFK ticket is open.
  - Detail: `<where>, <why>`. `<where>` maps `ssh-remote` → "Remote-SSH", `wsl` → "WSL", `tunnel` → "Remote Tunnel", none → "local window", anything else → the raw name. `<why>` is "no container marker", or "a toolbx or distrobox container" when vetoed.
  - Message: "Bypass permissions is on, but this window is not an isolated environment (<detail>), so sessions keep their permission prompts."
  - Hint: "Reopen the folder in a Dev Container, or turn off heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissionsOnlyWhenIsolated."
  - The detail is part of the dismissal key, as for every code today.
- `bypass-refused-as-root` is raised when the flag would actually be added (mode ≠ `off` and the gate passes), `root` is true and `sandboxEnv` is false.
  - Message: "Claude Code refuses bypass permissions as root, so bypassed sessions exit as soon as they start."
  - Hint: "Run the window as a non-root user (a devcontainer's `remoteUser`), or set heroSynergy.sessions.bypassPermissions to off." The hint never names `IS_SANDBOX`.
- `disableBypassPermissionsMode` is not detected and gets no code.

**Core: starting hint.** The session state machine's 15 s hint gains a bypass variant: "no status yet, the session may be waiting at the trust or bypass-permissions dialog, open the terminal". A session whose planned command carried the flag gets the variant; every other session keeps `NO_STATUS_HINT` as it is. The launch records whether it was bypassed, so the host doesn't re-derive it from settings that may have changed since.

**Host (VS Code extension).**

- At activation the host collects the isolation facts (`vscode.env.remoteName` plus the three marker checks). It also reads `root` (`process.getuid?.() === 0`, false on Windows) and `sandboxEnv` (`IS_SANDBOX=1` or `CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP` set in the host's env). None of these change while the window is open.
- The host reads both settings through its workspace service, as it reads `heroSynergy.claude.path`. The bypass policy (mode, gate, isolation) joins what the Cockpit uses to plan Actions. The triage label strings are read alongside the tracker, from the repo root.
- The flag is decided when Actions are planned, never at spawn time. On `onDidChangeConfiguration` for either setting the Cockpit plans again and calls `bypassHealth` again, so the Focus pane's command, Copy command and the spawned argv always agree.
- Running sessions are never touched.
- The Cockpit never writes `~/.claude`, never sets `IS_SANDBOX` or `CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP` in a session's env, and never answers a dialog.

**Docs.**

- Extension README: the Settings table gains both rows. A new section, "Bypass permissions", covers:
  - what each mode covers, and the AFK ticket rule;
  - the isolation gate and what counts;
  - that isolated means "in a container", not "sandboxed";
  - the one-time Claude Code dialog, and that a session can sit in "starting" until you accept it;
  - the root refusal, without naming the undocumented escape variables;
  - that `disableBypassPermissionsMode` silently downgrades;
  - that ask rules, `AskUserQuestion` and critical-path `rm` still stop a bypassed session.
- `docs/upstream.md`:
  - Launch flags: `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`; `--resume` drops the mode; root refuses unless `IS_SANDBOX=1`/`CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP` (undocumented); the bypass dialog leaves no registry entry; `disableBypassPermissionsMode` downgrades rather than refuses.
  - VS Code: the five resolver `remoteName` values.
  - Process: the marker files and the toolbx/distrobox `/run/.toolboxenv`.
  - mattpocock-skills: the `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` table.
  - Each row cites #124, #125, #126 or #127.

## Testing Decisions

A good test drives a module through its public interface and asserts what a user or caller sees: the planned command string, the spawned argv, the Health row's entries, the session's hint. It never asserts internal calls or intermediate structures. The harness is first-class: every rule below gets full coverage, and none is trimmed for CI cost.

There are two seams, both already in use:

1. **Core's pure functions, by table test** (Vitest, as in `health.test.ts`, `actions.test.ts`, `session.test.ts`, `read.test.ts`):
   - `isolationOf`: every `remoteName` (the five allowlisted names, `ssh-remote`, `wsl`, `tunnel`, none) crossed with every combination of the three marker files. Asserts the signal or the not-isolated `remoteName`/`vetoedBy`.
   - The isolation fact collector against an in-memory `FileSystem` layer (prior art: `file-system.test.ts` and the scout tests).
   - `isAfkTicket`: every type (research, task, prototype, grilling, none) × `ready-for-agent` × `ready-for-human`, with default and renamed label strings.
   - The triage-labels reader: the repo's own file, a renamed table, a missing file, a file missing a row.
   - The bypass decision: mode × gate × isolated × Action kind × AFK.
   - The Action builders: each builder with bypass on and off, asserting `argv` and `command`; the install builders never change.
   - `bypassHealth`: setting × gate × isolation (each `<where>` and `<why>`) × root × sandbox env, asserting codes and details. `healthEntryOf` asserts each code's level, message and hint.
   - The session state machine: the starting hint for a bypassed and a plain launch.
   - Snapshot reading: `Ticket.labels` from a GitHub collect and a local tracker.
2. **The Cockpit controller** (`cockpit.test.ts` with its fake services, the highest seam the host has). The facts, settings and triage file are fed in; the tests assert what the Focus pane shows, what is spawned and what the Health row lists:
   - an AFK and a HITL ticket under each mode, in and out of an isolated environment;
   - Resume and Resume by name carrying the flag;
   - plain Actions under `allSessions`;
   - a settings change re-planning the commands and the Health row;
   - the shown command equalling the spawned argv;
   - the root warning with and without a sandbox variable;
   - the bypass starting hint;
   - dismissing `bypass-not-isolated` keyed to its detail.

   Prior art: "the Cockpit controller launching a ticket", "…resuming, adopting terminals and showing worktrees", "…reporting health" and "…dismissing an entry".

Plus:

- `manifest.test.ts`: both settings exist with their enum, defaults and `"scope": "machine"`.
- The webview: if the hint is rendered differently, `Launch.test.ts` asserts the "no status yet" row with the new hover text.
- The extension-host integration suite gains no new case. Reading `vscode.env.remoteName` there is a one-line adapter, and the controller test covers its consumers.

## Out of Scope

- The `next` CLI: it reads no VS Code settings, and its commands stay unbypassed.
- A general permission-mode passthrough (`acceptEdits`, `auto`, …): this is bypass only.
- A per-ticket bypass toggle in the Focus pane.
- Setting up a sandbox or container.
- Inspecting a container's config (mounts, `--privileged`, the Docker socket).
- Detecting `disableBypassPermissionsMode`, in any settings source.
- Accepting or pre-accepting Claude Code's bypass dialog, writing `~/.claude`, or setting `IS_SANDBOX`/`CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP`.
- A canary check for the resolver names or the marker files.
- A "bypass is active" health note: the Focus pane's command already shows the flag.
- Isolation signals from environment variables, including as labels.

## Further Notes

- The flag can't be added while the bypass dialog is open, because the dialog leaves no registry entry. Such a session reads "starting" until someone accepts. The hint is the only signal.
- A bypassed session still stops for ask/deny rules, `AskUserQuestion` and critical-path `rm` (denied after two minutes since 2.1.281), and can show `waiting` for those.
- Measured on Claude Code 2.1.212 (floor), 2.1.289 (ceiling) and 2.1.292; the research lives on `research/bypass-contract` and `research/isolation-signals`.
- A wrong triage label name only means fewer sessions bypass: the safe direction.

Heads-up from #163 (local tracker state reading): on a local tracker, the snapshot's `Ticket` gains two fields:

- `role`: the triage role, read from the Status line (`Status: ready-for-human`, `open — needs-triage`) or a `Labels:` line;
- `modeNote`: `AFK` or `HITL`, the leading word of the type line's parenthesis (`Label: wayfinder:task (HITL — …)`).

On a local ticket, the AFK rule here has to read these two fields, not only a labels line. A `ready-for-human` role or a `HITL` note makes a ticket not AFK; a `ready-for-agent` role makes it AFK. On the mirror of a real local tracker, 15 of the 21 open tickets on open maps carry a `HITL` note.
