159.title: Only Eduardo merges to main
159.body:
## Destination

Only Eduardo can merge to `main`. Agent sessions push branches and open PRs under their own weaker identity, with no admin, no bypass and no merge, and a ruleset on `main` enforces that. The repo's agent instructions describe the new flow.

## Notes

- Domain: GitHub repository security: rulesets, token types, and GitHub App or machine-user identities.
- **Execution is carried into this map.** The destination is a live protection state, not just a spec, so `task` tickets may change repo settings and credentials. Settings and credential changes are HITL unless Eduardo hands one over in the session.
- Stopgap in force since 2026-10-09: ruleset **Protect main** (id 24813840), active, no bypass actors. It blocks deletion and force pushes, requires a PR, and requires the checks `check`, `vscode (linux)` and `vscode (macos)`. `live` stays optional, per the comment in `ci.yml`. It stops direct pushes and red merges. It does **not** stop an agent from merging a green PR, because agents still use Eduardo's `gho_` OAuth token (`repo` scope, admin) from the shared `~/.config/gh` volume.
- The core constraint: any rule set under Eduardo's identity can be bypassed or deleted by that same credential, so the fix needs a second identity.
- Consult `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` on grilling tickets and `/research` on research tickets.

## Decisions so far

<!-- the index — one line per closed ticket -->

- [Which agent identity can open PRs but never merge?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/160) — GitHub App recommended (machine user as fallback); a fine-grained PAT on `dbarjs` is ruled out because self-authored PRs can only merge through a bypass the agent would share. Any option needs a 1-approval ruleset and the `gho_` token removed from agent reach. Role-vs-token bypass is unconfirmed.
- [Pick the agent's GitHub identity](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/161) — a private App `dbarjs-agent`, one per person, installed only on chosen repos. It holds Contents, PRs, Issues and Workflows write and no admin, and it pushes and calls `gh`. Its key may sit in the container. Eduardo's admin login leaves the container entirely, and claims assign `dbarjs` by name.
- [Settle the final main ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/162) — gate the branch, not the review. A new ruleset restricts updates to `main`, with only the admin role exempt. Protect main keeps no bypass, requires a PR with 0 approvals, merge commits only, signed commits and the same three checks. `v*` tags can't be deleted or moved. The approval rule and its wait on the App rollout are dropped.
- [Fit the release flow to the final ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/189) — release 0.2.0 now by hand: apply the rulesets and release immutability first, then one "Approve workflows to run" click and the merge. From then on, `release.yml` starts CI on the Release PR with a `workflow_dispatch`. GitHub Releases become immutable, so the App can't swap a release's VSIX before a backfill.

## Not yet specified

- **Commit signing and authorship.** Agent commits are currently signed with Eduardo's key, under his name. Whether that stays true with a separate identity is open. Since [Settle the final main ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/162), Protect main requires every commit on a PR branch to be verified, so whatever signs agent commits must keep them verified.

160.title: Which agent identity can open PRs but never merge?
160.body:
## Question

Which agent identity can push branches and open PRs on `dbarjs/hero-synergy` (a public repo owned by a personal account) but can **never** merge to `main` or change repo settings, while Eduardo (`dbarjs`, admin) can still merge those PRs without friction?

Compare at least these:

1. A **GitHub App** installed on the repo, with agents minting short-lived installation tokens.
2. A **machine user** account added as a collaborator with the Write role.
3. A **fine-grained PAT** on Eduardo's own account (Contents and Pull requests write, no Administration).

For each one, answer from primary GitHub docs:

- Which ruleset rule actually stops its merge? Options include required approvals, `require_last_push_approval` and bypass actors. Can Eduardo still merge, via approval or admin bypass?
- Does admin bypass follow the **user's role** or the **token's permissions**? This decides option 3, because PRs authored by `dbarjs` can't be approved by `dbarjs`.
- Who appears as the PR and commit author? Does that change commit signing?
- What does minting and storing the credential in a devcontainer cost (expiry, rotation)? Does the "one free machine account" ToS rule apply?
- What can it still do that matters, such as create tags, trigger workflows or edit issues for wayfinder?

lastComment.body:
Findings are in [`docs/research/agent-identity.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/agent-identity/docs/research/agent-identity.md) on `research/agent-identity`.

**Recommendation: use a GitHub App.** Give it Contents, Pull requests, Issues and Metadata, and never Administration. Keep it off the bypass list. Change "Protect main" to `required_approving_review_count: 1`, `require_last_push_approval: true` and `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: true`. The App can't approve its own PRs. Eduardo merges by approving and then merging, so no bypass actor is needed. Tokens last 1 hour, and the App uses no seat or machine account.

- **Fallback:** a machine user as collaborator gives the same gate. It needs a **classic** PAT, because fine-grained PATs don't work for repository collaborators, and it uses up the one free machine account.
- **Reject the fine-grained PAT on `dbarjs`.** Merging needs only Contents: write. Eduardo can't approve his own PRs. The only way to merge is a bypass that, by the documented model, the agent's PAT would inherit.

**Prerequisite for any option:** move Eduardo's `gho_` token out of the agents' shared `~/.config/gh`.

**Unconfirmed:** no primary source says whether role or user bypass is evaluated against the token's permissions. The file describes a quick test using `current_user_can_bypass`.

161.title: Pick the agent's GitHub identity
161.body:
## Question

Which agent identity does hero-synergy adopt so agents can open PRs but never merge to `main`: a GitHub App, a machine user, or a fine-grained PAT? Where does its credential live in the devcontainer?

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Eduardo accepted the round as written on 2026-10-09.

**Identity: a private GitHub App, `dbarjs-agent`.** It is owned by `dbarjs` and installed only on selected repos, hero-synergy first. It is one App per person, not per repo: the devcontainer image is shared by every project, so another repo joins by adding an installation.

- **Permissions:**
  - Contents: write
  - Pull requests: write
  - Issues: write, for sub-issues, blocked-by and claims
  - Workflows: write. Agents edit `ci.yml`, and those edits still go through Eduardo's approval.
  - Metadata: read
  - It gets **no** Administration, Actions write or Secrets.
  - It is **never** a ruleset bypass actor.
- **Threat model:** a well-meaning agent following stale instructions or memory, like the `--auto` merges of #98 and #111. The rule: no credential an agent can reach without trying, whether in env, `gh`, the git credential helper or a shared volume, can merge to `main` or edit rulesets. The forwarded SSH agent stays. It can push branches as `dbarjs`, but it can't merge, and the ruleset already stops it pushing to `main`.
- **Eduardo's admin login leaves the container.** Agents and Eduardo's shell are the same Unix user `vscode`, so an admin `gho_` token anywhere in the container is within agent reach. Eduardo approves and merges from the GitHub web UI, or with `gh` on his host. The container's `~/.config/gh` ends up holding only the App credential.
- **The App token does both `gh` and `git push`.** The git side goes through `gh auth git-credential` for `github.com`. The VS Code credential helper stays only for other hosts. This is required, not a preference: with `require_last_push_approval: true`, a branch pushed as `dbarjs` makes Eduardo the last pusher, so he couldn't approve his own PR.
- **The App's private key is in the container and readable by agents, outside `~/.config/gh`.** It can only mint tokens with the App's own narrow power. Agents mint 1-hour installation tokens on demand.
- **Wayfinder claims assign `dbarjs` by name.** The App does the assigning, and `@me` would resolve to the bot.

**Carried forward:**
- The key's exact path, how tokens refresh, and swapping the shared `~/.config/gh` are left to the credential rollout ticket.
- Commit signing and authorship stay in the map's fog.
- The open question in #160, whether bypass is checked against a user's role or the token's permissions, no longer matters: there are no bypass actors, and the App holds no admin role.

162.title: Settle the final main ruleset

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Eduardo accepted the round as written on 2026-11-16.

**The gate is on the branch, not the review: only the admin role can update `main`.** Two rulesets on the default branch, plus one on tags:

1. **Protect main** (id 24813840, edited in place). It has **no bypass actors**, so it binds Eduardo too.
   - Rules: deletion, non_fast_forward, `required_signatures`, `pull_request` and `required_status_checks`.
   - `pull_request`:
     - `required_approving_review_count: 0`
     - `require_last_push_approval: false`
     - `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: false`
     - `allowed_merge_methods: ["merge"]`
     - No code-owner review and no thread resolution.
     - `require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes` stays at its default (`true`). It applies only to PRs Copilot opens, and it does nothing at 0 approvals.
   - `required_status_checks`: `check`, `vscode (linux)` and `vscode (macos)`, not strict. `live` stays optional.
   - No `required_linear_history`.
2. **Only Eduardo merges to main** (new). One rule, `update` ("Restrict updates"). Its single bypass actor is the repository admin role in **`exempt`** mode. In a personal repo, only the owner holds that role.
3. **Protect release tags** (new, tag target, `refs/tags/v*`). Rules `deletion` and `update`, no bypass actors, and creation unrestricted.

**Why this gate and not the approval.** The approval-based draft from [Which agent identity can open PRs but never merge?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/160) had three holes:

- **The App could merge whatever Eduardo approved.** Merging needs only Contents: write.
- **Eduardo couldn't merge PRs he authored.** Authors can't approve their own PRs.
- **A workflow could approve.** "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" is on for changesets. A workflow the App writes on its own branch could approve its PR with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

Restricting updates closes all three:

- The App, `GITHUB_TOKEN` and any workflow can never move `main`.
- Eduardo merges any green PR, his own included, with the normal button. `exempt` means no bypass checkbox and no audit entry. Layering means Protect main still holds him to a PR, green checks and signed commits.
- The App stays off every bypass list, as [Pick the agent's GitHub identity](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/161) decided.

**Merge commits only.** Every PR since #106 has merged with a merge commit. Build sessions branch off an unmerged blocker's branch, and squash or rebase rewrites the blocker's commits under the stacked PR. GitHub can't sign rebase merges, and the release notes read the changelog, not commit messages.

**Signed commits are required.** All of `main`'s last 100 commits are verified, and so is every commit on the five open PRs. GitHub signs the merge commits it makes in the web UI. The rule also checks every commit on the PR branch.

**Release tags.** Creation stays open because `release.yml` creates `v<version>` with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub Actions can't reliably be a bypass actor. The docs only name "GitHub Apps", and third-party reports show a 422 error. The accepted gap: the App could create a stray `v*` tag, and `release.yml` would then skip that version. Eduardo clears it by switching the rule off briefly.

**What this supersedes:**

- The ordering constraint in this ticket's earlier comment. With 0 approvals, `require_last_push_approval` is off, so nothing waits on [Run agent sessions as the App, not Eduardo](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/165). The rulesets can go live at once. They start binding agents as soon as the admin token leaves the container. Until then, agents hold Eduardo's admin token, so they're exempt like him.
- "No bypass actors" in that comment. The admin role is exempt from the update rule only.
- ADR 0008's gate paragraph. #167 had already merged it, so it's amended in #191.
- The reason [Pick the agent's GitHub identity](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/161) gave for pushing as the App, which was being the last pusher. That reason no longer applies. Pushing as the App stays decided.

**Unconfirmed facts, checked by [Apply the final main ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/188):**

- That "Restrict updates" blocks merging a PR and not only pushes. The REST wording is "update matching refs", and community threads report "The base branch does not allow updates". The proof is the `gh pr merge` failure in the smoke test of [Run agent sessions as the App, not Eduardo](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/165).
- That `exempt` is offered for the admin role. If it isn't, fall back to `pull_request` mode, which costs one bypass tick per merge.
- That the admin role's `actor_id` is 5. Only community sources give it, so check it in the UI.
- That the tag `update` rule leaves creation alone. The next release checks this.

**Carried forward:**

- Commit signing fog: whatever signs agent commits must leave them verified, or their PRs can't merge.
- Release and tag paths fog, now tickets:
  - [Fit the release flow to the final ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/189): the Release PR's CI waits on "Approve workflows to run", and the App can edit or delete a GitHub Release, which the tag ruleset doesn't cover.
  - [Limit the marketplace environment to main](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/190): the environment has no deployment-branch policy, so a workflow on any branch can publish.
- [Run agent sessions as the App, not Eduardo](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/165) is now blocked by [Apply the final main ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/188). Its smoke test (`gh pr merge` fails) can only pass once the update rule is live.

163.title: Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds
163.body:
From the map [#130 State reading for local trackers, tested against a real five-month tracker](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/130). Every reading rule below was settled there:

- [#131](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/131): the forms a real tracker holds, and their counts.
- [#134](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/134): the truth for the files a careful reader can't call.
- [#135](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/135): a ticket's Status line and claim.
- [#136](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/136): a map's own state.
- [#137](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/137): type, blockers and membership.
- [#138](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/138): the resolution.
- [#139](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/139): unmapped issues.
- [#145](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/145): semicolons between blocker items.

The fixtures the scout is tested against are already on `main`: the pattern fixture from [#133](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/133) and the scratch mirror from [#132](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/132).

This spec also settles the map's three "Not yet specified" items:

- the new drift codes' words and levels, and how a triage role and a long Status line show;
- whether the canary runs the mirror, and how the upstream register records forms upstream never shipped;
- what a refresh costs on a 49-effort `.scratch`.

Glossary terms used (`CONTEXT.md`): **Header line**, **Blocker**, **Claim**, **Triage role**, **Resolution**, **Unmapped issue**, **Map**, **Finished map**, **Stuck map**, **Frontier**, **Drift**, **Warning**, **Snapshot**, **Scout**. "State" is open or closed; "Status line" is the literal `Status:` line.

## Problem Statement

I keep a local tracker under `.scratch/` on a private production project. Over five months it grew to 49 effort directories, 35 maps, 257 tickets and 50 other notes. When I open the Cockpit on it, almost nothing it shows is true. Measured in #131:

- **Maps.** On Linux the Cockpit finds none of my maps. Every one is named `MAP.md`, and the scout opens only `map.md`, so every ticket lands in one flat Unmapped list as `no-map`.
- **State.** Even with the maps found, only 2 of the closed tickets read as closed. My tickets say `Status: closed (…)`, `done`, `wontfix` or a triage role such as `ready-for-human`. The scout knows only `claimed` and `resolved`, so it raises `unknown-status` on 255 tickets.
- **Type.** Only 18 tickets get a type. My types sit on `Label: wayfinder:task (AFK)` and `Labels:` lines, and nothing shows that a ticket is marked HITL.
- **Claim.** Claims live on `Assignee:` lines and in `open — claimed <date>`, so claimed tickets sit on the frontier.
- **Blockers.** My `Blocked by:` lines hold links, file names, numbers followed by notes, and none markers.
  - The scout drops every linked blocker.
  - It turns digits from notes and link titles into blockers.
  - It never reads `Blocks:`.

  So the frontier is wrong in both directions.
- **Resolution.** Only 17 tickets get a resolution, the ones that use `## Answer`. The rest put it in other places:
  - a `### Resolution (<date> …)` heading under `## Comments`;
  - a `## Resolution` heading;
  - a bold `**Resolution …**` label;
  - a last dated comment.

  The Detail shows no answer for those, and `closed-no-resolution` fires on most closed tickets.
- **Closed maps.** Maps I closed months ago (`Status: **DONE <date>** — …`) would show as open, with all their tickets.
- **Unmapped issues.**
  - Triage issues and `/to-tickets` issues under a PRD show as tickets, with `no-map` and `type-missing`.
  - Every effort numbers its files from `01`, so rows in the Unmapped list collide: 12 of the 24 mapless issue files are `#1`.

I can't tell what the Cockpit shows about this tracker from noise. I don't want my tracker rewritten to fit either: drift is reported, never corrected.

## Solution

The scout reads every form the real tracker holds, with code alone, by the rules map #130 settled. What code can't read is drift, never interpreted ([ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md)).

- **Maps.** A file named `map.md` in any casing is the effort's map. Its own Status line closes it only when it starts with `DONE` or `destination reached`. A closed map is hidden with its tickets, as a closed GitHub map is.
- **Ticket state and claim.**
  - The first word of the Status line decides the state. `closed`, `done`, `resolved` and `wontfix` close a ticket; `open`, `claimed` and the triage roles leave it open.
  - After `open`, one more word can set a triage role or a claim.
  - An open ticket is also claimed by a name on its `Assignee:` line.
- **Type.** It comes from `Type:`, `Label:` and `Labels:`. A `HITL` note takes a task or research ticket out of AFK.
- **Blockers.** A blocker is the reference at the start of each `Blocked by:` and `Blocks:` item.
- **Resolution.** It is `## Answer`; else the last Resolution heading or label; else, on a closed ticket only, the last comment.
- **Unmapped issues.** These are the issue files of an effort without a map, plus `/to-tickets` issues whose `Parent:` names a PRD.
  - They show in the Unmapped fold, grouped by effort.
  - They are never on a frontier, and they raise no `no-map` or `type-missing`.
  - They are hidden once closed.
- **In the Cockpit.**
  - A ticket's triage role shows as a chip on its row and in its panes. It never changes the frontier.
  - Its Status line shows on one line in the Focus pane and in full in the Detail.
- **Drift.** Eleven new codes. Each is quiet when the form was still read correctly, and loud when what the Cockpit shows may be wrong. The words are in the drift table.
- **Proof.** The scout agrees with the truth of both fixtures on `main`, file by file:
  - the pattern fixture: 164 invented files, one per form;
  - the scratch mirror: the real tracker's 342 files, with their text replaced.

  On the mirror, the Cockpit shows:
  - 20 open maps: 14 takeable, 3 stuck and 3 finished;
  - 16 tickets on their frontiers;
  - 17 open unmapped issues in 7 effort groups.

  It hides the 15 closed maps with their 70 tickets.

## User Stories

### Maps

1. As a Cockpit user on a local tracker, I want an effort's `MAP.md` found as its map, so that a tracker that names every map `MAP.md` shows its maps on a case-sensitive disk too.
2. As a Cockpit user, I want `map.md` in any casing read the same, with no drift for the casing the template doesn't use, so that a naming habit isn't reported as a fault.
3. As a Cockpit user whose effort holds `map.md` and `MAP.md` side by side, I want a loud `map-file-ambiguous` naming both files and the one that was read, so that I know the Cockpit picked one.
4. As a Cockpit user, I want a map whose Status line starts with `DONE` or `destination reached` hidden with all its tickets, in any case and bold or not, so that efforts I finished months ago stop filling the Tree.
5. As a Cockpit user, I want a map read as open with no drift when its Status line starts with `in progress`, `charted`, `REOPENED` or `route walked`, or when it has no Status line, so that the forms my maps use cost nothing.
6. As a Cockpit user, I want a `DONE` later in a map's Status line (`07 DONE <date>`, `<prose> **DONE <date>**`) never to close the map, so that a history of closed tickets isn't read as a closed map.
7. As a Cockpit user, I want a map whose Status line starts with any other word read as open, with a quiet `map-status-unknown`, so that the map stays visible and I can see the line wasn't understood.
8. As a Cockpit user, I want headings and prose such as `## Destination reached` and `Frontier: empty` never to close a map, so that only the map's own Status line decides.
9. As a Cockpit user, I want an open map whose tickets are all closed folded into Finished, so that a map marked `route walked`, or with no Status line, is still offered To spec.
10. As a Cockpit user, I want `Label: wayfinder:map`, `Charted:`, `Recharted:`, `Redrawn:` and a state word at the start of a decision's gist ignored with no drift, so that dates and gists never change a state.

### A ticket's state and claim

11. As a Cockpit user, I want a ticket read as closed when its Status line starts with `closed`, `done`, `resolved` or `wontfix`, in any case and with any `**` around it, so that my closed tickets read as closed.
12. As a Cockpit user, I want the annotation after the first word (a date, a parenthesis, a dash clause) never to reverse the state, so that `closed <date> (reopened and re-closed …)` stays closed.
13. As a Cockpit user, I want `open`, `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent` and `ready-for-human` read as open, and a ticket with no Status line read as open, so that a triage word never hides a ticket.
14. As a Cockpit user, I want `Status: claimed` read as open and claimed, so that the template's claim still works.
15. As a Cockpit user, I want `open — claimed <date>` and `open (claimed …)` read as claims, so that a claim written after `open` takes the ticket off the frontier.
16. As a Cockpit user, I want `open — needs-triage (blocked)` and `open (ready-for-human — …)` to set the triage role, so that a role written after `open` is seen.
17. As a Cockpit user, I want an open ticket whose `Assignee:` line names someone claimed by that name, so that the Focus pane says who holds it. The name is the text before any parenthesis or dash.
18. As a Cockpit user, I want `Assignee: —`, an empty Assignee, `(unclaimed)` and `— (unclaimed)` to name nobody, so that a placeholder never claims a ticket.
19. As a Cockpit user, I want a closed ticket never claimed, whatever its Assignee line or a leftover `claimed <date>`, so that history never reads as a live claim.
20. As a Cockpit user, I want a claim that names nobody, such as `Status: claimed` alone, shown as "claimed", so that the Focus pane never shows an empty claim.
21. As a Cockpit user, I want a named local claim never shown as "claimed by someone else", so that the Cockpit doesn't warn about a name it has no login to compare with.
22. As a Cockpit user, I want a Status line whose first word isn't in the vocabulary read as open, still claimable through `Assignee:`, with a loud `unknown-status`, so that the ticket stays visible and I'm told the line wasn't understood. One line holding a DONE half and an OPEN half is such a line.
23. As a Cockpit user, I want a second Status header line ignored, with `unknown-status`, so that two lines never fight over the state.
24. As a Cockpit user, I want a Status line never read when it is quoted in inline code under `## Question`, comes after the first H2, or sits in a code fence, so that a closing protocol written in a ticket's body doesn't close it.
25. As a Cockpit user, I want a header line with a bold key (`**Status:**`, `**Blocked by:**`) read like a plain one, with one quiet `header-key-bold` per file naming the bold keys, so that bold styling works and is noted once.

### Triage role and Status line in the Cockpit

26. As a Cockpit user, I want a ticket's triage role read from its Status line or its `Labels:` line, with the Status line winning, so that the role is seen wherever it's written.
27. As a Cockpit user, I want the triage role never to change the frontier, so that an open, unblocked, unclaimed ticket is takeable whatever its role, as the wayfinder skill and GitHub labels behave.
28. As a Cockpit user, I want `wontfix` to close a ticket and also be its role, so that a won't-fix ticket is closed and labelled.
29. As a Cockpit user, I want a ticket's role shown as a chip on its Tree row, beside its mode, so that I see `ready-for-human` before I launch it.
30. As a Cockpit user, I want the role shown in the Focus pane and in the Detail, so that the panes say what the row says.
31. As a Cockpit user, I want a ticket's Status line shown in the Focus pane on one line, cut with an ellipsis and complete on hover, when it says more than its first word, so that a long annotation doesn't swamp the pane.
32. As a Cockpit user, I want the Detail to show the whole Status line, rendered like the body, so that I can read a long annotation without opening the file.

### Type and HITL

33. As a Cockpit user, I want a ticket's type read from `Type:`, `Label:` and `Labels:` lines, with or without the `wayfinder:` prefix and with any parenthesis after it, so that my tickets are typed.
34. As a Cockpit user, I want `Labels: wayfinder:task, ready-for-agent` to give both the type and the role, so that one line can carry both.
35. As a Cockpit user, I want a plain `Type: <type>` to raise nothing, and a type on a `Label:` or `Labels:` line or with a `wayfinder:` prefix to raise a quiet `type-as-label`, so that the template's form is the silent one.
36. As a Cockpit user, I want lines that name different types to raise a loud `type-several` and give no type, so that a conflict is never settled by guessing.
37. As a Cockpit user, I want the H1 prefix (`# Task: …`) never read as a type, and the title kept verbatim, so that a title can't type a ticket.
38. As a Cockpit user, I want a leading `HITL` in the type's parenthesis to make a task or research ticket HITL, shown as HITL on its row, so that a ticket marked for me never reads as AFK.
39. As a Cockpit user, I want a leading `AFK` on a prototype or grilling ticket to leave it HITL and raise a loud `mode-conflicts-type`, so that a note can take a ticket out of AFK but never put one in.
40. As a Cockpit user, I want an `AFK` note on a task ticket shown as AFK, so that the row says who drives it.
41. As a Cockpit user, I want a HITL note read only from the start of the type's parenthesis, never from the prose after it, so that a word or number in a note never becomes data.

### Blockers

42. As a Cockpit user, I want each `Blocked by:` item to name the ticket at its start, so that every blocker form my tracker uses gates. The start is a link to a ticket file, a bare `NN-<slug>.md`, or a leading `NN` or `#NN`.
43. As a Cockpit user, I want a link's title, and everything after the reference (`(closed <date>)`, `**UNBLOCKED**`, `— <prose>`), never read, so that a blocker's state always comes from its own file.
44. As a Cockpit user, I want items split on commas outside brackets and parentheses, and on a semicolon only before a reference, so that `[A](01-a.md) (closed …); [B](02-b.md)` names two blockers and `NN resolved <date>; frontier — …` names one.
45. As a Cockpit user, I want `—`, an empty value, `none`, `nothing`, `(none …` and `(nothing …` to mean no blockers, with no drift, so that a none marker that names a closed ticket doesn't gate.
46. As a Cockpit user, I want the template's `Blocked by: NN, NN` to raise nothing and every other form that was read to raise a quiet `blockers-not-template` with the raw value, so that I can see which lines are off the template.
47. As a Cockpit user, I want an item with no reference at its start to raise a loud `blocker-unread` naming the item, and a lone slug to keep its loud `blockers-as-slugs`, so that a dependency the Cockpit can't follow is never silent.
48. As a Cockpit user, I want `Blocks:` read with the same grammar and merged into the blocked ticket's blockers, with a quiet `blocks-line`, so that an edge written on either side gates.
49. As a Cockpit user, I want the Detail's "clears the way for" to list the tickets a `Blocks:` line names, so that the neighbourhood follows both directions.
50. As a Cockpit user, I want a blocker resolved within the ticket's effort, and a reference to a missing file or one outside the effort to raise a quiet `blocker-outside-map` and not gate, so that a dangling reference never blocks forever.

### Membership and unmapped issues

51. As a Cockpit user, I want the directory to decide which map a ticket belongs to, and a `Map:` or `Parent:` line naming the effort's own map to raise nothing, so that GitHub-shaped lines cost nothing when they agree.
52. As a Cockpit user, I want a `Map:` or `Parent:` line naming another effort's map or a missing file to raise a loud `map-line-disagrees`, with the directory still winning, so that a moved ticket is pointed out.
53. As a Cockpit user, I want a `/to-tickets` issue whose `Parent:` names a PRD to be an unmapped issue, not a ticket of the map beside it, so that a map's counts, frontier and finished state count its tickets only.
54. As a Cockpit user, I want every issue file of an effort without a map to be an unmapped issue, so that triage issues and spec issues show without pretending to be tickets.
55. As a Cockpit user, I want unmapped issues in the one Unmapped fold above Finished, grouped by effort in directory order and in number order within a group, so that issues of different efforts never mix.
56. As a Cockpit user, I want a group labelled with its effort's map title when the effort has a map, and with the directory name otherwise, so that I recognise the effort.
57. As a Cockpit user, I want each unmapped row keyed by its effort and its number, so that two efforts' `#1` never select, reveal or dismiss each other.
58. As a Cockpit user, I want a closed unmapped issue hidden, and an effort with no open unmapped issue to show no group, so that the fold holds only open work.
59. As a Cockpit user, I want an open `/to-tickets` issue in an effort whose map is closed to stay in the Unmapped fold under that map's title, so that open work never vanishes with a closed map.
60. As a Cockpit user, I want an unmapped issue never on a frontier and never "next", whatever its role (`ready-for-agent` included), so that only a map's tickets are offered for work.
61. As a Cockpit user, I want an unmapped issue to raise no `no-map`, `type-missing` or `no-question-heading`, so that a normal local form isn't drift. Every other rule (state, claim, role, blockers, resolution) still applies.
62. As a Cockpit user, I want an effort with neither a map file nor issue files, such as a PRD or notes folder, ignored with no warning, so that folders without tickets cost nothing.
63. As a Cockpit user, I want PRDs, specs, research write-ups, asset notes, handoffs and checklists never read as tickets or maps, so that their header lines and tables change nothing.

### Resolution

64. As a Cockpit user, I want a closed ticket's resolution read from `## Answer`, else from its last Resolution heading or bold label (in English or the tracker's second language), else from its last comment under `## Comments`, so that the Detail shows the answer wherever it was written.
65. As a Cockpit user, I want the last Resolution label to win, so that a reopened ticket's second closing is its answer.
66. As a Cockpit user, I want a bold `**Resolved**` or `**Done**`, and a `## Decision` section, never read as a Resolution label, so that only the words the rule names count.
67. As a Cockpit user, I want an open ticket never to show a resolution, even with dated comments or a Resolution heading, so that work in progress isn't shown as answered.
68. As a Cockpit user, I want the resolution's date and author taken from the label's ISO date and a dated item's `(<person>)`, never from prose, so that the byline is a fact.
69. As a Cockpit user, I want each placement labelled by how sure its reading is, so that I can tell an answer from a fallback:
    - a resolution outside `## Answer` raises a quiet `resolution-outside-answer` naming its form;
    - the last-comment fallback raises a quiet `resolution-from-last-comment`;
    - no resolution at all raises a loud `closed-no-resolution`.

### Drift words and refresh

70. As a Cockpit user, I want every new drift code worded like the others, so that the warnings read as one catalogue:
    - its message says what was found, and its hint gives the template's form;
    - it is loud only where the Cockpit may be wrong, so that hundreds of tickets in an old form don't bury real drift.
71. As a Cockpit user, I want `unknown-status`'s hint to list the Status vocabulary, and `closed-no-resolution`'s hint to name the Resolution heading, so that each hint says what would have been read.
72. As a Cockpit user on a 49-effort tracker, I want a change under `.scratch` to refresh the Tree within about a second, so that a session's edits show at once.

### Maintainers

73. As a maintainer, I want one table test checking that the scout agrees with the pattern fixture's truth on every file, so that every rule is pinned by its form. The test covers state, claim, role, type, HITL note, membership, blockers, resolution and drift.
74. As a maintainer, I want the scout to agree with the scratch mirror's truth on all 342 files, so that the rules hold at real scale.
75. As a maintainer, I want the mirror's Tree checked end to end, so that a rule change that moves what I see shows up in review. The check covers maps by urgency, frontiers, unmapped groups and hidden maps.
76. As a maintainer, I want a census of the drift codes on the mirror asserted, so that a change in what the Cockpit warns about at real scale is a deliberate diff.
77. As a maintainer, I want the mirror truth's map decisions to follow the leading link of each Decisions-so-far line, as the scout does, so that a link inside a gist isn't counted as a decision.
78. As a maintainer, I want `docs/upstream.md` to list the forms the scout reads that upstream never shipped, each with its deciding ticket and drift code, so that an upstream review can tell a form from the wild from a contract.
79. As a maintainer, I want the canary to watch the local tracker template for the lines the scout reads, so that an upstream change to `Status:`, `Blocked by:`, `## Answer` or `## Comments` files an upstream break.
80. As a maintainer, I want the GitHub tracker's reading unchanged, so that this work can't regress the tracker most users have.
81. As the builder of [#155](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/155), I want the AFK rule to read a local ticket's triage role and HITL note from the snapshot, so that a `ready-for-human` or HITL-marked local ticket is never bypassed.

## Implementation Decisions

### The snapshot: schema version 2

- `Ticket` gains three fields. All three are null on GitHub, where nothing in this spec fills them:
  - `role`: the triage role, one of `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human` or `wontfix`, or null.
  - `statusLine`: the Status line's value as written, trimmed; null when the ticket has none. For display only: nothing derives from it.
  - `modeNote`: `'AFK' | 'HITL' | null`, the leading word inside the type line's parenthesis.
- On a local tracker, `claim.by` holds the `Assignee:` name, or is empty when nobody is named.
- `unmapped` becomes a list of groups:

  ```ts
  // One group of the Unmapped fold.
  interface UnmappedGroup {
    /** The effort's directory on a local tracker; null for a GitHub ticket outside every open map. */
    readonly effort: string | null
    /** The effort's map title when it has a map file, open or closed, else the directory name; null without an effort. */
    readonly title: string | null
    /** The group's open unmapped issues, in number order. */
    readonly tickets: ReadonlyArray<Ticket>
  }
  ```

  On GitHub, `unmapped` stays empty: only native sub-issues are collected. The generic reader's synthetic strays go in one group with no effort.
- The snapshot schema version goes to 2, so a cached version-1 snapshot is ignored rather than decoded.
- Nothing else in the snapshot changes. It holds open maps only, so a closed local map never appears in it.

### The local tracker reader

**Efforts and files**

- An effort is each directory directly under `.scratch`, in byte order, as today. A map keeps its number: the 1-based position of its effort's directory.
- **The map file.** A file directly in the effort directory whose name is `map.md` in any casing.
  - It is found by listing the directory, never by opening a fixed name. That way a case-sensitive disk and a case-insensitive one read the same files.
  - When several casings exist side by side, the reader takes `map.md` if it is there, else the first name in byte order. It raises a loud `map-file-ambiguous` on the map, whose detail names the files found and the one read.
- **Issue files** are `issues/NN-<slug>.md`, as today.
- **Other Markdown** is never read as a ticket or a map: PRDs, `spec.md`, research write-ups, asset notes, handoffs and checklists.
- An effort with neither a map file nor issue files is skipped without a warning.

**Header lines** (#137, and the glossary's Header line)

- A header line is a `Key: value` line before the first H2.
  - It sits outside code fences, and it is not a list item.
  - Its key is plain, or bold: `**Key:** value` or `**Key**: value`.
  - Keys match in any case, and the first line of each key wins.
- Nothing after the first H2, inside a fence, or quoted in inline code is ever read.
- Maps and tickets read their header lines the same way. A file with any bold key raises one quiet `header-key-bold`, whose detail lists the bold keys in order.

**A map's own state** (#136)

- Only the map's Status header line decides its state.
  - The reader strips `**` from the value and compares its first words in any case.
  - A map whose value starts with the word `DONE` or with `destination reached` is closed.
  - Anything else, including no Status line, is open.
  - The rest of the line is annotation and is never parsed.
- A map whose value starts with `in progress`, `charted`, `REOPENED` or `route walked` raises nothing.
  - Any other first word raises a quiet `map-status-unknown`, whose detail is that first word as written.
  - A missing Status line raises nothing, since upstream's map has none.
- The reader ignores these lines and words, with no drift:
  - `Label:` or `Labels: wayfinder:map`;
  - `Charted:`, `Recharted:` and `Redrawn:`;
  - a state word at the start of a decision's gist.
- A closed map is left out of the snapshot with its tickets.
  - Its title still labels the Unmapped group of its effort.
  - An open map whose tickets are all closed is a finished map, as today.
  - A map with no tickets is open and not finished, as today.
- The map's body sections are read as today: destination, notes, decisions, fog and out of scope, with their drift.

**A ticket's state, claim, role and Status line** (#135)

- **The first word.** It is the first word of the Status value: its letters and hyphens, matched in any case, with any `**` stripped.

  | first word | state | also |
  |---|---|---|
  | `closed`, `done`, `resolved` | closed | |
  | `wontfix` | closed | role `wontfix` |
  | `open` | open | reads one more word (below) |
  | `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human` | open | that role |
  | `claimed` | open | claimed |
  | no Status line | open | |
  | anything else | open | loud `unknown-status`, detail: the value |

- **The word after `open`.** After `open`, and only there, the reader reads one more word: the first word after a dash (`—`, `–`, ` - `) or an opening parenthesis.
  - A role there sets the role.
  - `claimed` there claims the ticket.
  - Nothing else is read, so no word in an annotation can reopen a closed ticket.
- **A second Status header line** is ignored, and raises `unknown-status`.
- **The role.**
  - It comes from the Status line first.
  - Failing that, it comes from a `Labels:` line, from a comma-separated item that is exactly a role.
  - The vocabulary is the five default role names. Renamed triage labels are not read on a local tracker.
- **Claims.** An open ticket is claimed by:
  - a `claimed` first word;
  - `claimed` after `open`;
  - an `Assignee:` line that names someone.

  The claim works like this:
  - **The name** is the Assignee value with `**` stripped, cut before the first parenthesis or dash, and trimmed.
  - **Values that name nobody** are `—`, `–`, `-`, an empty value, `(unclaimed)` and `— (unclaimed)`.
  - **A claim with no name** has `by: []`.
  - **A closed ticket is never claimed**, whatever its Assignee line or a leftover `claimed <date>`.
- **`statusLine`** holds the whole Status value as written, trimmed, for display.

**Type and HITL note** (#137)

- **Sources.** The reader takes the type from `Type:`, `Label:` and `Labels:`. A `Labels:` line is split on commas, and every `wayfinder:<type>` item in it counts.
- **Value.** An optional `wayfinder:` prefix, then the first word, which must be one of the four types. The parenthesis after it is never searched for types or numbers.
- **Conflict.** When the sources name different types, the reader raises a loud `type-several`, whose detail lists the types, and reads no type.
- **Drift.**
  - A plain `Type: <type>` raises nothing.
  - A `Label:` or `Labels:` source, or a `wayfinder:` prefix, raises a quiet `type-as-label`, whose detail is the value.
  - An unknown `wayfinder:` word raises `unknown-wayfinder-labels` on the ticket.
  - A ticket of a map with no type raises a loud `type-missing`, as today.
- **The H1** is never a type, and the title stays verbatim.
- **The HITL note.**
  - `modeNote` is a leading `AFK` or `HITL` inside the parenthesis right after the type word.
  - When several sources carry one, the first in source order wins: `Type:`, then `Label:`, then `Labels:`.
  - `(AFK …; HITL …)` reads as its leading word, `AFK`.
  - `HITL` on a research or task ticket makes it HITL.
  - `AFK` on a research or task ticket agrees with its type.
  - `AFK` on a prototype or grilling ticket leaves it HITL and raises a loud `mode-conflicts-type`, whose detail is the value.

**Blockers** (#137, #145)

- **None markers.** A `Blocked by:` value that is empty, or starts with `—`, `–`, `-`, `none`, `nothing`, `(none` or `(nothing` (in any case), names no blockers and raises nothing.
- **Items.** The value is split outside brackets and parentheses:
  - `,` always splits;
  - `;` splits only when the text after it starts with a reference; otherwise the `;` and the rest of the item are annotation.
- **One blocker per item at most**, taken from the item's start:
  1. a Markdown link to a ticket file, whose target's `NN-` gives the number (the link title is never read);
  2. a bare `NN-<slug>.md`;
  3. a leading `NN` or `#NN`.

  Whatever follows the reference is never read.
- **Items with no reference.** A lone slug-shaped item keeps raising a loud `blockers-as-slugs`. Any other such item raises a loud `blocker-unread`, whose detail is the item.
- **Drift.** The template's `NN, NN` and the none markers raise nothing. Any other value that was read raises a quiet `blockers-not-template`, whose detail is the raw value.
- **Targets.** A target resolves against the ticket's directory, and every blocker is an issue file of the same effort.
  - A link or path to a file outside the effort, or a number with no issue file, raises a quiet `blocker-outside-map` and doesn't gate, as today.
  - A blocker gates by its own state, whether it is a ticket of the map or an unmapped issue.
  - A blocker that isn't a ticket of the ticket's map still raises a quiet `blocker-outside-map`, as today.
- **`Blocks:`** follows the same grammar and the same none markers.
  - When A's `Blocks:` line names B, A becomes one of B's blockers, merged without duplicates with B's own `Blocked by:` items. So a one-sided edge gates.
  - A `Blocks:` line raises a quiet `blocks-line` on A, whose detail is the raw value.
  - An item that names no issue file of the effort is dropped, with nothing more raised.
- **Order.** A ticket's blockers are its own `Blocked by:` items in order, then the tickets whose `Blocks:` names it, in number order.
- **The neighbourhood.** "Clears the way for" is still derived by inverting the merged blockers.

**Membership** (#137, #139)

- An issue file is a ticket of its effort's map when the effort has a map file and the file has no `Parent:` line naming a file other than that map. Every other issue file is an unmapped issue.
- `Map:` and `Parent:` are read only as a link target or a bare path, resolved against the file's directory. Link titles are never read.
  - **The effort's own map file** (compared in any case): nothing is raised.
  - **Another effort's map file, or a missing file**: a loud `map-line-disagrees`, whose detail is the target. The directory still wins.
  - **An existing non-map file**, such as a PRD: on `Parent:`, the issue is an unmapped issue and nothing is raised. On `Map:`, the reader raises `map-line-disagrees` and the directory still wins.
- **What counts as a map's ticket.** A map's tickets, frontier, decided-of-total and finished state count only its own tickets.

**Unmapped issues** (#139)

- An unmapped issue reads its state, claim, role, Status line, type, blockers and resolution by every rule above.
- It never raises `no-map`, `type-missing` or `no-question-heading`. An issue with no map, no type and no `## Question` is a normal local form, not drift. #139 named the first two; `no-question-heading` follows from the same reasoning.
- It is never on a frontier and never "next", whatever its role.
- `no-map` stays in the drift table. It no longer fires on a local tracker.

**Resolution** (#138)

- **Only a closed ticket has a resolution.** It has exactly one, read in this order:
  1. `## Answer`.
  2. Otherwise, the last Resolution label, outside code fences. A label is either:
     - a heading, at any level, whose first word is `Resolution`;
     - a bold label leading a paragraph, whose first word is `Resolution`.

     The first word may also be the second-language form of `Resolution` the pattern fixture holds, accented or not, and is matched in any case. The word list is code in the reader.
  3. Otherwise, the last entry under the last `## Comments`: the last dated item, the last `###` subsection, or the trailing text.
- **Not labels.** A bold `**Resolved**` or `**Done**`, and `## Decision`, are never Resolution labels.
- **Extent.** The label line itself is never part of the body.
  - A heading runs to the next heading of the same or a higher level.
  - A bold label's body starts with any text after the label on its own line, and runs to the next heading.
  - A dated item is the item, its own line included, plus its continuation lines.
  - Trailing text runs to the end of the `## Comments` section.
- **Byline.**
  - `at` is the first ISO date in the label line or the dated item.
  - `author` is the `(<person>)` right after a dated item's date.
  - Otherwise both are null. Nothing is taken from prose.
- **Drift.**
  - `## Answer` raises nothing.
  - A Resolution label raises a quiet `resolution-outside-answer`. Its detail names the form: `Resolution heading`, `Resolution heading under ## Comments` or `bold Resolution label`.
  - The last-comment fallback raises a quiet `resolution-from-last-comment`. Its detail is `dated comment` or `comment text`.
  - No resolution on a closed ticket keeps raising a loud `closed-no-resolution`.

**The reader's interface** (one module, two functions over the `FileSystem` service)

- `readLocalEfforts(repoRoot)` reads every effort in directory order and hides nothing. Each effort gives:
  - its directory name;
  - its map with all its tickets, closed ones included, or null;
  - the map's own state (`open`, `closed`, or null with no map);
  - its unmapped issues, closed ones included, in number order.

  The table tests read through it, because the snapshot hides the closed maps and closed unmapped issues whose readings they check.
- `readLocalTracker(repoRoot)` builds the snapshot from it:
  - the open maps;
  - one Unmapped group per effort that has an open unmapped issue;
  - closed maps with their tickets, and closed unmapped issues, left out.

  The Cockpit keeps calling it as today.
- Both functions read and never write.
- The scout never imports the fixture tools. The truth builder stays an independent reading of the same rules, so that the table tests compare two readings rather than one.

### Derived functions

- `modeOf` takes the HITL note as well as the type:
  - no type gives no mode;
  - prototype and grilling are HITL;
  - a `HITL` note makes any ticket HITL;
  - research is AFK;
  - a task ticket is AFK with an `AFK` note, and `task` otherwise.
- The frontier, `next`, placement, urgency and decided-of-total don't change. The triage role is never read by any of them.
- The [#155](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/155) AFK rule has to read `role` and `modeNote` on a local tracker. A local ticket whose role is `ready-for-human`, or whose note is `HITL`, is not an AFK ticket; one whose role is `ready-for-agent` is.
  - Whichever of the two specs lands second wires this.
  - On the mirror, 15 of the 21 open tickets on open maps carry a `HITL` note.

### The drift table

New codes. Each message ends with `: <detail>` when the scout recorded one, as every code's does today. No new code carries the "newer mattpocock-skills" sentence: these forms come from a user's tracker, not from upstream.

| code | level | message | hint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `header-key-bold` | quiet | A header line has a bold key. | A header line is a plain "Key: value" line before the first ## heading. |
| `type-as-label` | quiet | The ticket gives its type as a label. | A local ticket names its type on a "Type: <type>" line. |
| `mode-conflicts-type` | loud | The ticket is marked AFK, but its type is HITL. | Prototype and grilling tickets are HITL; only a research or task ticket runs AFK. |
| `blockers-not-template` | quiet | The ticket's Blocked by line is not in the template's form. | A local ticket lists its blockers as "Blocked by: NN, NN". |
| `blocks-line` | quiet | The ticket names the tickets it blocks. | Blockers go on the waiting ticket's "Blocked by:" line; the Cockpit reads both sides. |
| `blocker-unread` | loud | A Blocked by item names no ticket. | Each item of a Blocked by line starts with a ticket number, a ticket file name or a link to one. |
| `map-line-disagrees` | loud | The ticket's Map or Parent line points away from its effort's map. | A local ticket belongs to the map in its effort directory; the directory decides. |
| `resolution-outside-answer` | quiet | The resolution is not under ## Answer. | A local ticket's resolution goes under an ## Answer heading. |
| `resolution-from-last-comment` | quiet | The ticket has no Answer or Resolution section; its last comment stands in. | A local ticket's resolution goes under an ## Answer heading. |
| `map-file-ambiguous` | loud | The effort has more than one map file. | An effort keeps one map file, map.md. |
| `map-status-unknown` | quiet | The map's Status line starts with a word this version does not read; the map reads as open. | Only a Status line that starts with DONE or destination reached closes a local map. |

Changed words:

- **`unknown-status`** (stays loud).
  - Message: "The ticket's Status line starts with a word this version does not read; the ticket reads as open."
  - Hint: "A Status line starts with open, claimed, closed, done, resolved or wontfix, or a triage role: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent or ready-for-human."
- **`closed-no-resolution`** (stays loud). Hint: "A closed ticket ends with its resolution: a comment on GitHub; locally an ## Answer section or a Resolution heading."
- **`type-missing`.** Hint: "A ticket carries one wayfinder:<type> label (a Type: line on a local tracker): research, prototype, grilling or task."
- **`type-several`.** Hint: "A ticket carries exactly one type: one wayfinder:<type> label, or one Type: line locally."

### The Cockpit

**Tree**

- **The Unmapped fold.**
  - It stays one fold above Finished, collapsed until opened. Its count is the number of open unmapped issues.
  - Inside it, each group is a plain row labelled with the group's title and its count; it doesn't fold and can't be selected. The group's issues follow it, one level deeper.
  - A group with no effort (GitHub strays) puts its issues straight under the fold, as today.
- **Keys.**
  - An unmapped issue in an effort: `unmapped:<effort>:ticket:<n>`.
  - One with no effort keeps today's `unmapped:ticket:<n>`.
  - Selection, reveal, open, the Detail and drift dismissal all use the new keys. Revealing an unmapped issue opens the Unmapped fold.
- **Role chips.**
  - A ticket row shows its role as a chip after its mode chip, in the same outlined, muted style.
  - An unmapped row shows its role chip too.
  - Rows show no Status line.

**Focus pane** (a ticket, mapped or not)

- A `Role` fact after `Claim`, when the ticket has a role.
- A `Status line` fact, when the value has more than its first word.
  - It is rendered as inline Markdown with the Detail's renderer: the same bundle, `html: false`, links sent to the host, as in [ADR 0007](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0007-markdown-it-renders-tracker-bodies-in-the-detail.md).
  - It is clamped to one line with an ellipsis, with the value as written on hover.
- A claim that names nobody shows as "claimed", not as an empty value.

**Detail** (a ticket)

- `Role` and `Status line` facts, the Status line in full and inline-rendered.
- An unmapped issue's Detail keeps today's shape: no Actions, and no selectable neighbours.

**Claims and the session side.** On a local tracker, the Cockpit still asks for no login, so `me` stays null. A named local claim therefore never raises "claimed by someone else". Core's comment that a local tracker "names nobody" is updated to say so.

### Refresh cost (the scout budget of [#27](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/27))

Point 11 of #27 stands unchanged:

- a watcher on `.scratch/**`, debounced 1 s;
- a full re-read on every change;
- no gap, no budget and no per-file cache.

The scope stays `.scratch/**` rather than `**/*.md`. Deleting an effort directory may report only the directory, and that must still refresh.

Measured on 2026-10-09 with today's reader, over the mirror's 342 files (985 KB):

| read | median | range |
|---|---|---|
| from disk | 50 ms | 31 to 97 ms |
| in memory | 9 ms | 44 ms cold |
| parsing every file alone | 6 ms | |

Reading the 35 map files as well adds little to this.

### Fixtures

**Pattern fixture** (`local-forms`)

- Every ticket and map entry in its truth gains a `drift` list: the codes the scout raises on that file, sorted, empty when none. The README documents it.
- One file is added: a type line whose parenthesis holds both modes, `(AFK …; HITL …)`. Its truth has `mode: 'AFK'`, as #137's leading-word rule reads it. It is the one catalogued form #133 left without a fixture.
- The PRD-parented file beside a map that #139 asked for already exists (`prd-in-map`), so nothing is added for it.
- Forms no real tracker holds are built in memory inside the tests, never committed as files:
  - two map casings side by side. A committed pair can't be checked out on a case-insensitive disk, so it can't be a file on `main`.
  - an effort that holds only a PRD;
  - a closed map with an open PRD-parented issue;
  - a bold key on a map;
  - a ticket with two Status header lines;
  - a `Blocks:` item naming no file;
  - a `Map:` line naming another effort's map;
  - a blocker link that leaves the effort.

**Scratch mirror** (`scratch-mirror`)

- The truth builder reads a map's decisions as the link that leads each Decisions-so-far entry, as the scout does. Today it reads every `issues/NN` link on the line, so a link inside a gist reorders two closed maps.
  - `MapReading.decisions` is documented as "the ticket each entry of Decisions so far leads with, in order".
  - The truth is regenerated, or those two entries are corrected by hand to agree with the fixed builder. Only those two change.
  - The change follows the README's rebuild and leak-check steps.
- No other truth change is planned. Where the scout and the truth disagree, the deciding ticket (#134 to #139, #145) says which one is wrong. A truth change cites that ticket in its PR.

**Local-tracker fixture.** Its README follows the rulings. The `onboarding-spec` issues become unmapped issues in an `onboarding-spec` group, with no `no-map`, and a closed one is hidden.

### The upstream register and the canary

**`docs/upstream.md`**

- **What the scout reads.** The "Local tracker layout" row gains two lines that are in the local template: triage role strings on the `Status:` line, and comments under a `## Comments` heading. Both were read from the installed 1.2.3; the canary's new needles cover the newest release.
- **A new table under mattpocock-skills: "Local forms from the wild, never upstream".** Columns: form, seen on (counts from #131), read as, drift, decided in. There is one row per form:
  - `MAP.md` and other casings;
  - the map Status line;
  - the Status vocabulary beyond `claimed` and `resolved`;
  - `open — <role|claimed>`;
  - `Assignee:` claims;
  - types on `Label:` and `Labels:`, and HITL notes;
  - non-template `Blocked by:` forms, and `;` before a reference;
  - `Blocks:`;
  - `Map:` and `Parent:` lines;
  - bold keys;
  - Resolution headings and labels;
  - the last-comment fallback;
  - mapless efforts and PRD-parented issues.

  These rows are not contracts: no upstream release can break them. The table says so.
- **The mirror.** A note says it runs in `vp test`: in CI on every pull request, and in the canary's `node` job, which already runs the whole suite on the newest Node.

**The canary**

- It gets no dedicated step for the mirror. The mirror and the scout both live in this repo, and neither changes with an upstream release.
- Its `skills` job checks each copy's `issue-tracker-local.md` for the needles below. A missing needle files an upstream break against the skills, like the GitHub template's needles today.
  - `# Issue tracker: Local Markdown`
  - `## Wayfinding operations`
  - `.scratch/<effort>/map.md`
  - `issues/NN-<slug>.md`
  - `Type:`
  - `Status:`, with `claimed` and `resolved`
  - `Blocked by:`
  - `## Answer`
  - `## Comments`
- The register's "Watched by the canary" list gains this line.

### Docs and release

- The extension README gets a short "Local trackers" section. It says what the Cockpit reads (the forms above), what it hides (closed maps and closed unmapped issues), and that drift is reported and never corrected.
- The glossary gains **Effort**: "One unit of work a map charts. On a local tracker, a directory under `.scratch` holding its map file, if any, and its issue files, beside specs and notes." _Avoid_: feature, folder. The glossary already uses the word in **Map** and **Unmapped issue** without defining it.
- A changeset (minor) for the extension: local trackers are read in every form a real tracker holds.

## Testing Decisions

A good test drives a module through its public interface and asserts what a user or caller sees: a snapshot's facts, a row, a pane, a warning's words. It never asserts internal calls or intermediate structures. The harness is first-class: every rule gets full coverage, and none is trimmed for CI cost.

There is one seam for the scout, and it is the highest one: **the local tracker reader over the in-memory `FileSystem`**. The rest are existing seams, each the highest its layer has. The only new surface is `readLocalEfforts`, beside `readLocalTracker` in the same module.

1. **The pattern table test.** For every file of the pattern fixture, `readLocalEfforts` finds it and checks it against its truth entry.
   - A ticket is found among its effort's map tickets or its unmapped issues. That answers membership: a ticket exactly when the truth has a `map` and no `parent`.
   - A map is found as its effort's map.
   - A note is found as neither.

   It compares:
   - **state**: closed; or open, and claimed when it has a claim;
   - **role**;
   - **assignee**, on tickets that aren't closed: the first name of the claim;
   - **type** and **modeNote** (the truth's `mode`);
   - **blockers**:
     - each ticket's own `Blocked by:` numbers are among its merged blockers;
     - each `Blocks:` target lists the ticket among its blockers;
     - the merged list equals the truth's own edges plus the inverted ones;
   - **resolution**:
     - its placement, from the drift detail that names its form (none means `answer`);
     - its first non-empty body line, trimmed, against `firstLine`;
     - `at` and `author`;
   - **a map's state and decisions**;
   - **drift**: the sorted codes on the ticket or map, against the entry's `drift`.

   Prior art: the fixture's own completeness test, and `local.test.ts`.
2. **The mirror test.** The same comparison over all 342 files, without drift, which the mirror's truth doesn't hold. Then `readLocalTracker` on the mirror, checked against what the truth implies:
   - **Maps.** 20 open maps in directory order, with the 15 closed ones absent.
   - **Map tickets.** 148 tickets on them: 127 closed, 18 open and 3 claimed.
   - **Urgency with no sessions.** 14 takeable, 3 stuck and 3 finished: effort-29, effort-38 and effort-41.
   - **Frontier.** Each map's frontier equals the one derived from the truth, 16 tickets in all.
   - **Unmapped groups.** 17 open unmapped issues in 7 groups. Effort-29 is labelled with its map's title and holds 9; six mapless efforts hold the other 8.
   - **Hidden.** The 22 closed unmapped issues and the 70 tickets of closed maps are absent.
   - **Drift census.** The count of each drift code on the snapshot is asserted exactly. The counts are settled when the reader lands, each one checked against the rules by hand. A later change that moves a count updates it in the same PR. These counts follow from the truth already: `unknown-status` 1, and `no-map`, `type-missing`, `mode-conflicts-type` and `map-file-ambiguous` 0.
   - **Time.** A guard: the in-memory read of the mirror takes under 2 s. Today it is 44 ms cold.

   The existing loading and completeness checks stay. Prior art: the existing mirror test.
3. **Hand-written cases on the same seam**, for what no fixture holds: the in-memory forms listed under Fixtures. The existing local-tracker fixture tests are updated to the rulings. Prior art: the edge cases in `local.test.ts`.
4. **The snapshot model.** A snapshot with the new ticket fields and unmapped groups round-trips through its JSON form, and the schema version is 2. Prior art: `model.test.ts`.
5. **GitHub unchanged.** The existing collect and read tests pass. GitHub tickets carry null `role`, `statusLine` and `modeNote`, and `unmapped` is empty. Prior art: `collect.test.ts` and `read.test.ts`.
6. **Derived functions.** `modeOf` over every type and note. The frontier ignores a role: a `ready-for-human` ticket can be next. Prior art: `derive.test.ts`.
7. **The drift table.** Each new code's level, message with and without a detail, and hint. The four changed hints and the new `unknown-status` message. Prior art: `drift-table.test.ts`.
8. **The host's view model**, over `readLocalTracker` of the fixtures, as the existing tests build their snapshots.
   - **The mirror's Tree.** 17 open maps in urgency order, Unmapped with its 7 groups, and Finished with 3 maps.
   - **Unmapped rows.** Their effort keys select, reveal, open the Detail and dismiss only their own issue.
   - **Roles and Status lines.** The role shows on rows, the Focus pane and the Detail. The Status line shows in the Focus pane and the Detail.
   - **Claims.** A claim with nobody named shows as "claimed", and a named local claim raises no disagreement.

   Prior art: `view-model.test.ts`, `drift-view-model.test.ts` and `disagreements.test.ts`.
9. **The webview.** Prior art: `Tree.test.ts`, `FocusPane.test.ts` and `Detail.test.ts`.
   - Group rows and their counts.
   - The role chip.
   - The Focus pane's clamped Status line, with its hover text and inline rendering.
   - The Detail's Role and Status line facts.
10. **The canary.** A local template copy missing each needle files a break; the full template passes. Prior art: `checks.test.ts`.
11. **The truth builder.** A Decisions-so-far entry whose gist links another ticket gives only its leading ticket. Prior art: `truth.test.ts`.

## Out of Scope

- **The GitHub tracker.** Its state comes from the API. Showing a triage role on GitHub tickets is a later change; `role` stays null there.
- **Changing the tracker.** Rewriting it into the current conventions, or any write to `.scratch`: drift is reported, never corrected.
- **A model reading a free-form line** ([ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md)).
- **Rendering.** How the Detail renders bodies ([ADR 0007](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0007-markdown-it-renders-tracker-bodies-in-the-detail.md)), and how the `next` CLI presents any of this.
- **Other files.** The content of PRDs, specs, handoffs, research notes and asset notes: the scout only needs to know they aren't tickets.
- **Renamed triage labels on a local tracker.** The vocabulary is the five default names.
- **A local map's Status narrative.** It decides open or closed, and is never shown.
- **Ticket numbers across efforts.** Local ticket numbers repeat across efforts. A session's name (`#<number> <title>`), its status events and the registry's grouping are all keyed by number, so a session can attach to another effort's ticket with the same number. This is a session concern for its own map.
- **Map keys.** On a local tracker, map keys are directory positions and shift when an effort directory is added before others. This existing behaviour is unchanged.
- **Caching.** Per-file caching or incremental re-reads of `.scratch`.
- **Fixtures from other real trackers**: a fresh effort.

## Further Notes

- **Dismissals.** Drift dismissed under an old `unmapped:ticket:<n>` key on a local tracker shows again once, under its new key.
- **The cache.** The version-1 cache is dropped on first activation. The Tree shows "loading" until the first collect, as on a fresh install.
- **The corpus.** The real tracker never leaves Eduardo's machine. Any change to the mirror or its truth follows the mirror README's rebuild and leak-check steps. Issues, PRs and commits carry shapes and counts only, and describe the source as "a private five-month production tracker".
- **Why the scout gets a second reading.** The mirror's states come from a careful reader and #134. Its other fields come from the truth builder's code reading of the same rules. A disagreement between the scout and the truth is the benchmark doing its job: one of the two misread a rule, and the rulings say which.
- **Splitting the work.** `/to-tickets` can split this spec along its sections: the reader and its fixtures first, then the drift words, the Cockpit's presentation, and the register and canary.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

#155 is in review as #179, so this ticket lands second and wires the AFK rule, as agreed in the #155 comment.

In #179, `isAfkTicket(ticket, triage)` (`packages/core/src/claude/bypass.ts`) reads `ticket.type` and `ticket.labels`. On a local tracker, `labels` comes only from a `Labels:` line (`readTicketBody`). Once `role` and `modeNote` exist, the rule should also treat a `ready-for-human` role or a `HITL` note as not AFK, and a `ready-for-agent` role as AFK. The table test in `bypass.test.ts` and the controller test "reads the repo's triage labels and a local ticket's Labels line" in `cockpit.test.ts` are the places to extend.

164.title: Create and install the dbarjs-agent App
164.body:
## Question

Create the private GitHub App `dbarjs-agent` under `dbarjs` and install it on hero-synergy only, as decided in [Pick the agent's GitHub identity](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/161). Only Eduardo can do this (HITL checklist):

- [ ] New GitHub App at https://github.com/settings/apps/new. Name: `dbarjs-agent`. Set "Only on this account". Turn webhook off.
- [ ] Repository permissions:
  - Contents: Read and write
  - Pull requests: Read and write
  - Issues: Read and write
  - Workflows: Read and write
  - Metadata: Read
  - Leave everything else at No access, especially Administration, Actions and Secrets.
- [ ] Install it on **Only select repositories**, choosing `dbarjs/hero-synergy`.
- [ ] Generate a private key (`.pem`).

169.title: Find every map file and close a local map by its own Status line
169.body:
## Parent

#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds. Spec sections: "The local tracker reader" (Efforts and files, Header lines, A map's own state, The reader's interface), "The drift table" (`header-key-bold`, `map-file-ambiguous`, `map-status-unknown`), "Fixtures" (the scratch mirror's truth builder), Testing Decisions 1, 2, 3, 7 and 11. User stories 1–10, 25, 62, 63 and 77. Decided in #136 (a map's own state) and #137 (header lines), measured in #131.

## What to build

A Cockpit user on a local tracker sees their maps on any disk, and stops seeing the ones they finished.

- **The map file.** The reader lists each effort directory and takes a file named `map.md` in any casing as its map. It never opens a fixed name, so `MAP.md` reads the same on a case-sensitive disk.
  - With several casings side by side, it reads `map.md` if it is there, else the first name in byte order.
  - It then raises a loud `map-file-ambiguous` on the map, naming the files found and the one read.
- **Header lines.** One reading of `Key: value` lines, shared by maps and tickets, that the later reader tickets build on:
  - before the first H2, outside code fences, never a list item;
  - keys in any case, the first line of each key winning;
  - a bold key (`**Key:** value`, `**Key**: value`) read like a plain one, with one quiet `header-key-bold` per file listing the bold keys in order.
- **A map's own state.** Only the map's Status header line decides.
  - `**` is stripped, and a value starting with `DONE` or `destination reached` (any case) closes the map. Anything else, or no Status line, is open. The rest of the line is never parsed.
  - `in progress`, `charted`, `REOPENED` and `route walked` raise nothing. Any other first word raises a quiet `map-status-unknown` whose detail is that word as written.
  - `Label: wayfinder:map`, `Charted:`, `Recharted:`, `Redrawn:`, headings, prose and a state word at the start of a gist change nothing.
- **Hidden.** A closed map is left out of the snapshot with all its tickets. It keeps its number, the position of its effort directory, so no other map renumbers. An open map whose tickets are all closed is still finished.
- **Other Markdown.** PRDs, `spec.md`, research write-ups, asset notes, handoffs and checklists are never read as a ticket or a map. An effort with neither a map file nor issue files is skipped without a warning.
- **The seam.** `readLocalEfforts(repoRoot)` beside `readLocalTracker`. It reads every effort in directory order and hides nothing:
  - its directory name;
  - its map with all its tickets, or null;
  - the map's own state (`open`, `closed`, or null with no map);
  - its unmapped issues.

  `readLocalTracker` builds the snapshot from it. Both only read.
- **The tests every later reader ticket grows.**
  - The pattern table test (spec test 1) over every file of `local-forms`, with the columns this ticket reads: a map is found as its effort's map, a note as neither, and a map's state and decisions. Each later reader ticket turns on its own columns, and drift comes last.
  - The scratch mirror's per-file comparison (spec test 2), with the same columns over all 342 files.
  - The truth builder reads each Decisions-so-far entry's leading link only, and `MapReading.decisions` is documented that way. Only the two mirror entries this moves change, rebuilt by the mirror README's steps and leak check.
- The drift table gains the three codes, with the spec's words.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On an in-memory case-sensitive disk, `MAP.md`, `Map.md` and `map.md` are each found as the effort's map, with no drift.
- [ ] Two casings side by side, built in memory (a case-insensitive disk can't check out a committed pair), read `map.md` and raise a loud `map-file-ambiguous` naming both.
- [ ] Every map Status form in `local-forms` reads as its truth says. `07 DONE <date>` and `<prose> **DONE <date>**` stay open; `## Destination reached` and `Frontier: empty` change nothing.
- [ ] A bold key on a map, built in memory, raises one `header-key-bold`. A Status line after the first H2, in a fence or in inline code is never read.
- [ ] An effort holding only a PRD, built in memory, raises nothing and adds no map.
- [ ] The pattern table test and the mirror's per-file comparison pass with this ticket's columns. On the mirror, `readLocalTracker` gives 20 open maps in directory order and the 15 closed ones are absent.
- [ ] The truth builder test: a Decisions-so-far entry whose gist links another ticket gives only its leading ticket.
- [ ] Drift table tests for the three new codes: level, message with and without a detail, hint.
- [ ] GitHub's reading is unchanged.
- [ ] Issues, PRs and commits carry shapes and counts only, and call the source "a private five-month production tracker".
- [ ] A changeset naming `hero-synergy` (minor), written for the person updating.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
