171.title: Read a local ticket's state, claim and triage role
171.body:
## Parent

#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds. Spec sections: "A ticket's state, claim, role and Status line", "Claims and the session side", "Derived functions" (the frontier never reads a role), the Focus pane's claim that names nobody, "The drift table" (`unknown-status`'s new words), Testing Decisions 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8 (claims). User stories 11–24, 26–28 and 71 (its `unknown-status` half). Decided in #135, with the truth from #134.

## What to build

A Cockpit user's closed local tickets read as closed, claimed tickets leave the frontier, and every ticket's triage role is known.

- **The first word** of the Status value (its letters and hyphens, any case, `**` stripped) sets the state, by the spec's table:
  - `closed`, `done` and `resolved` close the ticket; `wontfix` closes it with role `wontfix`;
  - `open`, `claimed` and the four open roles (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`) leave it open;
  - no Status line is open;
  - anything else is open with a loud `unknown-status` whose detail is the value. One line holding a DONE half and an OPEN half is such a line.
- **After `open`**, and only there, one more word is read: the first word after a dash (`—`, `–`, ` - `) or an opening parenthesis. A role there sets the role, `claimed` claims, and nothing else is read.
- **A second Status header line** is ignored and raises `unknown-status`.
- **The role** comes from the Status line first, else from a `Labels:` item that is exactly one of the five default role names.
- **Claims.** An open ticket is claimed by a `claimed` first word, by `claimed` after `open`, or by an `Assignee:` line that names someone.
  - The name is the value with `**` stripped, cut before the first parenthesis or dash, and trimmed.
  - `—`, `–`, `-`, an empty value, `(unclaimed)` and `— (unclaimed)` name nobody.
  - A claim with no name has `by: []` and shows as "claimed" in the Focus pane.
  - A closed ticket is never claimed, whatever its Assignee line or a leftover `claimed <date>`.
- **`statusLine`** holds the Status value as written, trimmed, for display only.
- **The session side.** `me` stays null on a local tracker, so a named local claim never raises "claimed by someone else". Core's comment that a local tracker "names nobody" says so.
- **The frontier** never reads the role: a `ready-for-human` ticket can be next.
- `unknown-status` gets the spec's new message and a hint listing the Status vocabulary.
- The pattern table test and the mirror's per-file comparison turn on the state, claim, assignee and role columns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The pattern table test's state, role and assignee columns agree with `local-forms` truth on every file, and the mirror's per-file comparison agrees on all 342 files. Where the scout and a truth disagree, #134 or #135 says which is wrong; a truth change cites it, and a mirror change follows the mirror README's rebuild steps and leak check.
- [ ] `closed <date> (reopened and re-closed …)` stays closed. `open — needs-triage (blocked)` sets the role. `open — claimed <date>` and `open (claimed …)` claim.
- [ ] A ticket with two Status header lines, built in memory, reads its first and raises `unknown-status`.
- [ ] A closed ticket with an `Assignee:` name or a leftover `claimed <date>` is not claimed.
- [ ] Derive test: the frontier ignores the role, and a `ready-for-human` ticket can be next.
- [ ] View-model tests: a claim with nobody named shows as "claimed", and a named local claim raises no disagreement.
- [ ] Drift table test for `unknown-status`'s new message and hint.
- [ ] GitHub's reading is unchanged.
- [ ] A changeset naming `hero-synergy` (minor), written for the person updating.

## Blocked by

- #168 Move the snapshot to schema 2: the new ticket fields and unmapped groups
- #169 Find every map file and close a local map by its own Status line

172.title: Read a local ticket's type and HITL note
172.body:
## Parent

#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds. Spec sections: "Type and HITL note", "Derived functions" (`modeOf`), "The drift table" (`type-as-label`, `mode-conflicts-type`, and the new hints of `type-missing` and `type-several`), "Fixtures" (the pattern fixture's one new file), Testing Decisions 1, 2, 6 and 7. A Cockpit user's local tickets are typed, and a ticket marked HITL never reads as AFK.

- **Sources.** The type comes from `Type:`, `Label:` and `Labels:` header lines. A `Labels:` line splits on commas, and every `wayfinder:<type>` item in it counts.
- **Value.** An optional `wayfinder:` prefix, then the first word, which must be one of the four types. The parenthesis after it is never searched for types or numbers.
- **The H1** (`# Task: …`) is never a type, and the title stays verbatim.
- **Conflict.** Sources naming different types raise a loud `type-several` listing them, and give no type.
- **Drift.**
  - A plain `Type: <type>` raises nothing.
  - A `Label:` or `Labels:` source, or a `wayfinder:` prefix, raises a quiet `type-as-label` whose detail is the value.
  - An unknown `wayfinder:` word raises `unknown-wayfinder-labels` on the ticket.
  - A ticket of a map with no type keeps its loud `type-missing`.
- **The HITL note** (`modeNote`) is a leading `AFK` or `HITL` inside the parenthesis right after the type word.
  - When several sources carry one, the first in source order wins: `Type:`, then `Label:`, then `Labels:`.
  - `(AFK …; HITL …)` reads as its leading word, `AFK`.
- **`modeOf`** takes the note as well as the type:

  - prototype and grilling are HITL;
  - a `HITL` note makes any ticket HITL;
  - research is AFK;

173.title: Read every Blocked by and Blocks form a local tracker holds
173.body:
## Parent

#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds. Spec sections: "Blockers", "The drift table" (`blockers-not-template`, `blocks-line`, `blocker-unread`), Testing Decisions 1, 2, 3 and 7. User stories 42–50. Decided in #137 and #145.

## What to build

A Cockpit user's frontier is right in both directions: every blocker form the tracker uses gates, and nothing in a note does.

- **None markers.** A `Blocked by:` value that is empty, or starts with `—`, `–`, `-`, `none`, `nothing`, `(none` or `(nothing` (any case), names no blockers and raises nothing.
- **Items.** The value splits outside brackets and parentheses:
  - `,` always splits;
  - `;` splits only when the text after it starts with a reference. Otherwise the `;` and the rest of the item are annotation.
- **One blocker per item at most**, taken from the item's start:
  1. a Markdown link to a ticket file, whose target's `NN-` gives the number (the link title is never read);
  2. a bare `NN-<slug>.md`;
  3. a leading `NN` or `#NN`.

  Whatever follows the reference is never read.
- **Items with no reference.** A lone slug-shaped item keeps its loud `blockers-as-slugs`. Any other such item raises a loud `blocker-unread` whose detail is the item.
- **Drift.** The template's `NN, NN` and the none markers raise nothing. Any other value that was read raises a quiet `blockers-not-template` whose detail is the raw value.
- **Targets** resolve against the ticket's directory, within its effort.
  - A link or path to a file outside the effort, or a number with no issue file, raises a quiet `blocker-outside-map` and doesn't gate.
  - A blocker gates by its own state.
  - A blocker that isn't a ticket of the ticket's map still raises a quiet `blocker-outside-map`.
- **`Blocks:`** follows the same grammar and none markers.
  - When A's `Blocks:` names B, A becomes one of B's blockers, merged without duplicates. A one-sided edge gates.
  - It raises a quiet `blocks-line` on A whose detail is the raw value.
  - An item naming no issue file of the effort is dropped, with nothing more raised.
- **Order.** A ticket's own `Blocked by:` items in order, then the tickets whose `Blocks:` names it, in number order. The Detail's "clears the way for" is still inverted from the merged blockers, so it lists what a `Blocks:` line names.
- The pattern table test and the mirror's per-file comparison turn on the blockers column.

The mirror's per-file comparison agrees on all 342 files. A truth change cites #137 or #145, and a mirror change follows the mirror README's rebuild steps and leak check.

- [ ] A `Blocks:` item naming no file and a blocker link that leaves the effort, both built in memory, behave as above.

174.title: Show unmapped issues in the Unmapped fold, grouped by effort
174.body:
## Parent

#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds. Spec sections: "Membership", "Unmapped issues", "The Cockpit" (the Tree's Unmapped fold and keys, the unmapped Detail), "The drift table" (`map-line-disagrees`), "Fixtures" (the local-tracker fixture), Further Notes "Dismissals", Testing Decisions 1, 2, 3, 8 and 9. User stories 51–61. Decided in #139 and #137.

## What to build

A Cockpit user sees triage issues and `/to-tickets` issues for what they are: open work outside every map, grouped by effort, never posing as tickets.

- **Membership.** An issue file is a ticket of its effort's map when the effort has a map file and the file has no `Parent:` line naming a file other than that map. Every other issue file is an unmapped issue.
- **`Map:` and `Parent:`** are read only as a link target or a bare path, resolved against the file's directory. Link titles are never read.
  - The effort's own map file (any case) raises nothing.
  - Another effort's map file, or a missing file, raises a loud `map-line-disagrees` whose detail is the target. The directory still wins.
  - An existing non-map file, such as a PRD: on `Parent:` the issue is an unmapped issue and nothing is raised; on `Map:` it raises `map-line-disagrees` and the directory wins.
- **A map's tickets, frontier, decided-of-total and finished state** count its own tickets only.
- **Unmapped issues** read every other rule: state, claim, role, blockers, resolution.
  - They never raise `no-map`, `type-missing` or `no-question-heading`. `no-map` stays in the drift table and no longer fires on a local tracker.
  - They are never on a frontier and never "next", whatever their role.
- **The snapshot.** One Unmapped group per effort that has an open unmapped issue, in directory order, its issues in number order.
  - A group is titled with its effort's map title, open or closed, else with the directory name.
  - Closed unmapped issues are left out.
  - An open `/to-tickets` issue in an effort whose map is closed stays, under that map's title.
- **The Tree.**
  - The Unmapped fold stays one fold above Finished, collapsed until opened, counting open unmapped issues.
  - Each group is a plain row with its title and count. It doesn't fold and can't be selected; its issues follow it one level deeper.
  - A group with no effort (GitHub strays) puts its issues straight under the fold, as today.
- **Keys.** An unmapped issue in an effort is `unmapped:<effort>:ticket:<n>`; one with no effort keeps `unmapped:ticket:<n>`. Selection, reveal, open, the Detail and drift dismissal all use them, and revealing an unmapped issue opens the fold. An unmapped issue's Detail keeps today's shape: no Actions, no selectable neighbours. Drift dismissed under an old key shows once more under its new one.
- **The local-tracker fixture's** README follows the rulings: the `onboarding-spec` issues are unmapped issues in an `onboarding-spec` group with no `no-map`, and a closed one is hidden.
- The pattern table test and the mirror's per-file comparison turn on membership: a file is a ticket exactly when its truth has a `map` and no `parent`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The pattern table test's membership column agrees with `local-forms` truth on every file (`prd-in-map` included), and the mirror's per-file comparison on all 342 files. A truth change cites #137 or #139, and a mirror change follows the mirror README's rebuild steps and leak check.
- [ ] On the mirror, `readLocalTracker` gives 17 open unmapped issues in 7 groups: effort-29, labelled with its map's title, holds 9, and six mapless efforts hold the other 8. The 22 closed unmapped issues are absent.
- [ ] Built in memory: a closed map with an open PRD-parented issue keeps the issue, under the map's title; a `Map:` line naming another effort's map raises `map-line-disagrees`, and the directory wins.
- [ ] View-model tests: two efforts' `#1` each select, reveal, open the Detail and dismiss only their own issue.
- [ ] Tree tests: group rows and their counts.
- [ ] Drift table test for `map-line-disagrees`.
- [ ] GitHub's reading is unchanged.
- [ ] A changeset naming `hero-synergy` (minor), written for the person updating.

## Blocked by

- #168 Move the snapshot to schema 2: the new ticket fields and unmapped groups

175.title: Read a closed local ticket's resolution wherever it was written
175.body:
## Parent

#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds. Spec sections: "Resolution", "The drift table" (`resolution-outside-answer`, `resolution-from-last-comment`, `closed-no-resolution`'s new hint), Testing Decisions 1, 2 and 7. User stories 64–69 and 71 (its `closed-no-resolution` half). Decided in #138.

## What to build

A Cockpit user's Detail shows a closed ticket's answer wherever it was written, labelled by how sure the reading is.

- **Only a closed ticket has a resolution**, and exactly one, read in this order:
  1. `## Answer`.
  2. Otherwise, the last Resolution label outside code fences: a heading at any level, or a bold label leading a paragraph, whose first word is `Resolution`. The first word may also be the second-language form the pattern fixture holds, accented or not, in any case. The word list is code in the reader.
  3. Otherwise, the last entry under the last `## Comments`: the last dated item, the last `###` subsection, or the trailing text.
- **Not labels**: a bold `**Resolved**` or `**Done**`, and `## Decision`.
- **Extent.** The label line is never part of the body.
  - A heading runs to the next heading of the same or a higher level.
  - A bold label's body starts with any text after the label on its own line, and runs to the next heading.
  - A dated item is the item, its own line included, plus its continuation lines.
  - Trailing text runs to the end of the `## Comments` section.
- **Byline.** `at` is the first ISO date on the label line or the dated item. `author` is the `(<person>)` right after a dated item's date. Otherwise both are null; nothing is taken from prose.
- **Drift.**
  - `## Answer` raises nothing.
  - A Resolution label raises a quiet `resolution-outside-answer` whose detail names the form: `Resolution heading`, `Resolution heading under ## Comments` or `bold Resolution label`.
  - The last-comment fallback raises a quiet `resolution-from-last-comment` whose detail is `dated comment` or `comment text`.
  - No resolution on a closed ticket keeps the loud `closed-no-resolution`, with the spec's new hint.
- The pattern table test and the mirror's per-file comparison turn on the resolution columns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The pattern table test's resolution columns agree with `local-forms` truth on every file: the placement (from the drift detail that names the form; none means `answer`), the first non-empty body line against `firstLine`, `at` and `author`. The mirror's per-file comparison agrees on all 342 files. A truth change cites #138, and a mirror change follows the mirror README's rebuild steps and leak check.
- [ ] A reopened ticket's second Resolution label wins.
- [ ] An open ticket with dated comments or a Resolution heading shows no resolution.
- [ ] The Detail shows a resolution read from each placement.
- [ ] Drift table tests for the two new codes and `closed-no-resolution`'s new hint.
- [ ] GitHub's reading is unchanged.
- [ ] A changeset naming `hero-synergy` (minor), written for the person updating.

188.title: Apply the final main ruleset
188.body:
## Question

Apply the rulesets decided in [Settle the final main ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/162) and the release immutability decided in [Fit the release flow to the final ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/189). These are settings changes, so only Eduardo applies them (HITL checklist). Run the calls with an admin `gh`. Nothing waits on another ticket: until [Run agent sessions as the App, not Eduardo](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/165) closes, agents still hold the admin token, so they're exempt exactly like Eduardo.

On 2026-11-16, every commit on the open PRs (#181 and #191) was verified, so `required_signatures` blocks neither. Before applying, re-check the PRs open then with `gh api repos/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pulls/<n>/commits --jq '.[].commit.verification.verified'`.

- [ ] **Edit Protect main** (24813840): no bypass, 0 approvals, merge commits only, signed commits.

```sh
gh api --method PUT repos/dbarjs/hero-synergy/rulesets/24813840 --input - <<'EOF'
{
  "name": "Protect main",
  "target": "branch",
  "enforcement": "active",
  "conditions": { "ref_name": { "include": ["~DEFAULT_BRANCH"], "exclude": [] } },
  "bypass_actors": [],
  "rules": [
    { "type": "deletion" },
    { "type": "non_fast_forward" },
    { "type": "required_signatures" },
    {
      "type": "pull_request",
      "parameters": {
        "required_approving_review_count": 0,
        "dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push": false,
        "require_code_owner_review": false,
        "require_last_push_approval": false,
        "required_review_thread_resolution": false,
        "require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes": true,
        "allowed_merge_methods": ["merge"]
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "required_status_checks",
      "parameters": {
        "strict_required_status_checks_policy": false,
        "do_not_enforce_on_create": false,
        "required_status_checks": [
          { "context": "check", "integration_id": 15368 },
          { "context": "vscode (linux)", "integration_id": 15368 },
          { "context": "vscode (macos)", "integration_id": 15368 }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
EOF
```

- [ ] **Create Only Eduardo merges to main**: "Restrict updates" on `main`, with the admin role exempt.

```sh
gh api --method POST repos/dbarjs/hero-synergy/rulesets --input - <<'EOF'
{
  "name": "Only Eduardo merges to main",
  "target": "branch",
  "enforcement": "active",
  "conditions": { "ref_name": { "include": ["~DEFAULT_BRANCH"], "exclude": [] } },
  "bypass_actors": [{ "actor_id": 5, "actor_type": "RepositoryRole", "bypass_mode": "exempt" }],
  "rules": [{ "type": "update", "parameters": { "update_allows_fetch_and_merge": false } }]
}
EOF
```

- [ ] **Create Protect release tags**: `v*` tags can't be deleted or moved, and creating them stays open for `release.yml`.

```sh
gh api --method POST repos/dbarjs/hero-synergy/rulesets --input - <<'EOF'
{
  "name": "Protect release tags",
  "target": "tag",
  "enforcement": "active",
  "conditions": { "ref_name": { "include": ["refs/tags/v*"], "exclude": [] } },
  "bypass_actors": [],
  "rules": [
    { "type": "deletion" },
    { "type": "update", "parameters": { "update_allows_fetch_and_merge": false } }
  ]
}
EOF
```

- [ ] **Turn on release immutability**: Settings → General → Releases → "Enable release immutability", as decided in [Fit the release flow to the final ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/189). It covers only releases published afterwards, so turn it on before merging "Release hero-synergy" (#181). If a personal repo doesn't offer the switch, record that here.

Then approve the latest CI run on "Release hero-synergy" (#181) and merge it when green, so 0.2.0 is the first release under these rules.

## Checks

The decisions rest on four facts no primary source confirms. Check each one:

- [ ] **The admin role.** In Settings → Rules → Only Eduardo merges to main, the bypass list must read **Repository admin**, mode **Exempt**. Only community sources give `actor_id: 5`. If the API rejects `exempt` for a role, add the bypass in the UI with mode "For pull requests only" instead, and record that each merge needs a bypass tick.
- [ ] **Eduardo's merge box.** On the next green agent PR, it offers only "Create a merge commit", with no bypass checkbox. While a required check is pending or red, the button stays blocked.
- [ ] **The App can't merge.** This is the `gh pr merge` failure in the smoke test of [Run agent sessions as the App, not Eduardo](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/165). It needs this ticket closed first. The failure must name the update rule: "The base branch does not allow updates" or similar.
- [ ] **Tag creation and the immutable release still work.** At the 0.2.0 release, the publish job's "Create the GitHub release" step succeeds, the new `v0.2.0` tag appears, and the release is marked immutable with the VSIX attached. If a rule violation stops the tag, switch Protect release tags off, re-run the step, and record the failure here. If immutability stops the upload, record the error here, switch immutability off and re-run the step.

Resolved when the three rulesets are live, release immutability is on and the first two checks pass. The answer records the new ruleset ids and the bypass mode that was actually set. "The App can't merge" lands on [Run agent sessions as the App, not Eduardo](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/165). The release check runs at 0.2.0. Record its result here, as a comment if this ticket has already closed.

189.title: Fit the release flow to the final ruleset
189.body:
## Question

How does the release flow fit the final ruleset from [Settle the final main ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/162) and the narrower agent identity? Decide on:

- **How the Release PR gets its required checks.** `changesets/action` opens "Release hero-synergy" (now #181) as `github-actions[bot]`. Since GitHub's 2026-06-11 change, CI on a bot-created PR waits in "approval required" until someone with write access clicks "Approve workflows to run". Its runs on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10 failed, and the one from 2026-11-16 is waiting. The PR is BLOCKED. The options:
  - Keep the click on every update of the PR.
  - Have `release.yml` start CI itself, e.g. `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref changeset-release/main`. That would also need a `workflow_dispatch` trigger in `ci.yml`.
  - Give changesets a token whose events start workflows, e.g. a release App whose key lives in Actions secrets.
- **Whether GitHub Releases become immutable.** The App's Contents: write lets it edit or delete a published GitHub Release, and Protect release tags guards only the tag. Decide whether to turn on release immutability, and check that `release.yml` (`gh release create` with the VSIX attached) and `backfill.yml` (`gh release download`) still work under it.

Already checked, and unaffected by the final ruleset:

- `canary.yml` pushes only `canary-keepalive`, and only when `CANARY_KEEPALIVE_COMMIT` is on.
- `capture.yml` uploads artifacts and never commits.
- `backfill.yml` only reads the release.
- `release.yml`'s version job pushes `changeset-release/main`, never `main`.

Whether tag creation survives Protect release tags is checked at the next release by [Apply the final main ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/188).

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

Eduardo accepted the round as written on 2026-11-16.

**Release 0.2.0 now, by hand.** "Release hero-synergy" (#181) is current and complete. It's built on `main`'s head, and since v0.1.3 only #179 and #180 changed what ships, both with changesets. Its diff holds only version bumps, changelogs and the two consumed changesets, so approving its workflows is safe. The order:

1. Eduardo works through [Apply the final main ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/188) and turns on release immutability in the same sitting.
2. On #181, he clicks "Approve workflows to run" on the latest CI run.
3. He merges once `check`, `vscode (linux)` and `vscode (macos)` are green.

This doesn't wait for the dispatch fix below: one click covers this release. Applying the rulesets first makes 0.2.0 the check that tag creation survives Protect release tags. Immutability covers only releases published after it's turned on, so turning it on first protects v0.2.0. If the tag rule stops the release, the recovery is in [Apply the final main ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/188). The registry publish runs before "Create the GitHub release", so 0.2.0 still ships.

**From then on, `release.yml` starts CI on the Release PR itself.** `ci.yml` gains a `workflow_dispatch` trigger. The `version` job gets `actions: write` and runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref changeset-release/main` after changesets. `GITHUB_TOKEN` can still start `workflow_dispatch`, which is one of only two events it can start. The check runs land on the PR's head commit, where the required checks look. No new credential is involved. Built by [Dispatch CI for the Release PR](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/192). Rejected:

- **Keep the click.** CI would start only when Eduardo arrives to merge, so every release would wait on the macOS e2e.
- **A release App token.** That's a new key in Actions secrets, and a workflow on any branch can read it unless it's scoped to an environment. The agent App has Workflows: write. GitHub's change names only `github-actions[bot]`, so it's unconfirmed that App-opened PRs skip the approval.

**GitHub Releases become immutable.** `backfill.yml` republishes whatever VSIX the GitHub release holds. Today the App's Contents: write could replace that file without anyone noticing, and the next backfill would ship the replacement to the Marketplace.

- **What it locks:** the release's files and its tag. The title and notes stay editable.
- **What it leaves open:** the App can still delete a release, but the tag name can never be reused. Deleting a release is visible, and nothing can quietly replace it under the same tag.
- **Nothing breaks.** `gh release create` with files already creates a draft, uploads, then publishes, which is the order immutability needs. `backfill.yml` only downloads.
- **Who applies it:** the switch is in Settings → General → Releases, with no documented REST endpoint, so Eduardo applies it. It's added as a checkbox on [Apply the final main ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/188).

**Unconfirmed, checked where noted:**

- That a dispatched run's checks satisfy Protect main's required checks. Checked by [Dispatch CI for the Release PR](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/192) at the next Release PR update.
- That a personal repo offers release immutability. The docs cover repository and organization settings without saying. If the switch is missing, it's recorded on [Apply the final main ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/188).
- That tag creation survives Protect release tags and that an immutable release still gets its VSIX. Both are checked at the 0.2.0 release, recorded on [Apply the final main ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/188).

Sources:

- [Bot-created pull requests can run workflows if approved](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-06-11-bot-created-pull-requests-can-run-workflows-if-approved/) (GitHub changelog, 2026-06-11)
- [Immutable releases](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/immutable-releases) and [Preventing changes to your releases](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/establish-provenance-and-integrity/preventing-changes-to-your-releases) (GitHub Docs)
- [`gh release create` manual](https://man.archlinux.org/man/gh-release-create.1.en): with files, it creates a draft, uploads, then publishes

190.title: Limit the marketplace environment to main
190.body:
## Question

Limit the `marketplace` environment to `main`. Today it has no deployment-branch policy and no protection rules (`deployment_branch_policy: null`), and the Marketplace's Entra ID credential trusts it. Open VSX trusted publishing will too, once it is switched on. So a workflow on **any** branch can publish the extension, without anything reaching `main`. Under [Pick the agent's GitHub identity](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/161), the App has Workflows: write, so a well-meaning agent testing a release fix on its branch could publish from that branch.

Only Eduardo can make this change (HITL checklist):

- [ ] Restrict deployments to the `main` branch.

```sh
gh api --method PUT repos/dbarjs/hero-synergy/environments/marketplace --input - <<'EOF'
{ "deployment_branch_policy": { "protected_branches": false, "custom_branch_policies": true } }
EOF
gh api --method POST repos/dbarjs/hero-synergy/environments/marketplace/deployment-branch-policies -f name=main -f type=branch
```

- [ ] Read it back: `gh api repos/dbarjs/hero-synergy/environments/marketplace --jq .deployment_branch_policy` shows `custom_branch_policies: true`, and the policy list holds only `main`.

What this leaves working:

- `release.yml`'s publish job runs on a push to `main`, so it is unaffected.
- `backfill.yml` is a `workflow_dispatch`, so it must be dispatched from `main`. That's its default.
- The OIDC subject is `environment:marketplace`, which doesn't change.

Resolved when the policy is live and the next release or backfill still publishes.

192.title: Dispatch CI for the Release PR
192.body:
## Question

Get the Release PR its required checks without anyone clicking, as decided in [Fit the release flow to the final ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/189). Since GitHub's 2026-06-11 change, CI on a PR opened by `github-actions[bot]` waits at "Approve workflows to run". `GITHUB_TOKEN` can still start a `workflow_dispatch`, so `release.yml` starts CI itself:

- `ci.yml`: add `workflow_dispatch:` to `on:`. No job branches on the event name, so the same jobs run.
- `release.yml`: give the `version` job `actions: write`. After `changesets/action/version`, add a step that runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref changeset-release/main --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"` with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`. The job runs only in version mode, and in that mode changesets always pushes the branch, so the step can run every time.
- `ci.yml`'s concurrency group is per ref, so a newer dispatch cancels the run it replaces.

The `pull_request` runs keep appearing as "action_required". They're noise and block nothing, because a run waiting for approval creates no check runs.

Execution is carried into this map: AFK, built in a worktree, PR to `main`. Eduardo merges. No test reads the workflow files today, so add a test that checks the dispatch trigger and the dispatch step are present, next to whatever the repo already tests.

Resolved when the PR has merged and the next Release PR update shows `check`, `vscode (linux)` and `vscode (macos)` green from a `workflow_dispatch` run, with nobody clicking. Record that run's URL. If the dispatched checks don't count toward Protect main's required checks, record why and reopen [Fit the release flow to the final ruleset](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/189).

195.title: Specs and build tickets in the Cockpit
195.body:
## Destination

The Cockpit follows Matt Pocock's flow past the map: specs and their build tickets are shown and launched like maps and their decision tickets, from the idea to the last build ticket closed, on GitHub and on local markdown, honouring the skills 1.3.2 decisions. Every question that depends on is resolved, so the result goes straight to `/to-spec`.

## Notes

- **Domain.** hero-synergy, an unofficial VS Code cockpit for Matt Pocock's agent skills. Read [`GLOSSARY.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/GLOSSARY.md), the ADRs in [`docs/adr/`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/tree/main/docs/adr) and the mattpocock-skills section of the upstream register, [`docs/upstream.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/upstream.md), before a ticket.
- **Words, settled while charting.** A **Spec** is the issue `/to-spec` publishes, or `.scratch/<feature>/spec.md` on a local tracker. A **Decision ticket** is a child of a map: one question, typed by `wayfinder:<type>`. A **Build ticket** is a child of a spec: one slice to build with acceptance criteria, carrying a triage role. **Ticket** is the word for either. Avoid "spec ticket", "wayfinder ticket", "PRD" and "story". The glossary entries are on `main` since [#212 Name specs and the two kinds of ticket in the glossary](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/212) merged.
- **The flow the Cockpit follows.** Upstream's own map of it is [`ask-matt`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/v1.3.2/skills/engineering/ask-matt/SKILL.md): a finished map hands off, it doesn't build. `/to-spec` collapses the map's decisions into a spec, `/to-tickets` splits it in the same context window, then `/implement` takes one build ticket per fresh session, or `/implement-spec` runs the whole spec on one integration branch. An idea small enough for one session starts at `/grill-with-docs` instead of a map. `/tdd`, `/code-review` and `/pr` run inside those sessions.
- **The 1.3.2 decisions** ([changelog](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/v1.3.2/CHANGELOG.md)) the result must honour:
  - A map and its decision tickets carry only `wayfinder:` labels, never a triage label. So a triage label never makes a decision ticket AFK, and a build ticket is never launched with `/wayfinder`.
  - `/to-tickets` makes each build ticket a sub-issue of its spec when the spec is an existing issue; native blocking edges were already there in 1.3.1. So the scout reads a spec's children the way it reads a map's: frontier, claim, blockers.
  - `/implement` may be passed a ticket reference, which it fetches and whose title it states. So Implement passes the build ticket's URL or path.
  - The GitHub tracker template gained four `gh` flags (`--parent`, `--add-sub-issue`, `--blocked-by`, `--add-blocked-by`), comment-then-close and an own-repo rule. This repo's tracker doc gets all of them from the `v1.3.2` template in [#214 Refresh the tracker doc from the skills 1.3.2 template](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/214), waiting for Eduardo to merge. The plugin installed here stays `49dd158` shown as 1.3.1, the marketplace's current pin, so the skills sessions load still lack the last two flags, comment-then-close and the own-repo rule. The upstream register's tested ceiling moves to 1.3.2.
- **Plan, don't build.** This map decides; the build comes afterwards through `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets` and `/implement`. One exception, the task ticket that refreshes this repo's skills and agent docs, lands by PR. A prototype is throwaway work on a `prototype/<name>` branch, linked from its ticket. Research findings are `docs/research/<name>.md` on a `research/<name>` branch, pushed with no PR.
- **Who writes.** [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md) stands: creating a spec and creating tickets are Actions that launch a session, and the session writes. The Cockpit never writes to the tracker and never runs git. A decision that needs otherwise is a change to that ADR and says so.
- **Skills.** Grilling tickets use `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling`. Prototype tickets use `/prototype`. Research tickets use `/research`.
- **Writing to the repo.** Every ticket session works in its own git worktree, never in the shared checkout. Glossary and ADR edits go up as a PR from the worktree branch; only Eduardo merges ([#159 Only Eduardo merges to main](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/159)). Nothing is pushed to `main`.
- **Toolchain.** The devcontainer has no global `vp`: run `pnpm exec vp <command>`. `pnpm exec vp check --fix` before pushing; it formats Markdown too. Every test runs through a `vp` command.
- **Tests.** The harness is first-class: a decision that changes behaviour says what it is tested on, and no coverage is trimmed for CI cost. The seams and tiers decided in [#18 How is the extension tested?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/18) stand.
- **Many maps, many specs.** Eduardo's repos hold dozens of maps, most of them finished (one project: 45). Design every view, budget and cost estimate for a repo with as many specs.
- **Issue numbers.** Every map, spec and ticket is shown as `#number title`, in the Cockpit, in session names and in narration. The number rides in front of the name, never instead of it.
- **Real examples to design against.** [#1 hero-synergy v0.1.0, fully decided](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/1) led to [#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/37) and its 26 build tickets, all closed. [#130 State reading for local trackers, tested against a real five-month tracker](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/130) led to [#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/163) and its 11 build tickets, being built now. [#123 Launch AFK sessions with permissions bypassed in isolated environments](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/123) led to [#155 Launch AFK sessions with permissions bypassed in isolated environments](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/155), a spec with its map's exact title and no build tickets, built and closed by one pull request. None of the three specs carries a label that says it is a spec, and none links back to its map except in prose.
- **In flight.** The build of #163 is moving the snapshot to schema 2 and adding the Unmapped fold. Start from what it lands; don't redo it.
- **Private corpus.** The real tracker behind the scratch mirror stays on Eduardo's machine: shapes and counts only, and only from the committed fixtures in `packages/core/fixtures/`.
- **Driver.** Eduardo (`dbarjs`). A claim is an assignment to him.

## Decisions so far

<!-- the index: one line per closed ticket, enough to judge relevance, then zoom the link for the detail the ticket holds -->

- [What did skills 1.3.2 change in the contracts the Cockpit reads or spawns?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/196): nothing the Cockpit parses changed; 1.3.2 changes only what sessions write (no triage labels on a map or its tickets, sub-issues when the source is an issue, an optional `/implement` reference, four `gh` flags); this machine runs `49dd158` shown as 1.3.1, the marketplace's current pin, which lacks `--blocked-by` and comment-then-close; the canary's red is an unlisted skill on `main`.
- [Which forms do specs and build tickets take, upstream and in the wild?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/197): a spec is seven H2s unchanged since 2026-02 (3 of 3 specs here, 0 of 144 other issues); a build ticket is `## What to build` and `## Acceptance criteria` under a native parent (37 of 37); both carry only `ready-for-agent`, and one spec has no build tickets; acceptance boxes say nothing about state; all 28 closed build tickets were assigned and 22 list a merged `worktree-<n>` pull request; the local mirror holds only `PRD.md` with bold `**Parent:**` lines, and 16 of its 218 decision tickets carry a triage role.
- [What can GitHub's API report about specs, build tickets and their pull requests, and at what cost?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/198): no API fact marks a spec; open parentless `ready-for-agent` issues ride in the scout's list request for the same 1 point, and a spec with no build tickets looks like any lone issue; the fragment reads build tickets unchanged at 4 points per spec; `closedByPullRequestsReferences` adds each ticket's pull request for 1 more, only when the description says `Closes #n` against the default branch; the three source maps are closed, so the map-to-spec link is prose on a hidden map.
- [Update the skills to 1.3.2 and refresh this repo's agent docs](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/201): templates taken straight from the `v1.3.2` tag, because the marketplace still pins `49dd158`; `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` now equals the 1.3.2 GitHub template (five hunks) in [#214 Refresh the tracker doc from the skills 1.3.2 template](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/214), waiting for Eduardo to merge; the other agent docs already matched; the shared plugin stays at 1.3.1 until Eduardo updates it.

## Not yet specified

- **The new drift codes**, their words and levels: a triage label on a decision ticket, a build ticket with no acceptance criteria, a spec's child that carries a `wayfinder:` label; and `header-key-bold`, which today fires on the bold `**Status:**` and `**Blocked by:**` lines upstream's own local ticket template writes. Hangs on how a spec is recognised.
- **Health and the canary.** Which missing skill is a loud health warning once the Cockpit launches more than `wayfinder` and `to-spec`, and what the canary watches of `to-tickets`, `implement`, `implement-spec` and `grill-with-docs`. Hangs on which Actions exist.
- **The fixtures and seams** the spec flow is tested on: recorded GitHub answers for a spec and its build tickets, local `spec.md` efforts, the end-to-end tier. Hangs on what the snapshot holds.
- **The upstream register.** The rows for the new contracts, the move of the tested ceiling to 1.3.2, the twelve stale places the 1.3.2 research lists, and two `gh` rows the API research corrects: 4 points per map, not 5, and sub-issues returned in the parent's own order. Hangs on which contracts the decisions lean on.
- **The front door.** How the README and the Marketplace listing describe a Cockpit that covers specs as well as maps. Hangs on the whole route.

## Out of scope

- **Row Actions for `/triage`, `/diagnosing-bugs`, `/retro` and `/improve-codebase-architecture`.** They stay reachable through Run skill…; `/tdd`, `/code-review` and `/pr` run inside a build session and get no button.
- **The Cockpit writing to the tracker or running git.** Ruled out by [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md), which this map keeps.
- **GitLab and other trackers.** GitHub and local markdown only, as in v0.1.0.
- **Agents other than Claude Code.** Tracked in [#182 Agent agnosticism](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/182).
- **Background sessions** (`claude --bg`): every session runs in a terminal, as decided for v0.1.0.
- **The canary's failure on an in-progress skill.** [#184 Upstream break: skills v1.3.2](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/184) stays its own issue.
- **Rebuilding what [#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/163) is building.** This map starts from its schema 2 and its Unmapped fold.

196.title: What did skills 1.3.2 change in the contracts the Cockpit reads or spawns?
196.body:
## Question

What changed between mattpocock-skills 1.3.1 (`24fe0ef`) and 1.3.2 (`d1478fc`, tagged 2026-10-29), and on `main` since, in every contract the Cockpit reads or spawns?

- **Row by row** against the mattpocock-skills section of [`docs/upstream.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/upstream.md): the wayfinder text, the three tracker templates, `triage-labels.md`, the manifest's skill list, the frontmatter shapes, and the arguments of `to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `implement`, `implement-spec`, `grill-with-docs` and `setup-matt-pocock-skills`.

- **What this machine runs**: the installed plugin's version string and commit, the marketplace's current pin, and how the installed copy differs from the 1.3.2 tag.
- **Ahead of 1.3.2**: what `main` holds that the tag doesn't (`implement-spec`'s fresh implementer per ticket, the `in-progress` skills behind [#184 Upstream break: skills v1.3.2](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/184)) and whether any of it touches a contract.
- **Stale in this repo**: `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` against the 1.3.2 GitHub template, the glossary's AFK ticket entry, the README's bypass paragraph, and any register row the diff contradicts.

The method and the previous diff are in [#31 Which mattpocock-skills version does the Cockpit read?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/31).

197.title: Which forms do specs and build tickets take, upstream and in the wild?
197.body:
## Question

Which forms do a spec and its build tickets take, in what upstream's skills write and in what real trackers hold, and what in each form could code recognise?

- **Upstream, over time.** Every template `/to-spec` and `/to-tickets` has shipped, under their earlier names too, from the first release to v1.3.2 and `main`: the spec's headings, the ticket's headings (`## Parent`, `## What to build`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Blocked by`), the labels applied, how a ticket points at its spec (a `## Parent` section, a sub-issue since 1.3.2), how blockers are written (text, native edges), and the local forms (`.scratch/<feature>/spec.md`, `issues/NN-<slug>.md`, `Status: ready-for-agent`). Date each form by tag and commit.
- **This repo's GitHub tracker.** [#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/37) with its 26 build tickets and [#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/163) with its 11: the headings actually present, the labels, the parent links, the blocked-by edges against any `## Blocked by` text, how each spec names its map, what a closed build ticket looks like (its closing pull request, its last comment), and the issues that are `ready-for-agent` with no spec, such as [#36 Write the upstream-review skill](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/36).
- **Local trackers.** The committed fixtures only (`packages/core/fixtures/scratch-mirror`, `local-forms` and `local-tracker`): which spec and PRD files exist, their names and casing, how issue files point at them (`Parent:` lines), the triage roles on their Status lines, and the efforts that hold both a map and a spec. Shapes and counts only.

For each form, say what a reader could key on to call an issue a spec or a build ticket with no label to go by, and where two forms could be confused: a map's decision ticket, an unmapped issue, a triaged bug.

The method is the one of [#10 Which wayfinder conventions exist in the wild?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/10) and [#131 State forms on a real local tracker](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/131).

## Answer

The full catalogue, with every form dated by tag and commit or counted, is in [`docs/research/spec-and-build-ticket-forms.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/spec-and-build-ticket-forms/docs/research/spec-and-build-ticket-forms.md) on the branch `research/spec-and-build-ticket-forms`.

### The forms

**Upstream** (`mattpocock/skills`, first commit to `v1.3.2` and `main`):

- **A spec** is one issue with seven H2s: `Problem Statement`, `Solution`, `User Stories`, `Implementation Decisions`, `Testing Decisions`, `Out of Scope`, `Further Notes`. They have not changed since 2026-02-03. It carried no label, then `needs-triage` (2026-04-28), and `ready-for-agent` since 2026-05-06, in every tag. It was called a PRD until `v1.1.0`. The template has no title rule, no link to a map and no label that says "spec".
- **A build ticket on a tracker** has held `## What to build` and `## Acceptance criteria` in every version since 2026-02-20. `## Parent` is left out when the source was not an issue. `## Blocked by` is left out since 1.3.2 when blockers are native edges. The label is `ready-for-agent`, the same as its spec.
- **The parent link** was a native sub-issue "where it has one" from 1.1.0 to 1.3.1, and upstream's docs record it often went missing. Since 1.3.2 each build ticket is a sub-issue of its source issue. The fallbacks since 1.3.2 are `Part of #<parent>` and `Blocked by: #<n>` at the top of the body, the same lines a decision ticket uses.
- **Locally**, the spec file was `PRD.md` (`v1.0.0` to `v1.1.0`) and is `spec.md` from `v1.2.0`. Build tickets were one root `tickets.md` in `v1.1.0` only. From `v1.2.0` they are one file per ticket, `issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, with bold `**What to build:**`, `**Blocked by:**` and `**Status:** ready-for-agent`, and checkboxes under no heading. No line names the spec.
- `/implement` never closes a build ticket and never ticks its boxes.

**This repo's tracker** (147 issues, read on 2026-11-16): 7 maps, 91 decision tickets, 3 specs, 37 build tickets, 9 others.

- The 3 specs hold exactly the seven H2s, carry `ready-for-agent` and nothing else, and have no native parent. Each names its map in the paragraph before `## Problem Statement` (3 of 3), which is not in upstream's template. Only one title starts with `Spec:`.
- [#155 Launch AFK sessions with permissions bypassed in isolated environments](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/155) is a spec with no build ticket, built and closed by one pull request, with the same title as its map.
- The 37 build tickets all hold `## Parent`, `## What to build`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Blocked by` and nothing else. All are native sub-issues and name the same spec in `## Parent`. Their 57 native blocked-by edges are repeated in `## Blocked by` on 37 of 37.
- Of the 28 closed build tickets, 22 list a merged pull request from a `worktree-<n>` branch, 11 have no comment at all, and 26 still have every acceptance box empty.
- `ready-for-agent` with no parent selects 4 issues: the 3 specs and [#36 Write the upstream-review skill](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/36), which has none of the template's headings.

**Local fixtures** (shapes and counts):

- The scratch mirror holds no `spec.md`. It holds 2 `PRD.md` in 49 efforts.
- One PRD sits beside a map. Its 12 issue files carry a bold `**Parent:** [<title>](../PRD.md)`, a bold `**Status:**` and checkboxes before any H2, and are numbered 11 to 22 inside the map's own sequence. 9 are open (8 `ready-for-human`, 1 `ready-for-agent`).
- The other PRD has no map. Its 10 issue files read `Status: done` and name the PRD nowhere; the PRD lists them in a table.
- The only `spec.md` is the invented one in the `local-tracker` fixture.

### What code could key on, with no label

- **A spec on GitHub**: the seven H2s (3 of 3 specs, 0 of 144 other issues). "Has sub-issues and is not a map" finds 2 of 3 and misses a spec with no build tickets.
- **A build ticket on GitHub**: a native parent that is a spec (37 of 37), and the pair `## What to build` with `## Acceptance criteria` (37 of 37, 0 of 110 others).
- **A decision ticket**, for contrast: `## Question` opens all 91, and nothing else has it.
- **Locally**: a file named `spec.md` or `PRD.md` in the effort directory; a `Parent:` header line that names it (12 of 12 in the effort with both a map and a PRD, but 0 of 10 under the PRD with no map); no type and no `## Question` (all 39 mirror files that are not a map's tickets, 0 of the 218 that are).

### Where forms can be confused

1. A spec and its build tickets share their only label, `ready-for-agent`.
2. A spec and its map can share a title, and `## Out of Scope` is the map's `Out of scope` to a reader that ignores case.
3. A spec is not always a parent: one here was built whole.
4. A triage role does not make a build ticket: 16 of the mirror's 218 decision tickets carry one.
5. The 6 `wayfinder:task` tickets of [#64 next, the terminal pre-alpha of the Cockpit](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/64) build, and are blocked by build tickets (9 edges).
6. The glossary now makes a local issue file under a PRD both a build ticket and an unmapped issue.
7. Boxes say nothing of state: 26 of 28 closed build tickets have every box empty, and 8 open mirror files have every box ticked.
8. A closed build ticket often has no comment, so the decision-ticket rule (the resolution is the last comment) finds nothing on 11 of 28.
9. The scout's `header-key-bold` drift fires on the exact lines upstream's local ticket template writes.

The scout reads none of this today: on GitHub it never fetches a spec or a build ticket, and locally it reads no `spec.md`, `PRD.md` or `Parent:` line.

### Not verified

- **Other repos.** One GitHub tracker (this repo's) and one mirrored local tracker were counted. How common each form is elsewhere is unknown.
- **No issue written by 1.3.2.** Nothing was run. What a 1.3.2 session really writes is read from the template only, and every build ticket here predates the 1.3.2 tag.
- **Which skills commit wrote each spec and ticket.** The register says sessions ran the installed 1.2.3 up to 2026-10-07. That was not checked per session.
- **The mirror's words and dates.** They are replaced and shifted. The PRD's headings beyond `Out of Scope`, the second bold key on 8 of the 12 PRD issues, and whether their H1 led with a number cannot be read, and its forms cannot be dated against upstream's.
- **Where the mirror's mapless issues came from**: `/triage`, an earlier `to-issues` or a person.
- **A triaged issue on GitHub.** None exists on this tracker. That form is upstream's template only.
- **Why a closed decision ticket lists a later pull request** in `closedByPullRequestsReferences`. What that field counts as a reference was not looked up.
- **`tickets.md`, `plan.md`, `./plans/` and a `spec.md` written by upstream's skill.** None is in the fixtures.
- **A remapped label.** Every tracker here uses the default role names as label strings.
- **Installs between tags.** The marketplace pins `main` commits, so which form an install wrote between two tags is not known.
- **Upstream's issue reports** are cited from upstream's changelog, docs and commit messages. The issues themselves were not read.
- **GitLab and other trackers.** Read for two lines only.
- **What the API can list, and at what cost.** That is the question of [#198 What can GitHub's API report about specs, build tickets and their pull requests, and at what cost?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/198).

198.title: What can GitHub's API report about specs, build tickets and their pull requests, and at what cost?
198.body:
## Question

With no label that marks a spec, what can the GitHub API report that lets the scout find a repo's specs, their build tickets and the pull requests that close them, and what does each route cost?

- **Finding specs.** The candidate routes: the `ready-for-agent` label together with `subIssues.totalCount` or `subIssuesSummary`, the issue search qualifiers for parents and sub-issues, a walk from each map through its cross-references. Which of them list a repo's open specs in one request, which miss a spec with no build tickets yet, and which bring back specs that are built and closed.
- **Reading a spec's build tickets.** Whether the fragment the scout already sends for a map's children (`packages/core/src/github/query.ts`) reads a spec's children unchanged, and what it lacks.
- **Pull requests.** What links an issue to the pull request that closes it (`closedByPullRequestsReferences`, timeline events, a `Closes #n` line, the development links), whether the link exists before the pull request merges, what state a pull request reports (draft, open, merged, checks, review), and what a pushed `worktree-<n>` branch with no pull request looks like.
- **Cost.** The rate-limit points per spec and per repo for each route, measured with `rateLimit { cost }` and `rateLimit(dryRun: true)` on this repo ([#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/37) with 26 closed build tickets, [#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/163) with 11 open), and an estimate for a repo with 45 maps and as many specs, against the budget of [#27 What is the scout's budget: refresh cadence, caching and rate limits?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/27).

Read-only queries only. The method and the earlier numbers are in [#9 Can one GraphQL query collect everything the scout needs?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/9).

lastComment.body:
## Resolution

**Nothing in GitHub's API marks a spec: it is found by position, as an open `ready-for-agent` issue with no parent. That list rides in the scout's existing list request for the same 1 point. The scout's fragment reads a spec's build tickets unchanged at 4 points per spec, and `closedByPullRequestsReferences` links each build ticket to its pull request for 1 point more per spec, but only when the pull request says `Closes #n` and targets the default branch.**

Measured on 2026-11-16, 19:15 to 19:45 UTC, with `gh` 2.100.0 and read-only requests. Full findings, every query with its cost and node count: [`docs/research/github-specs-and-pull-requests.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/github-specs-and-pull-requests/docs/research/github-specs-and-pull-requests.md).

### Finding specs

- **What marks a spec: nothing.** No label of its own, `issueType` is `null`, and the filter of `repository.issues` has no field for parent or sub-issues. A spec carries `ready-for-agent`, like its build tickets, and has no parent.
- **Cheapest route that lists every open spec:** `issues(labels: ["ready-for-agent"], states: [OPEN])` with `parent { number }` and `subIssuesSummary { total completed percentCompleted }`. 1 point per 100 open `ready-for-agent` issues alone; **no extra point** as one more connection in the scout's list request. On this repo it returned 11 issues: the open spec [#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/163), its nine open build tickets (each naming the spec as `parent`), and [#36 Write the upstream-review skill](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/36).
- **A spec with no build tickets yet** comes back, but looks exactly like a lone `ready-for-agent` issue (no parent, 0 of 0). Only the body tells them apart: the three specs here carry the template's seven H2s, the lone issue none.
- **Closed specs** are left out unless `CLOSED` is asked for. A spec can be open and fully built: [#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/37) sat open at 26 of 26 for 39 days; `percentCompleted: 100` shows it.
- **Search qualifiers** work but are not the default. `is:open has:sub-issue -label:"wayfinder:map"` returns exactly the open spec for 1 point, only under `type: ISSUE_ADVANCED`; under `type: ISSUE` the qualifier is ignored without an error and all 38 open issues come back. `has:sub-issue`, `no:parent-issue` and `sub-issue:` are undocumented, and `has:sub-issue` misses a spec with no build tickets.
- **The walk from each map through its cross-references** costs 1 point for 45 maps and is the only route that says which map a spec came from. It depends on the spec naming its map in prose (this repo's habit, not the template's), and it must start from closed maps: all three source maps are closed, and the scout lists open maps only.

### Reading a spec's build tickets

- The fragment in `packages/core/src/github/query.ts` reads a spec's children **unchanged**: state, triage label, assignee, parent, native blockers (closed ones kept with their state), last comment, body. 0.75 s and 101 KB for 11 tickets, 1.09 s and 186 KB for 26.
- **4 points per spec or map, not 5.** The fragment as shipped has four nested connections; the 5 in the upstream register and in [#27 What is the scout's budget: refresh cadence, caching and rate limits?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/27) was measured on an earlier shape.
- It lacks: the pull request; `stateReason` (a ticket closed as not planned was not built); the spec's own `state`, labels and `subIssuesSummary` (the list gives state, parent and summary for nothing).
- 12 of the 29 closed build tickets have no comment at all: a build ticket closed by a merge has no resolution comment.
- `subIssues` comes back in the parent's own order, not creation order.

### Pull requests

- **The link is `Issue.closedByPullRequestsReferences`** (mirror: `PullRequest.closingIssuesReferences`). It exists **from the second the pull request is opened**, draft included, and stays after the merge with `state: MERGED`. [#173 Read every Blocked by and Blocks form a local tracker holds](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/173) was read both ways: its pull request merged at 19:30:18 UTC, during the session.
- **It exists only when** the pull request's description holds a closing keyword and the pull request targets the default branch. A mention without a keyword does not link; a keyword on another base branch does not link (28 of 29 sampled on `microsoft/vscode`). Upstream's `/pr` template has no `Closes` line and `/implement` opens no pull request, so the link is this repo's convention. Under the closed spec, 6 of 26 build tickets have no linked pull request.
- **Pull requests closed without merging** come back only with `includeClosedPrs: true`; then add `orderByState: true`, which puts the open one first.
- **State a pull request reports, at no extra points:** `state` (`OPEN`, `CLOSED`, `MERGED`), `isDraft`, `statusCheckRollup { state }` (`null` when no check ran), `reviewDecision` (`null` on every pull request here: no review is required), `mergeable`, `mergeStateStatus`, `headRefName`. Each check by name is a connection: 10 points per spec instead of 5.
- **Other signals:** the timeline's `CrossReferencedEvent.willCloseTarget` is true only while the pull request is open; `ClosedEvent.closer` names a pull request, a commit or nothing. `linkedBranches` is empty for a branch pushed with `git push`. The issue's `updatedAt` does not move when a pull request links to it.
- **A pushed `worktree-<n>` branch with no pull request is invisible from the issue.** It is found by name only (`refs(refPrefix: "refs/heads/", query: "worktree-")`, 1 point per 100 branches): head commit, date, no checks, zero pull requests. 41 of the 43 `worktree-` branches here are merged leftovers, so a branch alone is not work in flight.

### Costs

| Request | Points |
| --- | --- |
| The scout's list, extended with open spec candidates and open pull requests | 1 (unchanged) |
| One spec or map with the scout's fragment | 4 |
| The same with each build ticket's pull requests and their state | 5 |
| The same with each check by name | 10 |
| Open pull requests with the issues they close, per 100 | 1 |
| `worktree-` branches with their pull requests, per 100 | 1 |
| A flat page of 100 open `ready-for-agent` issues with every ticket field and pull request | 5 |

- **45 maps and 45 specs, 7 of each open:** 29 points per collect today, 57 with specs, 64 with each build ticket's pull request (39 with flat pages, which lose closed build tickets and the spec's order).
- **Against the budget of [#27 What is the scout's budget: refresh cadence, caching and rate limits?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/27):** the worst hour, one collect a minute, uses 3,840 of the 4,000 points available before the pause, against 1,740 today.
- **All 90 open:** 406 points and 19 requests per collect.
- Chunks of five stand: five blocks with pull requests took 3.3 s for 670 KB; 45 blocks in one request are refused at 526,500 nodes.
- Time for 7 maps and 7 specs: about 12 s per collect, roughly double today's (extrapolated).

### Not verified

- **Manual links** from the Development sidebar (`userLinkedOnly`, `ConnectedEvent`, `DisconnectedEvent`): none exists on this repo.
- **Linked branches** made with "Create a branch" or `gh issue develop`: none exists here.
- **A whole-spec run.** `/implement-spec` was not run; its single draft pull request "marked as closing the spec and tickets" is read from the skill text. Whether one description can close a spec and 26 tickets by keyword was not tested.
- **A closing keyword in a commit message alone**, with none in the pull request's description.
- **`subIssuesSummary.completed`** when a sub-issue is closed as not planned or as a duplicate.
- **The undocumented search qualifiers** behaved as measured on this date only; the search index's lag was not measured.
- **`orderByState: true`** beyond "open first".
- **States not seen:** checks `PENDING`, `EXPECTED` or `ERROR`; review `APPROVED` or `CHANGES_REQUESTED`; `mergeable: CONFLICTING`. `isDraft: true` was seen only on `cli/cli`.
- **A commit that names an issue, pushed on a branch with no pull request:** one sample, which left no timeline event.
- **`updatedAt` and pull request links**, and **a link surviving a change of base branch:** one sample each.
- **The scout's decoder on a spec's answer:** the fragment's answers were checked with a script, not run through `collect.ts`.
- **Pull requests from forks**, and issues closed from another repository.
- **GitHub Enterprise Server.**
- **Pagination past 100 open `ready-for-agent` issues, and timings at 45 specs:** costs are computed from the query; times and sizes are extrapolated from two specs.
- **Two rate-limit counters.** `rateLimit.remaining` was answered from two counters with different `resetAt` times during the session, unexplained; every cost above is the `cost` field or a dry run.
- **The 2025-03-06 changelog** on `ISSUE_ADVANCED` was read through a fetch tool that summarises.

199.title: What do /to-tickets, /implement and /implement-spec need from a Claude Code session?
199.body:
## Question

What do the sessions the Cockpit would launch for `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets`, `/implement` and `/implement-spec` need from Claude Code, and what can the Cockpit see of them?

- **Continuing a session.** Upstream keeps `/to-spec` and `/to-tickets` in one context window. Whether `claude --resume <id>` accepts a new positional prompt that starts with a slash command, what `--continue` does, and what else carries a finished session's context into a second command. On the floor (2.1.212) and on the installed version.
- **Worktrees and branches.** `/implement` commits "to the current branch": what that branch is under `-w <number>`, how a pull request comes out of it, and what the 2.1.208 reset of a reused worktree name means for a second session on the same build ticket. `/implement-spec` wants one integration branch and one worktree per implementer subagent: where those worktrees and branches are created when the session itself runs under `-w`, and without it.
- **What the registry reports.** For a session running `/implement-spec`: whether implementer subagents appear in `claude agents --json`, under which names, and whether the parent's `status` says anything about them. For the other three, whether anything differs from a decision ticket's session.
- **Arguments.** What each skill takes at v1.3.2: `/to-spec` (it reads the conversation), `/to-tickets <reference>`, `/implement <ticket reference>`, `/implement-spec` (given a spec), on GitHub (a URL or a number) and on a local tracker (a path).

Read the docs, the changelog and the skills' text first; run `claude` only where reading can't answer, in a scratch directory, never against this repo's tracker. Mark what was read and what was run. The earlier measurements are in [#21 How does the Cockpit handle a session's lifecycle?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/21), [#30 Which Claude Code version does the Cockpit need?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/30) and [#124 Claude Code's bypass-permissions contract](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/124).

lastComment.body:
## Answer

Full findings, each with its source: [`docs/research/build-session-contract.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/build-session-contract/docs/research/build-session-contract.md) on the `research/build-session-contract` branch (never merged).

Measured on Claude Code 2.1.212 (the floor) and 2.1.325 (installed), with the skills read at `v1.3.2`. The runs used scratch configs and scratch repositories, and a scripted stand-in for the model: they measure what the harness does, not what a model chooses.

### Can a session be continued with a new slash command?

Yes. `claude --resume <session-id> "/to-tickets <spec>"` reloads the finished conversation and runs the skill on top of it. Run on both versions, in a terminal and in print mode: the request held the earlier turns, then the skill's text, with the same session id and transcript.

- `--continue "/to-tickets <spec>"` works the same way but reopens "the most recent conversation in the current directory", whichever that was. The Cockpit cannot aim it.
- `-n` with `--resume` renames the session, on both versions. `--plugin-dir` and bypass are not restored and must be passed again.
- **A session that is still open must not be resumed.** Claude Code neither refuses nor warns: it starts a second process on the same transcript, and the registry then lists two entries with one `sessionId` (run, both versions). While the session is open, the next command is typed in its terminal, which is also upstream's own way ("one unbroken context window").
- Today's To spec launch is a plain terminal with no name and no status plugin, so the Cockpit never learns its session id. Resuming it needs that launch to be tracked like a ticket session.

### Which branch does each skill commit to under `-w`?

- **`/implement`** commits "to the current branch", which under `-w <n>` is `worktree-<n>` in `.claude/worktrees/<n>`, branched from `origin`'s default branch (run, both versions). The skill does not push, open a pull request or close the ticket: a pull request comes from the session being told to, or from the developer.
- **A second `-w <n>`** reopens the old tip, except when the worktree is clean and either has no commits or was merged (a squash counts) with its remote branch deleted **and pruned in the clone**: then it is reset to the current `origin/main` (run, both versions, nine states). This repository keeps `origin/worktree-<n>` after a merge, so here a reused number always reopens the old tip.
- **`/implement-spec`**: a subagent spawned with `isolation: "worktree"` lands in `<repository root>/.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>` on `worktree-agent-<id>`, branched from `origin`'s default branch, never from the integration branch. That holds with and without `-w` on the session; under `-w` the subagent's worktree sits beside the session's, not inside it (run, both versions). With `worktree.baseRef: "head"` it branches from the session's `HEAD` instead (run, 2.1.325).
- Under `-w <n>` the integration branch is made inside worktree `<n>`, and `worktree-<n>` stays at its base with no commits. Without `-w` the session switches the branch of the checkout it was launched in.

### What does the registry show of an `/implement-spec` run?

One session. Subagents get no entry and no name in `claude agents --json`, and no field of the parent counts them (read in the docs, run on both versions, and seen in a logged-in 2.1.325 session).

- The parent reads `busy` for as long as a background subagent runs, including after its own turn has ended.
- It reads `waiting` with `waitingFor: "permission prompt"` when a subagent needs an approval.
- `cwd` stays the session's own directory.
- `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets` and `/implement` show nothing a decision ticket's session doesn't. To spec's entry carries a default display name, because it is launched without `-n`.

### Arguments

None of the four declares an argument (`disable-model-invocation: true`, no `argument-hint`, no `$ARGUMENTS`). Claude Code appends `ARGUMENTS: <text>` to the skill's text (run, both versions), and the skill's prose decides what it means.

| Skill             | Takes                                                                                              | GitHub                 | Local tracker                                   |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `/to-spec`        | Nothing in `SKILL.md` (it reads the conversation); upstream's page passes `/to-spec #<map_issue>`  | the map's URL or number | the map's path (not stated upstream for to-spec) |
| `/to-tickets`     | "a spec path, an issue number or URL", or nothing in the session that wrote the spec               | the spec's URL or number | `.scratch/<feature-slug>/spec.md`               |
| `/implement`      | "a ticket reference", fetched, its title stated first                                              | the ticket's URL       | `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md` |
| `/implement-spec` | "a pointer to the spec (an issue number or a file path)"                                           | the spec's URL or number | the spec's path                                 |

## Not verified

- **No real `/implement-spec`, `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets` or `/implement` ran.** Everything about them is their text at `v1.3.2`. Only a real `/implement-spec` run settles: whether the orchestrator uses the Agent tool's `isolation: "worktree"` or runs `git worktree add` itself; what it names the integration branch and where it creates it; whether implementers run in the background and how many at once; where the merger runs; whether it opens the draft pull request and when it closes tickets; what the exit prompt asks when the `-w` worktree sits on the integration branch.
- **No run reached a model.** Replies were scripted, so anything that depends on a model's choice is unmeasured, including whether `/to-spec` and `/to-tickets` ask their questions as plain text (`idle`) or through a question tool (`waiting`).
- **No login and no feature flags in the scratch runs.** Gated behaviour ran on built-in defaults. The one logged-in observation covers the registry only.
- **2.1.292**, the register's tested ceiling, was not run.
- **Reuse of a worktree name was run in print mode only**; an interactive `-w` exit with "keep", and the docs' sandbox condition, were not.
- **`worktree.baseRef: "head"`** was run on 2.1.325 only.
- **`--resume "<name>"` with a prompt, `--fork-session`, a resumed `-w` session with a new slash command, and a resume after a compaction** were read, not run.
- **A local tracker under `-w`** (the gitignored `.scratch` is absent from a worktree, and a `-w` session cannot edit the main checkout) was reasoned from the docs, not run.
- **Worktrees made by hand with `git worktree add` inside a `-w` session** were not run.
- **The `SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop` hooks**, the one documented way to see subagents from outside, were read, not run.
- **What a resumed session's second command costs** (prompt cache) was not measured.
- **linux-arm64 only.**
