200.title: What does a map's fog offer?
200.body:
## Question

What does the Cockpit offer on a map's fog?

Today the Fog fold lists a map's "Not yet specified" entries with a count and opens the Detail; it offers no Action. A map with every ticket closed is a finished map and offers To spec, even when fog is left. Upstream's wayfinder says a map is done "when the way is clear, with nothing left to decide", and that fog graduates into tickets as tickets resolve; nothing prompts a session to graduate the fog of a map whose tickets are all closed. Eduardo's note while charting: fog left on a map is work that still needs tickets, so it should lead to an Action.

- **The Action.** Whether a map with fog left gets one, what it runs (`/wayfinder <map>` with no ticket, and what the skill does with a map that has no open ticket), where it sits (the Fog fold, the map row, ▶) and what it is called.
- **Finished.** Whether a map with every ticket closed and fog left is still a finished map, and whether it still offers To spec.
- **The Tree.** What it says about such a map: its place in the order, its counts, its hover.
- **An empty fog.** What an entry that says nothing is left counts as. Real maps write one: "Nothing at the moment: every question in view is a ticket." on [#1 hero-synergy v0.1.0, fully decided](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/1), "Nothing left. The spec …" on [#130 State reading for local trackers, tested against a real five-month tracker](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/130).
- **The glossary.** Fog, Finished map and Stuck map.

201.title: Update the skills to 1.3.2 and refresh this repo's agent docs
201.body:
## Question

Is this repo on skills 1.3.2, with its agent docs refreshed from the 1.3.2 templates?

The work, the one exception to this map's "plan, don't build":

- **Get a 1.3.2 copy.** The official marketplace can't deliver it today: its pin is `49dd158`, the commit already installed here and shown as 1.3.1. Eduardo picks the route: wait for the marketplace's pin to pass the `v1.3.2` tag, install from upstream's own marketplace (which changes the plugin on the volume every container shares), or take the templates straight from the `v1.3.2` tag.
- **Refresh `docs/agents/`.** `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` equals the installed template byte for byte, so re-running `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` on that copy changes nothing. The real delta is five hunks of the 1.3.2 GitHub template: Blocking with `--blocked-by` and `--add-blocked-by`, Count open blockers, comment-then-close, the own-repo paragraph and Read a PR. Keep this repo's choices: the GitHub tracker, pull requests as a request surface off, the five default triage labels, single-context domain docs.
- **Open a pull request** with the refreshed docs for Eduardo to merge. `CLAUDE.md` keeps its own sections.

The answer records the route taken, the plugin's version and commit afterwards, and what changed in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. The diff, hunk by hunk, is in the findings of [#196 What did skills 1.3.2 change in the contracts the Cockpit reads or spawns?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/196).

lastComment.body:
## Answer

**The agent docs come from the `v1.3.2` tag, in [#214 Refresh the tracker doc from the skills 1.3.2 template](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/pull/214), waiting for Eduardo to merge. The plugin installed on the shared volume is unchanged.**

### The route

**Templates straight from the `v1.3.2` tag.** The other two routes were ruled out today:

- **Waiting for the marketplace** doesn't work yet. The official marketplace still pins [`49dd158`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/commit/49dd158d1076134a641b33efb035946536778336), checked 2026-11-16. Its only bump (claude-plugins-official PR 6821, to `5beb35b`) is still open and stops before the template fixes.
- **Upstream's own marketplace** rewrites the plugin on the volume every container shares, under every session running in parallel. That stays Eduardo's call.

Any of the three routes ends with the same `docs/agents/` files, because each one writes from the same 1.3.2 template. So the PR is the same whichever way the plugin is updated later. Taking the tag first leaves the plugin choice open.

### The plugin after this ticket

Unchanged: `mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official`, version `1.3.1`, commit `49dd158d1076134a641b33efb035946536778336`, last updated 2026-11-10. Sessions on this machine still load skill text that lacks `--blocked-by`, `--add-blocked-by`, comment-then-close, Count open blockers, the own-repo rule and the fresh-context lines. When the marketplace pin passes the `v1.3.2` tag, `claude plugin marketplace update claude-plugins-official` and then `claude plugin update mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official` bring it up. Re-running `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` after that should change nothing in `docs/agents/`.

### What changed in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`

It now equals `skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills/issue-tracker-github.md` at `v1.3.2` byte for byte, also after `vp check --fix`. The five hunks from #196's findings:

1. **Blocking** moves under Conventions and leads with `gh issue create --blocked-by <n>,<n>` and `gh issue edit <child> --add-blocked-by <blocker>` (`gh` 2.94+), keeping the REST call for older `gh`.
2. **Count open blockers** is new: `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by`, or `gh issue view --json blockedBy` filtered to `OPEN`.
3. **Close** is comment-then-close: `gh issue comment`, then `gh issue close`. On an already-closed issue `--comment` drops the comment.
4. **The own-repo rule** is new: never file into `mattpocock/skills`, and check `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner` before the first create.
5. **Read a PR** reads the body first, then `--comments`.

The Wayfinding operations' Blocking and Frontier query now point at the Conventions entries instead of repeating them.

### What didn't change

- `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` already equals the 1.3.2 template. `domain.md`'s template is unchanged since 1.3.1, and this repo's single-context copy stays.
- The repo's choices: the GitHub tracker, PRs as a request surface off, the five default triage labels (all five exist on the repo), single-context domain docs. `CLAUDE.md` is untouched.
- 1.3.2's new setup steps have nothing to do here: `gh repo view` reaches `dbarjs/hero-synergy`, and there is no legacy `CONTEXT.md` or `CONTEXT-MAP.md`.
- The scout reads only the doc's H1, `# Issue tracker: GitHub`, which is unchanged. `vp check` passed with 0 errors and the 2207 unit tests passed.
- `docs/upstream.md`'s tested ceiling still says 1.3.1. Moving it is the map's **upstream register** fog, not this ticket.

202.title: How do specs and build tickets render in the Tree and the Detail?
202.body:
## Question

How do a spec and its build tickets look in the Tree, the Focus pane and the Detail?

Prototype against this repo's real pairs ([#1 hero-synergy v0.1.0, fully decided](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/1) and [#37 Spec: hero-synergy v0.1.0, the Cockpit](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/37) with 26 build tickets; [#130 State reading for local trackers, tested against a real five-month tracker](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/130) and [#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/163) with 11) and against a repo with dozens of maps and specs:

- **Where a spec sits.** Under the map it came from, beside the maps, or in a section of its own; and where a spec with no map sits.
- **The spec row.** Its counts (takeable, built of total), its states (no build tickets yet, takeable, nothing takeable, built) and what ▶ does.
- **The build ticket row.** Its triage role, HITL or AFK, what it waits on, its session, its worktree, a pull request.
- **The Detail.** For a spec: the problem, the solution, a long list of user stories, the decisions. For a build ticket: what to build, the acceptance criteria with their boxes, the neighbourhood.
- **The map afterwards.** What a finished map shows once its spec exists.

The forms to draw are in the findings of [#197 Which forms do specs and build tickets take, upstream and in the wild?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/197). Prior art: [#7 How do maps render in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/7) with its prototype on `prototype/map-rendering`, and [#23 Where does the Cockpit live: sidebar, editor tab, or both?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/23).

203.title: How does the scout recognise a spec and its build tickets?
203.body:
## Question

With no label that says "spec", what makes an issue a spec and an issue a build ticket for the scout, on GitHub and on a local tracker?

- **A spec on GitHub.** Which of its sub-issues, its headings, its `ready-for-agent` label or its title the scout keys on; a spec with no build tickets yet; a spec whose build tickets are all closed; a closed spec.
- **A build ticket.** A sub-issue of a spec; a ticket written before 1.3.2, which points at its spec only through a `## Parent` section; blockers as native edges against `## Blocked by` text.
- **A spec's map.** How the scout knows which map a spec came from when the only link is prose in the spec's body; a spec with no map; a map with two specs.
- **A local tracker.** `spec.md` and the older file names, beside `map.md` or without it; which issue files of an effort are its spec's build tickets; and what becomes of the Unmapped issue rule ("one whose `Parent:` line names a PRD") decided in [#139 Which issue files are a map's tickets](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/139).
- **What is neither.** A `ready-for-agent` issue with no parent, such as [#36 Write the upstream-review skill](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/36); a map's sub-issue that carries a triage label; a spec's sub-issue that carries a `wayfinder:` label. Which of these is drift, and at which level.
- **The glossary.** Spec, Decision ticket, Build ticket, Ticket and Unmapped issue.

Every rule is code ([ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md)). The forms and their counts are in the findings of [#197 Which forms do specs and build tickets take, upstream and in the wild?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/197); what the API can list, and at what cost, in those of [#198 What can GitHub's API report about specs, build tickets and their pull requests, and at what cost?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/198).

204.title: Which tickets are AFK, and which sessions bypass?
204.body:
## Question

Once tickets are of two kinds, which are AFK, and which sessions start with permissions bypassed?

Today a ticket is AFK when it is a research or task ticket, or carries `ready-for-agent` whatever its type; `ready-for-human` wins over both. That rule was decided in [#127 Which Actions carry the bypass flag, and the settings' final names](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/127) and lives in the glossary and in `packages/core/src/claude/bypass.ts`. Skills 1.3.2 says a map and its tickets never carry a triage label.

- **A decision ticket.** Whether AFK now comes from its type alone, and what a `ready-for-agent` or `ready-for-human` label on one means: drift, ignored, or still honoured for maps charted before 1.3.2.
- **A build ticket.** AFK when `ready-for-agent`, HITL when `ready-for-human`; the other triage roles (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `wontfix`) and a build ticket with none.
- **Bypass.** Which of To spec, To tickets, Implement, Implement spec and Grill an idea count as a ticket Action under `afkTickets`, and which stay plain.
- **The Tree.** HITL or AFK on a build ticket row, beside its triage role.
- **The words.** The glossary's AFK ticket, Triage role and Bypassed session, and the README's bypass paragraph.

What 1.3.2 changed, word for word, is in the findings of [#196 What did skills 1.3.2 change in the contracts the Cockpit reads or spawns?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/196).

205.title: Which Actions carry an idea or a finished map to a spec and its build tickets?
205.body:
## Question

Which Actions take an idea or a finished map to a spec, and a spec to its build tickets, and what does each run?

- **Grill an idea.** A repo-level Action beside Chart a map that runs `/grill-with-docs`, the start of upstream's main flow and the place domain-modeling runs: its label, where it sits (the empty state, the Tree's title bar, the palette), its terminal (plain and untracked like Chart a map, or named), and when the Cockpit leads with it instead of Chart a map.
- **To spec.** On a finished map, as today; whether its name, its terminal or its tracking change now that what it produces is shown.
- **To tickets.** On a spec with no build tickets: the command and its argument.
- **One context window.** Upstream keeps the grilling, `/to-spec` and `/to-tickets` in one unbroken context window. Whether To tickets continues the session that wrote the spec, starts cold on the spec's reference, or is a hint to type `/to-tickets` in that session; and what the Cockpit does when that session is gone.
- **The boundary.** Whether any of this is "chaining user-invoked skills automatically", which [#1 hero-synergy v0.1.0, fully decided](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/1) ruled out for v0.1.0, and whether [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md) stands unchanged.
- **Names.** The command when a skill is found as a plugin or as a project skill, and the greyed reason when it is missing.

What a session can carry over is in the findings of [#199 What do /to-tickets, /implement and /implement-spec need from a Claude Code session?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/199); each skill's arguments at 1.3.2 in those of [#196 What did skills 1.3.2 change in the contracts the Cockpit reads or spawns?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/196). Prior art: [#24 How are actions placed and named in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/24).

206.title: How is a build ticket launched, and how does its work reach main?
206.body:
## Question

What does the Cockpit run for a build ticket, and how does the work get from the session to `main`?

- **Implement.** The Action on a frontier build ticket: its command (`/implement <reference>`), the session name (`#number title`), the worktree (`-w <number>` on GitHub, none on a local tracker), the status plugin and its env, the terminal's icon.
- **The claim.** `/implement` doesn't tell the session to assign the ticket. Whether a build ticket session claims, what tells it to (the repo's agent docs, the prompt), and what the Tree shows for a live session on an unclaimed build ticket.
- **Resume and Launch fresh.** On a build ticket whose session ended, and on one claimed elsewhere.
- **To `main`.** The branch a build session commits to, who opens the pull request, what closes the ticket, and what the Cockpit shows between the session ending and the merge. The Cockpit never runs git ([ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md)).
- **A blocker not merged yet.** A build ticket's blocker closes on the tracker only when its pull request merges: whether the ticket behind it is takeable before that, stacked on the unmerged branch.
- **No spec.** Whether Implement is offered on a `ready-for-agent` issue with no spec, such as [#36 Write the upstream-review skill](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/36), and where such an issue shows.
- **▶.** What it runs on a build ticket row.

What `/implement` does with branches and worktrees is in the findings of [#199 What do /to-tickets, /implement and /implement-spec need from a Claude Code session?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/199); its arguments at 1.3.2 in those of [#196 What did skills 1.3.2 change in the contracts the Cockpit reads or spawns?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/196). Prior art: [#21 How does the Cockpit handle a session's lifecycle?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/21) and [#5 How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/5).

208.title: What are a spec's states, and what becomes of its map?
208.body:
## Question

Which states does a spec have, what is derived for it, and what becomes of the map it came from?

- **The states.** A spec with no build tickets yet, with takeable ones, with open work and nothing takeable, with every build ticket closed, and closed: the name of each, which are shown, which fold away and which are hidden.
- **The frontier.** Whether a spec's frontier and `next` follow the map's rule (open, unblocked, unclaimed, first in order), and whether a triage role (`ready-for-human`, `needs-info`) takes a build ticket off it.
- **Counts and order.** Built of total, where specs sort among maps, and how urgency (needs you, takeable, stuck, finished) ranks a repo that holds both.
- **The map afterwards.** Whether a finished map that already has a spec still offers To spec, whether it folds under its spec or leaves the Tree, and what "finished" means then.
- **The words.** Frontier, Finished map and Stuck map in the glossary, and the names of a spec's states.

What makes an issue a spec, and which map it belongs to, is decided in [#203 How does the scout recognise a spec and its build tickets?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/203); what the rows look like comes from the prototype of [#202 How do specs and build tickets render in the Tree and the Detail?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/202). A map's own "finished" is revisited in [#200 What does a map's fog offer?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/200).

209.title: Does the Cockpit show a build ticket's pull request?
209.body:
## Question

Does the Cockpit show a build ticket's pull request, and what does it read of it?

- **A state of its own.** Whether a build ticket with an open pull request is shown as such (in review, checks failing, ready to merge) or stays a claimed ticket with a worktree line.
- **What is read.** The pull request's number and title, draft or open or merged, its checks, its review; from which link, at what cost per refresh, and what causes a refresh when the checks finish.
- **Needs you.** Whether a pull request waiting for a merge counts for the badge and for the order of specs.
- **The click.** A button that opens the pull request; never an Action that merges it.
- **A local tracker**, which has no pull requests.

What GitHub reports about the pull request that closes an issue, and what it costs, is in the findings of [#198 What can GitHub's API report about specs, build tickets and their pull requests, and at what cost?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/198). How a build session's work reaches `main` is decided in [#206 How is a build ticket launched, and how does its work reach main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/206).

210.title: How does a whole-spec run show in the Cockpit?
210.body:
## Question

What does the Cockpit offer and show for `/implement-spec`, one session that builds a whole spec?

- **Implement spec.** The Action on a spec row: when it is offered beside the per-ticket Implement, its command, its session name, its worktree and its tracking.
- **While it runs.** Implementer subagents build the frontier in parallel inside one session. What each build ticket row shows, what the spec row shows, and what "needs you" means for the run.
- **Mixing.** A per-ticket session on a spec that a whole-spec run is building; two whole-spec runs on one spec.
- **To `main`.** One integration branch and one pull request that closes the spec and its tickets: what the Tree shows until it merges.
- **Bypass.** Whether a whole-spec run follows the rule of [#204 Which tickets are AFK, and which sessions bypass?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/204) or has one of its own.

What the registry reports for implementer subagents, and where their worktrees and branches go, is in the findings of [#199 What do /to-tickets, /implement and /implement-spec need from a Claude Code session?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/199). The per-ticket launch is decided in [#206 How is a build ticket launched, and how does its work reach main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/206).

211.title: What does the snapshot hold for a spec and a build ticket?
211.body:
## Question

What does the snapshot hold for a spec and a build ticket, and how do they sit beside maps?

- **Where specs live.** A list beside `maps`, nested under the map each came from, or one list of two kinds; and the link between a spec and its map.
- **A spec.** Its facts (number, title, ref, state, body) and the sections code reads from its body (the problem, the solution, the user stories, what is out of scope).
- **A build ticket.** What it holds beyond a decision ticket: its triage role, its acceptance criteria and their boxes, its pull request if the Cockpit shows one; and what it lacks (a type, an outcome, a gist).
- **One shape or two.** A single `Ticket` with a kind, or a shape per kind.
- **The version.** The schema version after the schema 2 that [#163 Read a local tracker's state in every form a real five-month tracker holds](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/163) lands, and what happens to a cached snapshot.

Nothing derived and nothing about sessions, as decided in [#26 What does the snapshot hold for a map and a ticket?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/26). This ticket writes down what [#203 How does the scout recognise a spec and its build tickets?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/203), [#208 What are a spec's states, and what becomes of its map?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/208) and [#209 Does the Cockpit show a build ticket's pull request?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/209) need the snapshot to carry.

213.title: Does the scout's refresh budget hold once it reads specs and pull requests?
213.body:
## Question

Does the refresh budget decided in [#27 What is the scout's budget: refresh cadence, caching and rate limits?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/27) hold once the scout reads specs and their pull requests, and what changes if it doesn't?

Measured in [#198 What can GitHub's API report about specs, build tickets and their pull requests, and at what cost?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/198): for a repo with 45 maps and 45 specs, 7 of each open, one collect costs 29 points today, 57 with specs and 64 with each build ticket's pull request. At one collect a minute the worst hour goes from 1,740 points to 3,840, which leaves 160 before automatic refreshes pause. The fragment the scout ships costs 4 points per map, not the 5 that #27 recorded.

- **The numbers.** Whether the 60-second floor, the chunks of five and the 1,000-point pause stay as they are.
- **What is read when.** Whether specs and pull requests are read on every collect, or less often than maps: only open specs, only a spec with a live session or an open pull request.
- **Running out.** What the Cockpit says when the budget runs out while sessions wait.
- **The counter.** The research saw `rateLimit.remaining` answered from two counters with different reset times: which one the pause trusts.

It needs the route that [#203 How does the scout recognise a spec and its build tickets?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/203) picks for finding specs, and what [#209 Does the Cockpit show a build ticket's pull request?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/209) decides to read.

openPullRequests.title: Refresh the tracker doc from the skills 1.3.2 template
